trackers.name: Defensa Pública — 34 district directorates and the ALEGRA centres
trackers.desc: A FREE LAWYER THROUGH 34 DISTRICT DIRECTORATES nationwide, grounded in Article 139, numeral 16 of the Constitution guaranteeing effective access to justice, particularly for people in situations of vulnerability. HOW IT WORKS: go to a Centro de Asistencia Legal Gratuita (ALEGRA) with your DNI and any evidence; a public defender opens a carpeta de defensoría setting out what to do, and the case is tracked through it. The lawyer will accompany you to the relevant institution. You sign a declaración jurada of your economic situation. THE PART THAT MATTERS UNDER DEADLINE: they verify your situation within 20 days and the defence continues meanwhile — only if you are found able to pay does a Resolución de No Gratuidad follow. Representation starts before means are proven. CHECK SCOPE FIRST: the named specialities are criminal defence and assistance to victims of family and sexual violence, abandonment and offences against life, body and health, plus matters listed in the regulations to Ley 29360 as amended by Decreto Legislativo 1407 — a land or environmental matter is not a named speciality, so confirm it falls within the regulation. It also runs extrajudicial conciliation and popular arbitration.

trackers.name: Defensoría del Pueblo — what it can and cannot do for you
trackers.desc: USE IT FOR PRESSURE, NOT FOR A REMEDY. A constitutionally autonomous body created by the 1993 Constitution, with offices throughout the territory and a free line 0-800-15-170, handling complaints, queries and requests from citizens whose rights have been violated. It has an Adjuntía de Medio Ambiente, Servicios Públicos y Pueblos Indígenas and publishes guidance for human rights defenders, and it warns publicly about the risk of social conflict in communities — which is worth triggering early. BUT KNOW ITS LIMITS BEFORE YOU RELY ON IT: it does not act as judge or prosecutor, does not substitute any authority, does not issue judgments, and does not impose fines or sanctions. It produces reports with recommendations or exhortations whose force rests on persuasion and the strength of technical, ethical and legal argument. Governed by Ley Orgánica 26520, amended by Leyes 29882 and 32028.

trackers.name: Profonanpe — competitive funds, including money to create protected areas
trackers.desc: PERU'S ENVIRONMENTAL FUND, AND SOME OF IT PAYS COMMUNITIES DIRECTLY. Bosques Tropicales gives non-repayable grants funded by the Peru–United States debt swap, and its eligible applicants are exactly the right ones here: local organisations that directly use the natural resources of their own territory; indigenous, local and regional organisations with recognised experience working with indigenous peoples; holders of the various conservation and sustainable-management modalities; and universities with the participation of indigenous communities. CONSERVA AVES IS THE ONE TO NOTE IF YOU WANT LAND PROTECTED: it finances initiatives promoting the creation and/or expansion of subnational protected areas for threatened, endemic and declining migratory birds — it pays for making protection happen, not just for studying it. Other competitions fund bionegocios in Loreto, Amazonas, San Martín, Madre de Dios, Puno and Cusco, and ventures around ANP, ACP and ACR areas.

trackers.name: Fondo Concursable Puna — check which window you are in
trackers.desc: CLIMATE ADAPTATION MONEY IN 58 DISTRICTS of Arequipa, Apurímac, Cusco, Puno and Lima (Yauyos). THE WARNING FIRST — NOT ALL WINDOWS ARE GRANTS: in the second call, of 40 preselected initiatives 36 were in ventana 1, which is repayable funds, and only 4 in ventana 2, non-repayable. Ventana 2 targets micro and small enterprises, communal enterprises, producer associations and cooperatives with clear commercial objectives; ventana 3 requires a business plan approved and an agreement signed with Agroideas. Know which window you are applying to before treating the money as a grant. INCOMPLETE LEGAL STATUS IS NOT FATAL: campesino communities, producer associations and cooperatives in the process of formalisation may apply with the support of civil society organisations. ELIGIBLE MEASURES: conservation and restoration of bofedales and qochas, agroforestry, restoration of native forests and of andenes and terraces, integrated soil fertility management, infiltration ditches, contour and conservation agriculture, sustainable pasture management. EXPECT TWO STAGES: preselected initiatives go through diagnosis and planning with accompanying organisations before final selection.

trackers.name: FENAMAD — Federación Nativa del Río Madre de Dios y Afluentes
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the indigenous federation of Madre de Dios, running since the mid-1980s and defending the collective rights of Harakbut, Yine, Matsigenka, Ese Eja, Awajún, Kichwa Runa, Amahuaca and Shipibo communities, plus peoples in isolation and initial contact (PIACI), which it has worked on since the mid-1990s. Its practical work is legal security of territory: demarcation, georeferencing and legal recognition of communal land, run with the regional government's land titling directorate, and resizing Bosques de Producción Permanente that overlap communal territory. USE IT: where illegal gold mining or logging is entering titled communal land. It receives confidential satellite monitoring reports from Conservación Amazónica's MAAP project identifying which communities are being invaded. NOTE the domain is fenamad.com.pe, not .org.pe.

trackers.name: Grufides (Cajamarca)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Cajamarca organisation that advises, trains in rights and provides legal defence to communities whose eco-territorial rights are being violated — the region concentrating Peru's largest mining investment and, per the Defensoría del Pueblo, a long-running cluster of socio-environmental conflicts. It brought the amparo in the Conga case and took it to the Latin American Water Tribunal. WHO IT SUITS: campesino communities, rondas and water committees facing a mine, a hydroelectric project or informal mining. It also runs an Observatorio de Conflictos with case files, mining-concession maps and reports naming operators — useful before you have a lawyer at all — and tracks criminalisation of protest, which matters if leaders are already being prosecuted.

trackers.name: PRODHAB — Agencia de Protección de Datos de los Habitantes
trackers.desc: PRODHAB — Agencia de Protección de Datos de los Habitantes — Costa Rica’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: CEDARENA — Centro de Derecho Ambiental y de los Recursos Naturales
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Costa Rica's environmental and natural-resources law centre, a founding member of AIDA, working on environmental law and land and resource rights. WHO IT SUITS: Costa Rican environmental permitting and land-rights disputes. NOTE: canonical domain not yet verified; named as an AIDA founder on aida-americas.org. SOURCING UPGRADED, NOT CLOSED: the domain remains unverified, but the organisation is confirmed from the Inter-American Court of Human Rights' own published participant list for Advisory Opinion OC-32/2025, appearing as Asociación Centro de Derecho Ambiental y los Recursos Naturales. A body on the participant list of the Court's climate advisory opinion has demonstrated international litigation capacity — which is what you would have wanted the website to tell you.

trackers.name: AIDA — Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional organisation of Latin American environmental legal experts providing FREE legal and scientific support to communities and local groups, using international and inter-American human-rights law. Track record includes stopping a large dam in Mexico, halting clear-cutting of native forest in Chile, and the La Oroya smelter ruling in Peru. WHO IT SUITS: communities whose national system has already failed them and whose fight needs to go to an international body. AIDA works across Latin America, so it may be able to act in your country even if it has no office there — ask.

trackers.name: Asociación Costa Rica por Siempre
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: administrator of several standing Costa Rican conservation funds — the Fideicomiso Costa Rica por Siempre, SAVIA from the first US debt-for-nature swap, the second swap, and the Fondo Azul — supporting around 45 priority protected areas a year through open convocatorias. WHO IT SUITS: SAVIA calls target social organisations across six regions; the marine window has been open to natural and legal persons, national and foreign, which is unusually wide. HOW IT DIFFERS: an endowment tied to national protected-area commitments, so proposals strengthening a declared área silvestre protegida land best.

trackers.name: Nexus-PJ / CIJ
trackers.desc: Costa Rica's official judicial information center: free jurisprudence search across the courts via the Nexus-PJ platform. · Find here: the jurisprudence and judicial information centre of Costa Rica's Judiciary (Nexus-PJ).

trackers.name: Registry of Transparency and Final Beneficiaries
trackers.desc: Registry of Transparency and Final Beneficiaries — Costa Rica’s beneficial-ownership register, disclosing the real individuals who ultimately own or control companies. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A PLAIN COMPANY REGISTRY: this names the real HUMAN owners behind a company; a company registry names only the legal entity, its directors and filings. Use the registry first to find the entity, then this to pierce the shell to the people who profit. — Holds to account: the hidden owners behind firms dealing with Costa Rica’s government — find beneficial-owner filings.

trackers.name: Contraloría General de la República
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Costa Rica. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Costa Rica.

trackers.name: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos
trackers.desc: Costa Rica's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Costa Rica.

trackers.name: Registro Nacional
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: companies in Costa Rica — find the national registry of legal entities and property.

trackers.name: SICOP
trackers.desc: Costa Rica's unified public e-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Costa Rica, and for how much.

trackers.name: Servidumbre ecológica — protects part of a farm without freezing the rest
trackers.desc: THE INSTRUMENT THAT ANSWERS THE OWNER'S OBJECTION. A servidumbre ecológica (Ley de Biodiversidad 7788 art. 123, with art. 37 LOA) lets an owner permanently dedicate part of a farm to conservation, inscribed in the Registro Nacional — registration is what makes it durable rather than a promise. Crucially it does not limit permitted development on the rest of the property: only the dedicated portion must stay natural. That is precisely the objection that defeats designations elsewhere in this map. THE ALTERNATIVE: a Refugio Nacional de Vida Silvestre Privado (Ley 7317 arts. 82–87, Decreto 32633) is officially recognised protected status, requiring presidential decree published in La Gaceta and an application to SINAC with preliminary physiographic, biological and socioeconomic studies; it lasts 10 years, renewable indefinitely, and its main financial benefit is exemption from land tax plus authorised ecotourism income negotiated with MINAE. SO: the easement is perpetual but private; the refuge is renewable but carries tax relief. BE REALISTIC — legal analysis describes only a small line of judicial decisions actually enforcing easement conservation content, and the question of survival on transfer to a later buyer is the one to settle before signing.

trackers.name: Nosara — a biological corridor built entirely from voluntary agreements
trackers.desc: A MODEL A COMMUNITY CAN ACTUALLY RUN. Nosara is building Guanacaste's first biological corridor entirely through voluntary conservation agreements between private owners, using servidumbres ecológicas inscribed in perpetuity in the Registro Nacional — led by the Asociación Cívica de Nosara with SINAC under the regional biological corridors programme. The corridor links the uplands to the Ostional wildlife refuge on the coast, and Nosara still holds about 80 percent forest cover, exceptional for a coastal zone. THE ARGUMENT THEY USED IS THE REUSABLE PART: continuity protects fauna, regulates temperature, reduces erosion, prevents landslides and guarantees aquifer recharge supplying the district — framed as local self-interest, not abstract conservation. AND THE THREAT IT ANSWERS: the Informe del Estado de la Nación 2025 records that coastal development there has been marked by the segregation of former cattle properties into multiple parcels. Fragmentation by subdivision is the mechanism to watch — the same trap this map records for community land in Kenya. NOTE SINAC'S OWN DEFINITION: a corredor biológico is a territorial extension generally of private property whose function is to interconnect protected areas — so corridors are expected to be built on private land.

trackers.name: Contracorriente
trackers.desc: Contracorriente — Honduran in-depth investigative outlet (born of the 2015 anti-corruption protests) reporting on graft, mining, organized crime and power in one of the world’s deadliest countries for journalists. — Independent watchdog of officials and public power.

trackers.name: Instituto de Acceso a la Información Pública (IAIP)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; Honduras’ IAIP is the deconcentrated guarantor body under the LTAIP (2006) — it reviews recursos de revisión and runs the SINAIP/SIELHO transparency portals, Honduras.

trackers.name: ASJ — Asociación para una Sociedad más Justa (Transparency International Honduras)
trackers.desc: Honduras' national chapter of Transparency International, founded 1998, and one of the few national bodies documenting violence against environmental defenders: with CONADEH it published the 2026 report finding at least 111 environmentalists killed between 2015 and 2025, 92% of those crimes unpunished, and over 30% concentrated in Colón. It runs ALAC Honduras, an Advocacy and Legal Advice Centre that takes citizen corruption complaints - relevant where a concession was granted without the consultation the law required. WHO IT SUITS: communities needing their case documented and escalated rather than litigated; ASJ is a watchdog and advice centre, not a litigator. NOTE: its canonical domain could not be verified this session - reach it through Transparency International's national contacts directory at transparency.org. It runs ALAC Honduras (Centro de Asistencia Legal Anticorrupción), opened with technical support from Transparency International, which receives corruption complaints rather than only studying them: it advises victims and witnesses on filing with the competent authorities, explains the legal options, and accompanies and follows up cases until they are resolved. Report on 2213-1439, at diloaqui@asjhonduras.com, through diloaqui.asjhonduras.com, or via the Dilo Aquí Honduras app for iOS and Android. Between 2012 and 2016 ALAC filed 156 corruption complaints, of which 53 reached the courts. USE ITS RESEARCH TOO: ASJ counted 3,471 complaints to the Ministerio Público between 2008 and 2015 producing only 283 prosecutions — about 1 in 12 — which is the figure to cite when arguing that filing alone is not enough. NOTE: ASJ-US (asj-us.org) is a separate sister organisation; this entry is the Honduran chapter.

trackers.name: Bufete Jurídico Justicia para los Pueblos
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Honduran human-rights law office founded in 2000 by Kenia Oliva and Edy Tabora, combining litigation with investigation and documentation, and working in coordination with social, territorial and trade organisations rather than taking walk-in clients. It defended the Guapinol river defenders of Tocoa against criminalisation, and the Inter-American Commission's Precautionary Measure 137-23 covers the firm itself alongside the Comité Municipal para la Defensa de los Bienes Comunes y Públicos de Tocoa — its lawyers are under threat for this work. WHO IT SUITS: communities and campesino and indigenous leaders facing criminal prosecution brought to clear the way for a mine, dam or plantation. It works through organised movements, so approach with your committee or federation behind you.

trackers.name: MAR Fund — Small Grants Program (Mesoamerican Reef)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: an ecoregional fund created in 2004 by the national conservation funds of Belize, Guatemala, Honduras and Mexico, running a Small Grants Program by competitive Call for Proposals — now past its 17th call — with two windows, the Traditional Window and the Reef Rescue Initiative. WHO IT SUITS: civil-society groups working on coastal and marine protected areas anywhere in the Mesoamerican Reef System. HOW IT DIFFERS: transnational by design, so a project spanning the reef across two countries is a fit here where a national funder would balk.

trackers.name: HonduCompras
trackers.desc: Honduras's public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Honduras, and for how much.

trackers.name: Honduras — Instituto de la Propiedad (Registro Mercantil)
trackers.desc: National corporate registry; the Instituto de la Propiedad (IP) administers Honduras’s property & mercantile registries — company & trade-name registration under the Registro Mercantil — alongside intellectual property, Honduras. — Holds to account: companies in Honduras — find the Instituto de la Propiedad's mercantile registry of entities and trade names.

trackers.name: Tribunal Superior de Cuentas
trackers.desc: National — supreme audit institution of Honduras. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Honduras.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Honduras
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Honduras — supreme court in Honduras (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Contrato de manejo forestal comunitario — two vehicles, check tenure first
trackers.desc: THE ICF DELEGATES MANAGEMENT OF STATE-TITLED NATIONAL FOREST TO THE COMMUNITIES LIVING IN IT, by two different instruments — contratos de manejo forestal comunitario granted to legally constituted agroforestry organisations, or contratos de usufructo in favour of persons and families identified as possessors and occupants of the land. The distinction matters: an organised group needs legal personality; families already in possession have a separate usufruct route and do not. The stated purpose is to give legal security of tenure and generate economic, ecological and social benefits. Scale, as an indication: the Yoro region alone has assigned 37,768.08 hectares under community forest management contracts. THE SEQUENCE BEFORE ANY OF IT: ICF guidance says go first to the Instituto de la Propiedad, the Instituto Nacional Agrario and the municipalidades to request land tenure information — and to begin regularisation the ICF must issue an acuerdo de declaratoria of the zone to be regularised. Three offices, then a formal declaratory agreement. ALSO AVAILABLE: comanejo, defined in the forest law as shared management by contract between the State, municipalities, organised communities and specialised organisations with legal personality; and reservas naturales privadas, which have their own declaration and certification process.

trackers.name: Microcuencas declaradas — and the dictamen that must check for them
trackers.desc: THE WATER ROUTE IS OFTEN THE FASTER ONE. Honduras declares microcuencas as a protective designation and uses them heavily — the Yoro region alone holds 98 declared microcuencas, 10.35 percent of the national total, across 8 municipalities. Where a site supplies community water, seeking microcuenca declaration may be quicker and better supported than arguing for protected area status. AND HERE IS WHY IT BITES: before a forest management plan is approved, the Centro de Información y Patrimonio Forestal issues a dictamen determining whether the property contains protected areas, legally declared microcuencas, or already-approved management plans; once a no-objection opinion is granted it is entered into the SNIF. So ask for the dictamen and check the SNIF entry — an approval granted despite an existing declaration is a documented procedural failure, not just a policy disagreement. THE PARTICIPATION BODY: Consejos Consultivos Comunitarios Forestales, Áreas Protegidas y Vida Silvestre are established for areas identified by common agreement between ICF and the community — but the ICF will not recognise any Consejo that is not registered, so register it. Plans are self-evaluated every 6 months and evaluated jointly each year by ICF and the Corporación Municipal.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Comité Municipal de Defensa de los Bienes Comunes y Públicos de Tocoa
trackers.desc: The community committee at the centre of the Guapinol case: residents of Tocoa organised against the iron-oxide mining concession granted inside the Parque Nacional Montaña de Botaderos 'Carlos Escaleras' and over the ríos Guapinol and San Pedro, the town's water. Eight of its defenders were prosecuted and jailed; two, Aly Domínguez and Jairo Bonilla, were murdered in January 2023, and Óscar Oquelí Domínguez Ramos that June. The Inter-American Commission granted Precautionary Measure 137-23 for its members and their lawyers. WHO IT SUITS: this is a local committee, not a service — it is who you coordinate with if you are in the Aguán or Colón and facing the same concessions, and the template for how a municipal committee holds a national park boundary. NOTE: no canonical domain found; reach it through Bufete Justicia para los Pueblos, its legal representatives, already listed at national level. It is a coalition rather than a single body — the Comités Ambientales of Sector San Pedro (13 communities) and Sector Abisinia (14 communities), the Comité Ambiental de Guapinol, campesino groups, COPA, the Fundación San Alonso Rodríguez and the Parroquia San Isidro de Tocoa — and it has no website of its own, so the link is its Front Line Defenders profile, which carries the case history and urgent appeals. UNDERSTAND THE RISK BEFORE MAKING CONTACT: coordinator Juan López, also a Tocoa municipal councillor, was assassinated on 14 September 2024; Jairo Bonilla and the brothers Alí and Oquelí Domínguez were killed in 2023; members were criminalised and detained. The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights granted precautionary measures MC-137-23 on 5 October 2023 to 30 members and their legal team at the Bufete Justicia para los Pueblos, extended in March 2025. The dispute concerns mining affecting the Parque Nacional Montaña de Botaderos and the Guapinol and San Pedro rivers. USE IT: on 18 June 2025 the committee filed a recurso de amparo against acts and omissions of central and municipal administration after INHGEOMIN approved the ‘La Ceibita’ concession — a documented legal route others can follow.

trackers.name: Provita
trackers.desc: A Venezuelan non-profit civil association working since 1987, and one of the few conservation bodies still operating nationally. WHO TO ENLIST for two things in particular: it secured the Chacaracual Community Conservation Area on Margarita Island with World Land Trust, so it has done community-held land protection in practice; and since 2021 it co-coordinates Amazonía por la Vida with ORPIA, the regional Indigenous peoples' organisation of Amazonas, strengthening Indigenous territorial governance across Amazonas, Bolívar and Delta Amacuro. You CAN also use its RAISG work: since 2012 it produces the analysis of deforestation, mining, dams, roads and fire pressure on the Venezuelan Amazon, and the Libros Rojos red lists of threatened species and ecosystems.

trackers.name: COICA — Coordinadora de las Organizaciones Indígenas de la Cuenca Amazónica
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the basin-wide confederation of Amazonian Indigenous organisations, founded to act for 511 Indigenous peoples across the nine Amazon countries, around 66 of them in voluntary isolation or initial contact. It works through one national member organisation per country — in this country that is ORPIA, Organización Regional de los Pueblos Indígenas de Amazonas — and its governing Council brings those presidents together. Its standing work areas are territorial rights and natural resources, human and sociocultural rights, and international law, and it has issued a formal declaration on the defence of Amazonian Indigenous defenders. USE IT: go to ORPIA first — COICA is the regional weight behind a national organisation, not a direct service. It is the route to carry a territorial case or a threat against leaders from your community into regional and international forums.

trackers.name: Supreme Tribunal of Justice of Venezuela in exile
trackers.desc: Supreme Tribunal of Justice of Venezuela in exile — supreme court (Venezuela).

trackers.name: Armando.info
trackers.desc: Venezuelan investigative outlet exposing corruption and illicit finance; partner on the Panama Papers.

trackers.name: Contraloría General de la República (Venezuela)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution and head of the Sistema Nacional de Control Fiscal; receives the annual Informes de Gestión of every state and municipal comptroller in Venezuela. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find audit findings and how public money was spent or lost.

trackers.name: Venezuela — Ministerio del Poder Popular de Economía y Finanzas (MPPEF)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; administers public finances & State assets and prepares the national budget, Venezuela. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Venezuela.

trackers.name: SAREN
trackers.desc: National — Servicio Autónomo de Registros y Notarías (mercantile register), Venezuela. — Holds to account: companies in Venezuela — find the mercantile registry (SAREN) of entities and filings.

trackers.name: Tribunal Supremo de Justicia
trackers.desc: Official site of Venezuela's Supreme Tribunal of Justice with published decisions. · Find here: judgments of Venezuela's Supreme Tribunal of Justice, by chamber.

trackers.name: The two constitutional requirements the Arco Minero skipped
trackers.desc: THE CORE LEGAL ARGUMENT, AND IT IS TWO ARGUMENTS NOT ONE. The Arco Minero del Orinoco decree covers extraction and commercialisation of bauxite, coltan, diamonds, gold, iron, copper, kaolin and dolomite by national, transnational or mixed capital — and analysts record that it ignores two fundamental requirements of the 1999 Constitution: the obligation to carry out environmental and sociocultural impact studies, and consultation of indigenous peoples. Note that ‘sociocultural’ is a separate requirement from ‘environmental’, so its absence is independently arguable rather than folded into the EIA point. THE DOCUMENTED RESPONSE TO CRITICISM, recorded plainly: government replies run from evasion to criminalisation, including delay in decisions of the Tribunal Supremo de Justicia, dismissals of officials and teachers, and detention of journalists and human rights defenders; PROVEA records increased killings of indigenous defenders and threats to life arising from the violence driven by the mining boom. CIVIL SOCIETY'S STRUCTURAL DESCRIPTION: the AMO is characterised not as a conventional extractive industry but as a system where state entities, irregular armed groups, criminal networks and military structures operate together — producing systemic destruction, illegal mercury use and invasion of protected areas.

trackers.name: Anonymous denuncia, satellites and joint signatures — the methods in use
trackers.desc: WHAT VENEZUELAN ORGANISATIONS ACTUALLY DO WHEN ATTRIBUTION IS DANGEROUS. 1. ANONYMOUS DENUNCIA: SOS Orinoco states it made many denuncias anonymously to protect the integrity of those involved — where naming yourself is unsafe, anonymous publication is a recognised practice, not a failure of nerve. 2. SATELLITE EVIDENCE: degradation from illegal mining in Yapacana has been documented through the MAAP monitoring programme of Amazon Conservation — evidence gathered and published without anyone standing on the site, which here is a safety measure as much as an evidentiary one. 3. JOINT SIGNATURES DISTRIBUTE RISK: opposition has been expressed together by universities (UCV, ULA, Universidad Simón Bolívar), the Academia Nacional de Ciencias Físicas, Matemáticas y Naturales, the Sociedad Venezolana de Ecología, and organisations including PROVEA, Provita, Fundación Tierra Viva, Red ARA, Clima21, Centro Gumilla and SOS Orinoco. 4. FOREIGN LICENSING AS A LEVER: 11 NGOs led by SOS Orinoco warned that General Licences 51A, 54 and 55 expanding permitted activities with Venezuelan minerals were a dangerous regression — sanctions and licensing regimes abroad are a pressure point when domestic remedies are closed. 5. TECHNICAL ALLIANCES ARE HARDER TO DISMISS: the Grupo Orinoco and the Sociedad Venezolana de Ingeniería Minero Metalúrgica jointly criticised the Ley Orgánica de Minas approved 9 April 2026 for ignoring indigenous rights, retaining wide executive discretion, preserving mechanisms favouring opacity, and omitting recognised international standards — a mining engineers' society objecting on technical grounds is not easily labelled activism.

trackers.name: Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Informacion (ANTAI, Panama)
trackers.desc: Panama's transparency authority, created by Ley 33 de 2013 under the Ley 6 de 2002 transparency regime. You CAN get: a written answer within 30 calendar days, extendable once by up to 30 more only if the request is complex and the official tells you in writing before the first deadline runs out. If the official does not hold the document but knows who does, they are obliged to tell you. If access is refused or ignored, the remedy is an acción de Hábeas Data — and its terms are unusually favourable: ANY person has standing under article 17, and article 19 makes it a summary procedure with no formalities and NO NEED FOR A LAWYER. You CAN'T get: instant compliance — but the penalties are personal to the official, which is rare. An official who defies the tribunal's order is in contempt and fined at least twice their monthly salary, with dismissal for a repeat; one who obstructs access or destroys a record faces the same fine plus administrative and criminal liability; and you may sue them civilly for damages. For activists: use it for concession files, environmental authorisations and inspection records. WHEN NOT TO USE IT: ANTAI itself mediates and supervises — the order comes from a court on habeas data, so if you need compulsion, that is the step that matters.

trackers.name: Fundación Natura (Panamá) — FIDECO, Chagres y Darién
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: administrator of Panama's main environmental trusts — FIDECO, the Fondo Chagres from the country's first debt-for-nature swap in 2003, and the Fondo Darién — with a live Convocatorias page carrying project calls and a capacity-building programme. WHO IT SUITS: NGOs and organizaciones de base comunitaria; the capacity window is deliberately small (recent ceiling US$3,000) and aimed at groups needing institutional footing before a bigger grant. HOW IT DIFFERS: it also runs the donations programme for the state protected-areas system on behalf of MiAmbiente, so some calls are procurement rather than grants — check which.

trackers.name: CIAM — Centro de Incidencia Ambiental de Panamá
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: founded in 2007 by Panamanian civil society, a team of lawyers and environmental and social specialists litigating public-interest environmental cases before national and international tribunals, including the Supreme Court. Its record runs to the attempted reduction of the Donoso protected area, the Cobre Panamá mine, the Remance gold mine impact study, and ministry road routes pushed through with inadequate assessment time. WHO IT SUITS: its legal services are FREE for the communities most affected by environmental harm — that is the door, and it is unusually wide. It accompanies community complaints through administrative environmental processes as well as running strategic litigation, and it prioritises cases that set precedent, so a matter with wider application will get further than a purely local one.

trackers.name: Contraloría General de la República
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Panama, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Órgano Judicial de Panamá
trackers.desc: Official judiciary portal with jurisprudence and case information. · Find here: the portal and case information of Panama's Judicial Branch.

trackers.name: PanamaCompra
trackers.desc: Panama's electronic government-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Panama, and for how much.

trackers.name: Registro Público
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: companies in Panama — find the public registry of entities, directors and filings.

trackers.name: ANCON — a private body that owns a 263 km² reserve
trackers.desc: PRIVATE CONSERVATION OWNERSHIP AT NATIONAL-PARK SCALE IS DEMONSTRABLY POSSIBLE IN PANAMA. The Asociación Nacional para la Conservación de la Naturaleza, founded 1985, is a private non-profit that owns and manages the Punta Patiño Nature Reserve in Darién — 263 km² (about 65,025 acres) of forest and wetland, the largest private reserve in the country and a Ramsar wetland of international importance. Its name is an ode to Ancón Hill, the highest point in Panama City. It is an IUCN member. A READY-MADE MAP OF ALLIES: ANCON is one of 23 environmental groups with which the Ministry of Environment signed cooperation agreements — alongside the Sociedad Audubon de Panamá, Sociedad Mastozoológica de Panamá, Panamá Nature Center, FUNDESOJUR, the Parque Natural Metropolitano, Wetlands International and Fundación Avifauna. It co-leads Panamá Natural, a Project Finance for Permanence process led by MiAmbiente with Fundación Natura and developed with Enduring Earth (Pew, TNC, WWF, ZOMA Lab) — whose stated design includes voluntary participation of communities in caring for their natural heritage and active participation in decision-making, with PFPs described as locally led.

trackers.name: FIDECO — community associations can apply, but 45 percent is spoken for
trackers.desc: A PERMANENT ENDOWMENT, AND COMMUNITY ASSOCIATIONS ARE NAMED AS ELIGIBLE. The Fideicomiso Ecológico de Panamá was created 25 January 1995 by trust contract between the Government and The Nature Conservancy, with Fundación Natura as trustee, resting on Panama's Trust Law (Ley N°1 of 5 January 1984) and USAID agreement 525-0308. Initial endowment US$25 million — US$15m from Panama, US$8m from the United States — with support provided from the interest generated, so it is permanent rather than spend-down. WHO CAN RECEIVE: entities designated by government, principally the environment ministry, and qualified NGOs, educational entities and asociaciones comunitarias — community associations expressly, so this is not a government-only fund. THE NUMBER TO KNOW BEFORE APPLYING: 45 percent of FIDECO funds support the ministry's own management of protected areas, operation and maintenance — nearly half is committed before any external application, so plan for competition over the remainder. Signatories re-sign every 5 years to update strategy, which is a predictable review point. A CAUTION RECORDED FOR ELSEWHERE IN THIS MAP: FIDECO was originally to be capitalised by a debt-for-nature swap, but the price of Panamanian debt rose and the swap was no longer financially viable. Swaps depend on the debt trading cheaply — the mechanism can fail for reasons with nothing to do with conservation.

trackers.name: Consorcio Ambiental Dominicano (CAD)
trackers.desc: A membership organisation founded in 1999, made up of around nine state and civil-society institutions and working with more than 40 allied national and international organisations. WHO TO ENLIST as a route into the Dominican environmental sector rather than as a single actor: it convenes specialists across biodiversity, protected areas, sustainable agriculture and coastal-marine ecosystems, and concentrates its work inside protected areas and their buffer zones and along the border zone with Haiti. WHO IT SUITS: communities in or beside a protected area who need technical backing and an introduction to whichever member organisation actually handles their issue. It is a consortium and a technical service network, not a litigator or a grantmaker.

trackers.name: Ministerio de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales (República Dominicana)
trackers.desc: The Dominican environment ministry and the authority for the Sistema Nacional de Áreas Protegidas. You CAN get: the register of protected areas — 131 conservation units in six categories under Ley Sectorial 202-04 as at August 2023, covering 25.32% of the land area and 10.8% of marine waters under Ley 66-07 — downloadable protected-area maps, and the ministry's own lookup services for environmental authorisations, so you can check whether a project near you actually holds one. You CAN'T get: the underlying impact studies as a matter of course, or any guarantee the register is current. For activists: establishing that a project sits inside or beside a declared área protegida, or is operating without an authorisation, is the strongest opening move available here.

trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a regional environmental endowment established in 2012, managing an endowment plus a sinking fund for Ecosystem-based Adaptation, which it disburses mainly through partner National Conservation Trust Funds rather than directly — it helped establish several of them, including the Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia and St Vincent funds. Its EbA window runs open calls for proposals. WHO IT SUITS: organisations doing on-the-ground ecosystem work that reduces climate vulnerability. Check whether your country has a national trust fund first — that is usually the door, and the CBF itself is the wholesaler behind it. HOW IT DIFFERS: endowment income committed for the long term, so it funds sustained protected-area management rather than a campaign. APPLY TO YOUR NATIONAL FUND, NOT TO CBF — for most of the money. CBF is a regional umbrella: at national level the partner National Conservation Trust Funds (NCTFs) lead the grantmaking process, with endowment proceeds held in country-based subaccounts and channelled through them. So for the Conservation Finance stream, the regional body is the wrong door — find your NCTF. THE EXCEPTION IS THE EbA FACILITY, which awards through competitive calls for proposals and is a direct route. THE NUMBERS: EbA medium grants USD 250,000–1 million, large grants up to USD 2 million — large by the standards of most funds here, and not aimed at a small unincorporated group acting alone. Eligible recipients expressly include NCTFs, NGOs, community-based organisations, government agencies, universities and the private sector. SCOPE CHECK: the EbA Facility covers the marine and coastal zone of the insular Caribbean, so an inland project must show its connection to marine and coastal ecosystems. IF YOU ARE TOO SMALL FOR EbA: CBF partners with GEF SGP across 12 shared countries — that is the sibling route for community-scale grants, and it is recorded separately in this map. Endowment disbursements go to NCTFs that have signed agreements with CBF, the first in 2016 with Fondo MARENA in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.desc: Dominican Republic Ministry of Energy & Mines portal publishing the full text of special mining contracts and licences. Here you can trace who holds public concessions over land, resources or infrastructure in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.desc: National corporate & industrial-property registry; ONAPI registers company names & trade names and is the main source of registered-business information in the Dominican Republic (alongside the Registro Mercantil of the Chambers of Commerce), Dominican Republic. — Holds to account: companies in the Dominican Republic — find ONAPI's registry of company and trade names.

trackers.desc: Dominican Republic's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.name: Poder Judicial (Rep. Dominicana)
trackers.desc: Official judiciary portal with jurisprudence of the Supreme Court of Justice. · Find here: the Dominican Republic Judiciary's portal and case information.

trackers.name: Interés difuso — a legal interest that does not come from owning land
trackers.desc: THE DOORWAY FOR RESIDENTS WHO OWN NO PART OF THE SITE. Ley 64-00 defines interés difuso in the statute itself as an interest disseminated in a collectivity, corresponding to each of its members, and which does not emanate from titles of property, rights or concrete actions. That last clause is the point — in a field where most routes turn on tenure, this is a legally recognised interest that exists without property title. AND THERE IS A DEDICATED PROSECUTOR: the magistrado procurador fiscal for defence of the environment and natural resources of the corresponding jurisdiction, acting as judge of the querella, is obliged — if he considers the case has indications of gravity — to give it course. File with that office and frame the gravity explicitly, because gravity is the trigger the provision names. NOTE ALSO the definition of licencia ambiental: a document stating the impact study has been delivered and the activity may proceed conditioned on applying the programa de adecuación y manejo ambiental — so a licence is conditional by definition, and failure to apply that programme goes to the licence's own terms. CONSTITUTIONAL HOOK: Article 194 requires ensuring efficient and sustainable use of the Nation's natural resources.

trackers.name: Article 172 — directors are liable where the board authorised the act
trackers.desc: TWO THINGS THAT CHANGE WHO PAYS AND WHAT PROVES IT. ARTICLE 172: where two or more persons participated in the act they are jointly and severally liable (solidariamente) for the totality of the economic damages — and for legal persons that liability is established when the organs of direction or administration authorised the actions that caused the damage. So the board's authorisation is the fact to evidence: minutes, approvals, resolutions. That is what converts corporate conduct into liability here. WHAT THE TRIBUNAL IS DIRECTED TO WEIGH: in determining the magnitude of damages it shall take into account the actas drawn up by technicians and inspectors and formal reports issued by the environment ministry and other state environmental bodies — without prejudice to expert opinions the judge requires on his own initiative or at the request of a party. OBTAIN THE INSPECTION ACTAS AND MINISTRY REPORTS EARLY: they are the court's named evidence base, they are already being generated, and a party can ask the judge to appoint an expert rather than funding one alone. REPARATION means restoring the prior situation where possible, plus compensation for damage to the environment, to communities or to private parties — communities being a named claimant category in their own right.

trackers.name: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF)
trackers.desc: A FUND WHOSE SMALL-GRANT APPLICATION IS A SINGLE LETTER. CEPF (founded 2000; a joint initiative of the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the EU, the GEF, the Government of Japan, the MacArthur Foundation and the World Bank) has funded more than 2,500 grantees. FOR SMALL GRANTS THE LETTER OF INQUIRY IS THE ENTIRE APPLICATION — no longer project proposal is required — reviewed by the hotspot's Regional Implementation Team, with an offline template provided in the call's languages. Large grants go through the ConservationGrants portal and only then invite a full proposal. Reported averages: small grants around US$15,000, large around US$150,000; the small/large threshold varies by call (US$20,000 and US$50,000 both recorded), so read it. TIMING: calls run 6–8 weeks and notification comes several months after closing — but CEPF stops accepting letters once the designated funds are committed, so an open call can close early. WHO IS DISQUALIFIED: individuals cannot apply — you need a legally registered organisation with its own bank account — and government cannot apply. Community groups, farmers' cooperatives, Indigenous Peoples' organisations and women's groups all can, and CEPF welcomes first-time applicants. TWO RULES THAT SINK GOOD APPLICATIONS: your letter must aim at one single strategic direction; and site-based directions are geographically bound — community management work must be in a listed priority KBA, corridor work in a named corridor, while civil-society strengthening can be anywhere in the hotspot. THE STEP MOST PEOPLE SKIP: CEPF encourages you to contact RIT staff to discuss the idea before submitting — free, and the cheapest way to learn whether it fits.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: BAILII
trackers.desc: British and Irish Legal Information Institute: the most comprehensive free set of UK & Irish case law and legislation. · Find here: free UK and Irish case-law and legislation, including many historical law reports (BAILII).

trackers.name: Find Case Law (The National Archives)
trackers.desc: Official open-access service publishing court and tribunal judgments and decisions for England & Wales. · Find here: the official archive of judgments of the courts and tribunals of England & Wales (Find Case Law).

trackers.name: Legal Aid Agency
trackers.desc: Executive agency of the UK Ministry of Justice administering civil and criminal legal aid for England & Wales. · Find here: the body administering legal aid in England & Wales (Legal Aid Agency). IT FACES THREE SEPARATE TESTS — scope, means, and merits or interests of justice — and most people plan for means and are defeated by scope. THE SCOPE LOGIC REVERSED IN 2013: before April 2013, under the Access to Justice Act 1999, legal aid was available in any matter of English or Welsh law unless specifically excluded. Under LASPO 2012 a case must now come within the types of dispute listed in Part 1 of Schedule 1, with Part 2 listing express exclusions. So the question is not ‘is my case excluded’ but ‘is my case listed’ — which is why pre-2013 guidance misleads. WHAT IS IN: judicial review is a category for which means-tested legal aid can be available, alongside Human Rights Act claims — the route most environmental challenges take. IF YOU ARE OUT OF SCOPE: Exceptional Case Funding under section 10(3) or 10(4) of LASPO — but providers have no delegated power to grant it: under regulation 67(2)(a) of the Civil Legal Aid (Procedure) Regulations 2012 a written application goes to the Director of Legal Aid Casework for an exceptional case determination. TREAT IT AS A LONG SHOT, NOT A FALLBACK: Law Society evidence to Parliament states the discretion will be exercised sparingly and slowly and does not cover cases settled between refusal and renewal of a permission application. ASK ABOUT PROTECTIVE COSTS ORDERS in public law cases, and about the Aarhus costs regime for environmental challenges. The LAA has been an executive agency of the Ministry of Justice since 1 April 2013, replacing the Legal Services Commission.

trackers.name: JUSTICE (UK Section of the International Commission of Jurists)
trackers.desc: UK section of the International Commission of Jurists — an all-party law-reform and human-rights charity that researches and advocates on judicial independence, access to justice, fair trials and the rule of law, and intervenes as a third party in significant UK Supreme Court and ECtHR cases.

trackers.name: The Death Penalty Project
trackers.desc: London-based international legal-action charity providing free legal representation to prisoners facing the death penalty in more than 30 (mainly Commonwealth) countries — bringing appeals before the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council and international tribunals, challenging the mandatory death penalty, and producing empirical research on capital punishment.

trackers.name: Reprieve
trackers.desc: International legal-action charity (UK-founded, with a US sister organisation) providing free legal and investigative support to people facing the death penalty, arbitrary detention, torture and extrajudicial killing — pursuing strategic litigation, casework and public reporting on executions and secret detention.

trackers.name: Watershed Investigations (investigative outlet)
trackers.desc: Independent accountability-journalism outlet (GIJN member); Watershed Investigations — UK water & environmental accountability investigations.

trackers.name: WhatDoTheyKnow — FOI requests (GBR)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); WhatDoTheyKnow — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Parliamentary and Health Service Ombudsman
trackers.desc: UK ombudsman reporting to Parliament, investigating complaints of maladministration against public bodies.

trackers.name: Woodland Trust — woodland acquisition and protection
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the UK's largest woodland conservation charity — buys threatened woodland and adjoining land outright (funding purchases through public appeals), and campaigns to protect irreplaceable ancient woodland from development. USE IT: if woodland or land next to woodland is at risk of being built on, this is the body that can buy it and the campaign machinery that can fight the application.

trackers.name: John Muir Trust — wild land ownership and community buy-outs
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a conservation charity that protects wild land across the UK both by owning estates directly and by backing community buy-outs of land that comes up for sale. USE IT: for upland, wild and Scottish estate land — they buy, and they put money and weight behind communities trying to buy. IT HELPS OTHERS BUY, RATHER THAN BUYING AND HOLDING FOR YOU — grasp that before you approach it. Its record is a list of other bodies' purchases that it enabled: a major contributor to the Knoydart Foundation purchase (1999); helped Borders Forest Trust buy Carrifran woodland (2000); supported the North Harris Community buy-out of the 55,000-acre North Harris Estate (2002); a key role in the Assynt Foundation's purchase of Glencanisp and Drumrunie (2005); supported the Galson Estate Trust on North Lewis (2007); and supported the Langholm community buyout (2020). Six community buyouts across 21 years — and in every case the land ended up with the community body, not with the Trust. THE PLANNING HOOK IS THE MOST ACTIONABLE FACT HERE: in 2014 the Scottish Government adopted the Wild Land Areas map into planning policy — so a proposal inside a mapped area meets an existing policy objection rather than one you must construct. Establish first whether your site falls within a Wild Land Area. A REPLICABLE ARRANGEMENT: the Trust is recorded as the only external representative on the North Harris Trust, the community body managing that estate — a single external seat on a community landowner's board is a specific thing to propose. It works with crofters, landowners, other organisations and charities, manages estates of its own in the Highlands and Islands, and is a Scottish charitable company limited by guarantee based in Pitlochry, founded 1983. The John Muir Award (1997) exists to connect people with wild places that feel accessible to them — a route to people who do not already identify as conservationists. NOT TO BE CONFUSED with the John Muir Land Trust (jmlt.org), an unrelated California land trust.

trackers.name: Environmental Law Foundation (ELF)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a UK public-interest environmental law organisation that connects communities and individuals with legal help on environmental and planning matters. WHO IT SUITS: a community or individual affected by a development, a pollution source or the loss of green space, who needs to find out whether there is a legal route at all — and who could run it.

trackers.name: ClientEarth — environmental law charity
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an environmental law charity of roughly 250 lawyers and experts that goes to court to enforce environmental law against governments and companies, with around 168 active cases and offices in London, Brussels, Warsaw, Berlin, Madrid, Beijing and Tokyo. Won the case forcing the UK government to admit it was breaching legal air-pollution limits. WHO IT SUITS: systemic or precedent-setting challenges rather than a single local application — they pick cases that change the rules for everyone.

trackers.name: Rewilding Britain — Rewilding Innovation Fund and buyout support
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Rewilding Innovation Fund has awarded more than half a million pounds to dozens of rewilding initiatives across Britain since 2021, and the charity has put money behind community land buyouts (it helped fund the Langholm crowdfunder). WHO IT SUITS: restoration and rewilding projects in Britain, and communities preparing a buyout. HOW IT DIFFERS: it also publishes the legislation, subsidy and tax guides you need BEFORE taking land out of intensive use — do that homework first.

trackers.name: The Rivers Trust — find your local Rivers Trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the umbrella body for 65+ INDEPENDENT member Rivers Trusts across Britain, Northern Ireland and Ireland, each covering its own river catchment. Members restore waterways, run citizen-science monitoring, and drive policy change; the umbrella holds catchment data and expertise. USE IT: the map finds the trust for your catchment. Two reasons to go here rather than to a county body — rivers cross county lines, so a catchment trust may be the only organisation whose remit matches the actual impact area of a development; and they hold long-run water-quality monitoring data, which is documentary evidence a planning objection can rest on. Scotland and Wales have sister bodies (Fisheries Management Scotland, Afonydd Cymru).

trackers.name: National Lottery Heritage Fund — heritage grants
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the UK's largest heritage funder, awarding £10,000 to £10 million across the whole country. NATURE IS EXPLICITLY IN SCOPE — eligible heritage covers natural habitats and landscapes alongside buildings and archives, and funding can pay for capital works, staff posts, professional fees, conservation and volunteer costs. WHO IT SUITS: not-for-profit organisations, partnerships led by one, and — for the £10k–£250k tier only — private owners of a heritage asset who can show significant public benefit. HOW IT DIFFERS: three things decide whether it is worth your time. Applications are ROLLING, not to a deadline. You must bring MATCH FUNDING — at least 5% for grants under £1m, 10% above. And for requests up to £250,000 you can submit a Project Enquiry and get feedback on the idea WITHIN TEN WORKING DAYS, which is the cheapest way to find out if your project fits before writing anything. Note the limit: community sub-grants you pass on to others cannot be used to acquire land.

You CAN'T get: Scotland (SEPA), Wales (NRW) or Northern Ireland registers — separate systems.
