trackers.name: Umweltverbandsklage — suing when nobody has personal standing
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE WHEN NOBODY IS PERSONALLY AFFECTED: German administrative law normally requires you to show a violation of your own rights (Art. 19(4) Grundgesetz) — which fails when the injured interest is a habitat rather than your property. Under § 2 UmwRG an association recognised under § 3 UmwRG may challenge an administrative decision without asserting any violation of its own rights. Introduced in 2006 to implement EU Directive 2003/35/EC and the Aarhus Convention, and widened since after ECJ rulings. WHAT CAN BE CHALLENGED: approvals of industrial installations, waste-incineration and energy plants, water-law permits, Planfeststellungsbeschlüsse and large infrastructure requiring an EIA, plus decisions adopting plans and programmes. IT WORKS — ABOUT HALF THESE CASES SUCCEED: the Umweltbundesamt puts the success rate at roughly 48 percent for 2006–2016, 52 percent for 2017–2020 and about 51 percent for 2021–2023. But of roughly 400 recognised associations only 34 used their litigation rights in 2021–2023 — under 10 percent — because, as NABU states, the hurdles and costs mean it is used only where other participation has already failed, law is being broken and serious damage threatens. SO DO THIS: take your case to an already-recognised association rather than litigating alone. If you want your own recognition, start early but know it need not exist when you file — courts have treated § 3 recognition as needing to be in place by the close of the last oral hearing. One citizens' initiative applied on 10 November 2023 and was recognised on 19 August 2024. Each Land publishes its list of recognised associations.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Rechtsanwälte Günther, Hamburg — planning and environmental litigation
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL: a Hamburg law firm founded in 1976, a partnership since 2008, working mainly in administrative law, planning and environmental law, energy law and public and private construction law. It states its own client list, and Bürgerinitiativen and private individuals are on it, alongside environmental and animal-protection associations, companies, authorities, parliaments and municipalities. It has acted in constitutional litigation over the federal climate protection act. WHO IT SUITS: a German citizens' initiative or an association with standing that needs counsel who has run this kind of case before rather than a general practice learning on your file. The individual partners' listed specialisms include Grundstücksrecht, Entschädigungsrecht and öffentliches Baurecht — property, compensation and public building law — which is the combination a community facing a compulsory purchase or a planning consent actually needs. CHECK BEFORE YOU CALL: the same firm advises companies, including in the energy sector, and authorities and municipalities. That is not a criticism, it is a conflict check you should run first: name the developer and the consenting authority in your first email and ask directly whether the firm is free to act.

trackers.name: Anwaltskanzlei Günther, Berlin — a different firm, same surname
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL: a Berlin firm specialising in administrative disputes, based in the Haus der Demokratie since 2004. Its stated areas are general administrative law, public building and planning law, environmental law, monument protection, and public participation in public projects. It advises specifically where protected species or protected areas are affected by a construction project, and it helps with making and enforcing requests for information. WHO IT SUITS: a group at the point where it needs to know whether a species or site designation gives it a case, and one that wants the documents before it decides. Note what the firm says about its own approach: going to court is one route, but in its experience moderation with the authority or mediation is often more effective and less damaging. Expect to be advised out of litigation as readily as into it. DO NOT CONFUSE THE TWO: this is not Rechtsanwälte Günther of Hamburg, a separate and much older firm working in the same field. Different city, different practice, similar name. Check which one you have reached.

trackers.name: Kulturland eG — a €500 share buys the farm out of the market (Germany)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a registered cooperative at Hauptstraße 19, D-29456 Hitzacker (info@kulturland.de) which asks supporters of community-supported organic farms to buy shares or make loans, then uses the money to buy farmland and lease it to farmers long term. By 2022 it had secured 420 hectares across 30 projects nationally, on the strength of nearly 1,200 members. THE TERMS, WHICH IT PUBLISHES IN FULL: a share is €500 and carries no interest. After a minimum of five years a member may withdraw shares annually on six months' notice, and it undertakes to resell recalled shares to a new member. Loans can be secured by a land registry charge. Members who become convinced over time can convert shares into a tax-deductible donation, for which it works with the Schweisfurth Foundation in Munich. Lease contracts grant everlasting security of tenancy subject to stated conditions, and in the worst case, if it were forced to sell land to pay out departing members, farmers hold a pre-emptive right at the original purchase price. That last clause is the one a farmer will ask about first. THE OBSTACLE IT HAD TO SOLVE, WHICH MAY APPLY WHERE YOU ARE: German land-market regulation initially prevented it from acquiring land at all, because the cooperative is not itself an active farmer. Before assuming a purchasing vehicle can hold farmland in your country, ask whether the buyer has to be a farmer. SOURCING: verified on the Access to Land network's own member profile rather than the organisation's own website. The network is the body these organisations founded and belong to, so the profiles are close to first-hand, but confirm current figures directly.

trackers.name: DBU Naturerbe GmbH — owns 70,000 hectares of former military land (Germany)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the non-profit subsidiary of the Deutsche Bundesstiftung Umwelt, founded 2007, and the single largest recipient of Germany's Nationales Naturerbe — roughly 69,000 to 70,000 hectares across 71 properties in ten federal states. The wider programme covers about 156,000 hectares of federally owned land which the government decided not to privatise: former military training grounds, the Green Belt along the inner-German border, GDR trust land and disused lignite pits. Transfers are free of charge but carry strict, binding conservation conditions. Beyond the DBU subsidiary, the states and their nominated conservation organisations hold about 28,500 and 24,300 hectares respectively. WHY A COMMUNITY SHOULD KNOW: this is where large tracts of German land have gone instead of onto the market, and the recipients are named. If a threatened site adjoins, resembles or once formed part of a military training area, a lignite pit or the Green Belt, there is an existing route by which such land is transferred permanently to conservation ownership rather than sold. Ask the Federal Agency for Nature Conservation whether your site falls within it. THE FARMING POINT, WHICH SETTLES AN ARGUMENT: the ministry states that on the open-land parts of this estate — meadows, dry grassland, heaths — near-natural agricultural use is often the precondition for keeping the habitat at all, because without mowing or grazing they scrub over and become woodland. Protection here requires farming, and that is the federal government's own position. SOURCING: described here from the Federal Agency for Nature Conservation and the environment ministry, which run the programme; the company's own pages sit at dbu.de/naturerbe. Confirm current hectare figures there, as the transfers were made in tranches over many years.

trackers.name: Naturstiftung David — funds east German initiatives and networks the land-owning foundations
trackers.desc: TWO THINGS IT DOES FOR A COMMUNITY. First, it has supported more than 500 projects of east German environmental initiatives across twenty-five years, alongside eighteen of its own projects worth around €17 million. For a small group in Thuringia, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, Brandenburg or Mecklenburg, that is a funder with a long record of backing exactly that kind of group. Second, it is the coordinating body for the foundations and associations that own Germany's Nationales Naturerbe, running a networking project with the NABU foundation from March 2020 to February 2026 funded under the federal biodiversity programme — so it knows who owns what. THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR ANYONE LOOKING FOR A GERMAN LAND OWNER: its own survey found that around 175,000 hectares of nature conservation land in Germany is owned by conservation organisations, separately from the roughly 164,000 hectares of Nationales Naturerbe. Of the Naturerbe, some 24,000 hectares sit with about thirty foundations and associations, the NABU foundation alone holding close to 9,000. Germany is full of conservation landowners and there is no single directory; this is the organisation that has actually counted them. THE MODEL WORTH COPYING: it developed the 8,000-hectare Hohe Schrecke beech forest in northern Thuringia together with the neighbouring municipalities, explicitly as a model for people and nature coexisting, and it runs Weidewonne, a project supporting the shepherding trade as the means of maintaining valuable conservation land. Both are answers to the objection that protection removes local livelihoods. AND A ROUTE MOST GROUPS DO NOT KNOW: the federal BVVG transfers conservation land not only under the Naturerbe programme but also by sale to states, cities and municipalities and to organisations they commission — Erfurt bought about 13 hectares of meadow, woodland and orchard along the Wiesenbach that way. A German community whose council is sympathetic has a seller to point it at.

trackers.name: DBU — no formal ceiling on grant size, and it holds 70,000 hectares (Germany)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Deutsche Bundesstiftung Umwelt, the German federal environmental foundation, funding innovative, model and solution-oriented projects for environmental protection. Its funding themes give equal weight to new environmentally relieving technologies, the preservation and restoration of the National Natural Heritage, and promoting environmental awareness through information and environmental education. Germany had no funder in this file. THE TWO FACTS THAT DECIDE WHETHER TO APPLY: funding is a purpose-bound, non-repayable grant — Zuschuss — which may be proportional, fixed-sum or deficit financing, and the applicant must contribute an own share (Eigenanteil). And, unusually, the funding guidelines set no framework for the size of an award, so unlike other programmes there is formally no upper limit. The scale of a request is a matter for the case, not a published cap. HOW TO APPROACH IT, and this is the part that suits a small group: you may submit a short, meaningful project sketch (Projektskizze) first for an initial assessment; if it is assessed positively the office invites a full application. A community can test an idea in a couple of pages before committing to a full submission. Applications must be self-explanatory without reading cited or attached literature, and must state the recipient, the object and aim, the state of knowledge, expected costs, a cost plan by category, the financing plan, the scope, start and duration, how the project continues afterwards, and any funding from other programmes. Decisions are taken by the board of trustees or the general secretary; external assessors may be used, and an applicant may say which assessors they do not wish involved. ONE OF ITS NAMED FUNDING AREAS IS DIRECTLY ON POINT: nature conservation and sustainable use of nature in working landscapes and protected areas, alongside protection of nationally valuable cultural assets from harmful environmental influences. AND IT IS ALSO A LANDHOLDER: through DBU Naturerbe GmbH it holds around 70,000 hectares of protected open land in Germany, to be preserved permanently as National Natural Heritage. Note two changes: new funding guidelines took effect from the beginning of 2025, and an additional marine nature conservation funding area was created, supported by a 400 million euro endowment from the federal environment ministry and funding projects at around ten million euros a year.

trackers.name: Deutscher Naturschutzring — the umbrella of ~100 German organisations, with named contacts
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the German umbrella body for nature, animal and environmental protection, founded 1950 with 15 member associations and now bundling the interests of close to 100 member organisations — nature, animal and environmental protection bodies, nature-sport organisations, producer associations, foundations and institutes — which together reach more than eleven million people. It acts for its members as coordinator, mediator and representative in the political sphere, and describes itself as a constructive but critical partner to the state. WHY THE MEMBER LIST IS THE RESOURCE: it publishes its member organisations, and the range is wider than a conservation directory — producer associations and institutes sit alongside the campaigning bodies. For a German community, that is the map of who exists and what each one does, in one place. This file has found a published member or grantee list to be the most useful single artefact in five separate countries. AND IT WILL ANSWER TECHNICAL QUESTIONS: it states that contact people from its team help with specialist questions of all kinds across the thematic fields its coordinators work on, and that member associations can join mailing lists and expert rounds. If your ground raises a question nobody locally can answer, there is a named person for the subject. WHAT IT WORKS ON: biological diversity, valuable landscapes, undeveloped spaces, resource and climate protection, at national, European and international level. Beyond species and protected areas it has taken on leisure, tourism and transport, urban ecology and energy and economic policy. It has also been a supporting body for a competence centre on nature conservation and the energy transition. AN HONEST NOTE ON ITS LIMITS: critics have called it unwieldy and slowed by the self-interest of its large member associations and by internal hierarchy, and some significant organisations have not been members or were so only briefly. Treat it as a directory and a technical helpdesk rather than as a campaigner for your case.

trackers.name: Deutscher Alpenverein — 1.6 million members, and it holds the Verbandsklage right
trackers.desc: THE STATUS: the DAV was the first sports association recognised as a Naturschutzverband under the Bundesnaturschutzgesetz, and the first body recognised after the 2002 revision. It has been recognised in Bavaria since 1984, federally since the mid-2000s, and as an environmental organisation in Austria since 2008; its Baden-Württemberg Landesverband has been a recognised Naturschutzvereinigung under the Umweltrechtsbehelfsgesetz since October 2016. WHAT THAT RECOGNITION CARRIES, stated by the federal environment ministry: the formal participation and litigation rights under the federal nature conservation act — inspection of relevant expert opinions, the opportunity to comment on ordinances and statutes in the field of nature conservation and landscape management, and the right to pursue non-compliance with nature conservation norms in court. It has the Verbandsklage right. Inspection of the expert opinions is the part to note — a community usually cannot see the developer's expert reports; a recognised association can. THE SCALE: around 1.6 million members in more than 350 sections, running 325 huts and 220 climbing facilities and maintaining roughly 30,000 kilometres of paths. WHAT IT ACTUALLY OPPOSES: it says it seeks to break development spirals — for energy generation or tourism — and thereby preserve undeveloped areas, participating in hearing procedures and giving nature-conservation opinions; named examples include the proposed linking of the Pitztal and Ötztal ski areas and the extension of a hydropower plant in the Längental in the Stubai Alps. Its instruments include the Alpine Convention and the Alpenplan. BE REALISTIC ABOUT SCOPE: it states it generally participates in procedures where the nature and landscape of the Alps and the exercise of mountain sport are affected — so an alpine or Mittelgebirge case fits; a lowland one may not. Its climbing concepts for the German Mittelgebirge are drawn up to weigh conservation and climbing equally, and it works through the Arbeitskreise Klettern und Naturschutz.

trackers.name: NRW-Stiftung — Objektförderung und Flächenerwerb
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the state foundation for North Rhine-Westphalia, which both funds and buys. Its Objektförderung pays for securing land that is under nature or landscape protection OR merely suitable for it — so a threatened parcel does not need to be designated already — and its Projektförderung covers everything from a few hundred euros for a publication or a management measure up to large schemes. It has secured about 7,500 hectares by purchase and holds roughly 7,057 hectares outright, spending around €300M since 1986. WHO IT SUITS: local voluntary initiatives and charitable associations with a project rooted in NRW. Involving volunteer effort is a stated precondition of funding, and an application needs a coherent cost and financing plan plus your own contribution. HOW IT DIFFERS: most funders will not buy the land — this one will.

trackers.name: BUND NRW Naturschutzstiftung — Flächenankauf
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: buys land worth protecting in North Rhine-Westphalia and holds it as foundation property, which secures it permanently — the foundation is constituted 'for ever', charitable, and politically and financially independent. It has bought valley woodland in the Siebengebirge and old orchard parcels near Bornheim, and has accepted woodland by gift where a local BUND group initiated it. USE IT: but note the condition it states openly — it buys when the purchase makes conservation sense AND the local BUND group is willing and able to take on the necessary ongoing management of the site voluntarily. So find and commit the local group first; without people to mow the meadow, the purchase will not happen.

trackers.name: Bayerischer Naturschutzfonds
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Bavaria's state nature foundation, set up in 1982 as an independent foundation under public law, which funds the purchase or long-term lease of ecologically valuable land as well as biotope works, project management, applied research and public outreach. It separately administers the Ersatzgelder held by the lower nature-conservation authorities. WHO IT SUITS: both natural and legal persons may apply, but in practice the project carriers are conservation and landscape-management associations and municipalities, and they carry an own contribution of 15 to 50 percent — so budget for your share before you ask. Two screens that reject applications: it funds discrete projects only and gives no institutional or core funding, and it will not fund anything you are legally obliged to do, including compensation and replacement measures under the Bavarian nature conservation act. HOW IT DIFFERS: it stands behind the state's own programmes rather than beside them — if a Bavarian state funding scheme could cover your measure, check that route first, because the foundation will point you there.

trackers.name: Niedersächsische Bingo-Umweltstiftung
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Lower Saxony's environmental foundation, funded from the gambling levy and the Bingo environmental lottery, which funds practical conservation work explicitly as a complement to the state's statutory duties — creating new biotopes and ecologically upgrading existing ones, biotope networking, margin habitats along paths and watercourses, wet fallows, avenues, Wallhecken and field copses. Its stated principles are sustainability, VOLUNTEER involvement and practicality, so a project with real hands behind it beats a polished one without. WHO IT SUITS: tax-privileged bodies and bodies under public law only — registered associations, foundations, charitable companies, municipalities, schools. Private individuals cannot apply, and the applicant must hold its tax seat in Lower Saxony, proven with a Freistellungsbescheid from a Lower Saxony tax office. HOW IT DIFFERS: it publishes a routing rule. Applications up to €30,000 can come straight here; above that, ask NBank first whether your project fits a state programme. Separately, the Emsfonds is earmarked money for the ecological state of the Ems-Dollart region and is the one pot not tied to a Lower Saxony seat.

trackers.name: Stiftung Naturschutzfonds Baden-Württemberg
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a statutory foundation under public law, set up in 1976 under the Baden-Württemberg Naturschutzgesetz, which has backed more than 3,900 projects. Two streams, and the second is the one to understand. Ersatzzahlungen are the sums paid to the foundation as compensation for interventions in nature and landscape — and they are earmarked for practical conservation measures IN THE NATURRAUM THE INTERVENTION AFFECTED. So the money a developer paid for wrecking your area is legally tied to your area, and you can apply for it. WHO IT SUITS: unusually wide — charitable organisations, municipal bodies, universities, other organisations and PRIVATE INDIVIDUALS can all apply. Land purchase counts as a fundable project-related investment where it implements a measure. HOW IT DIFFERS: applications up to €50,000 are taken on a rolling basis and normally decided within three months; larger ones wait for the Stiftungsrat's cycle, so size your ask deliberately.

trackers.name: Stiftung NaturSchutzFonds Brandenburg
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the Land foundation whose statutory task is practical nature conservation, funded mainly by Ersatzzahlungen under § 15 BbgNatSchG — the sums paid by those who seal soil or erect wind turbines and masts — plus lottery proceeds. It steers that money back into the very districts where the damage was caused, and its council gives particular priority to projects in municipalities that took in Ersatzzahlungen from wind-energy impacts. So if a wind farm went up near you, there is money with your district's name on it. WHO IT SUITS: anyone. Any legal or natural person — district, municipality, private individual, association or society — may apply, and funding land purchase BY THIRD PARTIES is one of its three acquisition routes. Two constraints to plan around: land bought with Ersatzzahlung must have improvement potential the purchase can realise, so already-pristine ground does not qualify, and it will not fund recurring maintenance, anything you are legally obliged to do, or work already begun. HOW IT DIFFERS: its grants are recognised as your own contribution under EU, federal and Land schemes, so a euro from here can pull in roughly two and a half.

trackers.name: Stiftung Naturschutz Schleswig-Holstein (Stiftungsland)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a foundation under public law, created by the Land in 1978 and anchored in the Landesnaturschutzgesetz, whose statutory task is to secure land for nature conservation — and whose most important instrument, alongside long-term leasing, is outright purchase, because that is often the only way to hold a valuable biotope. It now holds over 35,000 hectares, more than one percent of the whole Land. The money for buying comes largely from levies and compensation payments, so it is the developer's mitigation money that funds it. USE IT: two doors, and the second is the one communities miss. You can sell or donate land to the foundation directly. But it ALSO funds the purchase of suitable land BY OTHER BODIES — municipalities and nature-conservation associations — so a parish council or a local Verein can be the buyer with the foundation paying. On peatland it has run a Klimapunkte model that buys rewetting rights rather than the land, priced on tonnes of CO2 avoided over thirty years and often paying more than a straight sale; ask whether it is currently open, as it began as a time-limited trial.

trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); MaDada — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Conservatoire du littoral — acquisition foncière (coastal land purchase)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a French public body that BUYS coastal and lakeshore land to protect it permanently — about 70% by negotiated purchase, 26% by pre-emption (right of first refusal, alongside the SAFER or the département), and rarely by expropriation. Land it acquires enters an inalienable public domain and cannot be sold on. In 2025 it covered roughly 750 sites and 203,762 hectares. USE IT: if the threatened land is near the coast or a large lake, the pre-emption right is the sharpest tool in France — alert them BEFORE a sale completes.

trackers.name: Fédération des Conservatoires d'espaces naturels (FCEN)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: the national federation (created 1988) of France's 23 Conservatoires d'espaces naturels — nature-protection associations whose whole method is MAÎTRISE FONCIÈRE ET D'USAGE: acquiring land, or securing use rights over it, to protect it. Together they hold or manage a network of more than 3,300 sites covering roughly 161,000 hectares, and since the Grenelle II law of 2010 they can be formally approved by the State and the regions. USE IT: to find the CEN covering your département via the federation's directory, and to propose a threatened site for acquisition or a long-term management agreement — the CENs also lease, not only buy, which can be faster than a purchase.

trackers.name: Terre de Liens — Foncière (citizen-funded farmland acquisition)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: buys farmland and farm buildings outright using citizen solidarity savings — shares from about €106, with a 25% tax reduction — and commits never to resell, permanently removing the land from speculation and leasing it to organic and peasant farmers. Backed by a network of regional associations across metropolitan France plus a public-utility foundation that accepts land donations. USE IT: if farmland near you is about to be sold to a developer, or you need land for a farming project — every acquisition is tied to an identified, assessed project, so bring the farmer as well as the parcel.

trackers.name: France Nature Environnement — fédération et pôle juridique
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the federation of roughly 9,000 French nature-protection associations, reconnue d'utilité publique since 1976, which litigates in its own name — it took the Water Framework Directive deterioration question to the CJEU and won, challenged the neonicotinoid derogation before the administrative courts, and has complained to the Aarhus Committee that France obstructs associations' access to justice. WHO IT SUITS: read this first if you are forming a group. Under article L. 600-1-1 of the Code de l'urbanisme, as amended by the ELAN law, an association can only challenge an urbanism authorisation if it filed its statutes at least ONE YEAR before the authorisation application was posted — so file now, not when the bulldozers appear. Its 46 member federations are also the route to a local ally already holding the agrément that carries standing.

trackers.name: SAFER — droit de préemption et veille foncière (Vigifoncier)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: holds two statutory powers over French rural land. A droit d'information under article L. 141-1-1 of the Code rural obliges the notaire to notify the SAFER of every transfer of rural property, land or farm — sale, gift, exchange or contribution to a company — at least two months before the final deed. A droit de préemption under article L. 143-1 then lets it buy in place of the original purchaser, resell at a state-approved price after a call for candidates, and attach a cahier des charges with environmental clauses that binds the new owner. USE IT: the early warning is the real prize. Notifications are published on the Vigifoncier portal, geolocated, with price, area, cadastral reference and the parties, and layers for water catchments, espaces naturels sensibles and wetlands. Access runs through collectivités that sign a veille foncière convention — so the route for a community group is via its commune, which can also stand as a candidate to buy. Individuals with a serious agricultural project can write to the departmental Conseiller Foncier while a notification is live. Two limits: pre-emption is exercised on only a small minority of notified sales, and purely forestry property is outside it.

Use the registry first to find the entity, then this to pierce the shell to the people who profit. — Holds to account: the hidden owners behind firms dealing with France’s government — find beneficial-owner filings.

Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in France.

trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); France Infogreffe (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in France — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in France.

HOW THIS DIFFERS: this shows the specific firms winning specific tenders and contracts — for aggregate budget totals use the open-data/statistics portal, and for findings of waste use the audit body. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in France, and for how much.

trackers.name: Droit de préemption ENS (DPENS) — departmental land acquisition
trackers.desc: THE STRONGEST LOCAL LAND-ACQUISITION TOOL IN FRANCE, and it exists in every département. Under articles L. 113-8 and following of the Code de l'urbanisme, a département runs an Espaces Naturels Sensibles policy and may create zones de préemption in which it holds a right of first refusal over any land put up for sale — it buys ahead of the developer at the sale rather than having to outbid or object afterwards. Article L. 142-2 allowed the funds to be used for acquisition by agreement, by expropriation, or by preemption. THE MONEY IS STANDING, NOT A GRANT ROUND: a dedicated departmental share of the taxe d'aménagement, capped at 2.5 percent, funds acquisition, development and management. Under L. 113-9 the département may delegate the preemption right to the Conservatoire du littoral, an établissement public foncier, the State or a commune. ACT INSIDE THE WINDOW: the département has 2 months to decide after a declaration of intention to sell — that is when a community must get to it, not after contracts. CONDITIONS AND LIMITS: land acquired must be opened to the public unless the site's fragility justifies otherwise, and needs a plan de gestion (L. 215-21); the département must keep a public register of preemption acquisitions and their actual use, which is worth requesting; and under L. 215-22 the former owner may demand the land back — the droit de rétrocession — if it has not been used as natural space within 10 years. Preemption zones must be displayed at the mairie and the hôtel du département for at least 1 month for the right to bite.

trackers.name: FDVA et appels à projets — money a small association can actually get
trackers.desc: THE FUND BUILT FOR SMALL GROUPS. The Fonds pour le développement de la vie associative has financed association functioning and innovative projects since 2018, and in principle all loi 1901 associations are eligible — no agrément, no minimum age, no sector restriction. In practice it goes where it is needed: about 80 percent of beneficiaries are associations run entirely by volunteers or with at most 2 employees. It runs 2 distinct annual calls, one for fonctionnement — rent, salaries, insurance — and one for innovative projects; funding core costs is rare among funders and is what keeps a campaign alive between projects. THE DEADLINE IS DEPARTMENTAL, NOT NATIONAL: calls and closing dates are published per department, so check yours. THE REST OF THE MAP: ADEME for ecological transition, circular economy, waste and air quality; DREAL, the ministry's regional relays, for biodiversity, protection of natural environments and climate adaptation; the 6 agences de l'eau, covering the whole territory, for river restoration, wetlands, water quality and awareness; and the collectivités territoriales. ONE TRAP: the Fondation du patrimoine's ecological strand is open to communes and intercommunalités holding protected areas, ENS or ZNIEFF type I and II sites — not to associations, so your commune would have to be the applicant.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: CNDP — the droit d'initiative, and one accredited association is enough
trackers.desc: THE ONLY INSTRUMENT IN THIS MAP THAT LETS RESIDENTS COMPEL A PARTICIPATION PROCESS ON A PROJECT THAT WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE NONE — everything else here is a right to object to a process already running. The CNDP, created by the loi Barnier of 2 February 1995, is an autorité administrative indépendante. THE DROIT D'INITIATIVE IS THE ROUTE: for a project subject to environmental assessment, below the CNDP's own thresholds but costing over 5 million euros, a demand goes through the préfet de département from any one of: adult EU nationals resident in the area numbering 20% of the project perimeter's population OR 10% of the department's or region's; one nationally accredited environmental association, or two associations, or an accredited federation; or a regional, departmental or municipal council or EPCI. NOTE THE SECOND LIMB — a single nationally accredited association is enough, with no population threshold at all. France Nature Environnement, recorded elsewhere in this map, is such a federation. That is by far the cheapest route and most communities do not know it exists. TIMING IS DECISIVE: ask as early as possible, with time to finish before the first authorisation application is filed — once the enquête publique opens, this route is closed. AND WATCH THE SILENCE RULE: the CNDP decides within two months, and absent an explicit decision it is DEEMED to have renounced — silence is refusal here, not consent. WHAT TO ASK THE GARANT FOR: the CNDP funds complementary expertise under L.121-1, at its own or the garant's request, and pays the garant's indemnity while the promoter finances the process — independent expertise not paid for by the promoter is the most valuable thing available here; ask for it by name. The garant conducts an independent study of context, prescribes the participation modalities, and issues a bilan with recommendations — but unlike a commissaire-enquêteur gives no personal opinion: expect a referee, not an ally. The statutory content must include alternative solutions, including not implementing the project. The CNDP does not take a position on whether a project should proceed. A LIVE THREAT: a draft decree of 4 December 2024 would remove industrial equipment from the CNDP's competence (deleting line 10 of R.121-2) expressly to accelerate such projects — mandatory saisine currently applies above 600 million euros. They could still get a garant-led concertation but not a débat public. Check the current R.121-2 before relying on mandatory saisine for an industrial project.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: France Nature Environnement — the legal network behind 6,000 local associations
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the federation's legal network, which links salaried and volunteer jurists across the whole country, in metropolitan France and overseas, to act on cases identified by local associations. The member associations together run in the order of a thousand contentious cases a year, and the network's stated aim is not symbolic or media litigation but having jurists distributed across the territory who can actually act on what local groups have found. WHAT IT HAS DONE THAT SHOWS THE METHOD: on the Aumelas wind farm it put protected-species law at the centre of a development argument, and on 30 November 2022 the Cour de cassation convicted EDF Energies Nouvelles for destroying lesser kestrels without the required administrative derogation while operating 41 turbines — the result of long mobilisation by the regional federation as much as the national one. On the Bure radioactive-waste repository it brought proceedings against the declaration of public utility together with 32 organisations and 30 residents. HOW TO USE IT: go to your departmental or regional FNE federation first, because that is where the jurists sit and where the case has to be identified. The national network exists to back what the local association brings it, not to replace it.

trackers.name: Bretagne Vivante — a regional legal service you can join (France)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Breton conservation association whose legal service devotes a substantial part of its work to litigation before both the administrative and the ordinary courts, to enforce the environmental code. Before the ordinary courts it most often claims reparation for environmental damage amounting to an offence — a different lever from an annulment action, and one communities rarely think of. THE UNUSUAL PART: it runs a regional legal group coordinated by its own jurist and made up of members, and when you join the association you can register your interest in the legal work. A resident with time and no legal training can end up inside the group that prepares these cases. Across thirty-nine batches this is the first organisation I have found that opens its legal function to its membership rather than treating law as something done to a community by professionals. SCOPE: Brittany and its biodiversity. If your fight is elsewhere in France the equivalent is your regional FNE federation — but the model is worth asking any regional association for by name: do you have a legal group, and can we be in it.

trackers.name: Fondation du patrimoine — runs the fundraising campaign for you (France)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES FOR YOU: it takes over the administrative, legal and tax side of a public appeal so the people running a local project can spend their time on the campaign itself. Local authorities, public bodies, non-profit associations and, under certain conditions, private individuals can ask it to launch a collecte de dons for a specific site, and donations are then tax-deductible for those who give. It supplies the donation forms and a project page on its own site, and it can add complementary money of its own through its network of patrons and partners on top of what the public gives. SET YOUR EXPECTATIONS FROM ITS OWN FIGURE: a collecte represents on average about 10% of a financing plan. This completes a funding round; it does not replace one. What it also does, and what several French communities have valued more, is gather people — residents, newcomers, visitors, local businesses — around a single named site, through the events run alongside the appeal. IT COVERS NATURAL HERITAGE, NOT ONLY BUILDINGS: it runs a programme dedicated to financing natural-heritage preservation and eco-renovation, its label extends to parks and gardens that are not classified monuments, and it has launched emergency collections for forests after fires. A threatened wood, park or garden is within scope, which most people assume it is not. HOW TO START: it works through departmental delegations with volunteers across the country, and the practical advice on its own pages is to approach the delegation covering your project. It also suggests creating or enlisting an association to carry the appeal — the same constituted-body requirement that decides applications elsewhere in this file. Note one exclusion it states: a private owner who has received the Fondation's label cannot then take the income-tax reduction on donations to the same works, and companies working on the restoration site cannot donate to it either.

trackers.name: Openpolis
trackers.desc: Independent Italian foundation liberating and curating public data on politicians, spending and power. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find open data on officials, votes and public money.

trackers.name: Camera – Register of Interest Representatives
trackers.desc: Italy's Chamber of Deputies register of lobbyists and interest representatives. — Holds to account: interest representatives at the Chamber of Deputies — find the register of lobbyists and their declared activity.

trackers.name: Italgiure (Corte di Cassazione)
trackers.desc: Official case-law database of the Italian Court of Cassation. · Find here: the Italian Court of Cassation's case-law system (ItalgiureWeb).

trackers.name: Corte di Cassazione – SentenzeWeb
trackers.desc: Free public archive of the last five years of civil & criminal Court of Cassation judgments — no registration. · Find here: the free public archive of recent Italian Court of Cassation judgments (SentenzeWeb).

trackers.name: Giustizia Amministrativa (Consiglio di Stato / TAR)
trackers.desc: Freely searchable decisions and opinions of the Council of State and Regional Administrative Tribunals. · Find here: the decisions of Italy's Council of State and Regional Administrative Tribunals.

trackers.name: Corte Costituzionale – Giurisprudenza
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court judgments from 1956 to present, freely searchable. · Find here: the judgments of Italy's Constitutional Court (1956–present).

trackers.name: Autorità Nazionale Anticorruzione (ANAC)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption / integrity authority.

trackers.name: Transparency International Italia
trackers.desc: Transparency International's Italy chapter (30+ years). Anti-corruption research, education and advocacy; runs an Advocacy and Legal Advice Centre (ALAC) for victims and witnesses of corruption; and helps citizens and organisations obtain public data.

trackers.name: FAI — Fondo per l'Ambiente Italiano (donate land or property)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: Italy's national trust, founded 1975 on the British National Trust model, which takes ownership or long-term concession of buildings, gardens and fragile natural habitats and protects them permanently, opening them to the public. It accepts land and property by donation in life, by bequest, or by concession, and runs its own conservation department. USE IT: if you own or can direct a threatened parcel — gifts and inheritances to FAI are exempt from succession and donation tax and from the imposta ipotecaria and catastale, so the whole value reaches the protection. Property that FAI cannot itself hold can be donated and sold to fund work elsewhere, so a non-scenic parcel is still worth offering. THE ARGUMENT THAT PERSUADES A LANDOWNER: FAI's first-ever property, in 1977, was just over 1,000 square metres of coastal land at Cala Junco on Panarea, given by the lawyer Piero Di Blasi expressly to avert a subdivision plan that would have irreparably disfigured the landscape — the very first gift FAI received was land donated to defeat a development, and at a thousand square metres, size is not the qualifying test. AND FOR AN OWNER WHO WILL NEITHER SELL NOR GIVE: 9 of FAI's 75 institutional properties (as at 31 December 2025) are held by concessione or comodato d'uso — a free loan-for-use where the owner keeps title and FAI takes on the care. IT HAS ALSO PUBLISHED WHAT IT WANTS: to increase the number and variety of its historic and natural properties in every region, particularly in the SOUTH and in major cities beginning with ROME — a published appetite for more property in a named region is an invitation.

trackers.name: Legambiente — Osservatorio Ambiente e Legalità / Ecomafia
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Italy's largest environmental association, which says plainly on its own legality page how it fights — by constituting itself parte civile in criminal trials, and by appealing to the regional administrative courts (TAR) and the Consiglio di Stato against unlawful and damaging administrative measures. It coined the term ecomafia in 1994 and publishes the annual Ecomafia report through its Osservatorio Ambiente e Legalità, which tracks the ciclo del cemento — abusivismo edilizio, illegal quarries, rigged public-works contracts — region by region and names the cases. WHO IT SUITS: a community facing illegal or corrupt construction, quarrying or waste dumping, where the route is a criminal prosecution you can attach to rather than a permit challenge you must bring alone.

trackers.name: Corte dei conti
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Italy, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Investigative Reporting Project Italy (IRPI)
trackers.desc: Italian investigative outfit tracing organized crime, corruption and illicit finance.

trackers.name: MASE VAS-VIA-AIA portal — national environmental assessment
trackers.desc: Italy's national VAS-VIA-AIA portal for state-competence environmental assessment and authorisation under Part Two of Legislative Decree 152/2006 (run by the environment ministry, now MASE; a platform migration is under way). You CAN get: technical documents for projects under national evaluation and the concluding acts issued since 1989, plus the 45-day public-comment windows. You CAN'T get: regional-competence procedures handled by the Regions. For activists: track a national project's file and file observations during the consultation window.

trackers.name: Acquisti in Rete PA (MEPA)
trackers.desc: Italy's central public-procurement marketplace. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Italy, and for how much.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Cassation
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Cassation — supreme court (Italy).

trackers.name: dati.gov.it
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Italy.

trackers.name: Italian Council of State
trackers.desc: Italian Council of State — administrative court (Italy).

trackers.name: ISTAT
trackers.desc: Italy's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Italy.

trackers.name: Registro Imprese
trackers.desc: Italy's official business register of companies and filings. — Holds to account: companies in Italy — find the business register of entities, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Register of Beneficial Ownership of Companies
trackers.desc: Register of Beneficial Ownership of Companies — Italy’s beneficial-ownership register, disclosing the real individuals who ultimately own or control companies. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A PLAIN COMPANY REGISTRY: this names the real HUMAN owners behind a company; a company registry names only the legal entity, its directors and filings. Use the registry first to find the entity, then this to pierce the shell to the people who profit. — Holds to account: the hidden owners behind firms dealing with Italy’s government — find beneficial-owner filings.

trackers.name: Art. 13 L. 349/1986 — recognition that carries standing to annul
trackers.desc: GET ON THE MINISTERIAL LIST AND STANDING COMES WITH IT. Associations recognised under article 13 of Law 349/1986 may, under article 18(5), intervene in environmental damage proceedings and appeal to the administrative courts for annulment of unlawful acts — standing conferred by law, not argued case by case. TO BE RECOGNISED: exist for at least 3 years, work in environmental protection, and be national in character or present in at least 5 regions — presence meaning member nuclei, a regional office and substantial activity across the region. The ministry assesses aims, democratic internal ordering under the statute, continuity of action and external relevance, and the criteria are cumulative, not alternative: fail one and recognition is refused. CHECK YOUR OWN POSITION: recognition covers the association and all branches governed by the same statute, but not affiliated or federated bodies with their own legal representative or a different statute.

trackers.name: How far that standing reaches — and the planning-law limit
trackers.desc: THE COURTS READ IT WIDELY. Standing under articles 13 and 18 covers environmental interests in the narrow sense and in the broad sense — conservation and enhancement of cultural property, the environment widely understood, urban, rural and natural landscape, monuments, historic centres and quality of life — grounded by the Council of State in the horizontal subsidiarity principle of article 118 of the Constitution. THE LIMIT, AND PLAN FOR IT: the legitimate interest in compliance with urban-planning and building rules belongs to specific, differentiated and qualified individuals, and recognised associations cannot assert it in their place — their special standing covers environmental interests, which are diffuse by nature. So run the association's environmental grounds alongside an affected neighbour's planning grounds. AND IF YOU ARE NOT ON THE LIST: the prevailing case law holds that listing creates no rigid automatism — a judge may admit an unlisted association after verifying its concrete representativeness, the so-called doppio binario. Committees, though, have been held to fall outside the article 13 category.

trackers.name: MASE sustainable development call — join the Forum as you apply
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY'S OWN CALL, open to non-profits based in Italy — associations, foundations, universities and research bodies whose activities are dedicated as a priority to sustainable development, under the Avviso pubblico for the National Sustainable Development Strategy. THE PREFERENCE THAT DECIDES WHO GETS THE MONEY: priority goes to proposals from organisations adhering to the Forum nazionale per lo Sviluppo Sostenibile — or that have applied to join by the date the proposal is sent. So joining is step one and can be done in parallel with the application, not years ahead. Submission is by certified email (PEC) to the address in the notice, by a fixed date and hour. REGISTER FIRST, THOUGH: most Italian third-sector funding runs through the RUNTS register — covering volunteering organisations, associazioni di promozione sociale, foundations with civic or social-utility purposes, philanthropic bodies and associative networks — and many regional calls admit only partnerships composed exclusively of ETS.

trackers.name: Where Italian environmental money actually comes from
trackers.desc: THE STANDING SOURCES. Fondazione Cariplo gives non-repayable contributions to third-sector organisations for cultural, social, environmental and research projects. Fondazione CON IL SUD runs environment calls for third-sector and volunteering organisations in Basilicata, Calabria, Campania, Puglia, Sardinia and Sicily — one Taranto call put EUR 970,000 into integrated environment-led development, requiring partnership with productive, institutional, university and research bodies. 5 per mille routes an annual contribution through taxpayers' income tax returns and is recurring, largely unrestricted income — rare enough to be worth registering for on its own; alongside it sit 8x1000, the Social Bonus and ordinary fundraising. If you have no grant experience, start at your local CSV (Centro di Servizio per il Volontariato), funded by the Fondo Unico Nazionale, which provides services and sometimes small local calls. TWO WARNINGS FROM ITALIAN SECTOR GUIDANCE: many bandi require co-financing — one large call sets a minimum 10 percent in cash — and money often arrives late, so you need a donations base to bridge the gap; and larger calls expect consolidated design experience with a budget, cronoprogramma and named territorial partners.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: SNPA — your regional agency, and the segnalazione that outperforms its programme
trackers.desc: CITIZEN REPORTS DROVE MORE THAN TWICE AS MANY INSPECTIONS AS THE AGENCY'S OWN PROGRAMME — and that comes from the agency's own published account. Arpa Toscana received 1,216 segnalazioni in 2019 from citizens acting individually or as organised groups, and in the reported period 346 accertamenti were carried out following a segnalazione against 160 programmed controls. That is the strongest argument in this map for making a formal report rather than assuming it will be ignored. WHERE TO SEND IT: every Italian region has its own agency — 19 regional ARPA plus the two provincial APPA of Trento and Bolzano, with ISPRA, forming SNPA under Legge 132/2016, operative since 14 January 2017. This link is SNPA's own directory of all 21 agency websites — find your region there. Each has an URP (public relations office) listed in the SNPA SI-URP section, and publishes both an ordinary email and a PEC address — in Italy a PEC is legally certified delivery, so use it where the report must be provable. KNOW THE FOUR OUTCOMES, BECAUSE ONE IS NOTHING: an inspection or notice of a programmed one; a request for support to your Comune to carry out preventive checks; a written reply based on the rules and existing knowledge; or archiviazione d'ufficio — filed without action. Controls are also triggered by an AIA permit's own terms, by local authorities, and on delegation from the Magistratura. THE SYSTEM-LEVEL POWER WORTH CITING: through the Consiglio SNPA the network gives a parere vincolante — a binding opinion — on Government measures of a technical nature, and may formally signal the opportunity for interventions, including legislative ones, for the reduction of consumo di suolo. Land take is named in its founding purpose. The agencies exist because the 1993 abrogative referendums stripped environmental control from the health service, moving it to ARPA/APPA under Legge 61/1994.

trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva.
