trackers.name: Rettslig klageinteresse — can your group appeal at all?
trackers.desc: SETTLE THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: the plan- og bygningsloven contains no provision on who may appeal decisions taken under it — it refers to the forvaltningsloven (pbl. § 1-9). Under forvaltningsloven § 28 a party to the case, and anyone else with rettslig klageinteresse (a legal interest in appealing), may appeal an individual decision. An environmental organisation that is not a party must establish that interest, and it is a legal standard requiring a concrete, discretionary assessment in every case, built from case law and theory rather than a checklist — so expect to argue it rather than assert it. WHAT THE GOVERNMENT CONFIRMS: the ordinary § 28 rules do not prevent environmental organisations from appealing an order to rectify (pålegg om retting) or a penalty decision (overtredelsesgebyr) — both are enkeltvedtak and both are appealable, and further clarity is expected to come through practice.

trackers.name: Miljøinformasjonsloven — what you can force out, and what you cannot
trackers.desc: USE IT, KNOWING THE EDGE: the environmental information law generally cannot be used to demand that new surveys or samples be carried out — but where information already exists in some form, the recipient has a duty to compile it so that it answers your questions. PRECEDENT WORTH CITING: Naturvernforbundet i Oslo og Akershus won a Supreme Court judgment on access to a forest owner's nature-value registrations, establishing that information must be delivered in a usable form — in practice written. Being invited to a single meeting where the material is shown once is not compliance, and that is the answer when an authority offers you a briefing instead of documents. You cannot use it to extract genuinely sensitive trade secrets of limited environmental relevance, such as mixing ratios or specific technical arrangements. RELATED RIGHT: under the forvaltningsloven public bodies must guide not only the parties but anyone else interested in the case, and ‘persons’ in Norwegian law includes legal persons — so a local association can simply ask the municipality for guidance on a plan affecting nature values.

trackers.name: Søknadssenter — Miljødirektoratet's grant schemes
trackers.desc: WHERE NORWEGIAN ENVIRONMENTAL MONEY IS APPLIED FOR: Miljødirektoratet's Søknadssenter carries the schemes in one place — support for voluntary climate and environment organisations, the pollution-area scheme, natural-science organisations, mapping and valuation of outdoor-recreation areas and route plans, and measures in state-secured outdoor recreation areas. CHECK THE THRESHOLD BEFORE YOU START: the headline scheme for voluntary climate and environment organisations requires more than 5,000 members (3,000 for children's and youth organisations), or a foundation of national significance — so a neighbourhood group does not qualify, and the realistic route is through a national organisation that does. Money there is paid as core operating support and allocated purely on objective criteria; grant size weighs activity level nationally and locally, the organisation's finances, its alternative funding options and its membership numbers. Some posts are earmarked to named recipients in the state budget (kap. 1420 post 77), which is worth knowing before investing effort. TIMING AND MECHANICS: forms generally open around 1 December and are closed outside the window — the pollution-area deadline was 15 January 2026. You need ID-porten to apply. Recipients are followed up on delivery and use of funds, documentation must be kept 5 years from 1 January of the application year, and organisations must report unprompted anything affecting their grant. Help: esshjelp@miljodir.no, 951 23 500.

trackers.name: Frivillig skogvern — the owner offers, the state pays, tax-free
trackers.desc: THE MECHANISM THAT INVERTS WHO STARTS: the forest owner offers an area for protection against compensation, instead of the state designating and the owner resisting. If it has the natural qualities and the authorities accept, it becomes a naturreservat under the Nature Diversity Act — bound for all time, with forestry no longer permitted. THE TERMS ARE BETTER THAN MOST CONSERVATION SALES ANYWHERE: compensation is a tax-free lump sum based on the value of forestry in the area, with the state paying interest from the day the owner signs until payment; the owner keeps freehold title and keeps hunting, fishing and grazing rights — only the right to conduct forestry is given up; and the owner may withdraw at any time until the compensation agreement is signed. Forest owner organisations give free advice and act as the owner's negotiating party against the state's valuation. PROCESS: biologists carry out a bioregistrering of the area's qualities (if the values are insufficient it ends there), then valuation, an offer, public consultation, and adoption by the King in Council — typically about 3 years. Where the area lies in reindeer grazing land the local reindeer grazing district must be consulted. SCALE: piloted in 2003 after the conflict-heavy processes of the 1980s and 90s, first 8 areas protected in 2005, and since then this has been the only route by which privately owned forest is protected — past 1,000 forest areas by June 2025, reaching 5.4 percent of all Norwegian forest and 4.2 percent of productive forest.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Frivillig vern — the forest-owners' co-operatives that run it for the owner (Norway)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: since 2005, protection of privately owned forest in Norway has happened one way only — the owner offers the ground, and their regional forest-owners' co-operative runs the whole process for them. Norges Skogeierforbund coordinates it with Miljødirektoratet; the co-operatives doing the work include AT Skog, Viken Skog, ALLSKOG and FramTre, several of them at it since 2002. They advise the owner free of charge, handle the delineation, commission the timber valuation, and negotiate the state's compensation offer on the owner's behalf. It began as a 2003 pilot and the first eight areas became nature reserves in 2005. USE IT: this is the offer to put in front of a landowner who has a buyer, and four facts decide it. The owner can withdraw at any point up to signature, so putting ground forward commits them to nothing. The compensation is exempt from capital-gains tax. The owner keeps ownership, hunting, fishing and grazing rights — and gets no compensation for them, because the payment covers forestry value only, which is also the answer to anyone claiming protection ends all use of the land. And the ecological survey that decides whether the ground qualifies, the bioregistrering, is commissioned by the conservation authorities rather than paid for by the owner. Be clear what these bodies are: forest-owners' co-operatives, part of the timber sector, acting for the owner and not for a community — which is exactly why an owner will take a meeting with them.

trackers.name: Fjellstyrene and Norges Fjellstyresamband — local boards holding rights over 26.6 million dekar
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY ARE: under the fjellov, every municipality containing a statsallmenning must have a fjellstyre, appointed by the municipal council but not a municipal body, which administers the use of rights and benefits in that common — summer farming, grazing, hunting and fishing. There are 93 to 94 of them. Norges Fjellstyresamband, at Stortingsgata 30, 0161 Oslo, nfs@fjellstyrene.no, is their joint organisation, funded by member subscriptions and a statutory contribution from the landowner fund. THE SCALE: the statsallmenninger of southern and central Norway total 26.6 million dekar. Norway had no acquirer in this file, and this is why the question was the wrong one — over much of the Norwegian mountains the relevant thing is not who owns the ground but who holds and administers the use rights on it, and that is a local board. THE THREE-WAY SPLIT A NORWEGIAN COMMUNITY NEEDS TO KNOW: Statskog SF holds the landowner right; the allmenningsstyre administers timber rights and, unlike the fjellstyre, is elected by and from among the rights-holders themselves; and the fjellstyre administers the other common rights including hunting and fishing. Where there is no allmenningsstyre, Statskog administers the timber right. Approach the right one of the three for your question. WHY THE RIGHTS MATTER BEYOND THE INDIVIDUALS HOLDING THEM: the Fjellstyresamband's own framing is that alongside their value as recreation areas for the whole country, the villages' collective rights in these areas are decisive for maintaining viable rural communities. Rights of use vary between commons and change over time; grazing, summer farming, hunting, trapping and fishing are the important ones today. WHAT THE FEDERATION WILL DO: act as the link between individual fjellstyrer and public authorities, guide them on particular questions, and give opinions to public authorities, private organisations and others on the basis of the fjellov's purpose. ONE THING IN MOTION: a government-appointed committee worked from 2016 to 2018 on a new fjellov, and NOU 2018:11 proposed one; as of May 2026 the proposal was reported to be with the department. The framework may change.

trackers.name: The six Norwegian associations that hold and defend appeal rights — and how to reach them
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST, and they act together: in a joint consultation response on the new Norwegian public administration act, six organisations welcomed the bill stating clearly that an association or foundation has a right of appeal where the decision lies within its purpose or natural field of activity. They are Den Norske Turistforening, Friluftsrådenes Landsforbund, Naturvernforbundet, Norges Jeger- og Fiskerforbund, Norsk Friluftsliv and Sabima. For a Norwegian community, that list is the set of national bodies with the standing to appeal on outdoor recreation, nature and species — and they are demonstrably willing to act jointly. Match your ground to the one whose purpose covers it. WHY STANDING IS THE WHOLE QUESTION IN NORWAY: the planning and building act contains no provision on who may appeal decisions made under it; it refers to the public administration act, under which parties and others with rettslig klageinteresse — legal interest in appealing — may appeal. For an environmental organisation that is not a party, the department's own interpretation is that whether it has that interest requires a concrete overall assessment in each individual case, on a legal standard developed through practice and theory. So it is arguable, not automatic. And if a body is found not to have it, that refusal is itself a decision which can be appealed. WHERE AN APPEAL GOES: municipalities do the area planning and grant building permissions; the Statsforvalteren is the appeal body for building cases and for cases concerning zoning plans, and takes a wholly fresh look at the case — it may consider new circumstances and may raise matters that do not concern the appellant at all. It also is not bound by the municipality's view that the conditions for hearing the appeal were met. Note the stopping rule: once the appeal body has decided, the administrative route is exhausted, and going further means a lawsuit or the Sivilombudet. AND A PRACTICAL POINT ON DEFECTIVE APPEALS: where an appeal has errors or gaps the municipality must guide the appellant under its general duty to advise, and the appeal should not be rejected outright — a short deadline for correction may be given instead.

trackers.name: Sabima — the biological societies, and money to survey the species on your ground
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: the umbrella organisation for Norway's biological societies, working to stop the loss of natural diversity, with 15 staff. Its member societies are the specialist bodies a community actually needs: Norsk Botanisk Forening, Norges sopp- og nyttevekstforbund, Norsk Zoologisk Forening and Norsk entomologisk forening — plants, fungi, animals and insects. It invites people with an interest in a biological field to join one. THE OFFER THAT MATTERS MOST, AND IT IS MONEY: each year Sabima distributes funds, on behalf of its member societies, to associations and members who carry out voluntary species mapping. There is an annual call. If your ground needs its species recorded and nobody will pay for a survey, this is a Norwegian route to funded fieldwork — and the file has repeatedly found that a survey is what turns a community's claim into evidence. AND VOLUNTEERS ALREADY DO MOST OF IT: more than half of all species mapping in Norway is carried out by voluntary mappers, who record findings in Artsobservasjoner, run by Artsdatabanken — and those records become immediately available to the administration, researchers and others working with species occurrences. A record made today is in the system the authorities consult. That is the cheapest evidence-creation route in this entire file. IT ALSO PUBLISHES ITS SURVEY NOTES: reports from mapping activity funded through those grants are published on its site, tagged by place and by subject — red-listed species, alien species, deciduous woodland, calcareous forest and so on. Check whether your area is already covered. WHY IT ENGAGES WITH MUNICIPALITIES, in its own framing: land-use change is the largest cause of species extinction, and many of the decisions to carry out interventions in nature are made in the municipalities, which need better competence on nature and on the consequences of losing biodiversity. It works on forest protection, mires and peat extraction, cultural landscape, alien species, sea and coast, and municipal nature management, and publishes its consultation responses.

trackers.name: Naturskyddsföreningen — talerätt och kretsar
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Sweden's largest environmental association, founded 1909, and the practical route to the statutory right of appeal. Under 16 kap. 13 § miljöbalken a non-profit association whose statutes give it the purpose of protecting nature or the environment may appeal decisions granting permits, approvals and dispensations under the Environmental Code — but the section sets minimum thresholds for membership and years of operation that exclude most local groups in practice. WHO IT SUITS: a neighbourhood group that does not itself qualify. The association's kretsar and länsförbund do, and there is case law where a länsförbund took over a local krets's action by power of attorney after the krets was found to fall short. trackers.name: LONA — Lokala naturvårdssatsningen (local nature-conservation grant)
trackers.desc: THE STANDING LOCAL GRANT, under Förordning (2003:598). Money comes from Naturvårdsverket and the länsstyrelse decides which projects get it. Ordinary LONA covers up to 50 percent of costs for nature conservation, outdoor recreation and public health, and its stated purpose covers both kommuner and ideella föreningar. THE CATCH THAT DECIDES EVERYTHING: only a kommun can apply. Projects may be initiated and run by associations, landowners or private individuals, but the kommun is always legally and financially responsible for delivery and reporting — so your first move is to contact the LONA-ansvarig at your kommun, or failing that at the länsstyrelse, well before the deadline, and expect an agreement between your association and the kommun if it succeeds. TIMING: kommuner normally submit by 1 December for projects starting the next year (it varies, and extra rounds happen); decisions usually come in spring; annual reports by 1 March, final report within 3 months of project end. CHECK STATUS FIRST — IT IS BUDGET-DEPENDENT: Naturvårdsverket states no new ordinary LONA projects are being approved at present except for vandringsleder and ängs- och betesmarker, with only ongoing projects completed in 2026 because of the budget situation. Targeted rounds can be far more generous — an extra wetland round spread about 12 million kronor across 17 län at up to 90 percent of costs. AND IT IS MONEY, NOT PERMISSION: a LONA decision does not release anyone from other law on consultation, permits and dispensations.

trackers.name: Sök bidrag — other Swedish grants for a local group
trackers.desc: SMALLER MONEY YOU CAN APPLY FOR DIRECTLY, which matters because LONA must go through your kommun. Alvins fond: Naturvårdsverket decides grants for projects promoting Swedish nature protection, especially bird protection — apply by 30 November each year. Grannskapsinitiativet from Postkodsstiftelsen: an ideell förening or public-benefit foundation can apply for 20,000–60,000 kronor. The page also routes you to LONA through your kommun. USE IT: these are the routes open to an association in its own name, on its own timetable.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Naturarvet — buys old-growth forest ahead of the felling plan (Sweden)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Swedish insamlingsstiftelse whose sole purpose is raising money to buy gammelskog — old forest with high conservation value — and hold it permanently. Its founding observation is the one to quote at a Swedish council: only a very small share of Sweden's forest is old-growth, half of what remains has no secure protection, and it is being felled faster than it is being protected. USE IT: the Djupsjöån purchase is a template worth reading in full, because it shows a community how a buy can be committed before the money exists. A forest management plan of August 2023 proposed felling 50 hectares of the old forest within two years — that document is the clock, and it is the thing to go and find. The property came up for sale; Naturarvet signed the contract and paid the deposit in May 2024 on the strength of earlier large gifts and an autumn-and-spring appeal, borrowed 4 million kronor from private lenders to cover the rest, and the state paid out 4 million kronor that September to clear the loans, with further financing following from the county administrative board on a nature-reserve decision. The sequence is buy first, designate after, and bridge the gap with private lending against the expected state money. THE CHEAP ENTRY POINT: donors buy a named umbrella tree or a forest square identified by coordinates, so anyone can visit the exact patch they paid for — a campaign shape that builds a constituency rather than a donor list.

trackers.name: Allmännings- och besparingsskogar — commonly owned forests, and their federation (Sweden)
trackers.desc: WHAT THEY ARE: commonly owned forests in Norrbotten and Dalarna, formed in the second half of the 1800s — the Dalarna besparingsskogar through the storskifte land reform, the Norrbotten allmänningsskogar through the avvittring of crown land to local farmers — and governed by the Act on common forests in Norrland and Dalarna. They were created precisely because timber companies had begun buying up forests and whole farms and the state feared the farmers would sell their land. The commons were the protection against that, and they still are. THE SCALE AND WHERE TO LOOK: their federation, Sveriges Allmänningsskogars Förbund, publishes a list of every allmänning and besparingsskog with its area and ownership. Examples from it: Jokkmokk's allmänning at around 81,000 hectares; Arjeplog's at over 40,000; Arvidsjaur's, formed 1877, owned in common by the owners of assessed properties in the municipality — about 32,000 hectares with some 1,600 co-owners; other commons with around 3,000 co-owners across some 1,500 properties. Reported totals for the allmänning and association forests run to around 670,000 hectares. WHY A SWEDISH COMMUNITY SHOULD CHECK: ownership goes with the property, not with a subscription. If your farm or house is an assessed property in one of these municipalities you may already be a delägare, entitled to attend the jordägarstämma — the landowners' meeting, held twice a year in Älvdalen — and to vote on how the forest is run. That is standing you already have. TWO FEATURES THAT MATTER FOR PROTECTING LAND: the statutory objective is even and good yield in perpetuity, with felling calculations made roughly every ten years, and Älvdalen's besparingsskog states sustainable forestry and preserving biological diversity as further aims. And the money is locked to land: if the besparingsskog receives money from selling a property it must use it to buy new forest. Rather than a cash dividend, the return goes back to the delägare and the district as grants, many tied to agriculture and forestry. BE CLEAR ABOUT THE POLITICS: the federation describes part of its purpose as giving these forests a voice as a consultee to the state and as a counterweight to the environmental lobby. It is a forest-owning interest, not a conservation body.

trackers.name: Naturskyddsföreningen i Stockholm — länsförbund
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Naturskyddsföreningen länsförbund for Stockholm — the county tier of Sweden's largest environmental association, an association in its own right with its own board, whose stated job is to support the local kretsar and to watch and influence nature and environment questions in its own county. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: under 16 kap. 13 § miljöbalken the right to appeal permits, approvals and dispensations is limited by membership and years-of-operation thresholds that most neighbourhood groups fail. The länsförbund clears them. There is case law of a länsförbund taking over a local krets's action by power of attorney after the krets fell short. WHO IT SUITS: a local group in Stockholm that has found a problem but cannot itself get standing — bring it here rather than filing alone and being dismissed. It also coordinates the kretsar in the county, so it can tell you which local group already covers your municipality.

trackers.name: SAOS – Court Judgment Analysis System
trackers.desc: Open database aggregating judgments of Polish common, administrative and supreme courts. · Find here: a free system aggregating and analysing Polish court judgments (SAOS).

trackers.name: Pracownia na rzecz Wszystkich Istot (Workshop for All Beings)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Polish association that has spent since 1990 forcing its way into administrative proceedings and winning — a civil suit against Lasy Państwowe over the Białowieża Forest logging, brought under art. 323 of the environmental protection act, produced an interim order banning felling in the most valuable fragments; the Gliwice administrative court confirmed its right to be a party in the environmental proceeding for a Pilsko chairlift; the Kraków court fined a building inspectorate for a 54-month delay over an illegally expanded resort. Publishes 'Paragrafy dla przyrody', a watchers' handbook on joining a proceeding as a party and appealing the decision. WHO IT SUITS: a group facing a road, ski lift, resort or logging plan that needs standing first and arguments second.

trackers.name: Klub Przyrodników — wykup gruntów i tworzenie rezerwatów
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: buys ecologically valuable ground and then gets the state to protect it — land it purchased was, on the Klub's own application, given nature-reserve status, which is the whole sequence a community needs and the reason this is more than a land trust. It has been buying since close to its founding: xerothermic grassland at Owczary, land in the Obra valleys, then peatlands and grasslands scattered across the country from the Odra to the Rospuda, passing 150 hectares owned or co-owned, latterly with WWF Polska under a privately-protected-areas programme. USE IT: two doors. If a parcel is for sale, this is the buyer of last resort for peatland, fen and dry grassland in particular. And its current programme exists precisely to bring local organisations, activists and enthusiasts into the creation of NEW nature reserves, working from a database of sites that qualify for reserve protection — so if your site is good enough, the route is to get it onto that list rather than to fight the development on its own terms.

trackers.name: Central Register of Beneficial Owners (CRBO)

trackers.name: WFOŚiGW — your statute wording is the eligibility gate
trackers.desc: APPLY REGIONALLY, NOT NATIONALLY. NFOŚiGW is central and has no regional branches; the 16 voivodeship funds (WFOŚiGW) are where a local association realistically applies. THE CLAUSE THAT DECIDES ELIGIBILITY: the offer is addressed to bodies with a provision in their statute and/or KRS entry stating that the organisation's purpose is environmental protection and/or ecological education. Your constitution is the gate — amend it before there is a dispute, as in Finland and Italy. TERMS: grants and loans with preferential interest, the possibility of partial write-off of loan capital, and no fees or commissions; a dotacjo-pożyczka can top a grant up to 100 percent of net eligible costs. A recorded window ran grants 1 February to 29 March, loans to 31 December or until funds ran out. FUNDABLE WORK includes preparing protection plans for areas protected under the 2004 Nature Conservation Act, and removal of invasive alien species.

trackers.name: Gdańsk WFOŚiGW rules — continuous intake, and two exclusions
trackers.desc: BETTER TERMS THAN MOST OF THIS MAP, IF YOU AVOID TWO TRAPS. The Gdańsk fund receives applications continuously and considers them at least once a quarter — no single annual window — and funding may reach 100 percent of eligible costs for ecological education and nature protection tasks, and in special cases for public finance bodies and NGOs. THE TWO EXCLUSIONS: it does not finance completed tasks, so do not start the work first; and it does not fund tasks that have already received foreign funding, including EU funds, so do not plan to stack it on an EU grant. NATIONAL CALLS ADMIT NGOs TOO: an Eastern Poland biodiversity call ran 13 November to 29 February with a budget of PLN 12.5 million, open to NGOs, local government, forest and water managers and education bodies — while a PLN 110 million call for national park education infrastructure was non-competitive because only 9 parks could apply. Some support is aimed explicitly at social dialogue and resolving conflicts over nature protection.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. trackers.name: Justice & Environment — a public-interest environmental lawyer in your country
trackers.desc: A LAWYER YOU CAN ACTUALLY GET, IN YOUR COUNTRY, WHO ALREADY DOES THIS WORK. ITS THREE PRIORITY ISSUES ARE EXACTLY WHAT A LAND CASE TURNS ON: the Aarhus Convention, environmental impact assessment, and Natura 2000. THE THING TO ASK FOR BY NAME: the ATOJ-EARL project, led by ClientEarth and coordinated by J&E with EU LIFE support, produced a public-interest lawyer database regrouping lawyers active in environmental law — precisely what a community searching for an attorney needs — covering Austria, Estonia, France, Germany, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Spain. Check the current membership.

trackers.name: Fundacja Frank Bold — takes your case to its legal team (Poland)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a public-interest legal foundation in Kraków, ul. Skłodowskiej-Curie 4/3, which asks you to submit a specific case to its legal team through a form on its site. Its published record is about stopping mines, and the numbers are concrete. Its arguments helped persuade the General Directorate for Environmental Protection to refuse the environmental decision for the planned Złoczów lignite mine, which it records as sparing 33 villages and 3,000 residents from displacement. Working with residents and councillors of the Gubin and Brody communes it helped bring the investor to abandon a lignite mine there. It supported local farmers facing an opencast lignite mine, and residents of Imielin. It was among the organisations that challenged the environmental decision for the Turów mine, where the court suspended that decision pending a full hearing. IT ALSO RUNS AN ADVICE LINE: it opened a free legal advice service aimed specifically at informal local groups, activists and NGOs facing harmful industrial air pollution, with a short verification form as the way in. If your fight is with an existing plant rather than a proposed one, that is the door. WHAT TO BRING: it works at the scale of environmental decisions, concessions and industrial permits. A single house extension is not its case; a mine, a plant or a road is.

trackers.name: Kancelaria Radców Prawnych Frank Bold — the fee-charging firm, and its conflict (Poland)
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL: the associated law firm, a team of legal advisers specialising in environmental protection and corporate responsibility. Its own list of services is unusually precise about what it will do for a resident: represent people exposed to the harmful effects of neighbouring investments, in administrative proceedings and in civil claims for nuisance; help local communities take part in environmental proceedings for schemes planned next to them; help NGOs join administrative proceedings; prepare legal analyses and opinions; and in criminal matters draft notifications of an offence, draft indictments, and represent private, subsidiary and auxiliary prosecutors. It states plainly that it does not act as defence counsel. READ THIS BEFORE YOU WRITE: the same firm advises individuals, companies and local authorities on planning and delivering renewable energy investments — checking a scheme against the local spatial plan, supporting investors in administrative proceedings, and drafting the lease agreements, transmission easements and connection contracts behind them. That is on its own services page. If you are fighting a wind or solar scheme, name the developer, the site and the consenting authority in your first email and ask directly whether the firm is free to act for you. WHICH ONE DO YOU NEED: the foundation takes public-interest cases; this is the commercial practice. Ask the foundation first, and let it tell you which of the two your case belongs to.

trackers.name: Fundusz Partnerstwa — Polish Environmental Partnership Foundation
trackers.desc: WHAT THE CONSORTIUM IS: the Environmental Partnership Association, headquartered in Brno, is a consortium of six independent national foundations in central and eastern Europe that give grants to community projects protecting the environment. It grew out of a programme begun in 1990 by the C.S. Mott Foundation, the German Marshall Fund and the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, and the national foundations were established as independent bodies in the early 1990s. Alongside grants they run education programmes, provide professional services and build the capacity of civic initiatives — which is the part a new local group needs most. THE POLISH MEMBER: Fundusz Partnerstwa, the Polish foundation of the consortium, founded 2004 and the youngest of the six, at ffp.org.pl. Poland already has a land buyer and a legal ally in this file; this is the missing funder. SOURCING: the consortium and its six national foundations are documented on the Environmental Partnership Association's own site; the national figures and founding dates come from consortium and partner material rather than each foundation's own pages. Confirm current grant rounds with the national foundation directly.

trackers.name: OTOP — buys and leases land, and fights the road (Poland)

Karsiborska Kępa was its first and is an active-management social reserve rather than a closed strict one. WHAT IT BRINGS TO A CASE. It coordinates the Monitoring of Polish Birds programme commissioned by the Chief Inspectorate of Environmental Protection — so the national bird dataset runs through it. ITS RECORD ON INFRASTRUCTURE: one of its activists co-organised the campaign defending the Rospuda valley against the Via Baltica expressway and won the Goldman Environmental Prize in 2010. Its current campaign tags include opposition to the E40 waterway and river protection work. This is an organisation with a proven record of stopping a road through a wetland. HOW TO WORK WITH IT: it recruits volunteers whose tasks it describes as requiring specialist knowledge of ornithology, law or ecology as well as general help, and it runs monitoring training. trackers.name: RUTI – Unique Register of Interest Transparency
trackers.desc: Romania's public register listing decision-makers' meetings with interest representatives. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: ROLII
trackers.desc: Romanian Legal Information Institute: free access to Romanian court decisions. · Find here: free Romanian case-law and legislation (ROLII).

trackers.name: Ia Statul la Întrebări — FOI requests (ROU)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Ia Statul la Întrebări — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is the Bankwatch Association. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on the Bankwatch Association's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS Bankwatch Association Romania (bankwatch.ro) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: Bankwatch Association (Asociaţia Bankwatch România)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Romania's member organisation in the Justice and Environment network of European environmental-law NGOs, and the Romanian arm of the CEE Bankwatch tradition of scrutinising internationally financed projects. WHO IT SUITS: communities affected by a project with public or development-bank money behind it, where the financing itself is the pressure point; the network does not state what casework it takes, so ask. Domain unverified this session — reach them through the member list on justiceandenvironment.org. Founded by the CEE Bankwatch Network (15 member organisations across 13 countries in Central and Eastern Europe). trackers.desc: Romania supreme audit institution

trackers.desc: Romanian investigative group probing organized crime, corruption and money networks.

trackers.desc: Bucharest Court of Appeal — appellate court in Romania (Wikidata record).

trackers.desc: High Court of Cassation and Justice — supreme court in Romania (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: AFM Biodiversitate — funding, but you must be a custodian first
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL FUND, AND NGOs ARE NAMED BENEFICIARIES. AFM is Romania's main source of financial support for environmental projects, built on the polluter pays and producer responsibility principles and financed entirely from its own revenues. Its Biodiversitate programme lists non-governmental organisations among beneficiaries, alongside administrative-territorial units, public institutions, museums, public research institutes, accredited universities and economic operators — where they hold the status of custode-administrator. SO THE ORDER MATTERS: get the custody contract first, and the funding follows. County environmental protection agencies may apply instead for protected areas that need no administration structure and are not assigned in custody, as may administrators of wildlife rehabilitation centres.

trackers.name: Custodie of a protected area — and who now issues the aviz
trackers.desc: AN NGO CAN BECOME THE CUSTODIAN OF A PROTECTED AREA. Under OUG 57/2007 on the regime of protected natural areas, with the methodology for assigning areas in administration and custody approved by Ordin 1052/2014, protected areas are administered directly or through partnership and administration contracts — the door for a civil society organisation. A quarter of Romania's territory is protected natural area; the Danube Delta has its own separate administration. CUSTODY IS REVIEWED, NOT PERMANENT: there is a formal commission for evaluation, transfer and takeover of areas assigned in custody, and periodic monitoring and evaluation of administrators. CHECK WHO ISSUES THE AVIZ BEFORE OBJECTING TO A PROJECT: ANANP, created in 2016, issued the opinion required for works interfering with protected areas as part of the environmental agreement documentation — but the government decided by emergency ordinance to merge ANANP into ANPM, and the environment ministry acknowledged that approving projects will be easier while saying legal rigour would hold. Critics argue reforming ANANP would have been preferable, since investments touching protected areas previously required a separate special opinion.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. trackers.name: Foundation Conservation Carpathia — buys forest to stop it being logged (Romania)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a foundation established in 2009 by Christoph and Barbara Promberger which buys forest and alpine meadow in the Făgăraș Mountains and takes hunting rights out of circulation, funded with private and public money. It has bought and restored more than 1,991 hectares of clear-cuts, alpine pasture and spruce monoculture, planted over 4.1 million saplings, built nine tree nurseries, and done erosion control on more than 30 kilometres of old tractor tracks. Over 8,000 hectares of what it holds are now non-intervention zones in the Făgăraș Natura 2000 management plan or core areas of Piatra Craiului National Park. USE IT: it keeps buying forest that comes onto the market specifically to stop it being logged, so a Romanian community that knows a block is about to be sold has somewhere to send that information before the sale rather than after the felling. It publishes what the work costs, which almost nobody does: €2.10 to plant a sapling including one to four years of care, and €60 per hectare to protect forest and wildlife. Those are the numbers to put in a local appeal, because they turn an abstract cause into an amount. Its restoration work employs an average of 200 seasonal workers hired from the surrounding communities. KNOW THE POLITICS BEFORE YOU ALIGN WITH IT: the foundation is contested in the Făgăraș region. It is largely financed by foreign philanthropists, its stated goal is a national park, and Romanian landowners' representatives and local press have run sustained criticism of a foreign-funded body accumulating Carpathian land. The foundation's own answer is that the holdings are meant to return to the Romanian public domain as a national park rather than stay with it. A community in that region should expect the association to be used against it, and decide with that in view.
