THE ROMANIAN MEMBER: Fundația pentru Parteneriat, founded 1998, at repf.ro. Romania has a substantial forest buyer in this file and no funder; this fills that. Note the practical pairing — a Romanian community that has found a block of forest coming up for sale needs both the buyer and the money to do the survey and the campaign around it. SOURCING: the consortium and its six national foundations are documented on the Environmental Partnership Association's own site; the national figures and founding dates come from consortium and partner material rather than each foundation's own pages. Confirm current grant rounds with the national foundation directly.

trackers.name: Fundația ADEPT Transilvania — makes the grassland pay so it stays grassland
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a biodiversity conservation and rural development NGO founded 2004 at Str. Principală 166, Saschiz, Mureș, +40 265 711 635, office@fundatia-adept.org, working the Târnava Mare region of southern Transylvania in the triangle between Sibiu, Sighișoara and Brașov — one of the most important High Nature Value farmland landscapes in continental Europe. Its own framing is that it protects those landscapes by working with and supporting the small-scale farming communities that created them and maintain them, giving them an economic future rather than a restriction. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DELIVERED, WHICH IS WHY IT IS HERE: its field surveys of habitats and species led to the area being included in the EU's Natura 2000 network. In 2011 it designed new national measures protecting grazed orchards and damp grasslands that had no protection until then, with the result that farmers managing 400,000 hectares of those two habitats became eligible for payment for good management. It has advised the Romanian ministry on agri-environment scheme design and worked with the European Commission's agriculture and environment directorates-general. An organisation that got a habitat type into the national payment system is an organisation that can tell you whether your grassland already qualifies for something. WHAT IT CAN BRING TO A THREATENED SITE: habitat, species and land-use mapping including landscape features; identification of High Nature Value grassland and of indicator species for judging condition; local management plans co-designed with small-scale land managers; and concrete restoration on the ground, with baseline and annual species monitoring. It is also developing a biodiversity-credit results-based payment scheme in Târnava Mare intended to pay farmers for nature-friendly management and reduce the pressure to expand agriculture. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a law firm. It works through cooperation with farmers and ministries rather than opposition, so bring it a grassland that needs an economic case and a management plan, not a confrontation. Romania's file entries now cover the forest buyer, the funder and this — the farmed landscape. ONE DISCREPANCY: its own pages give the founding year as 2004; a major funder's grantee page says 2014. Take 2004, which appears throughout its own site and history.

trackers.name: Agency for Prevention of Corruption
trackers.desc: Serbia's anti-corruption agency, handling officials' asset declarations. Also maintains the public Registers of Lobbyists & Legal Entities Engaged in Lobbying under the 2018 Law on Lobbying. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers, top officials & cabinet, officials handling public money & power — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held; their assets, interests and integrity declarations; corruption cases, sanctions and integrity data.

trackers.name: Commissioner for Information of Public Importance (Serbia)
trackers.desc: Serbia's independent commissioner enforcing access to public information and personal-data protection. — Holds to account: public bodies that hold records — find information-commissioner decisions and appeals.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Serbia
trackers.desc: Official site of Serbia's apex court publishing decisions and case-law positions. · Find here: information and judgments of the Supreme Court of Serbia.

trackers.name: Commissioner for Information of Public Importance and Personal Data Protection
trackers.desc: Serbia's independent state body enforcing the Law on Free Access to Information of Public Importance — handling appeals against public authorities that deny information and overseeing implementation.

trackers.name: Transparency Serbia (Transparentnost Srbija)
trackers.desc: Transparency International's Serbia chapter. Monitors implementation of anti-corruption legislation and works on access to information, political and campaign finance, public procurement, budget transparency and conflict-of-interest at central and local level.

trackers.name: RERI — Regulatorni institut za obnovljivu energiju i životnu sredinu
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Belgrade organisation that fights Serbian developments through the courts rather than the press. In 2025 alone it filed suit to annul the consent given to the environmental impact study for the National Football Stadium, and lodged a criminal complaint against the mining company Zijin over pollution — the two routes it uses most, administrative challenges to EIA consents and permits, and criminal complaints where a company is causing measurable harm. It has also succeeded in getting a government decision on the scope of an EIA quashed by the Administrative Court, which is the pressure point when a project is artificially split into pieces too small to require a proper assessment. WHO IT SUITS: communities facing mining, energy or large infrastructure, especially where the paperwork is the weak spot. It is a small team taking strategic cases, not a general advice service, so bring the decision you want overturned and the date it was published.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Serbia
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of Serbia — supreme court (Serbia).

trackers.name: Serbian Open Data Portal
trackers.desc: National — Serbian government open data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Serbia.

trackers.name: Portal javnih nabavki
trackers.desc: Serbia's public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Serbia, and for how much.

trackers.name: APR (Business Registers Agency)
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Central Records of Beneficial Owners
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Center for Investigative Journalism of Serbia (CINS)
trackers.desc: Serbian center reporting on corruption and public-money abuse.

trackers.name: KRIK
trackers.desc: Serbian crime-and-corruption reporting network tracing organized crime and illicit finance.

trackers.name: Statistical Office of the Republic of Serbia
trackers.desc: Serbia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Serbia.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Republic of Serbia
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Republic of Serbia — supreme court (Serbia).

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Republic of Serbia
trackers.desc: Supreme Court of Republic of Serbia — supreme court in Serbia (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Зелени фонд — public calls, and the uredba that holds the scoring
trackers.desc: SERBIA'S DOMESTIC ENVIRONMENTAL MONEY, with an unusually traceable legal chain. Public calls are issued by the Ministry of Environmental Protection under Article 90b of the Law on Environmental Protection, governed by the uredba (Sl. glasnik RS 25/18) on the conditions beneficiaries must meet, the manner of distributing funds and — the part to read first — the criteria and measures for evaluating requests, plus a pravilnik on closer conditions for awarding and using Green Fund resources. The scoring criteria are written down; find them before drafting. WHAT HAS BEEN CALLED: co-financing for projects on the conservation and protection of soil as a natural resource, run in successive years — a heading that fits erosion, degradation and contaminated-site work — alongside calls on heating plant replacement and other environmentally acceptable heating devices. TWO CAVEATS: the word is суфинансирање, co-financing, so budget your own contribution; and themes change year to year — check the live calls page rather than assuming a heading recurs, because there is no standing open window. The ministry also runs a route to report an environmental problem and to track a proceeding.

trackers.name: Do not apply to the wrong state — Serbia vs Republika Srpska
trackers.desc: A CONFUSION WORTH HEADING OFF. Searches for Serbian environmental funding surface the Fond za zaštitu životne sredine i energetsku efikasnost Republike Srpske constantly — but this is a fund of an entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina, not of Serbia, with its own eligibility and its own territory. If your site is in Serbia, the Green Fund route through the Ministry of Environmental Protection is the one that applies; if your site is in Republika Srpska, this is. The names are near-identical in search results and the distinction is easy to miss under time pressure.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Energy Community — private bodies may complain, and refusal is appealable
trackers.desc: A COMPLAINT MECHANISM WHERE REFUSAL BY THE GATEKEEPER CAN BE TAKEN OVER ITS HEAD — which is rare, and is the reason to know about this. Under Article 90 of the Energy Community Treaty, private bodies may approach the Secretariat with complaints about a Party's non-compliance, and under Article 12.2 of the Consolidated Rules the Secretariat initiates procedures in response to a complaint by a private body as well as on its own initiative. AND IF THE SECRETARIAT DECLINES: the revised Rules give the complainant the right to approach the Permanent High Level Group directly, which may hear the complaint directly or initiate a preliminary procedure — in most systems recorded in this map, a secretariat declining to act ends the matter. The PHLG can also take interim measures in matters of urgency under Article 47(c) — that is what matters when works are already under way, so ask for it expressly. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS IS IN SCOPE, including the EIA Directive as amended by 2014/52, which was to be transposed by 1 January 2019. CHECK THE TRANSPOSITION DEADLINE FOR THE DIRECTIVE YOU RELY ON — failure to transpose by the stated date is itself the non-compliance, and is a far simpler case than arguing about how a rule was applied. THE REALISTIC WIN CONDITION: a case opens with an Opening Letter, escalates to a Reasoned Opinion giving two months to rectify, then to the Ministerial Council — but a case closes whenever the Party complies, and many are recorded as complied with before any decision was adopted. The opening of proceedings is the lever, not the final decision. YOU CAN ALSO JOIN AN EXISTING CASE: interested third parties may access the case file and submit written observations, provided they substantiate their legitimate interest. Case law from Opening Letters is published with dates and numbers, so precedent is visible. Write to the Energy Community Secretariat, Am Hof 4, 1010 Vienna. ONE MORE ROUTE: the amended Rules provide for cooperation with national authorities and courts, giving concrete assistance to national courts on the interpretation of Energy Community law — a domestic judge unsure how an EU-derived rule applies can be pointed at it.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Ministarstvo prostora — writes the objection and lets you send it (Serbia)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Belgrade collective of urbanists and organisers whose stated purpose is supporting citizens in exercising the right to take part in urban planning, both by working with them directly and by helping them organise the local group in the first place. Ten years of it, and its founders come out of the architecture faculty rather than the NGO circuit. Its contact address for live cases is kriznistab@ministarstvoprostora.org — crisis desk. WHAT IT ACTUALLY HANDS YOU: for major Belgrade plans it drafts the objections itself and publishes them for anyone to download and send in their own name, with the postal address of the city's urbanism secretariat and the closing date. It also keeps a short guide to city planning containing the instructions and a form for writing your own. When the general urban plan to 2041 finally reached the public it assembled 31 expert organisations and civic and informal initiatives to demand public presentations. THE SENTENCE TO PUT IN FRONT OF ANYONE WHO THINKS THEY ARE NOT QUALIFIED: it states that there is no test of expertise for an objection, that the planning commission must treat every one as equally important, and that an objection which cites no law at all is still a citizen's position and therefore valid and significant. Write plainly, in your own words. That single point converts a neighbourhood of people who think they have nothing to say into a stack of submissions the commission is obliged to answer. WHAT IT KNOWS ABOUT THE PATTERN: from its own work with self-organised groups in Belgrade, two-thirds of them formed to resist plans that reduce green space. If that is your fight, you are not the exception and there are others in the city who have already run it.

trackers.name: CEKOR — Serbia's watchdog on the banks that finance projects
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Centre for Ecology and Sustainable Development, an independent NGO founded 1999 at Korzo 15/13, 24000 Subotica, +381 24 523191. Its own description of what distinguishes it from other Serbian environmental organisations is direct: it is first and foremost a watchdog organisation, monitoring the World Bank, the EBRD and the European Investment Bank as a full member of the CEE Bankwatch Network, in continuous dialogue with them in order to change or stop policies and projects with destructive environmental and social effects, and to promote alternatives. WHY THAT MATTERS FOR A SERBIAN COMMUNITY: large Serbian infrastructure, transport and energy projects are routinely financed by exactly those institutions, each of which has environmental and social rules and a complaints channel. This is the organisation in the country that already has the relationships and knows how to use them. Its own working fields include sustainable transport, waste, soil erosion and water, biodiversity, legislation and environmental policy making. SECOND THING IT HOLDS: it records being one of three Serbian organisations selected for the European Commission's Environment Forum, a platform of dialogue between the Commission, south-east European governments and regional environmental NGOs, with an advisory role toward the transport community. For a community whose project is tied to a regional transport corridor, that is a route upward that does not run through the national ministry. IT ALSO WORKS AT HOME: it has been involved in drafting Subotica's local sustainable development strategy, and runs practical local work including tree planting and windbreak restoration with the city and a local forest-protection initiative. So it is reachable on a small local case as well as a financed megaproject. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer, not a funder, not a law firm. Serbia's other entry in this file drafts planning objections in Belgrade; this one follows the money on the bigger schemes.

trackers.name: Trag fondacija — funds informal groups, and activists pick the winners (Serbia)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: Serbia's domestic community foundation, localised to Belgrade in 2004 and run by people in Serbia since. Across its work it has supported more than 1,200 to 1,300 citizens' initiatives with over five million dollars, reaching more than 200 local communities and active in over 200 towns and villages. Serbia had no funder in this file. IT TAKES INFORMAL GROUPS, and its Aktivne zajednice programme is aimed at civil society organisations and neformalne grupe — unregistered groups of citizens — directly, not only as partners. A village committee that has not registered anything can apply. THE DETAIL WORTH COPYING ANYWHERE: selection is participatory. Trag convenes an Odbor aktivista — a board of activists drawn from people who have run its earlier grants and successfully organised their own communities — and that board chooses which projects are funded. Selected groups are then brought to a training on identifying needs, mapping resources, building partnerships and planning, with two people per group invited. Money, training and a decision made by people who have done the same thing. AND THE NUMBER THAT SHOWS WHY THIS BELONGS IN THIS FILE: in one recent public-policy grant round it received 89 applications from 45 communities across Serbia, and the largest single group of project ideas — 45 of them — concerned environmental protection: clean air, accessible water, green towns and conserved biodiversity. Half the demand on Serbia's main community funder is environmental. A Serbian group is not an outlier here; it is the modal applicant. ALSO USEFUL: its public policy programme funds and mentors organisations to be advocates for change in local or national policy, with training in public advocacy alongside the grant. And it has built permanent local foundations in Niš, Pančevo and Stara Pazova by matching money the communities raised themselves — a route worth knowing if the aim is a lasting local fund rather than one grant.

trackers.name: Društvo za zaštitu i proučavanje ptica Srbije (BPSSS) — the species record
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Serbia's oldest bird conservation organisation, founded 18 November 1989 as the Vojvodina society and now the national BirdLife partner, with offices at Radomira Raše Radujkova 1a/211 in Novi Sad and Vukice Mitrović 62/5 in Belgrade. Its work is targeted species conservation and ecosystem protection, carried out with communities, the public and, wherever possible, the government. WHAT TO ASK IT FOR: what is recorded on your site. It runs Serbia's bird monitoring scheme, contributing to the pan-European common bird monitoring dataset, and it gathers individuals, institutions and communities into a network of active members with partner relationships across Europe. That makes it the body most likely to already hold survey evidence for a threatened Serbian site, and the one with standing to state what is there. That question — who already surveyed this — has now produced an answer in six countries in this file. IT TAKES VOLUNTEERS AND MEMBERS, which is the cheap way in: it says explicitly that anyone can contribute through active participation in its activities, and it works through members and volunteers. A community that can offer people rather than money has something it wants. WHAT IT IS NOT, AND I CHECKED SPECIFICALLY: not a land buyer. I searched for evidence that it purchases or holds land and found none — unlike the Slovenian and Polish BirdLife partners, which do. Serbia still has no conservation land buyer in this file. Its other allies here are the Belgrade planning-objection collective, the international-finance watchdog, an environmental law organisation and the national community foundation; this is the missing science.

trackers.name: Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights (Ombudsman)
trackers.desc: Ukraine's Parliamentary Ombudsman is the oversight body for the Law on Access to Public Information (No. 2939-VI), holding quasi-prosecutorial powers — there is no dedicated information commission. It handles complaints, monitors compliance and publishes reports. USE IT: take a refusal of disclosure here, and cite the quasi-prosecutorial powers when a body ignores you.

trackers.name: Nashi Groshi (Our Money)
trackers.desc: Ukrainian outlet tracking where public money goes — procurement, tenders and state spending. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find investigations into Ukrainian procurement and public funds.

trackers.name: Ukraine — Transparency Register (NACP, Law on Lobbying)
trackers.desc: National lobbying register; under the Law “On Lobbying” (in force 1 Sep 2025) the National Agency on Corruption Prevention (NACP) maintains the Transparency Register — a public platform recording lobbying entities & their twice-yearly reports, Ukraine. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Unified State Register of Court Decisions
trackers.desc: Official register publishing essentially every court decision in Ukraine (126M+ documents) under the Law on Access to Court Decisions — a major transparency mechanism. · Find here: Ukraine's Unified State Register of Court Decisions — the full text of virtually all court rulings.

trackers.name: Dostup do Pravdy — FOI requests (UKR)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Dostup do Pravdy — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Environment People Law (EPL) — екологія право людина
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Ukraine's public-interest environmental law organisation, founded in Lviv in 1994, whose lawyers give legal consultations and represent citizens' and NGOs' interests in courts and before public authorities and local self-government — over 590 cases and 4,000 consultations to date. Built a pro bono environmental legal-aid network in Ukraine and litigates its own access-to-information cases against state bodies. Works on national parks, forestry and green-space protection. WHO IT SUITS: a community or NGO refused environmental information, or fighting a development inside or beside a protected area.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is RACSE, the Resource and Analysis Center 'Society and Environment'. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on RACSE, the Resource and Analysis Center 'Society and Environment''s door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS Resource and Analysis Center ‘Society and Environment’ (RACSE) (rac.org.ua) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: Resource and Analysis Center 'Society and Environment' (RACSE)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Ukraine's member organisation in the Justice and Environment network of European environmental-law NGOs, working on access to justice in environmental matters. WHO IT SUITS: treat it as a second door in Ukraine alongside Environment People Law — the network lists it as the national green-law point of contact, but what it will take on is not stated on the network's page, so ask before assuming it litigates. Domain unverified this session — reach them through the member list on justiceandenvironment.org. A think-tank founded 2006 in Lviv, focused on environmental policy and law research and on capacity-building for environmental NGOs — giving other groups the information, skills and knowledge to pursue their own cases. It is a member of Justice and Environment, the European network of environmental law organisations, and sits on the Ukrainian national platform of the Eastern Partnership Civil Society Forum and the Ukrainian side of the Ukraine–EU Civil Society Platform, so it is a channel into the accession process. Its current work centres on green post-war reconstruction and climate governance — the frame in which Ukrainian land and infrastructure decisions are now being taken.

trackers.name: Prozorro (Public e-Procurement System)
trackers.desc: Ukraine's official open-source public e-procurement system, where state and municipal contracting authorities (including local hromada councils) publish tenders and disclose all procurement data — bids, contracts, prices and results — under the motto 'everyone sees everything', enabling open scrutiny of public spending at every level of government.

trackers.name: Prozorro
trackers.desc: Ukraine's landmark open public-procurement system — every government tender and contract, fully searchable. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Ukraine, and for how much.

trackers.name: Chesno (Honestly)
trackers.desc: Ukrainian civic movement monitoring the Verkhovna Rada. Tracks MPs' voting records, attendance, asset declarations, and campaign promises. — Holds to account: top officials & cabinet — find their assets, interests and integrity declarations.

trackers.desc: Ukraine's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Ukraine.

trackers.name: YouControl

trackers.name: NGO standing in environmental cases — and the forum that loses years
trackers.desc: SETTLED: AN ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATION MAY SUE. The Grand Chamber of the Supreme Court held on 11 December 2018 in case No. 910/8122/17 that a nature-protection organisation — charitable or civic — has the right to represent in court the ecological interests of society and of its individual members, to protect violated environmental rights or to remedy breaches of environmental legislation. The claimant relied on the Aarhus Convention on access to information, public participation and access to justice in environmental matters, ratified by Law No. 832-XIV of 6 July 1999, and on the fact that bringing the claim carried out its own statutory objectives. NOW THE TRAP, FROM THE SAME JUDGMENT: because such a claimant effectively substitutes the state authorities in supervising compliance with environmental law, the dispute has a public-law character and must be heard in administrative proceedings — not commercial ones. The organisation had filed in the commercial court and litigated through appeal before this was resolved. FILE IN THE ADMINISTRATIVE COURT or lose years to jurisdiction. ALSO USEFUL: under Article 1 of the Law on Civic Associations, a civic association is formed to protect rights and satisfy public interests including ecological ones, and the Cassation Administrative Court examined standing to sue in members' interests in case No. 640/28508/21 (21 December 2022).

trackers.name: Глобальний екологічний фонд (GEF) — the documented funding route
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE UKRAINE'S OWN ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY DOCUMENTS. The Global Environment Facility, created in 1991 and made a permanent separate institution after the 1994 Rio Earth Summit, is a financial mechanism giving grants to developing countries and countries with economies in transition — the category Ukraine falls in. Its members include 182 states plus international institutions, NGOs and private companies. FUNDING AREAS: biodiversity, climate change, international waters, land degradation, ozone protection and persistent organic pollutants — land degradation is usually the heading a land-defence project fits. It had allocated USD 8.7 billion since 1991 on the ministry's account. START WITH THE MINISTRY, which is the contact point for GEF cooperation and holds the national focal point, rather than approaching GEF directly. ALSO NOTE, AND MIND THE DISTINCTION: UNDP Ukraine has invited civil society organisations to administer small grants — acting as the intermediary that distributes them, which is a different role from receiving one. HONEST GAP: a standing domestic Ukrainian environmental fund with published eligibility for local groups could not be verified for this entry — if one exists it should be used in preference to this.

trackers.name: Energy Community — private bodies may complain, and refusal is appealable
trackers.desc: A COMPLAINT MECHANISM WHERE REFUSAL BY THE GATEKEEPER CAN BE TAKEN OVER ITS HEAD — which is rare, and is the reason to know about this. Under Article 90 of the Energy Community Treaty, private bodies may approach the Secretariat with complaints about a Party's non-compliance, and under Article 12.2 of the Consolidated Rules the Secretariat initiates procedures in response to a complaint by a private body as well as on its own initiative. AND IF THE SECRETARIAT DECLINES: the revised Rules give the complainant the right to approach the Permanent High Level Group directly, which may hear the complaint directly or initiate a preliminary procedure — in most systems recorded in this map, a secretariat declining to act ends the matter. The PHLG can also take interim measures in matters of urgency under Article 47(c) — that is what matters when works are already under way, so ask for it expressly. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS IS IN SCOPE, including the EIA Directive as amended by 2014/52, which was to be transposed by 1 January 2019. CHECK THE TRANSPOSITION DEADLINE FOR THE DIRECTIVE YOU RELY ON — failure to transpose by the stated date is itself the non-compliance, and is a far simpler case than arguing about how a rule was applied. THE REALISTIC WIN CONDITION: a case opens with an Opening Letter, escalates to a Reasoned Opinion giving two months to rectify, then to the Ministerial Council — but a case closes whenever the Party complies, and many are recorded as complied with before any decision was adopted. The opening of proceedings is the lever, not the final decision. YOU CAN ALSO JOIN AN EXISTING CASE: interested third parties may access the case file and submit written observations, provided they substantiate their legitimate interest. Case law from Opening Letters is published with dates and numbers, so precedent is visible. Write to the Energy Community Secretariat, Am Hof 4, 1010 Vienna. ONE MORE ROUTE: the amended Rules provide for cooperation with national authorities and courts, giving concrete assistance to national courts on the interpretation of Energy Community law — a domestic judge unsure how an EU-derived rule applies can be pointed at it.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Ukrainian Nature Conservation Group — writes the scientific case for protection
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an expert group that does the thing a community genuinely cannot do for itself — survey a site, write the scientific justification for protecting it, and petition the oblast council. On its petition the Mykolaiv oblast council created the Kovalivski Plavni hydrological reserve of over 394 hectares inside the Olshanska territorial community, and it has taken further proposals to completed-justification stage, including a roughly 300-hectare steppe system holding eleven Red Book plant species, twelve Red Book animal species and four Green Book communities. Ukraine's other allies are three legal bodies; none of them can write the botany. IT ARGUES TO THE VILLAGE, NOT ONLY THE COUNCIL: approval decisions are taken by the hromadas themselves, and it produced a booklet for residents of the Butska hromada setting out why the Voloshkovyi reserve should be created, as well as inventorying the biodiversity of a single hromada as a worked example. A community that has to vote on protecting its own ground needs something to read first, and almost nothing else here produces that. WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT ENFORCEMENT, WHICH YOU SHOULD READ BEFORE RELYING ON AN INSPECTORATE: it found clear-felling in a habitat of spring snowflake in the Drohobych forestry district and reported it to the eco-inspectors with photographs of the stumps and the plant; its published account of the response is that it exceeded the worst expectations. It publishes more broadly on how the eco-inspection covers illegal felling rather than fighting it, with worked examples from Zakarpattia.

trackers.name: Rewilding Ukraine — restores wetlands and helped a community get a national park proposed
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a Ukrainian team working in the Danube Delta since 2017, part of the Rewilding Europe network, operating alongside the Danube Biosphere Reserve, the Izmail water authority, Izmail Forestry, local fishermen, landowners and communities. Since 2019 it has restored seven wetlands covering more than 18,000 hectares and reconnected 20 kilometres of river networks; it reports improving water quality for more than 50,000 people. Its work has continued through the war. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES THAT A COMMUNITY CAN USE: physical restoration — removing sections of dyke on Ermakiv and Tataru Islands to restore natural current, reconnecting Kartal, Katlabuh and Kugurlui lakes to the Danube, reflooding 500 hectares of marshland, removing ten dams on the Kogilnik River, and restoring more than 500 hectares of Tarutino Steppe that had been illegally ploughed eight years earlier. If land near you has been drained, dyked or ploughed unlawfully, this is an organisation that has reversed exactly that, at scale. AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST HERE: it worked with the Borodino community to get the Budzhak Steppes National Nature Park proposed, running the public consultation with the Centre for Regional Studies, assembling a team of scientists to prepare the scientific rationale, and contributing both expertise and financial support to the community's own initiative. A Ukrainian community that wants its ground formally protected has a body that has taken another community through precisely that process, and paid towards it. WHAT TO EXPECT: it is a restoration and reintroduction organisation, not a land buyer and not a law firm, and it is working in a country at war — its own account records staff mobilised into volunteering and civil defence. Approach it about a delta, steppe or wetland site in the Odesa region and about getting a protection case scientifically documented.

trackers.name: National Ecological Centre of Ukraine (NECU) — 24 territorial branches, and it watches the banks
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: one of the first national-level environmental non-profits registered in independent Ukraine, founded 30 August 1991, working on the protection of natural territories, biodiversity, climate and the negative consequences of the energy sector. It has 24 territorial branches across Ukraine, plus a youth branch revived in 2003 — which is the single most useful fact here, because it means there is very likely a branch in your oblast rather than only an office in Kyiv. WHAT IT DOES WITH A CASE: it pushes officials and politicians to take decisions with environmental protection and public safety in view, prepares its own assessments and studies, and proposes alternative solutions. That last part matters: an alternative on the table is consistently stronger than an objection alone, as the Italian and British entries in this file also found. It is a member of IUCN and of the CEE Bankwatch Network, and it states that its staff pay particular attention to the projects of development banks. THE SPECIALISMS ITS OWN PEOPLE DECLARE, which tell you what to ask for: work with local communities; the state of water resources; biological and landscape diversity; the nature reserve fund and the development of the ecological network; green zones in settlements; organising public conservation campaigns; and countering corruption in the environmental sphere. One of its council members directs a regional landscape park and the southern branch of its ecology institute, so protected-area creation is inside its experience. IT RUNS NAMED CAMPAIGNS: including one to save the Buzkyi Hard, which is the kind of long single-site defence a community can ask to be added to. USE IT WITH THE OTHER UKRAINIAN ENTRIES: this file already holds a group that writes the scientific justification for protection and petitions oblast councils, a team that restores wetlands and steered a community through a national park proposal, and an environmental law organisation. NECU adds national reach, 24 local branches and the development-bank angle. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a funder, and it is operating in wartime.

trackers.name: ТОП — Ukrainian Society for the Protection of Birds, and the IBA programme
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Ukraine's first non-governmental bird conservation organisation, founded 1994, BirdLife partner since 1995 and full partner from 2006, with a membership network of around 2,000 individual members. PO box 143, Kyiv 03150, uspb@birdlife.org.ua, +380 44 339-99-81. Membership is open to anyone — conservationists, bird enthusiasts, scientists and amateurs alike — and the organisation is run by a democratically elected council between congresses of its members. For a Ukrainian community with people rather than money, that is the way in. WHAT TO ASK IT FOR: it runs Ukraine's Important Bird Areas programme, and its species work spans the aquatic warbler, greater spotted eagle, red-breasted goose, great bustard, white-tailed eagle and saker falcon across the Carpathians, ancient forests, peatlands, steppe grassland and coastal habitats. If a threatened Ukrainian site is an Important Bird Area, or holds any of those species, this is the organisation that can say so with standing — and it has spent thirty years mapping exactly that. ITS RECORD ON GETTING GROUND PROTECTED: with the wider BirdLife partnership it has played a key role in expanding Ukraine's network of protected areas, and in 2017 the Ukrainian government passed legislation protecting the country's remaining primeval Carpathian forests — an initiative it helped design and champion. A community seeking designation for its own ground is asking an organisation that has done it at national scale. IT ALSO RESTORES: it has worked on restoring wetland and peatland ecosystems, including freshwater lakes in the Dnipro delta, and takes part in international programmes for the aquatic warbler including translocation between countries. WHAT IT IS NOT, CHECKED SPECIFICALLY: not a land buyer — I found no evidence it purchases land. Ukraine's other entries here are the group that writes scientific justifications and petitions oblast councils, the Danube delta restoration team, an environmental law organisation, and the national centre with 24 branches. This adds the bird record and the IBA network.

trackers.name: ІСАР Єднання (ISAR Ednannia) — one of Ukraine's largest domestic grant-makers
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a Ukrainian civil society organisation that has spent about 25 years developing civil society and strategic philanthropy in Ukraine. It is described as one of the largest genuinely Ukrainian grant-makers, providing upwards of 500 grants a year for public-benefit initiatives across the whole territory of Ukraine. Ukraine had no funder in this file, despite having four other allies. THE SIZES AND SHAPES TO PLAN AROUND, from its published calls: a competition for local civic organisations with most supported projects budgeted up to 294,000 hryvnia, around 55 organisations supported, projects of about six months, open to bodies implementing local initiatives anywhere in Ukraine with priority to five oblasts — Chernihiv, Sumy, Kharkiv, Mykolaiv and Zaporizhzhia. A project grants competition for initiatives driving systemic change, democratic transformation and recovery of processes damaged by the war, expressly including advocacy campaigns. Grants for strategic partners strengthening the expert capacity of local civil society organisations, networking and sector development. And a fund for organisations working in communities that have suffered critical disruption. THE RARE ONE, AND IT IS THE MOST VALUABLE FORMAT IN THIS FILE: an institutional support competition of up to 2,500,000 hryvnia for the upkeep and development of the organisation itself — salaries, office rent, equipment and organisational development, with no tie to a specific project. Most grants pay for activities; this pays for the organisation to exist. Only PONT's operating costs, the EEA institutional grants and the southern Italian volunteering call compare anywhere in these 166 candidates. HOW TO USE IT FOR LAND WORK: it is not an environmental funder. Its themes are democratic governance, human rights, recovery and local initiative — so a Ukrainian community should frame a case as residents organising to solve a local problem or to advocate on a decision, which is what the calls describe. The Ukrainian entries already in this file supply the science, the restoration, the law and the branch network; this is the money.

trackers.name: Átlátszó (atlatszo.hu)
trackers.desc: Hungarian investigative and FOI newsroom exposing corruption and misuse of public funds. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find investigations and public-interest data requests.

trackers.name: Courts of Hungary
trackers.desc: Official judiciary portal with the collection of anonymized court decisions (BHGY). · Find here: information, case search and selected decisions of the courts of Hungary.

trackers.name: Hungarian National Authority for Data Protection and Freedom of Information (NAIH)
trackers.desc: Hungarian National Authority for Data Protection and Freedom of Information (NAIH) — independent body overseeing the right of access to public information.

trackers.name: Ki Mit Tud — FOI requests (HUN)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); Ki Mit Tud — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: Hungarian Helsinki Committee
trackers.desc: Leading Hungarian rule-of-law and human-rights NGO and a key election-integrity watchdog — publishes electoral-integrity assessments and the joint Citizen Election Report, litigates freedom-of-information cases, and tracks legislative changes to the electoral framework.

trackers.name: EMLA — Környezeti Management és Jog Egyesület
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Hungary's public-interest environmental law association, founded 1992, whose core activities are environmental legal advice AND legal representation of citizens and NGOs before authorities and courts, alongside research and training. Publishes free practical guides and document templates for people who want to take the legal route, plus a decision-tree tool on remedies. Also advises municipalities on their statutory environmental duties. WHO IT SUITS: a resident or civil organisation confronting a polluting or destructive project who needs an actual lawyer, not just information. Capacity is limited and cases are selected.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is EMLA. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on EMLA's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS Environmental Management and Law Association (EMLA) (emla.hu) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.desc: registration authority in Hungary

trackers.name: State Audit Office (ÁSZ)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Hungary, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: EKR
trackers.desc: Hungary's electronic public-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Hungary, and for how much.

trackers.name: K-Monitor
trackers.desc: Hungarian anti-corruption watchdog that monitors parliamentary activity, public spending, and political integrity. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Hungary, and for how much.

trackers.name: Hungarian Central Statistical Office (KSH)
trackers.desc: Hungary's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Hungary.

trackers.name: Természetvédelmi pályázat — 100 percent funded, paid in advance, no own funds
trackers.desc: THE MOST GENEROUS TERMS RECORDED ANYWHERE IN THIS MAP. The agriculture ministry's annual nature protection call gives a one-off non-repayable grant of up to 100 percent of all eligible costs, transferred in a single sum as an advance to your bank account — and providing own resources or co-funding is not a condition. Against Italy's 10 percent cash requirement, Serbia's co-financing framing and GEF's 50 percent expectation, Hungary asks for none and pays up front rather than in arrears. ELIGIBILITY TURNS ON YOUR STATUTE: you must qualify as a civil organisation under the Civil tv. and have environmental and/or nature protection purpose recorded in your alapító okirat or alapszabály — the fifth country in this map, with Finland, Italy, Poland and Greece, where your own constitution is the gate. FUNDABLE: habitat protection and management, habitat rehabilitation and reconstruction, operation of the Natura 2000 network, geological natural values, caves, landscape protection research, ecosystem mapping and valuation, publications, films and environmental education. Work must fit the Nemzeti Természetvédelmi Alapterv.

trackers.name: Which Hungarian call to enter — and read the exclusions first
trackers.desc: THERE ARE TWO NATIONAL CALLS AND THEY FUND DIFFERENT THINGS. The NKP környezetvédelmi call is the larger — a frame of HUF 400,000,000 with up to HUF 10,000,000 per application, again one-off, non-repayable and up to 100 percent of eligible costs — but its categories are awareness and consumption: air quality, environmentally conscious consumer behaviour, communication on greenwashing and on credible ISO Type I ecolabels. So this is the money for public-facing campaigning; the agriculture ministry's call is the one for habitat work. ELIGIBLE here are Hungarian-registered associations and foundations under Act CLXXV of 2011, expressly excluding parties, trade unions, mutual insurance associations, public foundations and party foundations. READ THE EXCLUSION LIST BEFORE DRAFTING: the nature call names topics for which support cannot be requested — some outside the portfolio's remit, others funded under a different framework — so a proposal aimed at an excluded topic is wasted work. In one round 22 organisations were funded, with the decision published as a table showing funded, reserve-list and unfunded applicants — so a near miss is visible and worth following up. The ministry also runs a workshop to help submit adequate applications; attend it.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. trackers.name: MME's nine county land-holding foundations (Hungary) — who actually buys the land

trackers.name: Ökotárs Alapítvány — Hungarian Environmental Partnership Foundation
trackers.desc: WHAT THE CONSORTIUM IS: the Environmental Partnership Association, headquartered in Brno, is a consortium of six independent national foundations in central and eastern Europe that give grants to community projects protecting the environment. Mott Foundation, the German Marshall Fund and the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, and the national foundations were established as independent bodies in the early 1990s. THE HUNGARIAN MEMBER: Ökotárs Alapítvány, founded 1992, at okotars.hu. SOURCING: the consortium and its six national foundations are documented on the Environmental Partnership Association's own site; the national figures and founding dates come from consortium and partner material rather than each foundation's own pages. Confirm current grant rounds with the national foundation directly.

trackers.name: Office for Personal Data Protection (SR)
trackers.desc: Office for Personal Data Protection (SR) — Slovakia’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Otvorené súdy (Open Courts)
trackers.desc: Civic project publishing Slovak court decisions, judge profiles and court performance data. · Find here: a civil-society database profiling Slovak judges and their decisions (Otvorené súdy).

trackers.name: VIA IURIS — Občan (public participation & environmental litigation)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Slovak public-interest law association behind the Pezinok landfill case that won a Goldman Environmental Prize, with a long litigation record for communities and conservation NGOs — small hydro plants on the Hron struck down, an unlawfully sited quarry expansion at Ludrová reopened, the Detva cyanide gold mine defeated, Banská Bystrica's zoning plan challenged, the Triblavina junction changes stopped. Publishes free manuals on participating in siting and building permit proceedings, EIA, and access to information. WHO IT SUITS: residents or a civic association trying to become a party to a permit or zoning proceeding, or facing intimidation for defending the public interest.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is VIA IURIS. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on VIA IURIS's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS VIA IURIS (viaiuris.sk) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: Slovakia Business Register (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Slovakia Business Register (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Slovakia — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: data.gov.sk
trackers.desc: National — Slovak Republic open data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Slovakia.

trackers.name: Register of legal entities (RPO)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Register of Public Sector Partners (RPVS)
trackers.desc: Slovakia's public register of the beneficial owners of any company doing business with the state. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their conflicts of interest with the state; who really owns and controls them.

trackers.name: Register of Public Sector Partners (RPVS)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic
trackers.desc: Slovakia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Slovakia.

trackers.name: Investigative Center of Ján Kuciak (ICJK)
trackers.desc: Slovak investigative center probing money laundering, organized crime and abuse of public funds.

trackers.name: National Council – Asset Declarations
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations.

trackers.name: Business Register on Internet
trackers.desc: Company / business register of Slovakia — official registry of legal entities.

trackers.name: UVO / EVO
trackers.desc: Slovakia's public-procurement office and electronic platform. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Slovakia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Environmentálny fond — grants up to EUR 200,000, and the procurement trap
trackers.desc: SLOVAKIA'S STATE ENVIRONMENTAL FUND, created by Act 587/2004 Z. z. and administered by the environment ministry, gives grants and loans. Oblasť D funds nature, biodiversity and landscape protection — natural species composition of ecosystems, management of invasive non-native species, measures for favourable status of protected species, wetland restoration, monitoring of species and habitats, breeding and rehabilitation stations, and prevention of brown bear damage. ELIGIBLE: municipalities, self-governing regions, občianske združenia, interest associations, foundations and non-profits, with support up to EUR 200,000 and about EUR 1.16 million allocated. THE TRAP TO PLAN FOR: public procurement is not required when you apply — but if the grant is approved, the support contract cannot be concluded without documents proving procurement was carried out, with the deadline and scope set out in the notice sent with the minister's decision. A small group can therefore apply without having run a procurement, but must be able to run one quickly afterwards. Prepare for it before the award, not after.

CEILINGS: EUR 5,000 for natural persons, municipalities, civic associations, foundations and non-profits; EUR 8,000 for micro-regional associations of municipalities.
