trackers.name: Centar za životnu sredinu, Banja Luka — sues permits and wins (Bosnia and Herzegovina)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a non-profit, non-partisan environmental association at Miše Stupara 5, Banja Luka, which brings administrative lawsuits against environmental permits and has a record of winning them. It publishes the judgments on its own site. In July 2024 the District Court in Banja Luka upheld its claim and annulled the environmental permit for the Ugljevik III thermal plant, ordering the ministry to pay its costs and rejecting the developer's costs claim. On the Jovići small hydro scheme it had already overturned two environmental permits in court before a third was issued. On Sutjeska 2B it has run a series of actions since 2019, after establishing that the ministry exempted the investor from impact assessment in 2018 despite its own binding 2010 decision requiring one. It also turns out to the site when residents call it. Its own account of the Pliva at Otomalj is exactly that — local people called, and it went to the ground to get ahead of works it suspected were coming. That is a rarer offer than litigation. THE EXPECTATION IT SETS, AND IT IS THE HARDEST THING IN THIS FILE: winning does not end the project. At Jovići the permit was quashed twice and issued a third time. A Bosnian community should plan for a sequence of annulments rather than one, and should understand that the costs recovered are nominal — two hundred convertible marks in the Ugljevik case — so success in court funds nothing. What repeated annulment buys is time and a public record of the authority ignoring its own decisions, and in several of these cases that has been enough.

trackers.name: Fondacija Mozaik — 50 municipal funds, and grants a village group can actually get
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: a development foundation founded in 2000 in Sarajevo, which has grown from supporting the local NGO sector into the main community-philanthropy body in Bosnia and Herzegovina. More than 3,000 projects supported with over 5 million convertible marks, across more than 100 communities. Bosnia had no funder at all in this file before this. THE STRUCTURE THAT MATTERS: its Omladinske banke — youth banks — have established 50 municipal funds, mobilised around 10,000 volunteers, and enable more than 550 projects a year. Decisions are made locally, in the municipality, by people from it. For a village group in BiH that is a nearer and far more reachable source of money than any national or international call in this file. THE GRANT SIZE, WHICH IS THE HONEST PART: its orange grants run to 3,000 convertible marks — roughly €1,500 — for a young person ready to start and run a socially useful project from beginning to end. That will not buy land or fund litigation. It will pay for a survey, a public meeting, printing, a valuation, a small piece of evidence, or the first organising work — and those are the costs that stop most community campaigns before they begin. WHO IT IS FOR, AND THE LIMIT TO ACCEPT: its focus is young people, entrepreneurship and community development, not environmental protection. Frame the ask as a young person leading a project that solves a concrete problem in their own community, because that is what it funds. If the group is not young, the youth bank route is not open, and the national programmes are the alternative. WHAT IT ALSO OFFERS: mentoring and advisory support to citizens across BiH since 2002, and membership of philanthropy networks including the regional SIGN network and European foundation associations, which is how a Bosnian group reaches funders outside the country.

trackers.name: Eko Bistro, Kruščica — the community that won, and what it says success required
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: an environmental citizens' association at Kruščica in the municipality of Vitez, central Bosnia, bistro.kruscica@gmail.com, formed by villagers — the women who had been blocking the bridge organised themselves into a citizens' association to formalise the fight. The river supplies drinking water to Kruščica's 2,500 residents and to some 145,000 people in two nearby towns. WHAT THEY DID AND WHAT IT COST: from August 2017 they held the access bridge to the construction site around the clock for over 500 days, through police violence, threats from the authorities and the investor, and winter. On 24 August a special police unit attacked women sitting on the bridge. Charges brought against them — assaulting a police officer — were dismissed by the court. AND THEY WON IN COURT: the cantonal court in Novi Travnik ruled that the environmental permit for the dam be annulled immediately, making further construction illegal, and on 14 December a court decision stopped all dam plans. But the concessions were not revoked — they remain in local planning documents, and the association has continued to challenge them. A community that wins a permit case has not necessarily removed the scheme from the plan. THE PART TO READ TWICE, because it is a checklist from people who did it: their own case study names what success requires as an attorney, a biologist, a spatial planner, and media communication, alongside strengthening the internal capacity of the local initiative — there the Eko Bistro association, the Kruščica Local Community and an informal women's group working together. It records 817 locals signing a petition to give power of attorney for the represented parties, and around 2,000 people taking part in the daytime vigil. IT ALSO NAMES WHO DECIDES: the Central Bosnia Canton government line ministry, and the Vitez Municipal Council through the municipal spatial plan. SUPPORT CAME FROM OUTSIDE TOO: the Czech organisation Arnika found the women in 2017 and began supporting them; the Centre for Environment in Bosnia and Herzegovina worked on the court case; and the campaign was carried internationally through the Balkan rivers network. Maida Bilal received the Goldman Environmental Prize.

trackers.desc: Agency for Information and Privacy (AIP) — Kosovo’s Agency for Information and Privacy overseeing the Law on Access to Public Documents (No. 06/L-081) and adjudicating access-to-information appeals. — Holds to account: Kosovo’s public bodies on disclosure — find access-to-information appeal decisions, guidance and annual reports.

trackers.desc: Information and Privacy Agency (Kosovo) — Kosovo’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of Kosovo
trackers.desc: Final authority on constitutional interpretation and judicial review in Kosovo, publishing its judgments. · Find here: the decisions of the Constitutional Court of Kosovo.

trackers.desc: Accountability source (FOI request platform); dumeditë — civic Freedom-of-Information request platform (Alaveteli/mySociety network) — lets citizens file public-records requests and publishes the requests and the authorities’ responses in a public archive.

trackers.name: ARBK – Kosovo Business Registration Agency
trackers.desc: National — central commercial register of Kosovo (fully electronic, searchable). — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: National Audit Office (ZKA)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Kosovo, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) of Kosovo
trackers.desc: Financial intelligence unit of XKS — receives and analyses suspicious-transaction reports to counter money laundering.

trackers.name: Neni 24 mbrojtja paraprake — protection before designation
trackers.desc: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO WAIT FOR DESIGNATION TO GET PROTECTIVE EFFECT. Under neni 24 of Ligji nr. 03/L-233 për Mbrojtjen e Natyrës, an area is placed under preliminary protection by decision where the Institute determines on professional justification that it has the characteristics of a protected area and/or where the procedure for taking it under protection has begun. The trigger is disjunctive — either limb suffices — so getting the Institute to state that an area has the characteristics is itself the intervention. This is the second such instrument in this map, alongside Bosnia's privremena zaštita. NENI 23 — WHO CAN UNDO PROTECTION: where a municipality-declared area loses the values for which it was protected, the body that protected it may terminate protection only after prior consent of the Ministry — but that consent is not required where termination comes by law or by a sub-legal act of the Government. So a municipality cannot unilaterally de-protect what it protected, while the Government can; the route by which de-protection is attempted tells you which safeguard applies. Municipalities do hold a nature-protection role — the law names the organi kompetent i komunës. DEFINITIONS THAT DO WORK: peizazh expressly includes elements of civilisation; përbërësit e natyrës names fossils and rocks among the components of nature; and përtëritja e natyrës defines restoration as returning damaged diversity to a state approximating the original.

trackers.name: Kosovo Institute for Nature Protection — approach it first
trackers.desc: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT BODY TO APPROACH FIRST, because it is the Institute whose professional justification triggers preliminary protection under neni 24. It is the central institution for nature conservation and for monitoring the state of protected natural values in Kosovo, sitting within AMMK, with a lineage from a nature-protection unit formed in 1968 inside the body for protection of cultural monuments, later separated into its own Enti and given statutory footing by the 1988 law on protection and development of natural values (article 78.2). SCALE, from the Ministry's Raport për Gjendjen e Natyrës 2010–2014: 116 protected areas covering 118,913.95 ha, or 10.9 percent of Kosovo — 11 strict nature reserves, 2 national parks (Sharri and Bjeshkët e Nemuna) and 99 nature monuments, among them the source of the White Drin with the Radavc Cave, the Gadime Cave, the Mirusha Waterfalls and the Rugova Gorge. NOTE THE DISTRIBUTION: 99 of 116 protected areas are nature monuments. That is the working category here, and it covers caves, waterfalls, gorges, springs and individual trees — so for a single feature, the monument is the realistic ask. Sources differ on whether the law sets six or seven categories; this entry does not resolve that — read the current text.

trackers.name: KCSF — it funds unregistered initiatives and individual activists
trackers.desc: NO INCORPORATION REQUIRED — which removes the commonest barrier in this entire map. The Kosovar Civil Society Foundation, mobilising resources since 1998, states that it provides grant instruments for civil society initiatives — NGOs, unregistered initiatives and individual activists — through a people-centred approach. That puts Kosovo alongside Bhutan, Andorra and the Pacific Development and Conservation Trust as places where a community group need not register first. DISTINGUISH THE INSTRUMENTS: Engagement for Joint Action (EJA Kosovo) gives grants plus capacity building, with an annual Democracy Award; Organisational Development Grants (ODGs) fund the development of the organisation itself rather than a project — where the problem is that your group cannot sustain the work, that is the instrument, and few funders anywhere in this map offer it; and small project grants are for concrete results within a set timeframe. It also runs a Resource Centre, and the Kosovo Resource Centre with Community Building Mitrovica. ALIGN WITH ITS STATED DIRECTION: KCSF has added resource diversification to increase local ownership and sustainability, including support from the private sector, diaspora, citizens and public funds — a proposal showing domestic co-support now matches where it says it is going.

trackers.name: EU Civil Society Facility — the Green Agenda is the named object
trackers.desc: AN ENVIRONMENTAL PROPOSAL IS NOT SQUEEZING INTO A DEMOCRACY PROGRAMME HERE — it is the programme's stated purpose. The EU Office in Kosovo's Civil Society Facility & Media Programme 2024–25 allocation (EuropeAid/183890/DD/ACT/XK) sought proposals to strengthen participatory democracy and EU integration ‘through an enhanced contribution by civil society to the implementation of the Green Agenda in the Western Balkans’. HOW IT RUNS: a concept note stage first — the 2024 allocation set 19 May 2025 at 15:00 — with guidelines and annexes as a single ZIP, calls published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal. A RULE THAT SHAPES YOUR CONSORTIUM: a lead applicant may not be awarded more than one grant under a call and nor may a co-applicant, so one organisation can appear in at most two submitted applications — once as lead, once as co-applicant, under two different lots. Grantees must collaborate with the EU-funded TACSO project. GET IN BEFORE THE CALL OPENS: EU TACSO runs online consultations with potential beneficiaries on the priority sectors and themes of planned calls, and webinars on applying in English with interpretation into Albanian and Serbian — attending the consultation is how a theme gets into a call. AND LOOK FOR THE SUB-GRANT LAYER, NOT BRUSSELS: under Green Horizons, the EU and CARE Deutschland allocated EUR 80,000 in sub-grants to 8 local organisations for 8–10 month projects in urban gardening, waste recycling and renewable energy. Eight grants averaging EUR 10,000 is the realistic community-end scale.

trackers.name: Energy Community — private bodies may complain, and refusal is appealable
trackers.desc: A COMPLAINT MECHANISM WHERE REFUSAL BY THE GATEKEEPER CAN BE TAKEN OVER ITS HEAD — which is rare, and is the reason to know about this. Under Article 90 of the Energy Community Treaty, private bodies may approach the Secretariat with complaints about a Party's non-compliance, and under Article 12.2 of the Consolidated Rules the Secretariat initiates procedures in response to a complaint by a private body as well as on its own initiative. AND IF THE SECRETARIAT DECLINES: the revised Rules give the complainant the right to approach the Permanent High Level Group directly, which may hear the complaint directly or initiate a preliminary procedure — in most systems recorded in this map, a secretariat declining to act ends the matter. The PHLG can also take interim measures in matters of urgency under Article 47(c) — that is what matters when works are already under way, so ask for it expressly. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS IS IN SCOPE, including the EIA Directive as amended by 2014/52, which was to be transposed by 1 January 2019. CHECK THE TRANSPOSITION DEADLINE FOR THE DIRECTIVE YOU RELY ON — failure to transpose by the stated date is itself the non-compliance, and is a far simpler case than arguing about how a rule was applied. THE REALISTIC WIN CONDITION: a case opens with an Opening Letter, escalates to a Reasoned Opinion giving two months to rectify, then to the Ministerial Council — but a case closes whenever the Party complies, and many are recorded as complied with before any decision was adopted. The opening of proceedings is the lever, not the final decision. YOU CAN ALSO JOIN AN EXISTING CASE: interested third parties may access the case file and submit written observations, provided they substantiate their legitimate interest. Case law from Opening Letters is published with dates and numbers, so precedent is visible. Write to the Energy Community Secretariat, Am Hof 4, 1010 Vienna. ONE MORE ROUTE: the amended Rules provide for cooperation with national authorities and courts, giving concrete assistance to national courts on the interpretation of Energy Community law — a domestic judge unsure how an EU-derived rule applies can be pointed at it.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: EC Ma Ndryshe — builds the neighbourhood group and watches the permits (Kosovo)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Kosovo organisation working on local governance, urban structure and cultural heritage, with offices at Fehmi Lladrovci 94 in Prizren and in Prishtina. Its stated method is community mobilisation and oversight of public decision-making. It has built local community groups at neighbourhood and village level across Prizren municipality and has been extending that practice to other Kosovo municipalities since 2018 — so the offer is not only advice on your case but help constituting the group that will carry it. WHAT IT DOES ON A LIVE CASE: it takes concerns from residents, obtains the official file from the competent institutions, and compares what was consented with what is being built. In one Prizren Historic Centre case both the Regional Centre for Cultural Heritage and the municipal Inspectorate confirmed the works did not match the approved project, and the Inspectorate imposed stop measures. It sends information requests to other institutions and publishes what comes back, including where a building inside the Historic Centre was demolished without heritage consent, and where works began on premises part-owned by the mayor's son. IT ALSO PUBLISHES THE GROUNDWORK: it has produced its own analysis of spatial planning in Kosovo municipalities covering unpermitted construction with Prizren as the case study, and it records that in the first half of 2012 alone 62 consents were issued for building or intervention inside Prizren's Historic Centre, with a considerable number of those works departing from the approved project. That is the context a Kosovar community needs before it assumes its case is unusual. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a law firm. It works on urban space, heritage and municipal governance, it names the shortage of reliable data and its own financial sustainability as standing challenges, and its reach outside those themes is limited.

trackers.name: Balkan Green Foundation — sub-grants to local groups, and the SLAPP warning (Kosovo)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES FOR A LOCAL GROUP: with the Institute for Development Policy it has run sub-granting schemes putting money directly into small Kosovar organisations — one project supported 59 local NGO project ideas across Kosovo with a total of €355,000, funded through the EU Office in Kosovo, in environmental protection, green energy and circular economy. Its current work includes empowering environmental civil society organisations in Kosovo with partners including Emancipimi Civil Ma Ndryshe, which is already in this file, and Let's Do It Peja and 7 Arte. Kosovo had no funder at all before this. WHAT IT SUPPLIES BESIDES MONEY: independent data and analysis, tracking of public and international funds, and convening of regional coalitions, working with municipalities across the Western Balkans. If your case turns on whether a scheme was properly financed or permitted, this is the organisation that follows those numbers in this region. READ THIS BEFORE YOU PUT YOUR NAME ON ANYTHING IN KOSOVO. The Deçan hydropower case shows both what is possible and what it costs. Civil society organisations and a local political coordinator filed suit in the Basic Court over environmental and operating permits; the Supreme Court ultimately held that three of the company's small hydropower plants must be shut down and confirmed the permits had not been handled by the book. But the company sued an environmental activist for €100,000 for defamation after she documented the damage, and sued a Deçan activist for €10,000 — lawsuits Amnesty International classified as SLAPPs intended to intimidate and silence them. The suits were later announced as withdrawn unconditionally. A Kosovar community should assume that naming a developer publicly may draw a personal lawsuit, and should line up organisational backing before an individual signs anything. WHAT IT IS NOT: a foundation, an analyst and a re-granter — not a law firm, not a land buyer.

trackers.name: FIQ — Forumi për Iniciativa Qytetare: grants and mentoring for informal groups (Kosovo)
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a Kosovar foundation founded around 2000–2001 by young community activists after the war, whose stated mission is to mobilise citizens and empower them to claim their rights and hold authorities to account. It has promoted local philanthropy since 2009. Note the address change: its site has moved to fiqorg.com from the older fiq-fci.org. WHAT ITS GRANT PROGRAMME OFFERS, AND THE ELIGIBILITY IS THE POINT: financial assistance and mentoring to local CSOs, informal groups, networks and innovative initiatives, to help them carry out meaningful community actions. Grants have ranged from €1,000 to €63,000, with sub-granting to over 42 local organisations and more than €280,000 given since the programme began in 2009. A group with no legal registration is explicitly inside the scope, and the range means both a small survey and a substantial piece of work are fundable. HOW IT DECIDES, WHICH TELLS YOU HOW TO APPROACH IT: it describes a triangular approach — involving community members of different target groups directly in community discussions, alongside representatives of local community-based organisations, local government and the private sector. Come with the community in the room, not with a paper application from outside it. IT ALSO WORKS ON ENVIRONMENT DIRECTLY: its sustainable development programme addresses economy, energy and environment, and its own framing is that local communities are the best place to develop civic activism and improve the environment for citizens. ONE CAVEAT ON ITS LARGER CALLS: some of its EU-funded schemes, including matching grants for coalitions of local organisations, have required applicants to be legally registered for at least a year with full tax and registration documents, and to co-fund. The small-grant route takes informal groups; the coalition route does not. Ask which call you are looking at. KOSOVO NOW HAS TWO FUNDERS in this file, this and the foundation filed in batch 108, plus the community-organising body from batch 32.

trackers.name: ERA Group, Peja — works across the Kosovo, Montenegro and Albania borders on rivers and lynx
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Environmentally Responsible Action, established 2003 in Peja, working on nature protection alongside tourism promotion, alpinism, cycling and ski touring. Kosovo's bucket held funders and a neighbourhood organiser but no body doing nature protection and species work. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY WORKED ON: many areas of wildlife conservation, most notably the study and protection of the endangered Balkan lynx, and the protection of rivers and their ecosystems in Kosovo and beyond. If a Kosovar river or mountain site is threatened, this is the organisation with the field record on both. THE CROSS-BORDER PART, which matters because these mountains are shared: it is a member of international associations and works with Mountain club Hajla and PSKH Hrid in Montenegro and the Valbona NGO in Albania, all operating in the bordering areas. It coordinated a trek across three countries promoting the Balkan Peace Park project, and hosted the meeting at which participating NGOs established a Coalition of NGOs for the Balkan Peace Park. A threat on one side of these borders has organised counterparts on the other two. IT ALSO RAN A COMMUNITY PROCESS: with Milieukontakt of the Netherlands and two other local organisations it implemented the Green Agenda — a community-driven initiative working towards sustainable development — in three communities: Istog, Rugova (Peja) and Prizren. That is a named participatory method already run in Kosovar villages. PRACTICAL: based at the Haxhi Zeka Mill cultural heritage site, V. Gërvalla street, Peja; info@eradirect.org; +383 49 204 421; contact person Fatos Lajçi, who is also credited as a naturalist and film-maker and helped gather residents' questionnaires in the Bjeshkët e Nemuna settlements ahead of the area's declaration as a national park. Its members speak English, German, Italian and Serbian. HONEST NOTE: it has described itself as volunteer-based with projects completed on a volunteer basis, so expect capacity limits.

trackers.name: Personal Data Protection Agency (DZLP)
trackers.desc: Personal Data Protection Agency (DZLP) — North Macedonia’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: State Commission for Prevention of Corruption
trackers.desc: North Macedonia's anti-corruption commission. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers, top officials & cabinet, officials handling public money & power — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held; their assets, interests and integrity declarations; corruption cases, sanctions and integrity data.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of North Macedonia
trackers.desc: Official site publishing the decisions of North Macedonia's Constitutional Court. · Find here: the decisions of the Constitutional Court of North Macedonia.

trackers.name: Agency for Protection of the Right to Free Access to Public Information (North Macedonia)
trackers.desc: Agency for Protection of the Right to Free Access to Public Information (North Macedonia) — independent body overseeing the right of access to public information.

trackers.name: Agency for Free Access to Public Information (KOMSPI)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority; North Macedonia’s KOMSPI decides appeals and monitors implementation of the Law on Free Access to Public Information, reporting to Parliament, North Macedonia.

trackers.name: Justice and Environment — European green-law network
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the European network of environmental-law NGOs, whose national member here is FRONT 21/42. Its fifteen members act as the environmental-law service point in their own countries, taking cases and intervening in legislative processes, while the network defends communities and nature in court and lodges infringement complaints against member-state governments. Its standing themes are access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, environmental assessment and pollution control. WHO IT SUITS: anyone who does not yet know which lawyer to call — knock on FRONT 21/42's door first, and use the network only if your problem crosses a border. The network itself does not take individual cases; its members do. YOUR NATIONAL MEMBER IS FRONT 21/42 (front.org.mk) — go to them, not to the network. J&E members serve as environmental law ‘service points’ in their countries, handling cases, participating in legislative processes and sometimes providing legal analyses and consultations for national governments. The network has 11 full and 4 associate members, and can launch infringement proceedings against faulty governments — a route a national body alone does not have. CURRENT SCOPE: access to justice under the Aarhus Convention, climate, environmental assessments, and the Environmental Liability Directive. It previously worked on waste, transport, health and Natura 2000, so an older document may overstate what it covers today.

trackers.name: FRONT 21/42
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: North Macedonia's member organisation in the Justice and Environment network of European environmental-law NGOs. It is the only green-law contact point the network names for the country. WHO IT SUITS: anyone in North Macedonia with an environmental permit or access-to-justice problem and nowhere else to start; the scope of work it accepts is not stated on the network's page, so ask first. Domain unverified this session — reach them through the member list on justiceandenvironment.org. No website or directory listing could be verified for FRONT 21/42 across two rounds of searching, so none is given rather than guessing a plausible domain. Do not substitute the Regional Environmental Center country office in Skopje (mk.rec.org) — that is a different organisation. A targeted search in Macedonian is the next step. DOMAIN NOW CONFIRMED: front.org.mk, taken from Justice and Environment's own members page, which lists each national member organisation with its own website. The fallback route this entry originally gave — go to the network's member list — is what produced it. Recorded for provenance: two earlier search rounds found no primary domain for this organisation and deliberately declined to guess the obvious .mk address; the domain here is the one J&E publishes beside its member's name, not an inference.

trackers.name: State Audit Office (DZR)
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of North Macedonia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Center for Investigative Journalism SCOOP-Macedonia
trackers.desc: North Macedonian investigative-journalism center reporting on corruption and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: E-nabavki
trackers.desc: North Macedonia's electronic public-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in North Macedonia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Investigative Reporting Lab
trackers.desc: North Macedonian nonprofit newsroom focused on corruption, crime and governance.

trackers.name: Central Registry
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Open Data Macedonia
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in North Macedonia.

trackers.name: State Statistical Office
trackers.desc: North Macedonia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in North Macedonia.

trackers.name: Студија за валоризација — no study, no protection: fund that first
trackers.desc: THE GATE, AND THE THING TO ASK FOR. Under the Закон за заштита на природата, only with a completed valorisation study can an initiative to declare or re-declare a protected area be submitted. These studies need field research, expert data processing and multiple expert profiles, so the cost of professionally preparing the documentation is part of the real financial framework of protection. AND THAT COST IS WHERE CAMPAIGNS DIE: the Jablanica citizens' initiative reached the Government in 2019 and received support at a working session — but funds for the valorisation study were not allocated, so legal protection could not proceed. Political support was not enough. Unlike Montenegro and Turkey, where the state funds the study by statute, here the money is discretionary — so make funding for the valorisation study the explicit ask, not protection in the abstract. WHAT THE STUDY CONTAINS, from Šar Planina: published data plus 2 years of field research on geodiversity, climate and pedology, flora, fungi and fauna, ecosystems and landscapes, valorisation of natural heritage and socio-economic values, and an analysis of threats — which is where a specific development belongs.

trackers.name: The Vodno precedent — a city council initiated the protection
trackers.desc: A SEQUENCE WORTH COPYING EXACTLY. The proposal to declare Vodno a protected area in category V — protected landscape was submitted to the ministry by the City of Skopje (letter of 29 April 2020), based on a decision adopted by the Council of the City of Skopje. That decision was itself preceded by preparation of the Study, communication by the expert team with affected parties, and analysis of development and natural-resource-use plans, the area's size, its population, the needs of the population and traditional values — on which basis category V was judged best to reflect the specific interaction of people and nature there, consistent with IUCN standards. SO: study → engagement with affected parties and the population's needs → council decision → the city submits to the ministry. AND WHERE THE STUDY MONEY CAME FROM: the Vodno study was prepared inside an EU-financed IPA 2 project implemented by UNDP, while Šar Planina's was authored by UNEP with the ministry — so the practical move is finding a project to attach to rather than a grant to win.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Eko-svest, Skopje — has a community support coordinator (North Macedonia)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Centre for Environmental Research and Information Eko-svest, whose stated mission is to research, inform and act to improve public policy and practice. It employs a coordinator for community support — a named person whose job is backing local communities, which across thirty-one batches almost no organisation in this file has. It also keeps a local office at Vevčani rather than working only from Skopje, running the sustainable-management project for the Vevčani Springs protected area and the Jablanica–Karaorman biological bridge, both funded by the Prespa Ohrid Nature Trust. WHAT IT IS ALREADY FIGHTING: small hydropower inside protected areas. It points to the State Audit Office's 2021 findings on the damage those schemes cause and on irregularities in how their permits were issued, and notes that institutions carried on encouraging them regardless. Its public concern in early 2026 was that investors would start building in the window before a required study was completed — which tells a Macedonian community what to watch for: the gap between a deadline extension and the study that is supposed to fill it. It has also opposed amendments allowing permanent conversion of agricultural land into construction land for renewable projects. THE LEGAL ROUTE IT OPENS: Eko-svest is not a law firm, but it has produced regulatory analysis jointly with the Macedonian Young Lawyers Association. If your case needs counsel rather than research, that partnership is the introduction to ask for. WHAT TO BRING: it works on rivers, protected areas and energy consents. A case outside that is unlikely to be its priority, so say in the first message which protected area or watercourse is affected.

trackers.name: Macedonian Young Lawyers Association (MZMP) — free legal aid and strategic litigation
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL: an independent non-profit professional organisation established in 2003, at Donbas St. 14-6, 1000 Skopje, +389 2 3220 870, contact@myla.org.mk. It describes its expertise as free legal aid, strategic litigation and public policy development, and it is one of the leading legal organisations in North Macedonia. Around nineteen staff. WHY IT IS IN THIS FILE: it is Eko-svest's partner on regulatory analysis of renewable energy law, and it has run a project on youth activism for greener municipalities funded by the EU delegation in Skopje, publicly recruiting trainers on the legal protection of the environment. North Macedonia previously had no named counsel in this file at all — only the cross-national Justice and Environment network and two campaigning organisations. This is the domestic legal body that the country's environmental organisation goes to. HOW TO APPROACH IT: it is a human rights and rule-of-law organisation whose core caseload is asylum, statelessness, discrimination and access to justice, not planning. So do not open with the landscape. Open with the right that is being denied — access to information, exclusion from a consultation, unequal treatment of a community — because strategic litigation is what it does, and a case that changes a practice is what it selects for. Ask specifically whether the environmental strand of its work is currently funded, since that strand has run on project money. USE IT WITH EKO-SVEST: batch 31 filed Eko-svest, which has a community support coordinator and a local office at Vevčani but is not a law firm. The two have already worked together. Bring them the same case.

trackers.name: Macedonian Ecological Society — holds the country's biodiversity data
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an environmental civil society organisation founded in 1972, based at Todor Skalovski 9A, Skopje, +389 2 240 2773, contact@mes.org.mk, an IUCN member and described by IUCN as the leading national expert on ecology and environment in Macedonian civil society. It is the largest environmental CSO in the country by staff, members, volunteers and university collaborators. THE REASON TO RING IT FIRST: it holds what is almost certainly the largest collection of biodiversity data in North Macedonia, with a dedicated GIS and databases programme, and it publishes scientific material publicly. A community that needs to establish what lives on a threatened site does not need to commission a survey before it knows whether one already exists. Ask what records it holds for your location, and ask for them in a form you can attach to an objection. WHAT ELSE IT HAS DONE THAT MATTERS: it carried out the development of a national representative network of protected areas under a UNDP and GEF project on the ecological, institutional and financial sustainability of the country's protected area system — so it has already assessed which parts of the country ought to be protected and were not. If your site appeared in that work, that is a national-level finding you did not have to pay for. It also runs species recovery work including the griffon vulture across the Balkans and long-running research in Prespa. USE IT AS THE THIRD LEG: this file already holds Eko-svest for community support and a local office at Vevčani, and the Macedonian Young Lawyers Association for free legal aid and strategic litigation. This is the science. Three organisations, three jobs, all in Skopje, all reachable. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer, not a funder, not a law firm. It works through projects and scientific gatherings, so ask whether a current project covers your area — that is what determines whether anyone has time.

trackers.name: HORUS — teaches a local group to raise its own money (North Macedonia)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a North Macedonian foundation, the country's member of the SIGN network of independent south-east European foundations, working on building the capacity of civil society organisations. Its main focus is strengthening the skills to mobilise resources from local sources and to build cross-sector cooperation for solving problems in the community, along with support in devising sustainability strategies and in identifying and developing project ideas for corporate and individual donors. WHY THAT IS THE RIGHT OFFER FOR A COMMUNITY RATHER THAN THE WRONG ONE: this file has recorded again and again that international rounds are slow, that national funds are oversubscribed, and that the money which actually arrives is local. An organisation whose speciality is teaching a local group to raise money from its own town, its own businesses and its own diaspora is addressing the constraint rather than the symptom. North Macedonia had no funder of any kind in this file. SOMETHING CONCRETE TO ASK FOR: it publishes a study of how 15 different civil society organisations in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro and Kosovo raised money in their own communities. Fifteen worked examples from neighbouring countries with comparable economies is a more usable document than any general fundraising guide. WHAT IT IS NOT: not an environmental organisation, not a land buyer, not a law firm, and its grants are not the point — capacity is. Pair it with the two Macedonian bodies already in this file, the community support organisation with a coordinator and local office and the free legal aid and strategic litigation association, and with the Prespa Ohrid Nature Trust, which funds environmental actors in this region including their operating costs.

trackers.name: Agency for Personal Data Protection & Free Access to Information
trackers.desc: Agency for Personal Data Protection & Free Access to Information — Montenegro’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Agency for Prevention of Corruption (ASK)
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers, top officials & cabinet — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held; their assets, interests and integrity declarations.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Montenegro
trackers.desc: Official site of the Vrhovni sud Crne Gore with a national case-law database. · Find here: information and judgments of the Supreme Court of Montenegro.

trackers.name: Agency for Personal Data Protection & Free Access to Information (AZLP)
trackers.desc: National right-to-information authority (dual-mandate); Montenegro’s AZLP is the supervisory authority for both personal-data protection and free access to information, Montenegro.

trackers.name: Green Home (NVO Green Home, Podgorica)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Podgorica environmental organisation that RERI's regional environmental-law conference names as its Montenegrin participant, alongside the Serbian and Bosnian bodies in that circle — which makes it the country's point of contact in the Western Balkans environmental-law network. WHO IT SUITS: anyone in Montenegro looking for a first door on an environmental or land question, but note that what it will take on is not stated in the source that names it, so ask before assuming it litigates or takes casework. Domain unverified this session — only aggregator listings resolved, so no URL is given rather than a guessed one. Reach it through the participant listing on RERI's conference site at envlawcon.reri.org.rs, or via RERI in Belgrade. Green Home convenes Coalition 27, the informal network of Montenegrin NGOs that acts as the civil-society platform on EU environmental standards, and publishes a shadow report on Chapter 15.

trackers.name: Eko-fond — Fond za zaštitu životne sredine Crne Gore
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: Montenegro's state environmental fund, set up by government decision under the Law on Environment as a single-member company wholly owned by the Government, to finance the preparation, implementation and development of programmes and projects in environmental conservation, protection and improvement, energy efficiency and renewables, at both state and local level. Its founding remit expressly covers nature, soil, forests, water and the sea, and the promotion of sustainable use of natural resources, and it awards money through public calls. WHO IT SUITS: read the current call before investing effort. The awards visible on its own site skew heavily towards waste infrastructure and energy efficiency, and towards companies and municipalities rather than residents' groups — a €200,000 contract for a tyre shredder is a fair sample. HOW IT DIFFERS: it is the state's own money rather than a foundation's, so a municipality willing to sponsor your site is a far stronger route in than an association applying alone.

trackers.name: Crime and Corruption Reporting Network — LUPA
trackers.desc: Montenegrin crime-and-corruption reporting network exposing organized crime and illicit finance.

trackers.name: Center for Investigative Journalism of Montenegro (CIN-CG)
trackers.desc: Montenegrin center investigating organized crime, corruption and abuse of public funds.

trackers.name: State Audit Institution
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Montenegro, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Electronic Public Procurement (CeJN)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Montenegro, and for how much.

trackers.name: Statistical Office of Montenegro (MONSTAT)
trackers.desc: Montenegro's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Montenegro.

trackers.name: CRPS Business Registry
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Zakon o zaštiti prirode — your municipal assembly can protect land itself
trackers.desc: A ROUTE THAT DOES NOT START AT THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT. Under the Zakon o zaštiti prirode (‘Službeni list CG’ 54/16), declaration of protected natural assets — articles 55–61 — happens at the level matching the category: national assets by Government decision, but other protected natural assets by the assembly of the local self-government unit, and where an area crosses two or more municipalities the assemblies of each adopt the decision. AND THE STUDY IS PAID FOR FROM PUBLIC BUDGET, NOT BY YOU: the studija zaštite is prepared by a legal person and funds for it are provided in the budget of Montenegro or of the local self-government unit — as in Turkey, the decisive expense falls on the state. ONCE DECLARED, use must follow the studija zaštite or special purpose spatial plan and the management plan; prohibited is use causing damage to land and loss of its natural fertility or damage to geological, hydrogeological and geomorphological values. Actions not subject to impact assessment and not in the management plan need a permit from the administrative body — which is where small unassessed works get caught.

trackers.name: What the studija zaštite must contain — including the cost to owners
trackers.desc: EFFECTIVELY THE CHECKLIST FOR MAKING YOUR CASE. The study must set out: the natural, created and landscape features; the locality's characteristics and values; the existing state of resources with valorisation; an opinion on placing the asset under protection; proposed classification by significance; the proposed category and protection regime (zones); a cartographic display with boundaries drawn from cadastral real estate data; the concept of protection, improvement, sustainable development and management; and the consequences the declaration will produce, particularly for ownership rights and existing economic activities, plus possible sources of funds for implementation. THAT LAST ELEMENT IS WHERE A LOCAL CAMPAIGN IS WON OR LOST — and it is a required part of the document, so engage with it rather than leaving it to be raised against you. THREE INSTRUMENTS IN THE REGISTER WORTH KNOWING: the act on preventive protection, useful where a threat is imminent; the revision study; and the act on cessation of protection — watch for that one if protection is being removed. NGOs do feature: Montenegro's second marine protected area was credited to national institutions together with the NGO sector, naming Green Home and MEDCEM.

trackers.name: Energy Community — private bodies may complain, and refusal is appealable
trackers.desc: A COMPLAINT MECHANISM WHERE REFUSAL BY THE GATEKEEPER CAN BE TAKEN OVER ITS HEAD — which is rare, and is the reason to know about this. Under Article 90 of the Energy Community Treaty, private bodies may approach the Secretariat with complaints about a Party's non-compliance, and under Article 12.2 of the Consolidated Rules the Secretariat initiates procedures in response to a complaint by a private body as well as on its own initiative. AND IF THE SECRETARIAT DECLINES: the revised Rules give the complainant the right to approach the Permanent High Level Group directly, which may hear the complaint directly or initiate a preliminary procedure — in most systems recorded in this map, a secretariat declining to act ends the matter. The PHLG can also take interim measures in matters of urgency under Article 47(c) — that is what matters when works are already under way, so ask for it expressly. THE ENVIRONMENTAL ACQUIS IS IN SCOPE, including the EIA Directive as amended by 2014/52, which was to be transposed by 1 January 2019. CHECK THE TRANSPOSITION DEADLINE FOR THE DIRECTIVE YOU RELY ON — failure to transpose by the stated date is itself the non-compliance, and is a far simpler case than arguing about how a rule was applied. THE REALISTIC WIN CONDITION: a case opens with an Opening Letter, escalates to a Reasoned Opinion giving two months to rectify, then to the Ministerial Council — but a case closes whenever the Party complies, and many are recorded as complied with before any decision was adopted. The opening of proceedings is the lever, not the final decision. YOU CAN ALSO JOIN AN EXISTING CASE: interested third parties may access the case file and submit written observations, provided they substantiate their legitimate interest. Case law from Opening Letters is published with dates and numbers, so precedent is visible. Write to the Energy Community Secretariat, Am Hof 4, 1010 Vienna. ONE MORE ROUTE: the amended Rules provide for cooperation with national authorities and courts, giving concrete assistance to national courts on the interpretation of Energy Community law — a domestic judge unsure how an EU-derived rule applies can be pointed at it.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: MANS — investigates the permit and files the criminal complaint (Montenegro)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Montenegrin investigative organisation that takes building and planning cases apart on the documents and then puts them in front of the state prosecutor. It has filed a criminal complaint over unlawful construction against a sitting minister of ecology, spatial planning and urbanism and his son, having compared site conditions from 2018 with the present to show that work continued after the legalisation request had been formally refused. WHAT IT ACTUALLY PRODUCES, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART FOR A COMMUNITY: the Valdanos case in Ulcinj is the model. It established that a building permit had been issued for a structure inside an olive grove where the municipality's own spatial-urban plan forbids construction and the governing plan reserves the land for olive growing; that the Olive Growing Act separately bars residential building there; that the municipality later added a use permit; and that the same operation had drawn close to €140,000 of IPARD agricultural support intended for farm production. A community can supply the local knowledge; MANS assembles the paper trail that makes it actionable. WHAT TO EXPECT: this is an anti-corruption investigator, not a legal aid office. It selects its cases, it works from documents, and it is politically exposed in a small country — expect the association to be attacked rather than the findings. Bring it dates, parcel numbers, permit references and photographs from before and after, because that is the material its cases are built from. A complaint to a prosecutor is also a slower and less certain route than an administrative challenge, so it is best used alongside one rather than instead of it.

trackers.name: fAKT — funds informal local groups, and prioritises outside Podgorica (Montenegro)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Fund for Active Citizenship, a local non-governmental grantmaking foundation at Vaka Đurovića 20/1, Nova Varoš II, 81000 Podgorica, +382 20 665 600, fond@faktcg.org. It supports citizens' initiatives that tackle problems people face in their own communities, using local resources, and its stated aims include strengthening communities by backing initiatives that come from the local community rather than being brought to it. Montenegro's only other money in this file is a state fund. THE TWO ELIGIBILITY FACTS THAT MATTER MOST, AND THEY ARE UNUSUAL: its grant calls have been aimed explicitly at less developed organisations, local informal groups, activists and civic movements — and particularly those outside Podgorica. A village committee with no legal form, in a place a long way from the capital, is not an awkward fit here; it is the intended applicant. Across 138 candidates only the Belgian foundation in batch 47 has been as explicit about taking unincorporated groups. GRANT SIZES TO PLAN AROUND: recent small-grant schemes have run €3,000 to €6,000 per project. Its wider programme has combined three grant streams — community in action, active participation and public advocacy — with mentoring, capacity building and peer learning, aimed deliberately at newly formed organisations and informal groups in less developed parts of the country. The public advocacy stream is the one to ask about if the problem is a decision rather than a project. WHAT IT IS NOT: not an environmental funder, not a land buyer and not a law firm. Frame the application as citizens organising to solve a concrete local problem and to take part in a public decision, which is precisely what it exists to fund. It belongs to the regional SIGN network of independent foundations alongside its Bosnian, Serbian, Kosovar and Macedonian counterparts, which is the route to the equivalent body in a neighbouring country.

trackers.name: CRNVO's konkursi page — every open Montenegrin call in one place, including two on nature
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the running list of open calls (konkursi) for Montenegrin non-governmental organisations, published by CRNVO, the country's NGO resource centre. Montenegro already has fAKT and the Eko-fond in this file; what it lacked was the page that tells you what is open right now. THE TWO CALLS THAT MATTER MOST, both from the Ministry of Ecology, Sustainable Development and Development of the North: a javni konkurs distributing funds to non-governmental organisations for protected species of the Natura 2000 network, and a javni konkurs distributing funds to non-governmental organisations for the protection of Montenegro's breeding birds. The deadline for applications to these calls is 30 days from the day of publication, which is short — watch the page rather than waiting to hear. AND MUNICIPALITIES RUN THEIR OWN: the page also carries municipal calls, such as Danilovgrad's annual public competition for the distribution of funds to non-governmental organisations, again with a 30-day window. Your own municipality may fund you to oppose what another arm of it is permitting, and in a country of this size the municipal call may be the least contested money available. WHO MAY APPLY, from the national co-financing rules: non-governmental organisations registered and operating in Montenegro, with projects carried out wholly or partly in Montenegro, either as project holder or as partner in implementation. Registration in the Register of Non-Governmental Associations must be completed within 20 days of a proper and complete application — so an unincorporated group can become eligible quickly. IT ALSO CARRIES CIVIL-SOCIETY CALLS ISSUED BY NGOs THEMSELVES, including a public call issued jointly by MANS — already filed here as Montenegro's permit investigator — and another association.

trackers.name: Natural Justice: Lawyers for Communities and the Environment
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an African public-interest law organisation — lawyers and paralegals working with communities facing mining, oil and gas, logging and large infrastructure, combining legal empowerment, community protocols, policy work and litigation. Hubs in Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar, staff in Madagascar, Botswana and Guinea, and country programmes in Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal and South Africa. It also runs the Environmental Lawyers Collective for Africa and an EIA Process Tracker. WHO IT SUITS: an Indigenous or rural community whose land, water or customary rights are threatened by an extractive or infrastructure project. It takes selected cases and works project-to-project outside its programme countries, so expect an approach-and-assess conversation rather than open intake. IS THERE AN OFFICE NEAR YOU? YES — Nairobi (East Africa hub). Natural Justice keeps 3 hubs: Cape Town, Nairobi and Dakar. A hub means staff on the ground rather than a project relationship. WHAT IT DOES: founded 2007 in Cape Town, it supports communities to know the law, use the law and shape the law — access to land and governance of natural resources, the struggle against harmful extractive and infrastructure developments, traditional knowledge and benefit sharing, community rights within conservation, and climate action. ITS SIGNATURE TOOL IS THE COMMUNITY PROTOCOL — a documented instrument letting a community set out its biological, cultural and spiritual resources, norms and values, and assert existing rights under customary, domestic and international law, aimed squarely at laws and projects developed by government and industry without consultation. Ask for it by name. Contact: 63 Hout Street, Cape Town 8001; +27 21 426 1633; info@naturaljustice.org.

trackers.name: African Environmental Defenders Fund (emergency grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: the African Environmental Defenders Fund — an emergency grant fund run by Natural Justice with the International Land Coalition Africa, ICCA Consortium, PACJA, Oxfam Novib, FEMNET and others, giving up to US$5,000 to land and environmental defenders anywhere in Africa who are under threat because of their activism. It can cover the cost of legal representation where a defender is arrested, summoned or prosecuted, plus relocation and other short-term transitional costs. WHO IT SUITS: an individual frontline defender who is a citizen or legal resident of an African country, facing an imminent threat, and not already supported by another body — it is not project or core funding, and routine office and administrative costs are excluded. HOW IT DIFFERS: applications are rolling, by email or helpline, not to a grant round. Natural Justice's own site names Burkina Faso, Guinea, Kenya, Madagascar, Namibia, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Botswana as its country programmes, which is where this entry is placed; the fund's stated eligibility is any African country, so apply from elsewhere on the continent too.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: Business Registration Service
trackers.desc: Kenya's Business Registration Service company registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC)
trackers.desc: Kenya’s statutory anti-corruption body — investigates graft, enforces integrity law and recovers corruptly-acquired assets.

trackers.name: e-GP Kenya
trackers.desc: Kenya's national electronic government-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Kenya, and for how much.

trackers.name: ICJ Kenya (Kenyan Section, International Commission of Jurists)
trackers.desc: Nairobi-based NGO of jurists drawn from the Bar and Bench (founded 1959) that works to develop and protect the independence of the judiciary and legal profession in Kenya, monitor judicial reform and integrity, and advance freedom of information.

trackers.name: Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA-Kenya)
trackers.desc: Independent Kenyan public-policy think-tank (est. 1994) producing analysis of the national budget, taxation and economic policy and promoting informed public debate. Here you can trace Kenya's budget, taxation and economic policy, analysed independently.

trackers.name: Kenya Law
trackers.desc: National Council for Law Reporting: official free database of Kenyan judgments and legislation. · Find here: free Kenyan case-law, the Kenya Gazette and legislation (National Council for Law Reporting / Kenya Law).

trackers.name: Public Procurement Portal
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Kenya, and for how much.

trackers.name: Transparency International Kenya (TI-Kenya)
trackers.desc: Transparency International's Kenya chapter (since 1999). Anti-corruption research and advocacy, runs Advocacy and Legal Advice Centres, and works on transparency in public procurement, devolved government, the extractives sector and humanitarian aid.

trackers.name: TISA — The Institute for Social Accountability
trackers.desc: Kenyan civil-society institute (since 2008) promoting social accountability and good governance, with a strong focus on devolution and county governments. Tracks national and county public finance management and budgets, campaigns on public debt and fiscal accountability (Okoa Uchumi), and equips citizens and oversight institutions to hold duty-bearers to account between elections.

trackers.name: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics
