trackers.name: Hima — a village with no municipal council still has a route
trackers.desc: THE MOST ACCESSIBLE DESIGNATION ROUTE IN THIS ENTIRE MAP. Under Protected Areas Framework Law 130/2019, a Hima — one of four categories alongside nature reserves, natural sites and natural parks — is established by decision of the municipal council, or joint councils where it spans several municipalities. AND IN VILLAGES WITH NO MUNICIPAL COUNCIL AT ALL, the Hima is designated by the district commissioner (Qa'im Maqam) on a proposal from the village chief (Mukhtar). Almost every route recorded here assumes a functioning local authority; Lebanon provides an explicit fallback for villages that have none. A Hima designation requires only the consent of the local municipality. The council — or commissioner — then develops a management plan; across municipalities, a committee formed by the commissioner or governor does. THE TEMPLATE TO COPY: Hima Aaiha, Lebanon's 40th, formalised by Municipal Decision No. 4/2025, adopted unanimously in a legally convened session on 9 August 2025, over public state land, cadastral parcel No. 2327, based on environmental and scientific studies. A numbered decision, a unanimous vote, a named parcel, a scientific basis. AND IT IS NOT EXCLUSIONARY: Hima exist for sustainable hunting, fishing, grazing and water use — 25 covering 6 percent of Lebanese territory.

trackers.name: The framework law's decrees were never issued — which is why Hima works
trackers.desc: KNOW THE GAP BEFORE YOU RELY ON THE LAW. Law 130/2019 foresees a minimum of five application decrees and two ministerial decisions — none of which have been adopted to date, and the law details management only for nature reserves. The framework is enacted but its implementing instruments are not. That is precisely why the Hima route matters in practice: it runs on a municipal decision, not on a decree that has never been issued. IF YOUR SITE IS PRIVATE LAND: a nature reserve on private property is established after the written consent of all owners, by contract between the state (the Minister of Environment) and the owners, for not less than 20 years, renewable, defining the scope, the surrounding belt zone and management — reserves on public land are established by a law instead. Note that natural sites are still governed by the law of 8 July 1939 on protection of landscapes, reading ‘Ministry of National Economy’ as Ministry of Environment. TARGETS TO QUOTE: by 2030, at least 20 percent of natural terrestrial and marine ecosystems protected with all ecosystem types represented, and nature reserve coverage raised to at least 5 percent of Lebanon's area. A Hima proposal also wants a local Hima committee of community members, environmental activists and municipal representatives.

trackers.name: Lebanon Reforestation Initiative — registered, and it does quarry restoration
trackers.desc: A DELIVERY PARTNER WITH A REGISTRATION NUMBER YOU CAN QUOTE. LRI is a not-for-profit NGO registered at the Lebanese Ministry of Interior under no. 1186 of 16 June 2014 — useful when a counterparty asks whether a partner is properly constituted. It began in 2010 as a project funded by USAID and managed by the US Forest Service International Programs, and has since supported planting of more than 850,000 native tree seedlings nationwide, improved the native seedling production sector, and contributed to best practice in reforestation, fire prevention, forest management, quarry restoration and climate resilience. QUARRY RESTORATION IS A NAMED CAPABILITY — which matters, since quarrying is among the most common land-damage complaints in Lebanon and few bodies have restoration experience for it. It works across all of Lebanon in five programme areas: landscape management, climate resilience, outreach and capacity development, advocacy, and R&D. BE CLEAR WHAT IT IS: this is a technical and delivery partner, not a grant window — approach it for partnership on restoration work and for its advocacy capacity, not to apply for money. For a community-scale grant in Lebanon, see the GEF Small Grants Programme; for the designation route, see the Hima entry recorded separately in this map.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: RTI Portal (India)
trackers.desc: You CAN get: any record, file noting, order, inspection report or status report held by a public authority, under the Right to Information Act 2005, on payment of a ₹10 fee — waived for BPL applicants. Any Indian citizen may ask; you do not have to say why. The Public Information Officer must ordinarily answer within 30 days. Know which site does what: rti.gov.in is the GATEWAY — use it to identify the right PIO and First Appellate Authority and to read proactive disclosures. Filing happens at rtionline.gov.in. You CAN'T get: state records through that filing portal. It covers CENTRAL ministries, departments and public authorities only, and an application wrongly filed there against a state body — including the Government of NCT of Delhi, which runs its own portal — is returned WITHOUT REFUND. State authorities need the relevant state portal or a postal application. An online first appeal can only follow an online application. For activists: this is how you get an environmental clearance file, a public-hearing record or project correspondence from MoEFCC or a central regulator — but a State Pollution Control Board is a state body, so check the tier before paying. If the PIO misses the 30 days or answers badly, appeal to the First Appellate Authority within 30 days, then to the Central Information Commission within 90; the Commission can order disclosure and fine the officer.

You CAN'T get: reliable machine access — the interfaces change and dataset endpoints have been dormant. trackers.name: Legal Initiative for Forest and Environment (LIFE)

Awarded the Right Livelihood Award in 2021. trackers.name: NALSA (Legal Services Authority)
trackers.desc: Constitutional body providing free legal aid to weaker sections, cascading to State and District Legal Services Authorities. · Find here: India's National Legal Services Authority — free legal aid and Lok Adalats. INDIA GATES ON THE PERSON, NOT THE CASE — which is the opposite of England and Wales, recorded separately in this map. NALSA states it in terms: ‘there is hence NO BAR AS TO WHICH KIND OF CASES one can apply and not apply for. All kinds of cases are included as long as the individual satisfies the eligibility under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.’ So the question is never whether an environmental case is covered — it is whether the person qualifies. AND TWO SECTION 12 CATEGORIES REACH ENVIRONMENTAL HARM DIRECTLY: eligibility is not based on income alone and includes members of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe and victims of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster. Flood, drought and industrial disaster are named eligibility grounds — a community harmed by an industrial release or displaced by flooding qualifies on that basis irrespective of income. Income thresholds otherwise vary by state (for example ₹3 lakhs per annum in Delhi for civil cases in the High Court). THE MERITS FILTER IS LIGHT: under section 13(1) you are entitled provided the institution is satisfied you have ‘a genuine case to prosecute or defend’ — far below a prospects-of-success test. APPLY AT DISTRICT OR TALUKA LEVEL, NOT TO NALSA: District Legal Services Authorities and Taluka Legal Services Committees handle applications; NALSA sets policy. WHAT IS PAID FOR IS BROADER THAN A LAWYER: section 2(c) covers proceedings before any court OR OTHER AUTHORITY OR TRIBUNAL, and inclusions cover process fees, witness expenses, and preparation of pleadings and paper books including document translation and printing — often decisive in a technical environmental case, where expert and document costs defeat claimants more than fees do. Aid runs from the lowest court to the Supreme Court, and you may apply at any stage. ON CHOOSING YOUR LAWYER, READ TWO RULES TOGETHER: regulation 7(6) of the 2010 Regulations lets the Member-Secretary consider a named preference from the panel — but aid can be withdrawn where the person engages a legal practitioner other than the one assigned. Express a preference among panel lawyers; bringing in an outside practitioner ends the aid.

trackers.name: National Green Tribunal — file an application
trackers.desc: THE FORUM TO FILE IN: established under the NGT Act 2010 and functioning since 4 July 2011. STANDING IS OPEN — you do not need to be directly affected; anyone with an interest in protecting the environment may bring a case, which removes the barrier that stops most communities elsewhere. It is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 and is guided by principles of natural justice, so a case is less likely to die on pleading technicalities, and it is mandated to dispose of applications within 6 months of filing. Applications may be filed online after registering, or offline. It can review violations and also orders or decisions of Government under the Schedule I laws. THE JURISDICTIONAL HOLE, CHECK IT BEFORE YOU FILE: the NGT has no jurisdiction over the Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972, the Indian Forest Act 1927, or state forest and tree-preservation laws — a tree-felling or forest matter under those Acts must instead go as a Writ Petition by Public Interest Litigation to the State High Court or Supreme Court, or as an original suit before the civil judge in the taluk where the project lies. PRECEDENT WORTH CITING: the NGT has held that an entire dam proposal must be placed before the village council for approval under the Forest Rights Act — consent over the whole project, not a fragment of it.

trackers.name: CSR funding and the CSR-1 gate
trackers.desc: INDIA'S BIGGEST REALISTIC FUNDING CHANNEL IS CORPORATE, AND IT IS STATUTORY. Under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013, companies above a threshold (net worth ₹500 crore, turnover ₹1,000 crore, or net profit ₹5 crore) must spend at least 2 percent of average net profit on CSR, and Schedule VII lists environmental sustainability and conservation among its 14 permitted categories. Roughly ₹25,000–30,000 crore is spent yearly across more than 18,000 companies. THE GATE IS ABSOLUTE: no NGO can legally receive CSR money from any company without CSR-1 registration with the Registrar of Companies on the MCA portal, mandatory since 1 April 2021. AND THE 2025 CHANGE MATTERS MOST TO NEW GROUPS: from 14 July 2025, only NGOs with valid 12A registration and a 3-year track record can register on CSR-1 — a group formed to fight a specific development cannot register and must work through an already-eligible implementing partner. WHAT CSR-1 NEEDS: Trust, Society or Section 8 form; trust deed or incorporation certificate, 12A, 80G if held, PAN; a Class 3 DSC belonging to someone formally authorised in the trust deed or board resolution (old DSCs of former trustees cause rejections); and certification by a practising CA, CS or CMA. Your last 3 years of activities must be mapped specifically to Schedule VII categories — ‘activities not clearly mapped to Schedule VII’ is a stated rejection reason. PRACTICALITIES: the money must be spent within India, a foreign NGO needs a registered Indian partner, administrative costs are capped by agreement at roughly 5–10 percent, and expect 3–6 months from first approach to first disbursement.

trackers.name: Right of Passage — four models for securing a corridor
trackers.desc: FOUR WAYS LAND GETS SECURED IN INDIA, from the organisation that has done most of it. Private purchase: buy the land with partners, rehabilitate affected people, then transfer it to the state forest department for legal protection — note the endpoint, the NGO does not keep it, and legal protection comes from the state. Community securement: community-owned land set aside through easements or bilateral benefit-sharing, with no transfer of ownership. Government acquisition: policy advocacy and support to the state. Plus a network of Green Corridor Champions institutionalising community organisations in corridor protection. THE STRUCTURAL POINT, TRANSFERABLE ANYWHERE: Elephant Reserves include areas of human use and, unless they fall inside Reserve Forests or the Protected Area network, are not legally protected habitats — designation on a map is not protection. The project mapped 88 corridors from 2005 and now lists 101. Funders record that purchasing even a small land parcel can be highly effective when done meticulously by a body that works well with local communities. NOW THE OTHER HALF, AND READ IT BEFORE COPYING THE MODEL: peer-reviewed research in Environmental Management describes a conservation-agrarian squeeze in South India — farmers whose land was identified for acquisition were already facing state neglect of agriculture, rising debt and unstable weather; the concept note proposed acquisition or a land-for-land deal, but farmers said only monetary compensation was provided; and the plan opened with ‘entry point activities’ such as a health camp. If you secure land this way, land-for-land must be delivered and not merely offered.

trackers.name: District Legal Services Authority — free lawyer in every district
trackers.desc: A FREE LAWYER, IN EVERY DISTRICT, BY STATUTE. Under the Legal Services Authorities Act 1987 — given force by Article 39A of the Constitution — legal services institutions run from national down to taluka level, and the District Legal Services Authority exists in every district. ELIGIBILITY IS BY WHO YOU ARE, NOT WHAT THE CASE IS. Under Section 12 the entitled include: a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe; a woman — irrespective of income or financial status; a child under 18; a mentally ill or disabled person; a person in custody; a victim of trafficking; and anyone affected by a mass disaster, ethnic or caste violence, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster. Otherwise, anyone below the income ceiling set by their State Government (below Rs 5 lakh for a Supreme Court case) — and under Section 13(2) an affidavit of income is generally enough proof. THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR A LAND FIGHT: Section 13(1) means there is no bar on the type of case — all kinds are included so long as the person qualifies and the institution is satisfied there is a genuine case to prosecute or defend. An environmental or land matter is not excluded; only the applicant's status is tested. WHAT YOU GET: representation by an advocate; process fees and witness expenses paid; pleadings and memos of appeal prepared, including printing and translation of documents; drafting of legal documents and special leave petitions; certified copies of judgments and evidence. Available at any stage and from the lowest court to the Supreme Court — and you can seek a second opinion from panel lawyers even while using a private lawyer.

trackers.name: Community Forest Resource rights — Form C and two pieces of evidence
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE THAT SHIFTS GOVERNANCE, NOT JUST TENURE. Section 3(1)(i) of the Forest Rights Act 2006 vests in a community the right to protect, regenerate, conserve or manage any community forest resource it has traditionally protected — defined in section 2(a) as customary common forest land within the village's traditional boundaries, including reserved and protected forests, accessed before 13 December 2005. Recognition moves forest management from the Forest Department to the Gram Sabha. THE PROCEDURE: the Gram Sabha resolves to initiate and elects a Forest Rights Committee of 10 to 15 members; the FRC demarcates the customary boundary and prepares maps, which may include reserved forest, protected forest, national park or sanctuary; the claim goes on Form C. EVIDENCE — AT LEAST 2 FORMS ARE REQUIRED UNDER RULE 13: gazetteers, revenue and forest records, elders' statements, traditional structures, and physical features such as sacred groves or burial grounds. Forest and Revenue officials shall be present at site verification and shall sign the proceedings with their designation — get those signatures. Then Gram Sabha resolution → SDLC → DLC under the District Collector, which is the final authority. WHO MAY CLAIM: Scheduled Tribes depending on the forest, and others resident for 3 generations (75 years) before the cut-off.

trackers.name: FRA in practice — rejection rates, and check who is on your FRC
trackers.desc: KNOW THE FAILURE MODES BEFORE YOU FILE. Only Forest Rights Committees and the Gram Sabha may receive, reject or modify a claim at block, panchayat, forest or range level — and in Chhattisgarh, patwaris and forest guards were illegally included in FRCs to manipulate decisions at Gram Sabha level. Check your FRC's composition against the Rules. REJECTION IS THE NORM, NOT THE EXCEPTION: in Karnataka in 2021, of 2.81 lakh applications about 1.8 lakh were rejected; in Shivamogga district 44,016 of 97,074. Recurring causes: rejection of OTFD claims for failing to produce written 75-year evidence, rejection without reasons or a hearing, weak revenue surveys blocking demarcation, and forest department resistance to handing over CFR governance. WHERE IT HAS WORKED: in Vidarbha, Maharashtra, much of the region's potential CFR was recognised in the name of Gram Sabhas — attributed to Gram Sabhas acting collectively together with NGOs, grassroots organisations and state implementing agencies. AND A STRUCTURAL UPGRADE TO PUSH FOR: Maharashtra, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh have recognised Gram Sabhas as body corporates under PESA 1996, giving them legal personality as self-governing institutions.

trackers.name: Sahabat Alam Malaysia (Friends of the Earth Malaysia)

trackers.name: Native Customary Rights — which state you are in decides everything
trackers.desc: ESTABLISH THE LEGAL GEOGRAPHY FIRST. NCR is an official term in Sabah and Sarawak only: the Sarawak Land Code 1958 and Sabah Land Ordinance 1930 set out how it is acquired and extinguished by the state, and forestry and conservation law in both states provides for extinguishment and compensation when an area is gazetted. IN PENINSULAR MALAYSIA, Orang Asli customary land rights are not mentioned at all by any land, forestry or conservation legislation — a Peninsular community cannot rely on this framework. In Sarawak, Native Customary Land covers land where NCR was created before 1 January 1958 and still subsists, land in a Communal Native Reserve gazetted under section 6, and Interior Area Land where NCR has been created. THE BLUNT POSITION, FROM MALAYSIAN CIVIL SOCIETY: holders of usufructuary rights may use and benefit from the land, but with or without title or reserve status, from the state's perspective the land is still its property — and where transfers are permitted at all they may only be between people legally recognised as members of indigenous communities.

trackers.name: What NCR claims must prove — and how far the courts have retreated
trackers.desc: WHAT IS CLAIMED: Iban claims distinguish temuda (cultivated land) from the wider pemakai menua (communal territorial domain) and pulau — reserved virgin forest kept for domestic needs: timber for boats and houses, fruit trees, medicinal jungle produce, hunting and fishing grounds. THE HIGH POINTS: in Nor Anak Nyawai [2001] 2 CLJ 769 pemakai menua and pulau were recognised as Native Customary Land; and the Federal Court held that NCR pre-existed any statute, so reserving land under the Rajah's Order of 1921 for an oil company did not extinguish it. NOW THE RETREAT, AND IT IS THE REASON TO GET ADVICE BEFORE FILING: in 2016, in Director of Forest, Sarawak v TR Sandah Tabau, the Federal Court held by majority that common law recognition did not extend to the broader pemakai menua; commentary records the courts again declining to uphold Iban claims in 2021. Common law NCR rights have been severely restricted in Sarawak and Sabah, the evidentiary burden falls hardest on orally transmitted cultures, and even recognised NCR land can be reclassified unilaterally into Native Communal Reserves, giving the state discretion over use often without community consent. HELP THAT EXISTS: SACCESS produced a guidebook for Sarawak NCR landowners using the civil courts — which also warns that state surveys of selected NCR land, presented as granting titles and recognition, have been read as an attempt to quiet discontent rather than to recognise rights fully.

trackers.name: Hasanah Micro Grant — open year-round, but only once per organisation
trackers.desc: GRASSROOTS MONEY ON UNUSUALLY GOOD TERMS. Yayasan Hasanah, the grant-making foundation under Khazanah Nasional established 1 July 2015, funds five areas including alam sekitar (environment). The micro grant gives up to RM 50,000 per project over 6 to 12 months. APPLICATIONS ARE OPEN YEAR-ROUND and reviewed quarterly — rare, when most funds in this map have one annual window of a few weeks. Eligible: registered NGOs, non-profits, civil society and community-based organisations active for at least 6 months, one of the shortest track-record requirements anywhere here. TWO RULES THAT DECIDE ELIGIBILITY: organisations that have previously received Yayasan Hasanah funding are not eligible — so this favours newcomers, and an existing grantee should not spend time applying; and you must implement directly, not as an intermediary, managing the project yourself and engaging the community directly. WHAT TO SUBMIT: organisational profile, financial records, and objectives, target communities, approach and expected outcomes. Stated failure causes: previous Hasanah support, missing financial documentation or profile, and proposals lacking clarity, feasibility or a community engagement plan. PILOTS ARE WELCOME — the programme explicitly encourages experimentation. Funded work has included permeable bamboo wave screens installed by a community at Tanjung Kepah, and work with Bateq children of the Orang Asli community — so coastal protection and Orang Asli community work are both in scope. The larger annual Hasanah Grant and the Hasanah Special Grant, run with the Ministry of Finance, cover the same areas.

trackers.name: Sahabat Alam Malaysia (Friends of the Earth Malaysia)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Malaysia's oldest environmental organisation, founded in 1977 — pollution and extractives, land use and planning, deforestation, marine and fisheries, agriculture and Indigenous customary land rights, from a head office in Penang and a field office at Marudi in the Baram, Sarawak. Legal support is one strand of a campaigning organisation rather than a separate law practice: it briefs and backs communities through planning and permit challenges, was closely involved in the litigation over planning permission for the Penang South Reclamation, and publishes plain-language explainers on customary land rights and on the legal classes of Malaysian forest and conservation area. WHO IT SUITS: a community facing a quarry, reclamation, plantation, dam or forest-carbon project — especially in Sarawak, where the Marudi office is the contact point. Expect campaigning support, evidence and referral rather than a retainer.

trackers.name: 特別緑地保全地区 — designation that forces a purchase
trackers.desc: A DESIGNATION THAT FREEZES LAND, AND THEN MAKES THE CITY BUY IT. Under Article 12 of the Urban Green Space Act a Special Green Space Conservation District preserves green space in its current state by requiring permission for new building, rebuilding or extension; land reclamation, clearing, quarrying or mining or any change to the form or quality of land; felling of trees and bamboo; and filling or draining water surfaces. Permission comes from the ward or city, or the prefecture for towns and villages. The district is decided by the municipality — or by the prefecture where it is 10 hectares or more and spans 2 or more municipalities. THE PART THAT INVERTS THE USUAL PROBLEM: where the restrictions significantly hinder use of the land, the owner may apply to the ward or city to buy it, and the municipality, prefecture or a designated green space conservation body is required to buy — with JPY 20 million of the transfer income deducted, reducing income tax. Elsewhere conservation depends on persuading an owner to sell; here designation creates a right to compel the purchase. TWO COMPANION TOOLS THAT REDUCE THE BURDEN OF HOLDING LAND: a 管理協定 (management agreement) has the authority carry out the management instead of the owner, and the 市民緑地 scheme opens the land to residents.

trackers.name: 市民緑地制度 — open private land to residents by contract
trackers.desc: A CONTRACT ROUTE WHEN PURCHASE IS NOT POSSIBLE. Under Article 55 of the Urban Green Space Act a local authority or a green space body contracts with a landowner to establish and manage a 市民緑地 — green space or greening facilities on land, artificial ground, buildings or other structures, opened for residents' use. CONDITIONS: land of 300 m² or more inside a city planning area; land inside Special Green Space Conservation Districts and green space conservation areas also qualifies; and the contract term is at least 5 years. Under Article 60 a private body may instead establish and manage one under a citizens' green space plan certified by the mayor. USE IT: this keeps title with the owner while securing public access and management — the middle option between doing nothing and raising a purchase price.

trackers.name: 地球環境基金 — the national grant for environmental NGOs and NPOs
trackers.desc: JAPAN'S STANDING GRANT FOR PRIVATE ENVIRONMENTAL GROUPS, run by ERCA and built from government investment plus corporate and public donations, operating on the investment return with expert committee advice. Its stated aim is to support the autonomy, independence and diversity of environmental NGOs and NPOs. ELIGIBLE FIELDS run to 10 categories, and the useful ones here come first: nature protection, conservation and restoration; forest conservation and greening; environmentally conscious agriculture; air, water and soil environment conservation; comprehensive environmental conservation activity. A borderline classification is not fatal — the activity field may be changed during the review process. THE CYCLE: recruitment is in principle once a year, in the year before the activity year, with timing and eligibility set out in an annual 募集案内; a recorded window ran 14 October to 17 November 2025 with awards announced the following March. Briefings are held across 8 regions, and for online sessions you may attend any region's briefing wherever you are. ERCA also publishes a general list of NGO/NPO grant schemes and a searchable list of past grantees by area and field — a fast way to see who near you has been funded and for what.

trackers.name: Applying — the non-profit-type condition and the system-only submission
trackers.desc: TWO THINGS THAT SINK APPLICATIONS. 1. THE NON-PROFIT-TYPE CONDITION: a 一般社団法人 or 一般財団法人 must meet the 非営利型法人 (non-profit-type corporation) requirements under corporation tax law. If you do not meet them when you apply, transitioning to non-profit type by the grant application submission — around May of the funding year — is a condition of the award decision. So you may apply mid-conversion, but the conversion must complete before the money is confirmed; start it now if it applies to you. 2. THE WORD FILE IS NOT THE SUBMISSION: requests go through the 地球環境基金助成金申請システム online. A Word draft and a submission manual are provided, but the Word file is for drafting only — you must transcribe each item into the system, so budget time for that rather than assuming you can attach the document. Applications are examined by the fund's operating committee and paid under the 交付要綱. Contact: 地球環境基金部, 044-520-9505.

trackers.name: JELF — 400+ environmental lawyers, in all 47 prefectures
trackers.desc: WHO TO CALL, AND THEY ARE EVERYWHERE. JELF has more than 400 lawyers as full members across all 47 prefectures — so it is usable from anywhere, not only the big cities. Many lawyers from Japan's four great pollution lawsuits, the origin of its environmental law, remain members, and successors have worked on dioxin and asbestos. IT LITIGATES AGAINST LARGE PUBLIC WORKS: the Isahaya Bay reclamation in Nagasaki, the Henoko base in Okinawa and the Linear Shinkansen, framing its aim as stopping environmental destruction from wasteful public investment. Ecosystem cases are core — including litigation with the Amami rabbit as plaintiff, and cases for the Ezo pika and Blakiston's fish owl. BE REALISTIC: its own news records losses — in the Kadoku beach ‘rights of nature’ case on Amami Ōshima the Supreme Court declined to accept the plaintiffs' appeal on 23 May 2025, leaving the rejections below standing.

trackers.name: JELF local government support — get your municipality to act
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE MOST COMMUNITIES DO NOT KNOW EXISTS. JELF runs a project team supporting municipalities to protect the local natural and living environment, whose members serve as in-house municipal lawyers, municipal advisers and members of councils and expert committees. It offers drafting of ordinances (条例策定) and legal advice, firm handling of illegal operators carrying out fly-tipping of waste and construction spoil, and sharing of advanced cases and know-how across its national network — and it invites municipalities to consult freely. It expressly names the problem as developers acting without regard to local conditions, citing large-scale disorderly renewable energy development destroying natural and living environments. THE TACTIC: if your group cannot litigate itself, persuading your municipality to seek this help — and to enact a local ordinance — may be the stronger route, because the ordinance binds future developments rather than fighting one at a time.

trackers.name: 日弁連 公害対策・環境保全委員会 — opinion papers that get revisited
trackers.desc: THE BAR FEDERATION TREATS POLLUTION HARM AS A HUMAN RIGHTS ISSUE. The JFBA began with a special committee inside its human rights committee, established an independent pollution committee in May 1969, and renamed it to its present form in 1985. It now has 7 sub-committees plus project teams, working through research, 意見書 (opinion papers), symposia and publications to advance national and local environmental policy and prevent environmental destruction. A METHOD WORTH COPYING: a project team formed in March 2014, before approval of the Linear Chuo Shinkansen construction plan, issued an opinion that approval should not be given until environmental concerns were resolved — then went back 5 years later, in 2019, to investigate Ōshika village in Nagano where the South Alps tunnel generates vast spoil, and Kasugai in Aichi where disposal of spoil containing naturally occurring arsenic and fluorine is contested, and held a public session on which predicted harms had materialised — returning again in November 2022. An objection is worth far more when someone documents, years later, that it was right.

You CAN'T get: the approval agency's internal deliberations. For activists: this is where you read the proponent's own study, find its gaps, and time your opinion submissions to the statutory windows.

trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a dedicated environmental legal centre whose stated purpose is to act as a partner on environmental problems that cannot be solved by an individual alone. THE PART THAT MAKES IT REACHABLE: it sits inside 환경운동연합 (KFEM, the Korean Federation for Environmental Movement) alongside the Citizens' Institute for Environmental Studies, and KFEM has 54 grassroots local organisations across the country — so a community can come to legal help through its own local chapter instead of approaching a law centre cold.

trackers.name: 환경운동연합 (KFEM) — 54 local organisations
trackers.desc: THE NATIONAL BODY WITH LOCAL PRESENCE: KFEM comprises 54 grassroots local organisations across Korea, together with the Citizens' Institute for Environmental Studies and the 환경법률센터 (Environmental Law Center), and works with allied specialist bodies. USE IT: for a site-specific fight, start with the local chapter — it is the route into research and legal support that already has people near the site.

trackers.name: 원고적격 — the standing barrier in Korean environmental cases
trackers.desc: KNOW THIS BEFORE PLANNING A CASE. Korean administrative litigation requires the plaintiff to show a 법률상 이익 — a legally protected interest — and environmental harm characteristically does not crystallise immediately into a concrete infringement, so ordinary standing and ripeness requirements sit badly on environmental cases. ENVIRONMENTAL ORGANISATIONS DO NOT CURRENTLY HAVE STANDING to sue on behalf of the environment itself. Scholarship proposes granting it to bodies with the expertise and structure to carry it, under statutory criteria and with court permission, and a legislative notice proposed widening 법률상 이익 to 법적 이익 so the constitutional environmental right could ground an administrative remedy — but that is a reform proposal, not present law. The Seoraksan cable car case is the standard illustration of how far current administrative litigation falls short of preventing damage to the natural environment. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: build the case around individually affected residents who can show their own legal interest — an association cannot stand in for nature here, which is the opposite of the German position.

trackers.name: 한국내셔널트러스트 — buy the land with citizens' donations
trackers.desc: AN ORGANISATION WHOSE BUSINESS IS BUYING LAND THAT DEVELOPMENT WOULD OTHERWISE TAKE. The National Trust of Korea exists to preserve natural and cultural heritage at risk of disappearing through development projects, by purchasing or securing the sites with citizens' donations. Its first 시민유산 (citizens' heritage) site was the Maehwamareum colony on Ganghwa Island — a paddy wetland holding an endangered plant, designated a Ramsar site in 2008. By 2020 it held 11 citizens' heritage sites (8 natural, 3 cultural) covering 136,106 square metres, funded by about 7.84 billion won in citizen donations, including the Yeoncheon DMZ crane habitat. THE LEGAL POINT THAT MATTERS MOST: sites secured as citizens' heritage are guaranteed the principle of inalienability (양도불능의 원칙), which makes permanent preservation possible — land bought this way cannot simply be sold on, which is the difference between a purchase and a protection. HOW IT WORKS IN PRACTICE: sites are identified by the organisation or reported by the public, citizen and expert opinion is taken, the board decides, and purchase money is then raised through citizen fundraising campaigns, major donors and corporate sponsorship. You can also donate or entrust land or buildings directly, and donations attract year-end tax deduction as a designated public-interest donation body. Contact 02-3675-3401~2, ntfund@naver.com. Internationally the movement is linked through INTO, founded December 2007 across around 30 countries, though each national trust is independent.

trackers.name: 녹색서울실천사업 — Seoul's green grant, and it bars repeat winners
trackers.desc: A CITY GRANT WHERE CIVIC GROUPS PROPOSE THEIR OWN PROJECTS. Seoul's 일반사업 track is explicitly for civic organisations to put forward original projects for environmental improvement and awareness and to lead them themselves, alongside a designated track on city-chosen themes. Judging is by the city's local subsidy management committee on three criteria: suitability of purpose and content, the organisation's capacity to deliver, and the reasonableness of the budget. THE RULE THAT FAVOURS NEWCOMERS: organisations selected 3 years running, or 4 or more times in 5 years, are excluded — the reverse of the usual pattern where track record is an advantage, and it means a new or small group faces less entrenched competition here than in most schemes. MECHANICS: applications go only through the local subsidy system 보탬e (losims.go.kr) — no paper or email route — in a window of about 3 weeks once a year, with the 2026 round running 12 January to 3 February and results announced in February. WIDER ROUTES: the integrated subsidy portal 보조금통합포털, the Ministry of the Interior and Safety's NPAS support programme for non-profit private organisations, and the Ministry of Environment's open call for nature conservation organisations.

trackers.name: Wild at Heart Legal Defense Association (台灣蠻野心足生態協會)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Taiwanese public-interest environmental law association founded by the lawyer Robin Winkler, which litigates against permits and environmental impact assessments rather than only commenting on them. Its cases run to a two-decade Indigenous land-rights dispute in Hualien, the Miramar Resort built on Shanyuan beach on what it argued were illegal construction licences, industrial park developments in central and southern Taiwan, an algae reef off the north-west coast threatened by port development, the Taipei Dome, and challenges to offshore wind-farm permits it says rested on deeply flawed assessments. WHO IT SUITS: a community or Indigenous group facing a permitted project where the EIA is the weak point. It is a small association that takes strategic cases and works alongside allied groups rather than running open legal aid. Note its English-language pages carry markedly older material than the Chinese site.

trackers.desc: Taiwan's Government Commerce Industrial Services company registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Judicial Yuan – Judgment Search
trackers.desc: Official portal of Taiwan's Judicial Yuan, including the Constitutional Court and a public judgment-search system. · Find here: the Judicial Yuan's judgment search covering Taiwan's courts.

trackers.name: Government e-Procurement (PCC)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement / budget-transparency portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this shows the specific firms winning specific tenders and contracts — for aggregate budget totals use the open-data/statistics portal, and for findings of waste use the audit body. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Taiwan, and for how much.

trackers.name: Taiwan — Lobbying Act register (Ministry of the Interior)
trackers.desc: National lobbying register; under the Lobbying Act (2007) lobbyists must register with the lobbied government agency before lobbying & file annual financial statements — the Ministry of the Interior is the designated competent authority, with public access to registrations, Taiwan. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Fuchien High Court Kinmen Branch Court
trackers.desc: Fuchien High Court Kinmen Branch Court — tribunal in Taiwan (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: Fuchien Kinmen District Court
trackers.desc: Fuchien Kinmen District Court — first instance court in Taiwan (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: 環境信託 — permanent protection, but check your land category first
trackers.desc: THE MECHANISM FOR PERMANENT PRIVATE PROTECTION, AND ITS PRICE. Under the 信託法 (Trust Act, 1996) an environmental trust is covered only by the catch-all at the end of article 69 — ‘or other trusts for the purpose of public interest’ — its full name being 環境保護公益信託. An owner finds a professional organisation, or acts themselves, as 受託人 (trustee), and the trustee applies to the environment authority with the period set as permanent. WHAT IT COSTS THE OWNER, STATED PLAINLY: the land must be transferred into the trustee's name and marked as trust property; it becomes independent, the original owner no longer owns it and has no power of disposal — and equally the trustee cannot dispose of it at will, which is exactly what makes the purpose permanently enforceable. An owner wanting to manage it themselves uses a 宣言信託 (declaration of trust). CHECK YOUR PARCEL CATEGORY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: under domestic law agricultural land and indigenous reserved land cannot be placed in environmental trust with a legal person not engaged in the relevant field; forest land can. That determines whether this route is open to you at all.

trackers.name: One case in thirty years — the tax reason, and the campaign precedent
trackers.desc: BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE ODDS, AND KNOW WHY. 自然谷環境信託基地 (Natural Valley, Hsinchu, 2011) is Taiwan's first and essentially only successful environmental trust since the Trust Act of 1996 — recognised as such by the environment ministry, and eligible to become an environmental education facility under the 環境教育法. On a 2020 review Taiwan had 281 financial-type public interest trusts worth NT$72.5 billion, but only 1 environment-related affairs-type trust and zero cultural heritage trusts. THE DECISIVE OBSTACLE IS TAX: the organisation behind Natural Valley concluded after years of practice and legal research that public interest trust taxation is unreasonable and unfair — donating land for environmental benefit brings no incentive and still attracts tax. Reform is an active campaign, so check the current position before assuming the cost. THE PRECEDENT WORTH COPYING IS A CAMPAIGN, NOT A COMPLETION: the first attempt was the 濁水溪口海埔地公益信託 over the Zhuoshui estuary tidal flats, launched with the slogan ‘everyone buy a share to guard the white dolphin’ to oppose the Kuokuang petrochemical development after IUCN listed the local white dolphin population as critically endangered. The trust was used as a mobilising instrument against a specific project — share subscription as public organising. WHO TO APPROACH: 台灣環境資訊協會 (TEIA), which set up an environmental trust centre in 2007 on Japanese and British models, and 自然保育與環境資訊基金會 (TNF), which campaigns for trust tax reform.

trackers.name: eFOI — Freedom of Information (Philippines)
trackers.desc: You CAN get: records held by the Philippine EXECUTIVE branch — national departments, bureaus, government-owned and -controlled corporations, state universities and colleges and local water districts — filed online through the portal and tracked there, with agencies required to answer within 15 working days (extendable, with notice, where the request is voluminous or needs consultation). If the agency does not hold the record but another executive agency does, a 2021 memorandum circular requires it to refer your request on rather than deny it. You CAN'T get: anything from Congress or the courts — there is no enabling statute covering all branches, so the order reaches the executive only. Critically for a local fight, LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS ARE MERELY ENCOURAGED to follow it, not bound, so a barangay, municipal or provincial record may need a local FOI ordinance instead. Records are also withheld under national-security, privacy and banking confidentiality exceptions. For activists: this is the route to an EIA, a permit file, a procurement record or project correspondence held by DENR, DPWH or a GOCC. Use it early — a denial can be appealed to the agency head within 15 calendar days, then to the Office of the President or by petition for mandamus, and that clock is slower than most project timetables.

trackers.name: National Secretary of Social Action (NASSA)
trackers.desc: The National Secretary of Social Action was established in 1966 as a humanitarian and advocacy arm of the Catholic Bishops’ Conferences of the Philippines (CBCP). The aim of NASSA is to address poverty alleviation, sustainable agriculture, empowerment of women and children, and ecological protection.

trackers.name: Environmental Legal Assistance Center (ELAC)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Philippine environmental law NGO founded in 1990 — lawyers, paralegals, researchers and community organisers, backed by volunteer lawyers and scientists, working from offices in Palawan, Cebu, Bohol and Leyte. It provides free legal representation in environmental court cases against deforestation, mining and other destructive projects and coastal degradation, trains community paralegals and forest, wildlife and fish wardens, and litigates on forest, coastal and land-tenure disputes. WHO IT SUITS: a community or indigenous group in its coverage areas, especially Palawan, facing an extractive or large development project — it is a small office under political and corporate pressure, so cases are chosen, not queued.

trackers.name: The Samdhana Institute — grants programme
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Southeast Asian grantmaker giving micro to medium-sized grants, plus urgent-action grants, directly to Indigenous peoples and local communities, community-based and civil-society organisations, informal groups and individual activists — for land and territorial rights, natural-resource governance, and community-led climate and livelihood work. Its own site names offices only in Bogor, Indonesia and in Cagayan de Oro and Quezon City, Philippines, which is where this entry is placed; it describes its remit as Southeast Asia generally, so groups elsewhere in the region should still ask. WHO IT SUITS: groups that cannot get money from conventional donors — Samdhana states its grantmaking principle as funding the "un-fundable", and an unregistered informal group is not disqualified. HOW IT DIFFERS: it supplies environmental conflict mediation and technical support alongside the grant rather than only writing cheques.

trackers.name: Foundation for the Philippine Environment (FPE)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: an endowment-based Philippine grantmaker for biodiversity conservation and sustainable development, with small grants of up to PHP 500,000 and a youth stream of up to PHP 100,000. Its grant framework (CARES) explicitly includes Environmental Defense and advocacy alongside research, constituency building and site work. WHO IT SUITS: civil-society organisations, people's organisations, Indigenous peoples' organisations and academic institutions — not individuals. Much of the money is site-focused: FPE identifies a priority conservation site and invites organisations based there to apply, so check whether your area is currently one before writing anything. HOW IT DIFFERS: FPE has also served as implementing partner for the GEF Small Grants Programme in the Philippines, so one relationship can reach more than one pot.

trackers.name: Forest Foundation Philippines
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a Philippine grantmaker for forest protection, running microgrants for community-led work to reduce deforestation and forest degradation, conserve high-conservation-value forest and improve ecosystem connectivity — concentrated in priority landscapes including the Mindoro and Eastern Mindanao Biodiversity Corridors. WHO IT SUITS: duly registered individuals, organisations and firms — NGOs, social enterprises, professionals and consultancy groups — working on forest protection and conservation in the Philippines. HOW IT DIFFERS: programmes open and close, and the Foundation openly lists past programmes that are no longer accepting proposals, so write to the proposals address and confirm what is live before preparing a submission.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center — Kasama sa Kalikasan (LRC-KsK)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Philippine public-interest law centre founded in 1987 by four young lawyers, one of them now a Supreme Court Justice, working for recognition and protection of the rights of Indigenous peoples and upland rural poor communities to land and natural resources. It runs three programmes — research and policy development, direct legal services, and advocacy and campaigns support — and was instrumental in drafting the Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act of 1997 and defending its constitutionality, the statute under which ancestral domain is recognised in the Philippines. It campaigned to repeal the Mining Act of 1995 and still petitions against it. For partner communities it runs paralegal training and field briefings, supplies documentary research, and files cases in court. WHO IT SUITS: an Indigenous or upland community facing mining, logging or encroachment. The model is supporting a community's own campaign rather than taking a client, so it suits a group that is already organised, and it works through partners rather than open intake.

trackers.name: Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism (PCIJ)
trackers.desc: Philippine center reporting on corruption and public money since 1989.

trackers.name: Open Data Philippines
trackers.desc: National — Philippine government open data portal. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Philippines.

trackers.name: DENR-EMB EIA portal
trackers.desc: The Philippines' Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB) EIA portal. You CAN get: Environmental Impact Statement System filings and Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC) records. You CAN'T get: files for projects that skipped the system. For activists: check a project's ECC status and its EIA documents.

trackers.name: Supreme Court E-Library
trackers.desc: Official Philippine Supreme Court e-library of decisions and resolutions. · Find here: the Supreme Court of the Philippines' E-Library of decisions and resolutions.

trackers.name: PhilGEPS
trackers.desc: The Philippines' single centralised electronic procurement portal — all government bid notices, awards and contracts. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in the Philippines, and for how much.

trackers.name: Philippine Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (PH-EITI)
trackers.desc: National Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative body — discloses oil, gas and mining revenues, contracts and company ownership in Philippines.

trackers.name: PH-EITI Beneficial Ownership Registry
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC)
trackers.desc: The Philippines' Anti-Money Laundering Council — the national financial intelligence unit and AML/CFT authority. Here you can trace how suspicious transactions are reported and money-laundering intelligence is produced in the Philippines.

trackers.name: Commission on Audit (COA)
trackers.desc: The Philippines' independent constitutional supreme audit institution — audits all accounts and expenditures of government funds and properties. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find audit findings and how public money was spent or lost.

trackers.name: Department of Budget and Management (DBM)
trackers.desc: The Philippine executive agency overseeing the national budget — allocation, release and management of public funds. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Philippines.

trackers.name: Office of the Ombudsman (Philippines)
trackers.desc: Philippine constitutional body investigating and prosecuting graft and corruption by public officials.

trackers.name: Philippine Statistics Authority
trackers.desc: Philippines's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in the Philippines.

trackers.name: SEC Philippines
trackers.desc: The Philippines' Securities and Exchange Commission corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Writ of Kalikasan — how to file, and who qualifies
trackers.desc: THE REMEDY, NOT AN ORGANISATION. Founded on Section 16, Article II of the Constitution and operationalised by A.M. No. 09-6-8-SC, Rule 7. THERE ARE NO DOCKET FEES — the rules waive them so public-interest litigants can reach the court. File directly with the Supreme Court or the Court of Appeals; it is not filed in the Regional Trial Courts, and a petition lodged in an RTC is in the wrong forum. The petition must be verified (sworn), naming the law violated, your circumstances and the respondents, or stating that their identities are unknown. Procedure is summary: petition, writ, the respondent's Return, a summary hearing, a possible TEPO, then judgment — with liberal admission of evidence and site inspections. Reliefs include injunction, environmental protection orders, rehabilitation and continuing mandamus. TEST THE THRESHOLD FIRST: the harm must transcend personal or property rights and threaten the life, health or property of inhabitants in 2 or more cities or provinces — a single-site development inside one municipality does not qualify however severe, and that disqualifies most local fights. AND WINNING THE WRIT IS NOT WINNING A HALT: in the Sibuyan Island case the Court issued the writ against the miner, DENR and the MGB, gave 10 days to comment and referred the case onward — but denied the temporary environmental protection order; and reporting on the writ's record notes that granted petitions have not always been implemented by local governments.

trackers.name: Public Attorney's Office — district offices nationwide
trackers.desc: THE GOVERNMENT'S OWN LAW OFFICE FOR PEOPLE WHO CANNOT PAY, under Republic Act 9406, with district and field offices nationwide — many inside Halls of Justice, court buildings or local government complexes, so this is a local service rather than a capital-city one. Go to the office covering either your residence or where the case will be filed. TWO TESTS, BOTH MUST BE PASSED. Indigency: published limits are ₱24,000 net monthly income in NCR, ₱22,000 in other cities outside NCR, ₱20,000 in municipalities outside NCR — and owning a modest family home does not by itself disqualify you. Merit: the case must have a genuine legal basis and not be frivolous or harassing. BRING: an Affidavit of Indigency plus an income tax return, payslip, or a Certificate of Indigency from the DSWD, the Municipal Social Welfare Office, or your Barangay Chairman. Filing fees are 90 percent discounted for indigents and fully waived with a PAO certificate. THREE LIMITS. PAO can act for one side only — if your opponent is also indigent, one of you is referred to the Integrated Bar of the Philippines. Caseloads are extreme: a PAO lawyer averaged 458 cases in one recorded year against about 40 for a private lawyer, so expect little time per client and turnover of the lawyer on your case. And for a public-interest environmental matter, also try the IBP provincial and city chapters under Rule 139-A, law school clinics — some of which waive means tests where the case involves environmental protection — and groups such as FLAG and SALIGAN, which take landmark land-rights cases at their discretion.

trackers.name: CBFMA — 25-year tenure, and a consent right over permits
trackers.desc: HOW A COMMUNITY GETS SECURE TENURE OVER FOREST LAND IT DOES NOT OWN. Under EO 263 and DENR AO 96-29, a Community-Based Forest Management Agreement runs between the DENR and a people's organisation for 25 years, renewable for another 25, under the community's own Community Resource Management Framework. It is also the instrument issued to POs in allowable zones within protected areas. THE RIGHT THAT STOPS THINGS: a PO must be informed of and consulted on all government projects in the area — and the PO's consent must be secured by DENR before granting or renewing contracts, leases and permits for extraction and utilisation of natural resources inside it, with an equitable sharing agreement reached first where the grantee is not from the affected community. A consent right inside your own tenure area is far stronger than objecting to someone else's permit from outside. You also receive all income from sustainable use within the area (subject to NIPAS), and exemption from forest charges on plantation products under RA 7161. THE PROCESS TRAP: your LGU must endorse the application before DENR can act — and PENRO/CENRO are mandated to orient local executives about CBFM, so ask DENR field staff to run that orientation rather than lobbying the LGU alone. KNOW WHAT IT IS: CBFM is a production sharing arrangement and communities under it have been oriented toward timber plantation harvesting — it secures tenure, it does not by itself mean preservation. For indigenous peoples the stronger route is ancestral domain recognition under RA 8371 (IPRA).

trackers.name: Datalex
trackers.desc: Official Armenian judicial information system: case search, schedules and court decisions. · Find here: free Armenian legislation and court decisions (Datalex).

trackers.name: EcoLur Informational NGO
trackers.desc: Armenia's environmental information organisation, built around a repeatable model rather than a single campaign: it runs named S.O.S. campaigns site by site — Amulsar, Teghout, Akhtala, Qajaran, Kapan, Agarak, Sotq, Ararat and others — acting as the information coordinator for residents living beside a mine or a polluter. WHO TO ENLIST when what you need is the evidence and the timetable rather than a lawyer. You CAN: use its independent-experts library, which collects geologists' and geomorphologists' opinions, social-impact surveys of affected communities and reports on new circumstances in an ESIA — the material that turns an objection into an argument. It also publishes notices of scheduled public hearings on exploration and mining permits and reports the council votes on them, which is the single hardest thing for a rural community to learn in time. For activists: it works with CEE Bankwatch and other Armenian groups on complaints to development-bank accountability mechanisms, so it is a route to the financing side as well as the permit.

trackers.name: FPWC — Caucasus Wildlife Refuge (Foundation for the Preservation of Wildlife and Cultural Assets)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: gives a community an alternative buyer for its own land. FPWC built the Caucasus Wildlife Refuge from 2011 by taking on land from more than a dozen communities across Ararat and Vayots Dzor — mostly by lease, with the payments going back to the villages for their own improvements — and it now covers around 30,000 hectares buffering the Khosrov Forest State Reserve, the first privately protected area in the South Caucasus. It employs local rangers and funds part of the work through ecotourism rather than donations alone. USE IT: this is the counterparty when someone else wants your community's land. Gnishik gave its land to the refuge under pressure to lease it as a hunting ground instead; another community turned down a company's cash offer and ceded the land for conservation. If a concession, a hunting lease or a mine is being dangled at your council, FPWC is the competing offer that keeps the ground intact and still pays. Note it is lease-based, so the community keeps title.

trackers.name: ARMEPS
trackers.desc: Armenia's electronic procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Armenia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Audit Chamber
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Armenia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Statistical Committee of Armenia (ArmStat)
trackers.desc: Armenia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Armenia.

trackers.name: Corruption Prevention Commission
trackers.desc: Armenia's independent commission overseeing asset declarations and integrity.

trackers.name: Hetq
trackers.desc: Armenian investigative outlet reporting on corruption and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Union of Informed Citizens (UIC)
trackers.desc: Armenian NGO (since 2014) working to consolidate democracy through multi-component election observation, state-procurement monitoring, and advocacy for electoral, constitutional and anti-corruption reform. Runs the Fact Investigation Platform (FIP.am) fact-checking outlet and the Reforms.am tracker.

trackers.name: State Register of Legal Entities
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Armenia Multi-Sector Register
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Court of Cassation of Armenia
trackers.desc: Court of Cassation of Armenia — appellate court in Armenia (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: SLAPP suits against Armenian defenders — take advice before you post
trackers.desc: READ THIS BEFORE CAMPAIGNING PUBLICLY. International groups issued a solidarity statement over Armenian environmental and human rights defenders facing defamation and criminalization. Around one mining project the recorded pattern was: dozens of activists sued for social media posts or for comments made during meetings; 2 media outlets sued for publishing news stories about the project; and 2 members of parliament sued for their speeches during parliamentary meetings. That last fact is the measure of the exposure — if parliamentary speech draws a suit, an ordinary resident's comment certainly can. Anyone campaigning on an Armenian extractive project should assume defamation exposure for ordinary public comment, keep records of the factual basis for every claim made, and take legal advice before posting rather than after being served. This is recorded plainly because listing funding opportunities alone would understate what this work costs here.

trackers.name: Caucasus Nature Fund — it matches the state budget, so that is the lever
trackers.desc: RECURRING CORE FUNDING, WHICH IS THE SCARCEST KIND. CNF was founded in 2007 by Conservation International, Germany's development ministry and WWF, and has a programme office in Yerevan supporting protected areas across Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia. Its purpose is long-term funding for operating costs, improved management and sustainable development — not one-off projects. THE MECHANISM IS THE ARGUMENT: it works through partnership with the three governments by matching, but not exceeding, the state budgets, so each side commits long-term. For an Armenian campaign that means arguing for a larger state protected-area budget is also arguing for more international money — the two move together, and the domestic budget line is the lever. ALSO PRESENT: UNEP and REC Caucasus run capacity development jointly with the Ministry of Environment, including on biodiversity strategies — programmes to attach to rather than apply to. HONEST GAP: no standing Armenian domestic grant programme with published eligibility for local community groups could be verified; what exists is a regional trust fund, international agency programmes, and organisations to partner with.

trackers.name: Leasing, not buying — how private conservation works in Armenia
trackers.desc: THE MECHANISM THAT HAS ACTUALLY WORKED HERE. Private conservation in Armenia has proceeded by leasing community-owned and state land for conservation rather than by purchase, with rangers employed from the local communities — the model behind the Caucasus Wildlife Refuge. Where buying is impossible, or politically impossible, a long lease plus local employment is the route to look at: it gives the community income and a role rather than presenting conservation as land being taken away. The same shape appears in Austria's Pachtvertrag fallback and China's entrusted management, so it is a transferable pattern. TO FIND PARTNERS: CANEECCA, the Eastern Europe, Caucasus and Central Asia network, lists Armenian organisations working on afforestation and reforestation, public participation and civic activism, advocacy and lobbying, organic farming and ecological education — useful both for co-applicants and for the letters of support that several funds in this map require.

trackers.name: EPBC Act Public Portal — federal referrals
trackers.desc: Australia's public list of every project referred for federal environmental approval under the EPBC Act (administered by the new National EPA from mid-2026), with each referral's documents and a public comment window. You CAN get: every proposed action touching nationally protected matters — the proponent, location, documents, decisions, and 10 business days to comment on whether it's a 'controlled action'. You CAN'T get: projects with only state-level impacts — those sit with state EPAs. For activists: the comment window opens the moment a referral is published, so watching this portal for your region is how campaigns get ahead of a mine or development while the federal decision is still open.

trackers.name: Australian Government Register of Lobbyists
trackers.desc: Federal register of third-party lobbyists under the Lobbying Code of Conduct. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Australian Government Register of Lobbyists
trackers.desc: Public register of third-party lobbyists and clients who contact Australian Government ministers and officials. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Foreign Influence Transparency Scheme
trackers.desc: Register giving the public visibility of activities undertaken on behalf of foreign principals to influence government and politics. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find foreign influence, funding and agents.

trackers.name: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC)
trackers.desc: Australia's independent regulator for freedom of information and privacy — FOI reviews and complaints. — Holds to account: public bodies that hold records — find information-commissioner decisions and appeals.

trackers.name: AustLII
trackers.desc: Australasian Legal Information Institute: free primary legal materials including decisions of courts and tribunals. · Find here: free Australian legislation and the full case-law of federal, state and territory courts and tribunals (AustLII).

trackers.name: National Legal Aid (Australia)
trackers.desc: Peak body representing the eight state and territory Legal Aid Commissions, with national access-to-justice data. · Find here: the network of Australia's state and territory legal-aid commissions. IT DOES NOT TAKE APPLICATIONS — go to your state or territory commission. National Legal Aid represents the eight independent Legal Aid Commissions and their directors; the commissions are independent statutory bodies and NLA is a peak body for policy, advocacy and national projects. The national name is the most findable and the least useful — the same pattern recorded here for Canada's 13 provincial plans. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS FOR LAND WORK: NLA's own budget submission records that disaster response legal assistance has become a specialised area and an expansive area of law, expressly including insurance, housing and tenancy, grants, environmental and planning issues and income support. That is a named, separately funded stream in which planning and environmental matters are an express component — where general civil legal aid would not reach an environmental question, a post-disaster framing may. New South Wales, Victoria and Western Australia have received funding to deliver disaster response legal services, each state delivering differently on a place-based approach. BUT THE FUNDING IS DESCRIBED AS TEMPORARY and only three states are named — ask whether a service is currently operating. FOR NON-DISASTER ENVIRONMENTAL WORK, ASK ABOUT COMMUNITY LEGAL CENTRES: some CLCs specialise in particular areas of law, including environmental law, and the commissions administer the Community Legal Services Program funding — Victoria Legal Aid alone funds 42 CLCs. Ask your commission which CLC in your state specialises in environmental law; it administers the funding and will know — a more productive question than asking it to take the case. WHO WILL DO THE WORK: over 70 percent of approved legal aid cases are assigned to external practitioners under a mixed delivery model — but there are falling rates of private practitioners willing to take legal aid work due to disproportionately low remuneration, especially in regional and remote communities, which is where most land disputes are. The Justice on the Brink report found $484 million more per year is needed and the commissions critically under-resourced for over a decade.

trackers.name: National Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander Legal Services (NATSILS)
trackers.desc: National peak body for Australia's community-controlled Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Legal Services, advocating on justice issues, law reform and access to justice for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

trackers.desc: Community-controlled Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Legal Service (ATSILS) providing free, culturally safe legal advice, representation and prisoner through-care to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in Queensland, with a focus on reducing over-incarceration and deaths in custody.

trackers.name: Aboriginal Legal Service of Western Australia (ALSWA)
trackers.desc: Community-controlled Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Legal Service (ATSILS) providing free, culturally safe legal advice, representation and prisoner through-care to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in Western Australia, with a focus on reducing over-incarceration and deaths in custody.

trackers.desc: Community-controlled Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Legal Service (ATSILS) providing free, culturally safe legal advice, representation and prisoner through-care to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in South Australia, with a focus on reducing over-incarceration and deaths in custody.

trackers.desc: Community-controlled Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Legal Service (ATSILS) providing free, culturally safe legal advice, representation and prisoner through-care to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in the Northern Territory, with a focus on reducing over-incarceration and deaths in custody.
