WHO TO WORK WITH: Suomen luonnonsuojeluliitto has about 150 local associations and 15 district organisations, which bring these appeals themselves and employ environmental lawyers. ITS STRATEGY IS WORTH COPYING: appeal only after careful consideration, where environmental effects were not sufficiently taken into account in the permit or the plan — the point is to make existing regulation actually apply. It reports winning most often on peat extraction permits. WHAT WINS: in the Sokli appeal the grounds were procedural — material relevant to the application was gathered but not publicly notified, so affected people and associations had no real chance to object (YSL 43§); no opinion was sought from the municipality or its health authority (YSL 42§); and fishers and reindeer herders were not heard. Consultation defects are the most reliable ground.

trackers.name: The appeal right is being narrowed — check before you rely on it
trackers.desc: A WARNING TO VERIFY BEFORE PLANNING A CASE. Parliament has moved to restrict associations' right to appeal building projects: associations would be able to appeal building exemption permits, planning-need decisions and so-called clean transition siting permits only where the project is large enough to require a statutory environmental impact assessment. Suomen luonnonsuojeluliitto warns the effect would be that a solar field of under 200 hectares, or 9 wind turbines, or a data centre could be placed in a local forest of recreational or natural value with no possibility for environmental organisations to intervene. Its director notes that courts around the country have overturned unlawful municipal decisions precisely because SLL districts and associations appealed them. CONFIRM THE CURRENT LAW — if the restriction is in force, the association route may be closed for your project size and an affected landowner becomes the necessary appellant instead.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Snowchange Cooperative — buys damaged land on the open market and rewilds it (Finland)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Finnish cooperative that buys peatlands and forests damaged by peat production and intensive forestry, on the open market, and restores them. Its Landscape Rewilding Programme began in 2018 and its own account by 2025 is 8,500 hectares owned outright and land concessions offered over more than 60,000 hectares, across five main catchment areas — with a later figure of 10,000 hectares owned. Over 178 sites, including Sámi sites. THE CASE THAT SHOWS THE WHOLE ROUTE, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL SINGLE EXAMPLE IN THIS FILE: Linnunsuo was a former peat production site responsible for fish kills in the Jukajoki river in 2010 and 2011. Snowchange bought the 110 hectares from Vapo, Finland's largest peat industry company, in April 2017 after a year of negotiation, funded by a €75,000 loan from Rewilding Europe Capital. It became a strict IUCN protected area that November. A second loan of €200,000 in late 2018 paid for a further 72 hectares next door, taking the site to 182. A community bought a damaged site from the company that damaged it, with borrowed money, and had it protected within seven months. WHY IT WORKS WITHOUT DISPLACING PEOPLE: Linnunsuo is co-managed so that a limited harvest of water birds by Selkie hunters continues, and the hunters help control invasive mink and raccoon dog. Its sites are registered as Indigenous and Community Conserved Areas, its stated method is that communities guide the work through collaborative management, that Indigenous women lead decision-making on their own territory, and that no decision is made without the consent of the affected community. Where it does not own, it negotiates land use agreements with private owners on what restoration will happen. WHAT TO BRING IT: drained peatland, a ditched forest, a river catchment damaged by peat extraction or forestry — and ideally one where the damage is documented, because that is what made the Vapo purchase possible. Finland has over five million hectares of drained peatland; this is the organisation that treats that as a supply of buyable sites rather than a loss.

trackers.name: CADA — Comissão de Acesso aos Documentos Administrativos
trackers.desc: Portugal's independent authority on access to administrative documents — the right-to-know regulator. — Holds to account: public bodies that hold records — find information-commissioner decisions and appeals.

trackers.name: DGSI
trackers.desc: Official databases of Portuguese higher-court jurisprudence. · Find here: the official databases of Portuguese higher-court case-law (DGSI).

trackers.name: Quercus — ONGA nacional / ação popular ambiental
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: read the standing rule first, because Portugal's is the most open in Europe. Article 52(3) of the Constitution gives everyone — personally or through an association — the right of ação popular, naming preservation of the environment expressly, and Lei 83/95 regulates it. It is not a special procedure but a species of active standing: you can bring ANY action, in ANY court, including interim measures, to defend diffuse interests, WITHOUT having to show a personal and direct interest or any connection to the matter. A citizen can act alone. WHO IT SUITS: everyone, which is the point — but an association carries weight and evidence a citizen cannot, and Quercus is the national environmental NGO of public utility, founded 1985. Note the screen for associations under article 3: legal personality, the interest in your statutes, and no professional activity competing with firms or liberal professionals.

trackers.name: Portugal IRN (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Portugal IRN (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Portugal — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: Portal Justiça – Registo Comercial
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Central Register of Effective Beneficiaries (RCBE)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: BASE – Contratos Públicos
trackers.desc: Portugal's public-contracts portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Portugal, and for how much.

trackers.name: dados.gov.pt
trackers.desc: National — official government open data / budget portal. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this is the broad budget/open-data hub for how money is allocated overall — for the specific firms winning tenders use the procurement portal, and for findings of misspending use the supreme audit institution. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Portugal.

trackers.name: Statistics Portugal (INE)
trackers.desc: Portugal's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Portugal.

trackers.name: Portuguese Court of Audits
trackers.desc: high-court in Portugal

trackers.name: Entidade das Contas e Financiamentos Políticos
trackers.desc: National campaign / political-finance disclosure body — party and candidate financial reports.

trackers.name: ONGA status — 100 members buys you a seat at the table
trackers.desc: THE REGISTRATION THAT TURNS AN ASSOCIATION INTO A STATUTORY CONSULTEE. Under Lei n.º 35/98 of 18 July, registering in the RNOE gives an association the right of consultation and information on administrative documents or decisions with environmental incidence; representation in the consultative bodies of local, regional and central administration according to the territorial incidence of its activity; status as a social partner in the scope recognised; and eligibility to apply for financial support. THE GATE IS A NUMBER: the application must include a declaration signed by the President of the Direção stating the number of members, and the mandatory minimum is 100 associados — above Iceland's 30, far below Norway's 5,000. Also required: the geographic area of activity, minutes of the general assembly electing the governing bodies, Cartão de Cidadão copies for the Direção, and the IRC declaration filed with the tax authority. The entity must be an association, legally constituted, non-profit, aiming exclusively at defence and valorisation of the environment — and registration is voluntary but not automatic: all the rights depend on it.

trackers.name: What registration unlocks — and why local scope is the norm
trackers.desc: TWO FINANCIAL CONSEQUENCES AND ONE REASSURANCE. MECENATO: ONGA and equiparadas registered in the RNOE — and other associations pursuing environmental defence — may receive donations in money or in kind from patrons under the Estatuto dos Benefícios Fiscais, so registration unlocks tax-advantaged private giving as well as public grants. UTILIDADE PÚBLICA: after 5 years of activity and registration an association may request the estatuto de utilidade pública under Lei n.º 36/2021. AND THE REASSURANCE — LOCAL IS THE NORM: of 116 actively registered ONGA at the end of 2024, up 8.4 percent on the previous year, 36 (31 percent) hold local scope against just 17 national and 13 regional, plus 27 equiparadas. A neighbourhood association defending one place is the typical ONGA, not the exception. ADMINISTRATION: the register is run by the Agência Portuguesa do Ambiente and published annually in the Diário da República, recording inscriptions, modifications, suspensions and annulments — registration can be suspended and later lifted, so check an organisation's current status rather than a historic list.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: MONTIS — land-purchase fund and land-donation route (central Portugal)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Portuguese land-conservation association, founded March 2014 and based at Vouzela in Viseu district, that acquires abandoned and marginal ground and manages it for biodiversity. At the end of August 2025 it had 345 members and 34 properties in central Portugal plus four more near Lisbon. Some parcels it bought with public subscription, some it received as donations, and others are baldio commons or company ground it manages under protocol without owning — Baldio de Carvalhais and Baldio da Granja are both on its managed list. USE IT: it runs a standing land-purchase fund and posts the running balance in public, and that balance is the fact to act on. It stood at €12,073.94 on 31 August 2025 and €12,098.94 on 31 July 2026 — a gain of twenty-five euros in eleven months. MONTIS will not outbid a developer. What it will take is a parcel offered by donation, or ground it can manage under protocol while the owner keeps the title, which is the route for an owner who will not sell. Two figures for its area appear side by side on its own pages, about 300 ha and about 313 ha, depending on which one you read. For cash gifts to the fund it states the tax position: an individual deducts 25% of the amount given against tax due, capped at 15% of that tax, and a company books the donation as a cost at 120% of its value, under articles 62 and 63 of the Estatuto dos Benefícios Fiscais.

trackers.name: LPN — Liga para a Protecção da Natureza (Portugal)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the oldest environmental association in the Iberian Peninsula, founded in 1948, a national ONGA with Utilidade Pública status, headquartered at Estrada do Calhariz de Benfica 187, 1500-124 Lisbon. It holds its own reserves in the Castro Verde cereal steppe and runs long-running territorial programmes there and elsewhere — Castro Verde Sustentável, the lynx programme, and a forests programme — describing its method as concrete measures worked in close partnership with local communities. WHY IT IS DIFFERENT FROM A LAND TRUST: since Castro Verde was made a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve on 14 June 2017, LPN has sat on its Management Council and is responsible for its governance — alongside the municipality and the Associação de Agricultores do Campo Branco, the local farmers' association. A Portuguese community told that protection means taking land away from farming can point at a designation where the conservation body, the câmara and the farmers govern the same ground together, and has done for years. WHO IT SUITS: a case in the Alentejo steppe or anywhere its species programmes reach, and any group that needs an established national association rather than a new committee to carry the argument. It complements MONTIS, which works in central Portugal on abandoned and marginal ground; LPN's holdings are working estates in the south. ON THE FIGURES: a Portuguese wildlife directory reports LPN as holding six estates of about 1,800 hectares at Castro Verde plus a further estate at Vila Nova de Poiares. I could not confirm those numbers on LPN's own site, which refers to its reserves without totalling them. Treat the holdings as real and the hectares as unverified.

trackers.name: ZERO — takes Portuguese cases to the European Commission (Portugal)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an environmental association founded at the end of 2015 by around a hundred people, working on climate, pollution, waste, ecosystems and public participation. It files complaints against the Portuguese state with the European Commission — one recent example alleged that Portugal was allowing 28 municipal waste landfills to operate outside the law, in breach of European rules in force since 2014 requiring pre-treatment before landfill, with the cases also reported to the national environment and spatial planning inspectorate. That is the route above the ministry, and this is the Portuguese organisation that uses it. THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST FOR A COMMUNITY, AND IT IS UNUSUALLY WELL DOCUMENTED: it publishes what happens when you ask public bodies for environmental information. Of eight requests it made to the Portuguese Environment Agency, it had to resort to the formal complaint mechanism in five, and two were still unanswered months later. It also points out that the access-to-information commission publishes an annual list of the public bodies that receive the most complaints for failing to answer. A Portuguese community that is being stonewalled is not unlucky, and there is a documented pattern and a named list to cite. IT ALSO WATCHES THE FARM MONEY: with the European Environmental Bureau it has issued joint statements on how Portugal plans to spend Common Agricultural Policy funds, arguing public money is going to those causing environmental and social harm and that Commission supervision is weak. If the threat to your land is subsidised farming rather than construction, that is the file. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a law firm. Portugal's other entries here are a small land-buying foundation and a body holding estates in the Alentejo; this is the complaints and public-participation leg.

trackers.name: Programa Cidadãos Ativ@s — Gulbenkian as fund operator, and named project managers
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Portuguese Active Citizens Fund, the EEA Grants component built specifically to support non-governmental organisations, run by the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in consortium with the Fundação Bissaya Barreto with a budget of €11 million across 2018 to 2024, financed by Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. Portugal and Greece are the two western states inside a scheme otherwise aimed at newer member states, which is not something a Portuguese group would guess. WHAT IT FUNDS, BY OUTCOME — and the fourth one is the interesting one: strengthened democratic culture and civic awareness; increased support for human rights; empowerment of vulnerable groups; and enhanced capacity and sustainability of civil society, which has included training, mentoring, coaching and consulting in the cross-cutting areas of advocacy, watchdog work and fundraising, based on an organisational needs assessment. Being taught to do watchdog work and to fundraise is a durable asset for a community group in a way a project grant is not. THE PRACTICAL DETAIL: it publishes a named project manager for each outcome, with contact addresses, plus a promoter's manual and online application forms, and it ran calls annually with access rules and assessment criteria published on the programme site before each call opened. Ask the manager for the outcome your case fits rather than writing to a general address. AND IT CONSULTED FIRST: the programme's rules were negotiated after a wide consultation of Portuguese NGOs in January 2018, with their conclusions taken into account. A funder that asked the sector what it needed is a funder worth telling what is missing. PORTUGAL NOW HAS FOUR ROUTES in this file: a small land-buying foundation, a body holding estates in the Alentejo, the complaints and public-participation association, and this — the money and the capacity building. Note the period: 2018 to 2024. Check what has succeeded it before relying on an open call.

trackers.name: BALADI — the baldíos federation, and it is telling communities not to sign
trackers.desc: WHAT A BALDÍO IS: communal land belonging to the Local Community, restored to the compartes by Decree-Laws 39/76 and 40/76 in February 1976 and written into the Constitution of the Portuguese Republic by the Constituent Assembly that April as property belonging to Local Communities — a common property, neither public nor private. The Assembleia de Compartes holds broad administration and management powers and decides the use and products of the communal property for the development of the local community, electing the assembly board, the conselho diretivo and the supervisory commission for terms of one to four years. Baldíos exist across the national territory but are now concentrated in the north and centre. WHY THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN HISTORICAL: BALADI has issued a public warning to all local communities about new draft 'delegation of powers' agreements circulating from the state forestry institute, accompanied by model convocation notices and minutes for approval by Assembleias de Compartes. Its assessment is blunt — this is not simple technical support and not a continuation of co-management, and the drafts should be examined with maximum prudence. It asks every conselho diretivo, baldío commission, managing parish council and assembly to: get independent legal and technical analysis before signing anything; weigh alternatives to the institute and to contracts with financial funds; contact BALADI and its affiliated associations before any deliberation; and propose alternatives that keep the decision in the hands of the compartes. WHAT IT OFFERS A COMMUNITY: its affiliated associations provide technical, administrative, legal and forestry and environmental support without substituting for the baldío's own organs and without taking the decision over its territory away from the Assembleia de Compartes. That is the distinction to test any offer of help against, anywhere. IT ALSO KNOWS THE PRESSURE ON GRAZING: it has reported receiving dozens of baldíos, compartes, shepherds and farmers in open conflict, attributing it to national agricultural payment agency criteria reducing the area available for agricultural applications year after year since 2014. AND IT WORKS WITH GALICIA: it has held Iberian and European congresses of community areas jointly with the Galician organisation of montes veciñais.

trackers.name: Data State Inspectorate (DVI)
trackers.desc: Data State Inspectorate (DVI) — Latvia’s independent data-protection / information commissioner, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: KNAB
trackers.desc: Latvia's Corruption Prevention and Combating Bureau. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers, officials handling public money & power — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held; corruption cases, sanctions and integrity data.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Latvia
trackers.desc: Official site of the Augstākā tiesa with case-law archive. · Find here: the judgments and case-law of the Supreme Court of Latvia.

trackers.name: Latvijas Dabas fonds (Latvian Fund for Nature)
trackers.desc: Latvia's principal nature-conservation NGO, founded in 1990, working on protected areas, threatened species and habitats, and running a standing advocacy programme rather than only projects. WHO TO ENLIST when a protected area, grassland or wetland near you is in play. You CAN: draw on its participation in drafting policy documents and normative acts and in ministry consultative councils and working groups, and on Dabasdati.lv, the nature-observation portal it maintains — species records are often the difference between an objection and an argument, since a documented protected species on the site changes what a developer may lawfully do. For activists: it has begun long-term cooperation with Rīga neighbourhood associations on identifying, restoring and managing urban meadows, so there is a precedent for it working with residents' groups rather than only with ministries. No verified litigation, so treat it as expertise and standing-by-participation, not as counsel.

trackers.name: State Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Latvia, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Re:Baltica
trackers.desc: Baltic investigative center reporting on corruption, finance and public accountability.

trackers.name: Constitutional Court of the Republic of Latvia
trackers.desc: Constitutional Court of the Republic of Latvia — supreme court (Latvia).

trackers.name: Register of Enterprises
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia
trackers.desc: Latvia's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Latvia.

trackers.name: EIS
trackers.desc: Latvia's electronic procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Latvia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Latvia Enterprise Register
trackers.desc: Latvia's business register, which publishes beneficial-ownership information. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find who really owns and controls them; their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: LVAF nolikumi — a model landowner agreement, and the scoring sheets
trackers.desc: TWO PUBLISHED ANNEXES MAKE THIS PAGE WORTH OPENING BEFORE YOU DRAFT ANYTHING. Annex Nr. 3 is a VIENOŠANĀS AR ZEMES ĪPAŠNIEKU (paraugs) — a model agreement with the landowner, supplied as a standard part of the application pack. A state fund publishing a template landowner agreement means that step is expected, normal and pre-drafted: you are not inventing it, and neither is the owner being asked to sign something unfamiliar. Annexes Nr. 4.1, 4.2 and 5 are the project evaluation criteria, published separately for the Expert Commission, the Fund administration and the Consultative Council — the scoring sheets are public before you apply, so read the criteria rather than the call text. Also published: application forms per activity, the cost estimate template, and the Fund's multi-year darbības koncepcija and annual competition plan, so you can see which activities are coming before they open. ELIGIBILITY is simply a biedrība or nodibinājums registered in Latvia — no membership floor.

trackers.name: LVAF — data-gathering is fundable, but the window is days not months
trackers.desc: WHAT THE FUND BACKS, AND THE TRAP IN HOW IT OPENS. The Latvijas vides aizsardzības fonds is a pool of state budget funds whose stated aim includes securing citizens' right to live in a quality environment and sufficient measures for conserving biological diversity and protecting ecosystems — language worth quoting back. A worked call funded cooperation projects between NGOs and environmental institutions, supporting work that addresses current environmental problems by collecting data and analysing it, alongside capacity building and educational materials, with EUR 70,000 available. THE SUBMISSION WINDOW WAS ABOUT 11 DAYS. That is the trap: you cannot react to the announcement, you have to be watching the annual competition plan and drafting beforehand. Submission is in person at the Fund administration in Rīga, by registered post, or electronically signed with a secure electronic signature — which must already be set up. ALSO WORTH KNOWING: for Sabiedrības integrācijas fonds competitions, an eligible association is one where the majority of members or founders are natural persons or NGOs, not state bodies, municipalities or merchants.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: Latvijas vides aizsardzības fonds — grants an association can apply for (Latvia)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: Latvia's environmental protection fund, a pool of state budget money run through open project competitions, with indicatively around €2.07 million a year in its environmental projects sub-programme. A registered Latvian biedrība or nodibinājums — an association or foundation — can apply directly, alongside research institutions and municipalities. That is the point for a community: this is not restricted to state bodies, and Latvia has no conservation land buyer, no other funder and no named environmental counsel that I could find across three separate searches. WHAT IT HAS FUNDED THAT IS RELEVANT: competitions have covered implementation of species and habitat protection plans, and protection and management measures inside specially protected nature territories where those measures are set out in a valid nature protection plan. Sums have run to €600,000 for a round with a €40,000 minimum per project and 10% co-financing, and to €190,000 for a round with no minimum and no compulsory co-financing at all. It has also funded data collection and analysis for environmental policy, and cooperation projects between NGOs and environmental institutions. THE CONDITION THAT SHAPES AN APPLICATION: for the protected-area rounds, the measures you propose must already be set out in a valid protection plan for that species, habitat or territory on the day you apply. So the first question is not what you want to do but whether it is already written into the plan — and if it is, this fund exists to pay for it. BE CLEAR WHAT IT IS: a state fund, administered through the ministry and the regional development agency, awarding money by competition. It is not an ally that will take your side against a project. It is money a constituted local association can win to do the survey, the plan implementation or the management work that a case needs.

trackers.name: Latvijas Ornitoloģijas biedrība (LOB) — Latvia's largest conservation NGO
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: founded 27 April 1993 and, on BirdLife's account, the largest non-governmental nature conservation organisation in Latvia, working on bird and habitat protection to maintain the numbers, diversity and geographic distribution of important sites, species and habitats. Its own site is lob.lv. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: Latvia is the thinnest bucket in my region — eleven entries, no land buyer that three searches could find, no named environmental counsel, and a state fund as the only source of money. This is the country's main independent conservation body, and the one organisation able to say what a threatened Latvian site actually holds. THE PART THAT IS USEFUL TO A COMMUNITY: it combines professional and volunteer ornithologists and explicitly welcomes bird conservation enthusiasts into study and conservation work, and it consults, lectures, publishes and keeps regular contact with the media. Two practical asks follow: bring it a site and ask what is recorded there, and ask whether it will put that on the record publicly. Latvia's partner has also worked on the consequences of forest clearcutting alongside the Finnish and Estonian partners, so a Latvian forestry case is within its experience. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a buyer and not a funder. I checked specifically, because the BirdLife family owns 320,000 hectares across the region, and found no evidence that the Latvian partner holds land.

trackers.name: Baltijas Vides Forums (BEF Latvia) — the planning and grassland expertise Latvia lacked
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a non-profit association founded 2003 in Riga, Aspazijas bulvāris 24-14, +371 6735 7555, bef@bef.lv. It works on nature, wildlife and marine ecosystem conservation, water quality and river basin management among other fields, and describes its own position as working at the interface between science, civil society, policy and administration, cooperating closely with city and municipal administrations across many European countries. More than a hundred national and international projects. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR LATVIA: Latvia is the thinnest bucket in this region — no land buyer that three searches could find, a state fund as its only source of money, and a bird society as its main conservation body. What was missing was somebody who does landscape and spatial planning. BEF does. Its board includes an expert whose declared fields are nature conservation, ecosystem services, landscape ecology and maritime spatial planning, and its recent work includes coastal landscape assessment fieldwork and a landscape and urban planning workshop hosted with a municipality. If a Latvian development turns on a spatial plan or a coastal landscape assessment, this is the organisation that does that work in the country. ITS GRASSLAND CREDENTIAL: it led the analysis of policy and experience in grassland management and contributed grassland management proposals and a landscape development plan for the Baltic grassland viability project covering all three Baltic states. That pairs directly with the Estonian grassland inventory body already in this file — the two work the same habitat across the border. IT IS A GROUP, NOT ONE OFFICE: BEF operates as a network with organisations in Latvia, Estonia, Lithuania and Germany, so a case that crosses a Baltic border has one family of organisations rather than three unrelated ones. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer, not a funder and not a law firm. It is a facilitator and expert body that works with administrations, so bring it analysis, planning input and stakeholder process — not a confrontation.

trackers.name: Latvijas Zaļā kustība — gives consultations and joins specific problem cases
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Latvian Green Movement, founded 2004 on the base of eight branches of the former Environmental Protection Club, an open and democratic membership organisation bringing together environmental activists, volunteers and experts who want to work actively to improve environmental quality and to prevent criminal offences against the environment. Over 100 individual members and five regional groups. Latvia had no legal or casework ally in this file. THE SERVICE THAT MATTERS, in its own words: defence of the public interest and promotion of effective participation by giving consultations and becoming involved in resolving specific problem situations relating to urban environment, construction, protective zones (aizsargjoslas), waste management and environmental impact assessment. That is casework, named as such, for exactly the kinds of dispute this file exists to serve. AND AT LOCAL LEVEL IT DOES THE REST: active participation in policy planning processes on city development planning and environmental impact assessment, the fight against illegal construction and criminal offences against the environment, and involving local residents in environmental protection activities. It also runs coastal dune protection through public control and involvement in territorial planning — useful in a country whose coast is its most contested ground. IT HAS EXPERTS ON CALL: it has established an Expert Council of specialists in their fields who give it qualitative advice and help it plan its activities. For a community that needs a specialist opinion, that council is the reason to approach this organisation rather than a campaign group. ITS STANDING: member of the Environmental Advisory Council, which brings together 20 national environmental NGOs, represented on the Green Investment Scheme advisory board and other advisory bodies, a CEE Bankwatch Network member group, and part of a consortium coordinating NGO participation in EU funds planning. Facebook: ZalaKustiba.

trackers.name: State Data Protection Inspectorate (VDAI)
trackers.desc: State Data Protection Inspectorate (VDAI) — Lithuania’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Transparency Register (skaidrumas)
trackers.desc: Lithuania's official lobbying/transparency register. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Register of Lobbyists
trackers.desc: National lobbying register. — Holds to account: lobbyists & influence-seekers — find who is lobbying whom, and meetings held.

trackers.name: Supreme Court of Lithuania
trackers.desc: Official case law of the Lietuvos Aukščiausiasis Teismas. · Find here: the judgments and case-law of the Supreme Court of Lithuania.

trackers.name: Lietuvos gamtos fondas (Lithuanian Fund for Nature)
trackers.desc: Lithuania's long-standing nature-conservation NGO, founded in 1991 and based in Vilnius, working on rare and endangered species and their habitats, on the management and restoration of natural habitats, and on the protection and restoration of the country's wetlands and peatlands. It helped build Lithuania's ecological network and works alongside state and municipal institutions, research bodies and other organisations rather than against them. WHO TO ENLIST when the site at issue is a bog, wetland or habitat of a protected species and you need someone who can say authoritatively what is there and what it is worth. For activists: no verified litigation record, so treat this as expertise, survey capacity and a route into official consultation processes — not as counsel. If you need a lawyer in Lithuania, this is not yet answered in this file.

trackers.name: CVP IS (Central Procurement)
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Lithuania, and for how much.

trackers.name: Vilnius Court of Commercial Arbitration
trackers.desc: Vilnius Court of Commercial Arbitration — tribunal (Lithuania).

trackers.name: Registrų centras
trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Information System of Legal Entities Participants (JADIS)
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Publicly searchable.

trackers.name: Statistics Lithuania
trackers.desc: Lithuania's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Lithuania.

trackers.name: National Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Lithuania, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Chief Official Ethics Commission (VTEK)
trackers.desc: Legislator / public-official financial interest & asset declarations.

trackers.name: Supreme Administrative Court of Lithuania
trackers.desc: Supreme Administrative Court of Lithuania — supreme court in Lithuania (Wikidata record).

trackers.name: SAARSP — municipal money funded by environmental fines
trackers.desc: MUNICIPAL ENVIRONMENTAL MONEY, AND ENFORCEMENT FEEDS IT. Under a draft law, fines for breaches of environmental and natural resource law imposed by municipal officials would be transferred to the SAARSP of the very municipality whose officials imposed them — so pressing your municipality to enforce directly funds local environmental work. The same draft would establish participation by representatives of the public in allocating SAARSP funds, for transparency and public involvement in decisions; ask your municipality whether that is in force, because it is a seat at the table over the money. WHAT IT FUNDS: environmental activity by target groups including NGOs and communities, implementation of environmental programmes and projects, and preparation of the documentation needed to implement those measures — plus protection, management, monitoring, creation and inventory of green spaces, and preparation of green space projects. A PRECISE EXCLUSION WORTH KNOWING: money from game animal resource use goes to measures by owners, managers and users of land plots, and hunting clubs are not owners, managers or users — so it cannot fund hunting club measures.

trackers.name: Anyone can propose a Natura 2000 site — including a private person
trackers.desc: THE PROPOSAL RIGHT IS UNUSUALLY OPEN. Proposals to the Environment Ministry to designate territories meeting Natura 2000 criteria may be submitted by scientific institutions, by non-governmental organisations — named examples being LOD, Baltijos aplinkos forumas and Lietuvos gamtos fondas — by protected area directorates, and by private persons. Proposals cover new sites and changing the boundaries of existing ones, and are often made when ecosystem restoration work has given a location higher conservation value meeting the criteria. So restoration you carry out can itself become the basis for designating the site — a sequence worth planning for deliberately. Selection criteria are approved by ministerial order. FUNDING CONTEXT: the national AARP programme allocated EUR 907,200 across 2014–2018 to protecting natural resources, monitoring protected species and restoring landscape complexes in Natura 2000 territories; AARP also pays compensation for damage caused by bison and, since 2019, wolves.

trackers.name: Compensation for farming restrictions — and the default mowing regime
trackers.desc: WHAT MAKES PROTECTION ACCEPTABLE TO A LANDOWNER. Natural and legal persons holding land in Lithuanian protected areas where agricultural activity restrictions apply may apply for financial support — the answer to the landowner who says designation costs them their livelihood. THE DEFAULT REGIME, WHERE TERMS ARE NOT OTHERWISE SET by the special land use conditions law, protected area regulations, planning documents or protection agreements with private landowners: mowing begins 15 June and cut grass must be removed from the field by 30 October inclusive; where livestock graze, no grazing term is set. Knowing the default matters, because a protection agreement can specify different terms — which is the negotiating space between a conservation body and an owner.

The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions.
