Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Fiji.

trackers.name: SPREP — three conventions, and 26 members is not 12 parties
trackers.desc: THE REGIONAL BODY FOR PACIFIC ENVIRONMENT, AND IT IS SECRETARIAT TO THREE CONVENTIONS. SPREP is an independent intergovernmental organisation, autonomous since the Agreement Establishing SPREP was signed at Apia on 16 June 1993, with the Article 2 purpose of providing assistance to protect and improve the environment and ensure sustainable development for present and future generations. It has 26 members — 14 Pacific island countries, 7 territories and 5 metropolitan states — and is headquartered in Apia, Samoa. ESTABLISH WHICH CONVENTION FITS YOUR ISSUE: the Noumea Convention (1986, in force 1990), described by UNEP as the only comprehensive multilateral umbrella agreement for protection of natural resources and environment in the region; the Waigani Convention on hazardous and radioactive waste imports; and the Apia Convention on nature conservation. THE NOUMEA CONVENTION IS UNDER ACTIVE REVIEW — WHICH IS AN OPENING: a 2021 Review produced recommendations now being implemented through a Noumea Workplan and Budget whose stated aim is to elevate the work of the Convention and enhance awareness and implementation, with a Communications Plan and a Finance Strategy named as critical. BUT CHECK WHETHER YOUR STATE IS A PARTY: SPREP has 26 members while the Noumea Convention has only 12 contracting parties — membership and party status are different things, and this entry does not assert the latter. GOVERNANCE POINT WORTH KNOWING: the SPREP Meeting is the plenary decision-making body; the Executive Board (established 2015) is subordinate to it and has no power to make decisions requiring input of all Members — so a decision affecting all members must go to the Meeting. IF YOUR ISSUE IS SEABED MINING: UNEP records deep sea mining as an emerging contentious issue the region is dealing with — the regional body has already named it. SPREP is also developing a portal for protected areas managers. THERE IS A SPREP PRESENCE IN YOUR COUNTRY: beyond Apia, host country agreements exist with the Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, the Marshall Islands, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu — so you need not approach Samoa first.

trackers.name: Pacific Development and Conservation Trust — citizens may apply
trackers.desc: AN INDIVIDUAL CAN APPLY, AND THE FIRST DOCUMENT IS SHORT. The Pacific Development and Conservation Trust, administered through the New Zealand government's Community Matters service with requests assessed by Advisory Trustees, states that ‘citizens or organisations’ from eligible Pacific places may request funding — so no incorporated body is required, which removes the commonest barrier recorded across this map. THE PROCESS IS TWO-STAGE: submit an Expression of Interest; only successful applicants are invited to submit a full project application. Do not prepare a full proposal before the EOI is accepted — wasted work, and expensive wasted work where drafting means travelling. Applications must be on the current form with all sections completed, submitted online where connection allows. READ THE PUBLISHED GRANT RECORD BEFORE DRAFTING: the Trust publishes records of grants by round — 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23 (two rounds), 2023/24 and 2024/25 — showing what the Trustees have actually funded, at what size and in which countries. That is better evidence of what will succeed than any guidance note. UNDP SUPPORT HERE IS COUNTRY-LEVEL: UNDP's Pacific Office provides country support to this state, so an in-country office is a realistic second route alongside the Trust.

trackers.name: SPREP EIA and SEA guidelines — intervene at scoping, not after
trackers.desc: SCOPING IS WHERE STAKEHOLDER CONCERNS BECOME TERMS OF REFERENCE — and the guidelines say so themselves. Assessments must be individually customised to the aspects most relevant to stakeholders, and ‘customisation usually occurs during the scoping phase and results in the preparation of terms of reference’. Intervene at scoping and the assessment is required to examine your issue; intervene later and you are commenting on an assessment that was never asked to look. SPREP's Strengthening Environmental Impact Assessment: Guidelines for Pacific Island Countries and Territories (60pp, English and French) is the regional practice standard, SPREP having been mandated on EIA capacity since the 1990s. KNOW WHICH INSTRUMENT YOUR FIGHT NEEDS: EIA assesses a project; the companion Strategic Environmental Assessment guidelines (developed 2018–2020) assess a policy, plan or programme and are addressed to environment agencies, national planning offices, development control agencies, municipal authorities and provincial administrations — so if the problem is a tourism plan or a zoning programme rather than one hotel, SEA is the instrument and the municipal or provincial authority is the addressee. There is also a sector guideline for coastal tourism development, made with the South Pacific Tourism Organisation. THE HONEST PART, FROM A REGULATOR'S OWN ACCOUNT: Vanuatu's Principal EIA Officer publicly described her department's challenges as lack of staff, lack of political support, weaknesses in public consultation, and low capacity in monitoring and enforcement. Expect to supply evidence the agency cannot gather itself, and expect post-consent monitoring to be weak unless someone outside government does it — it is also a citable admission when arguing that a condition needs an independent monitoring mechanism attached. CHECK YOUR OWN ENVIRONMENT ACT FIRST: many Pacific countries have EIA mandated under their Environment Acts and EIA Regulations, and these guidelines support the implementation of current legal requirements rather than replacing them — the practice standard, not the obligation. SPREP runs in-country EIA training workshops, and the Pacific Environment Portal carries regional and national data.

trackers.name: Waigani Convention — radioactive waste, and 200 miles not 12
trackers.desc: IT REACHES WHERE BASEL CANNOT — and for island states that is the whole point. The Waigani Convention is modelled on Basel and is the regional implementation of the hazardous waste regime, but differs in two decisive ways: it also covers radioactive wastes, and its territorial coverage includes each Party's Exclusive Economic Zone — 200 nautical miles — rather than stopping at the 12 nautical mile territorial sea as Basel does. That makes it the instrument for dumping, transhipment and seabed disposal cases Basel cannot touch. It is annex-driven: obligations extend to all wastes in Annex I or those possessing the listed characteristics — check Annex I first; if the substance is listed the obligations attach automatically, and if not, the argument runs through the hazard characteristics instead. It is closely tied to the London Convention on dumping at sea. THE BODY TO CONTACT: the Pacific Regional Centre for the Waigani and Basel Conventions, based at SPREP in Samoa, which has developed a model law implementing all four waste conventions (Basel, Rotterdam, Stockholm, Waigani) with a worked Tonga project — so where a national statute is missing or fragmented, the model already exists and a government can be pointed at it. AND A CONSULTATION WINDOW IS OPEN NOW: Cleaner Pacific 2025, the regional waste and pollution strategy built with 21 member countries around four goals and 15 strategic actions, is being replaced — the successor CP2036 was endorsed at the 31st SPREP Meeting (September 2023) with consultation in Suva, 21–22 July 2025. Priorities for the next decade are being set now. Ask whether your country has a national waste and pollution policy written against the regional strategy — it is the document your government is measured against. Delivery vehicles include PacWaste Plus (EUR 16.5 million, 72 months, EU-funded, across eight waste streams). THE HONEST LIMIT, FROM SPREP'S OWN REVIEW: Australia's reporting capability far exceeds that of most Pacific island countries, relying on weighbridge data requiring infrastructure that is not available — so do not assume an absence of data means an absence of a problem, and community-gathered data may be the best evidence there is. Watch the Clean Pacific Roundtable and CIRCLE EXPO, held alternately for an annual meeting of countries, industry and civil society — named as a participant category, not an observer.

trackers.name: Right to information — what your country actually has
trackers.desc: ASK EVEN WHERE THERE IS NO STATUTE — UNESCO's 2022 report on SDG 16.10.2 records that even Pacific states without access-to-information laws have an environment ‘generally favourable to the public's exercising of their right to information’. The absence of a law is not, on the region's own evidence, a reason to expect refusal. AND THERE IS A COMMITMENT TO CITE WHERE NO LAW EXISTS: the Boe Declaration on Regional Security (2018) Action Plan includes the adoption and implementation of constitutional, statutory and/or policy guarantees for public access to information as a measure for success — a government that signed Boe has already agreed that access to information is a measure of its own success. The Pacific Plan 2005 and the UN Pacific Strategy urge the same. The underlying right sits in article 19 of the ICCPR and of the Universal Declaration. REGIONAL POSITION: only four Pacific island countries have adopted RTI laws — Cook Islands (2008), Palau (2014), Vanuatu (2016) and Fiji (2018) — with several others drafting. A SOURCING WARNING FROM VANUATU'S OWN RTI UNIT, which applies region-wide: its site carries the notice ‘beware of fake websites pretending to be official’ — verify the domain before submitting anything containing your identity and your concern. IN FIJI — READ THE LIMITS BEFORE RELYING ON IT: the Information Act 2018 defines information broadly, but only Fijian residents or citizens may apply; requests are limited to cases where the information directly affects a decision regarding the requester; and only if the information came into existence after the law entered into force. Exemptions are broad, the Act does not address conflicts with secrecy provisions in other laws, and the only ground of appeal is where access is refused. Historic documents about a site are outside it entirely.

trackers.name: Fiji EIA Administrator — the public-concern trigger and the cash bond
trackers.desc: TWO PROVISIONS MOST COMMUNITIES NEVER LEARN ABOUT, AND BOTH HAVE TO BE ASKED FOR. FIRST, THE PUBLIC-CONCERN TRIGGER: if the EIA Administrator has reason to believe that there is a public concern relating to a proposal, the Administrator may require the approving authority to submit the EIA report for consideration to take into account the public concern — the threshold is not proof of harm, it is the Administrator having reason to believe concern exists, so documented concern addressed to that office by name is what the provision contemplates. SECOND, THE ENVIRONMENTAL CASH BOND: an approval may be subject to an environmental cash bond deposited into the Fund as security to cover the probable cost of preventing or mitigating environmental damage — the strongest condition available here, and discretionary, so ask for it by name at approval with a figure and a basis. THREE SEPARATE 21-DAY WINDOWS: the public may inspect and view an EIA report within 21 days of submission; a second public meeting must be held within 21 days of submission; and appeal to the Environmental Tribunal is within 21 days of the decision. To read, to be heard, and to appeal — diarise all three. Consultation happens twice and the first shapes the report: the proponent must consult during the EIA study, and hold a public hearing within the vicinity of the proposed development once it is complete — held by the proponent, not the regulator, and it must be near the site. CHECK THE REPORT FOR THE NO-ACTION OPTION: it must state the alternatives considered including the option of taking no action, and the reasons for choosing the proposed action — if it does not, it is incomplete on the face of the regulations. CONTACT: the Environment Impact Assessment Unit, senimili.baleicakau@govnet.gov.fj, +679 3311699, mobile 9905176; Monday–Thursday 8:00–16:30, Friday to 16:00; screening determination in 14 working days; application form EMA/EIAP 1. AND THE FILE CONTAINS THE LEASE OR TITLE among required supporting documents — which establishes who actually holds the land, often the first thing a community needs and cannot easily get elsewhere. Two structural points: a ministry or local authority proposing its own development must refer it to the EIA Administrator — government cannot assess its own project — and an approved EIA is valid only for the specific activity approved and must not be transferred, so if the project has changed, the approval may not cover it.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: NatureFiji-MareqetiViti — the NGO that works through customary landowners
trackers.desc: Fiji's first and only local biodiversity conservation NGO, working on habitat conservation, endangered species and sustainable use through collaborative conservation action, research and education. THE REASON TO CALL THEM ABOUT LAND: it expressly recognises the key role to be played by Fiji's indigenous landowners — and in Fiji most land is under customary ownership, so an organisation that works THROUGH landowners rather than around them is the one that can change what happens on a site. It also aims to generate local expertise in wildlife conservation and management — which means it can supply the biodiversity evidence a community needs and cannot produce alone. IF YOU NEED A DIFFERENT ORGANISATION, TWO DIRECTORIES WILL FIND YOU ONE: PIANGO publishes a member directory of national umbrella NGOs across 25 Pacific countries, with named contacts and addresses — an umbrella body is the fastest route to the right local organisation when you do not know who to call. PICAN lists members including the Anglican Church of Melanesia (nine dioceses across Solomon Islands, Vanuatu and New Caledonia) — a community-level network with reach no NGO in the region matches — and Vanuatu's Campaign for Justice, whose stated mission is to actively confront and expose those who obstruct natural justice with impunity. Live & Learn runs Climate Resilient Islands with rural communities in Fiji, Tonga, Vanuatu, Tuvalu, Solomon Islands, PNG and Samoa, with outcome areas including nature-based land management, and publishes filterable case studies and fact sheets. AND A FUNDING MODEL PACIFIC NGOs HAVE STUDIED: at Mida Creek in Kenya, 22 organisations share resources and finances around one protected area, funding guided eco-tours and alternative livelihoods such as beekeeping to relieve harvesting pressure — pooling finances around a single site is a funding model, not just a partnership.

trackers.name: Nakau — income instead of logging, with the land staying with the clans
trackers.desc: WHERE LAND IS UNDER CUSTOMARY OWNERSHIP AND CANNOT BE BOUGHT, THIS IS THE EQUIVALENT OF BUYING IT: an income stream that makes keeping the forest worth more than felling it, with ownership staying with the landholders. Nakau works with Indigenous customary landowners across the Pacific, within local governance systems, expressly to ensure all projects are owned by the customary landholders — which is the difference between this and a concession. Its delivery partner across Fiji, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu and PNG is Live & Learn. THE CASE THAT PROVES IT AGAINST AN ACTIVE LOGGING THREAT: at Drawa on Vanua Levu, logging coupes were already mapped and clearing had started when eight mataqali united to form the Drawa Block Forest Community Cooperative — a reversal at the last moment, and the vehicle was a cooperative formed by eight clans together. It now protects close to 4,000 hectares, is verified under Plan Vivo Climate, and won the International Energy Globe Award. WHERE THE MONEY WENT MATTERS MORE THAN THE HECTARES: credit income funded water and sanitation across five villages and supported women-led enterprises, honey, agroforestry, ecotourism and youth initiatives — the argument to put to neighbours who fear protection means poverty. ASK TO BE CONNECTED TO A WORKING PROJECT: Babatana, Drawa and Loru are verified and producing credits, not proposed. Others include Yato on Makira (10,000 hectares, with timber concessions still encroaching as recently as early 2025), East Rennell with 11 tribes, and 1,000+ hectares on New Georgia. NOW THE TWO REAL RISKS, BECAUSE THE RESEARCH RECORDS THEM: such agreements may create social unease by emphasising the disparity in wealth and power between rural landowners and environmental NGOs and donors, or cause within-community tensions through elite capture; and in one Manus case covering 83 clans in 19 villages and over 20,000 hectares, carbon financing had not yet started flowing. So the money may not arrive, and the benefits may be captured by a few — settle the benefit-sharing arrangement BEFORE any distribution, as that project did. Named backers include the EU, Ekos, MFAT, WWF-Australia and the Solomon Islands Threshold Program; Nakau and Live & Learn publish a toolkit for project coordinators.

trackers.name: Environmental Defenders Office — Pasifika Program
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the largest environmental legal centre in the Australia-Pacific region, whose Pasifika-led programme works on extractive industries, forestry, marine protection and climate across Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Fiji, Vanuatu and Tuvalu. WHO IT SUITS: an in-country organisation rather than an individual — EDO works predominantly through partner organisations (CELCOR in PNG, the Landowners Advocacy and Legal Support Unit and the Solomon Islands Environmental Law Association, the Fiji Environmental Law Association and the Vanuatu Environmental Law Association), supplying strategic legal capacity, co-authored law-reform papers and litigation support. Approach your national environmental law association first; its free advice hotline is for Australia only. YOUR NATIONAL PARTNER IS the Centre for Environmental Law and Community Rights (CELCOR). EDO is an Australian organisation based in Sydney, and its Pasifika Program is Pasifika-led — including diaspora Pasifika lawyers with cultural and spiritual links to the region — working predominantly through partner organisations. So the partner is the front door and EDO is the legal capacity behind it. Focus areas: climate change, threats to marine environments, forestry and mining. EDO is an accredited community legal service with a community advice hotline, the largest environmental legal centre in the Australia-Pacific, and records a historic Solomon Islands bauxite mine case. REACH IS LIMITED AND STATED: EDO names PNG, Solomon Islands, Fiji and Vanuatu, plus Tuvalu — it does not cover the other Pacific states, so do not assume regional coverage.

trackers.name: Centre for Environmental Law & Community Rights (CELCOR)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Papua New Guinea's public-interest environmental law NGO, established in 2000 — legal advice and representation for customary landowners, community organisations and NGOs facing logging, mining, oil palm, other extractives and marine development, alongside community legal education, paralegal training and mediation. It has intervened in most of PNG's provinces and supported the Mesulam v Joku ruling on the public's right to project information. WHO IT SUITS: a customary landowning group or CBO facing a resource project on its land — assistance to landowners is the core mandate, but this is a nine-person office working from Port Moresby only, so travel and capacity limit what it can take.

trackers.name: Friends of the Earth Asia Pacific
trackers.desc: The Asia Pacific regional structure of Friends of the Earth International, formed in 2008, whose member groups work on community-based struggles against destructive projects, particularly mining and other extractive industries, alongside Indigenous peoples, peasant farmers, fisherfolk and trade unions. WHO TO ENLIST: the national member group nearest the project. In this region Friends of the Earth International's own directory names groups in Bangladesh (BELA, the Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers' Association), India, Indonesia (WALHI), Japan, Malaysia (Sahabat Alam Malaysia), Nepal, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines (the Legal Rights and Natural Resources Center), South Korea and Sri Lanka. You CAN: reach an organisation that already works community-side in your own country, and draw regional weight onto a local fight. For activists: in several of these countries the Friends of the Earth affiliate is the most experienced community-side environmental body there is.

trackers.name: Office of the Auditor-General
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Papua New Guinea, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: IPA Companies Office
trackers.desc: National — Investment Promotion Authority company register, Papua New Guinea. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: PacLII – Papua New Guinea
trackers.desc: Free case law and legislation for Papua New Guinea via the Pacific Islands Legal Information Institute. · Find here: free Papua New Guinea legislation and court decisions, hosted by PacLII.

trackers.name: Papua New Guinea — Department of Treasury
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares the national budget and publishes annual budget volumes & economic updates, Papua New Guinea. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Papua New Guinea.

trackers.name: CEPA and the Director — the permit gate, and a seat on the Council
trackers.desc: FIRST, A DOMAIN WARNING: a site presenting itself as ‘PNG CEPA’ on a .com address carries official-sounding guidance with an injected gambling advert mid-sentence in its advice to proponents. That is SEO spam inside a page pretending to be a regulator. This map does not cite it, and CEPA's own canonical domain was not verified in this round — verify any CEPA address before sending anything. This link goes to SPREP's PNG portal, which hosts CEPA's own EIA guideline. THE STRONGEST PROVISION IN THE ACT IS A GATE ON EVERY OTHER AGENCY: under the Environment Act 2000, other governmental authorities shall be restrained from issuing permits or licences for level 2 or level 3 activities until an environment permit exists — so if a mining, forestry or works authority issued something first, that is a question worth asking in writing. Any other authority receiving an application for a level 2 or 3 activity shall refer it to the Director. The carve-out, stated plainly: this does not apply to approvals under the Investment Promotion Act 1992. THE EARLIEST DOCUMENTARY SIGNAL AVAILABLE: a proponent must register its intention in writing with the Director at least one month before commencing any preparatory work — that registration exists before any site clearance, earlier than an EIA or a permit application. Ask the Director whether an intention has been registered for your area. AND A SEAT ON THE DECIDING BODY, WHICH IS RARE: the Environment Council is appointed from a list of not less than 10 persons prepared after applications have been publicly invited by the Director from among citizens of Papua New Guinea — almost nothing else in this map offers a community member a seat on the body rather than a submission to it. Watch for that invitation. Activities are classified Level 1, Level 2 (2A/2B) and Level 3, but not all activities are listed in the Regulation — which makes a project's level classification itself contestable. For a large project, ask for the environmental and social management plans and the monitoring and reporting conditions, not just the permit — that is where monitoring obligations live, as in the Papua LNG Upstream Level 3 permit granted in September 2025 after more than a decade of assessment. Working without a permit can bring stop-work orders, substantial fines and prosecution of company directors. Provincial environment offices are a named point of consultation alongside CEPA.

trackers.name: ELAW — free attorneys and scientists who will critique the developer's EIA
trackers.desc: IT WILL READ THE DEVELOPER'S EIA AND TELL YOU WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT — which is the thing a community cannot produce alone and usually cannot afford. ELAW is a global alliance of attorneys, scientists and other advocates, founded 1989 in Eugene, Oregon by public interest lawyers from ten countries, that provides legal and scientific support to grassroots advocates to challenge destructive projects. FOUR CONCRETE FORMS OF HELP: legal support to local public interest lawyers; scientific support, including critiquing environmental assessments; economic insights on projects; and security expertise — ‘ELAW helps environmental lawyers improve their security so they can work without fear. When our partners are targeted, we act quickly to help defend and protect them.’ That last one is a named function, not an aspiration, and ELAW co-founded the Alliance for Land, Indigenous and Environmental Defenders. HOW TO USE IT — THROUGH A LAWYER, NOT AS A CLIENT: ELAW works through more than 300 public interest advocates in its network, and its stated strategy is ‘locating strong lawyers who are committed to protecting the environment in their home countries’. You can approach ELAW directly, but the leverage is greatest when a local advocate is the conduit — that is how the network is built. It has hosted nearly 300 advocates from more than 65 countries as Fellows and provided support on thousands of cases; several partners have won the Goldman Environmental Prize. Focus areas include biodiversity, fossil fuels — expressly assisting advocates in contesting fossil fuel development projects — plastic pollution, and work with coastal communities. It publishes guidebooks, including one to give communities sufficient understanding to challenge oil and gas projects, and clause-level summaries of national EIA law — so its site is also a route to learning exactly what your own EIA law requires. ASK WHETHER ELAW HAS A PARTNER IN YOUR COUNTRY: the network is described as spanning 70 to 80 countries but the member list is not published country by country, so this entry does not assert a presence in yours.

trackers.name: Nakau — income instead of logging, with the land staying with the clans
trackers.desc: WHERE LAND IS UNDER CUSTOMARY OWNERSHIP AND CANNOT BE BOUGHT, THIS IS THE EQUIVALENT OF BUYING IT: an income stream that makes keeping the forest worth more than felling it, with ownership staying with the landholders. Nakau works with Indigenous customary landowners across the Pacific, within local governance systems, expressly to ensure all projects are owned by the customary landholders — which is the difference between this and a concession. Its delivery partner across Fiji, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu and PNG is Live & Learn. THE CASE THAT PROVES IT AGAINST AN ACTIVE LOGGING THREAT: at Drawa on Vanua Levu, logging coupes were already mapped and clearing had started when eight mataqali united to form the Drawa Block Forest Community Cooperative — a reversal at the last moment, and the vehicle was a cooperative formed by eight clans together. It now protects close to 4,000 hectares, is verified under Plan Vivo Climate, and won the International Energy Globe Award. WHERE THE MONEY WENT MATTERS MORE THAN THE HECTARES: credit income funded water and sanitation across five villages and supported women-led enterprises, honey, agroforestry, ecotourism and youth initiatives — the argument to put to neighbours who fear protection means poverty. ASK TO BE CONNECTED TO A WORKING PROJECT: Babatana, Drawa and Loru are verified and producing credits, not proposed. Others include Yato on Makira (10,000 hectares, with timber concessions still encroaching as recently as early 2025), East Rennell with 11 tribes, and 1,000+ hectares on New Georgia. NOW THE TWO REAL RISKS, BECAUSE THE RESEARCH RECORDS THEM: such agreements may create social unease by emphasising the disparity in wealth and power between rural landowners and environmental NGOs and donors, or cause within-community tensions through elite capture; and in one Manus case covering 83 clans in 19 villages and over 20,000 hectares, carbon financing had not yet started flowing. So the money may not arrive, and the benefits may be captured by a few — settle the benefit-sharing arrangement BEFORE any distribution, as that project did. Named backers include the EU, Ekos, MFAT, WWF-Australia and the Solomon Islands Threshold Program; Nakau and Live & Learn publish a toolkit for project coordinators.

trackers.desc: KVKK — Personal Data Protection Authority — Turkey’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Ortak
trackers.desc: Istanbul-based independent investigative-journalism newsroom producing collaborative deep-dive investigations into power, corruption and environmental harm in Turkey. — Holds to account: officials handling public money & power — find investigations into Turkish state and corporate power.

trackers.name: TEMA Vakfı — hukuk mücadelesi ve il temsilcilikleri
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Turkish foundation that has been suing the state over land since 1997, when it took the Prime Ministry and the Forestry Ministry to the Council of State to strike down part of a regulation. Its biggest win was legislative — the Pasture Law, stalled for 38 years and lapsed four times, passed unanimously in 1998 after its campaign. It brings annulment actions against environmental plans and ÇED (impact assessment) decisions, including two cases against the 1/100,000 Mersin-Adana environmental plan covering the nuclear site. WHO IT SUITS: any community anywhere in the country, because of the thing that makes it unusual — it publishes a directory of provincial representatives, named individuals with phone numbers and emails, and it operates in all 81 provinces. Start with the temsilci for your province, not the head office. Be realistic about the odds: its 2014 action to annul the positive ÇED decision for the Akkuyu nuclear plant was dismissed and construction proceeded. This is a large mainstream foundation that litigates steadily and does not win everything.

trackers.name: Turkish Statistical Institute (TurkStat)
trackers.desc: Türkiye's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Turkey.

trackers.name: WWF-Türkiye (Doğal Hayatı Koruma Vakfı) — protection record
trackers.desc: WHO HAS ACTUALLY GOT LAND PROTECTED HERE. Founded as Doğal Hayatı Koruma Derneği in 1975, became a foundation in 1996 and the WWF network's Turkey office in 2001. Its record is protection rather than campaigning: protection status secured for 20 areas of unique natural value, international status for 8 critically important wetlands, a role in 5 areas being declared national parks, identification of Turkey's important bird areas, and contributing to stopping activities that threatened important natural areas. Landscapes worked in include the Caucasus Ecological Region, Eastern Black Sea Basin, Konya Closed Basin, Küre Mountains, Akyatan, Çıralı, Kaş, İğneada and the Susurluk Basin. As of 2025: over 100,000 supporters and more than 40 staff. THE TAX POINT, IF YOU ARE MOVING MONEY: it is registered with the Vakıflar Genel Müdürlüğü under registry number 3787 and holds vergi muafiyeti (tax exemption) granted by Council of Ministers decision no. 2009/15313 of 10 August 2009 — that Council-of-Ministers grant is the marker to check for any Turkish foundation before routing donations. Note the website takes individual transactions only; corporate requests go via info@wwf.org.tr.

trackers.name: Sivil Düşün — support for groups with no legal personality
trackers.desc: THE ONE THAT WILL TAKE YOU BEFORE YOU INCORPORATE. Alongside associations, foundations and unions, the EU's Sivil Düşün programme explicitly supports civic initiatives with no legal personality, networks, platforms and individual activists — so a residents' group formed last month to fight a development can apply in its own right, without first becoming a dernek or vakıf. That is rare anywhere. Support comes under 5 categories: events and meetings, organising, mobility and network-building, advocacy and campaigning, and communication. It takes applications from all 81 provinces and had supported 794 pieces of work at the time of this record. USE IT for the campaign phase — the advocacy and organising categories fit a land fight far better than a conservation grant would.

trackers.name: STGM — where Turkish grant calls are listed
trackers.desc: THE STANDING PLACE TO WATCH FOR MONEY. Sivil Toplum Geliştirme Merkezi announces open calls and publishes a guide to the grant programmes of 7 Turkish foundations that run them — Açık Toplum Vakfı, Bolu Bağışçılar Vakfı, Hayata Artı Vakfı, GençBank (TOG), Sabancı Vakfı, Türkiye Vodafone Vakfı and WWF-Türkiye, which runs its own grant programme as well as protecting land. STGM is also technical implementer for EU-funded civil society grant programmes, with the Central Finance and Contracts Unit (MFİB) as contracting authority. TWO THINGS TO CHECK BEFORE DRAFTING. EU programmes have run with Çevre ve Doğanın Korunması as a named thematic area — but sitting alongside children's, women's, disability and cultural rights, and requiring projects to cover at least 2 different thematic areas and build cooperation between CSOs from different fields, so a single-issue environmental project may need a partner from another sector to qualify. And Sivil Toplum için Destek Vakfı's programmes, open to associations, foundations and cooperatives established in Türkiye for work up to 12 months (an organisation supportable at most 2 years, reapplying each year), are aimed at social participation and the welfare of disadvantaged groups rather than conservation as such. TEMA Vakfı has separately hosted an environmental participation grant programme under ENV.net for advocacy and lobbying on the EU environmental acquis.

trackers.name: Tescil — apply to have an area registered as protected
trackers.desc: YOU CAN ASK FOR AN AREA TO BE REGISTERED. The Tabiat Varlıklarını Koruma Genel Müdürlüğü sets the procedures for determining, registering (tescil), approving and announcing natural assets, doğal sit alanları and special environmental protection zones, and fixes their boundaries — as it does for nature parks, nature monuments, nature conservation areas and wetlands. APPLICATION IS MADE TO THE GENERAL DIRECTORATE OR THE PROVINCIAL İL MÜDÜRLÜĞÜ, and the Directorate then carries out or commissions the research. The assessment team is specified by regulation: a city planner and landscape architect plus, according to the area, forest, agricultural, environmental, architectural or survey-cadastre engineers, hydrologists, biologists, zoologists and ecologists. THE PART THAT SAVES A COMMUNITY THE DECISIVE COST: for natural site areas the ecologically based scientific research report covering at least 4 seasons is commissioned by the General Directorate, not by the applicant — four seasons of survey is precisely the expense that defeats community groups elsewhere. NOTE THE SPLIT: national park boundaries are set by the forestry ministry and registered by Council of Ministers decision. Where natural, archaeological and urban site designations overlap on one property, a protocol of 01.10.2012 governs which rules apply.

trackers.name: Trampa — swap a building-banned parcel for Treasury land
trackers.desc: WHAT MAKES PROTECTION SURVIVABLE FOR THE OWNER. A regulation allows building-prohibited immovables left inside natural assets, doğal sit alanları and special environmental protection zones to be exchanged for Treasury (Hazine) land. The eligible applicant is defined as the owner of a separately owned property, all co-owners together where ownership is shared, and real or private-law legal persons wishing to transfer their closed or restricted-use property to the public. So an owner whose land has been made unbuildable by protection can seek land in exchange rather than absorb the loss — which is often what decides whether a designation is politically survivable locally. Apply through the provincial Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği directorate. CHECK THE EXCLUSIONS FIRST: land not registrable in the Treasury's name; land that must be allocated to the forestry ministry because it falls inside a national park, nature park, nature monument or nature conservation area; land in agrarian reform application areas where exchange is not approved; and land under the Cultural and Natural Heritage Law where the ministry has not approved exchange.

trackers.name: Çevre Hukuku AĞı — legal support network for urban and environmental cases (Turkey)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Turkish network whose stated purposes include providing legal support to vulnerable groups in urban, environmental and climate cases, supporting strategic cases that change a law or a practice, and encouraging pro bono mechanisms for public-interest legal help. It is open not only to lawyers but to public administrators, engineers, archaeologists, planners, anthropologists and economists — which matters, because a mining or dam case needs a hydrologist and an archaeologist as much as an advocate, and this network is built to carry both. WHERE IT COMES FROM: it stands in a line running back to the Izmir bar association's environment commission and the Çevre Hareketi Avukatları who fought the Bergama cyanide gold mine for over twenty years, and to the Çevre ve Ekoloji Hareketi Avukatları formed in 2011. Its legal coordinator has published on standing and legal interest in urban and environmental cases for the Union of Turkish Bar Associations, on the ecosystem effects of small hydro schemes and the case types that follow, and on the legal problems of the Akkuyu agreement. THE SOBER PART, FROM THAT SAME HISTORY: at Bergama the Council of State ruled in 1997 that the cyanide mine was contrary to the public interest, and the company accelerated its operations instead of complying. Over twenty-two years of litigation the mine was closed twice, once for less than a day. Lawyers who worked that case have said publicly that the non-implementation of judgments is what exhausted the villagers. Turkish communities should go in knowing that a favourable judgment is a step, not an ending, and plan for enforcement from the start.

trackers.name: Doğa Derneği — can tell you your site is one of Turkey's 305 key areas
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Turkish conservation association based at Seferihisar near İzmir which holds the country's baseline biodiversity record and works to remove threats to specific species and sites. It compiled Turkey's inventory of Önemli Doğa Alanları — Key Nature Areas — completed in 2006, synthesising data on plants, dragonflies, butterflies, freshwater fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals, and identifying 305 such areas across the country. If your site is one of the 305, that is a national-level designation you can put in front of a governor, a court or a newspaper, and it exists already: nobody has to survey anything first. Ask them whether it is, and ask for the underlying record. WHAT ELSE IT OFFERS: it describes advocacy as its method for eliminating threats to a species or a habitat, and it runs volunteer bird monitoring that a local group can join — which is one of the cheapest ways for a community to start generating its own evidence about a site rather than waiting for someone else's. Membership is open, at a stated annual subscription, and it publishes a donor bill of rights setting out that you may ask questions and receive immediate, accurate and open answers about how your money will be used. WHAT IT IS NOT, AND THIS IS A GAP IN TURKEY: it does not buy land, and across this work I found no Turkish organisation that does. For a Turkish community the available allies are the environmental law network, TEMA, and bodies like this one that supply the science. If your case needs the ground taken off the market, that route does not appear to exist domestically and you should plan without it.

trackers.name: Sivil Toplum için Destek Vakfı — grants that reach very small associations (Turkey)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: the Support Foundation for Civil Society, a Turkish grant-maker to civil society organisations, running among other things a şartlı hibe — conditional grant — programme. Turkey had no funder at all in this file. THE EVIDENCE THAT IT REACHES THE RIGHT KIND OF ORGANISATION: it granted to DOĞÇEV, the Nature and Environment Protection and Preservation Association, which described using the grant to meet the feeding, health and care needs of the animals it looks after, to provide for the care of its forests, and to keep the association's activities running. AND THE SENTENCE THAT SHOWS WHY THIS MATTERS MORE IN TURKEY THAN ELSEWHERE, in that association's own words: organisations like it survive on the small contributions of a few concerned people, those contributions are meaningful but insufficient, and associations with no other income have to stand on donations — and when the subject is nature and animals, it gets harder still. A Turkish community group should expect to be funding itself from donations, and this is one of the few doors that opens onto anything else. WHAT TURKEY STILL DOES NOT HAVE, recorded honestly across four searches now: no conservation land buyer. Its other entries in this file are the organisation holding the 305 Key Nature Areas inventory and the environmental law network. This adds money. AND THE SECTOR IS LARGER THAN THE FILE SUGGESTS: alongside those, publicly listed Turkish environmental organisations include TEMA, which has planted across thousands of hectares and campaigns on erosion, desertification and land protection; ÇEKÜL, working on natural and cultural heritage across Anatolian cities through volunteer representatives and expert staff in the localities themselves; TÜRÇEK, founded in Istanbul in 1972 as one of Turkey's first voluntary environmental bodies; and TURMEPA on the seas and coasts. SOURCING NOTE: the grant and the association's account of it come from the foundation's own published interview; the wider sector names come from third-party Turkish directories and are given as leads to verify, not as filed entries.

trackers.name: ÇEKÜL Vakfı — volunteer representatives in the towns, and the city inventories
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a foundation established in 1990 to protect Turkey's natural, historical and cultural assets, at Ekrem Tur Sok. No 8, Beyoğlu 34435 Istanbul. Its own description is the reason it is here: a civil society organisation that Anatolian cities consult, are guided by and trust, working through its volunteer representatives and expert staff to meet demands for the protection of natural and cultural heritage. Its approach runs deliberately from the smallest settlement outward to the country as a whole. THE MOST USEFUL THING IT PRODUCES: kent envanterleri — city culture inventories — prepared with local authorities as usable databases of what a place actually holds. Inventories have been prepared in Adana, Amasya, Antalya, Battalgazi, Burdur, Gaziantep, Gümüşhane, Gürün, İzmir, Karaman, Kilis, Mardin, Muğla, Ordu, Tekirdağ and Uşak. They are held and continuously updated at the ÇEKÜL Information and Documentation Centre, which it describes as one of Turkey's most comprehensive reference centres for nature and culture, open to researchers. If your site is in one of those cities, the record of what is there may already exist and be public. That is the seventh country in this file where the answer to who already surveyed this is yes. HOW IT WORKS WITH COMMUNITIES AND COUNCILS: its stated method is bringing together experts from local authorities, civil organisations, professional chambers and universities to join a city's conservation process, turning what they find into books, inventories and maps, and helping each city build conservation plans suited to its own fabric and living practices. Its Çarşamba meetings at the ÇEKÜL house exist to give direction to ongoing conservation work in Anatolian cities and to build road maps for it, on a stated principle of public, local, civil and private working together. IT ALSO PLANTS: it continues afforestation work in cooperation with the General Directorate of Forestry to protect natural heritage and prevent deforestation. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer, not a funder and not a law firm. It is expertise, documentation, convening and local representation — which in a country with no conservation land buyer is what a community can actually get.

trackers.name: TEMA Vakfı — Adana il temsilciliği
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: TEMA Vakfı's provincial representative for Adana. TEMA publishes a temsilcilikler directory of named İl Temsilcisi with phone numbers, email addresses and in many cases a street address, and it operates in all 81 provinces — which makes this the rare case where a land defender gets a person to ring in their own province rather than a head office. The foundation behind them has sued the state over land since 1997, brings annulment actions against environmental plans and ÇED decisions, and drove the Pasture Law through parliament in 1998. WHO IT SUITS: anyone in Adana facing a mine, quarry, plan or permit. Two honest caveats: representative posts fall vacant and TEMA periodically advertises for them, so check the directory rather than assuming Adana is currently staffed; and these are volunteers, not staff lawyers — they route you to the foundation's legal work, they do not conduct it.

WHO IT SUITS: anyone in Çanakkale facing a mine, quarry, plan or permit. Two honest caveats: representative posts fall vacant and TEMA periodically advertises for them, so check the directory rather than assuming Çanakkale is currently staffed; and these are volunteers, not staff lawyers — they route you to the foundation's legal work, they do not conduct it.

trackers.name: Information & Data Protection Commissioner (IDPC)
trackers.desc: Information & Data Protection Commissioner (IDPC) — Malta’s national data-protection / information authority, overseeing how public bodies handle personal data and enforcing access and privacy rights. — Holds to account: officials handling public information & personal data — find rulings, guidance and complaint channels.

trackers.name: Parliamentary Ombudsman of Malta
trackers.desc: Malta’s Parliamentary Ombudsman, investigating complaints against public bodies and monitoring places of detention.

trackers.name: Din l-Art Ħelwa — National Trust of Malta
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the National Trust of Malta, founded 1965, which does two things a community needs. It holds around seventeen sites under Deeds of Guardianship with the government or in trust from the ecclesiastical authorities, restoring and opening them — so it can take on a threatened site. And its Heritage and Environment Protection sub-committee reads the list of planning applications published WEEKLY IN THE GOVERNMENT GAZETTE, which is how you find out at all, and files objections at scale: 1,500 in one year against 9,599 applications. It built DLHAlert so the public can follow objections. WHO IT SUITS: everyone in Malta and Gozo, but understand the ladder before you climb it. Objecting is cheap; appealing is not. By its own account an appeal costs €200 to €1,000, needs a written case citing the policies and legislation, and runs to three or four sittings with photomontages, surveys, drawing analysis and expert affidavits, all rebutted and then defended in person — with a court appeal beyond that. It is volunteer-run with professionals acting pro bono, so it prioritises hard, and it cannot appeal everything it objects to. A GUARDIANSHIP DEED DOES NOT REQUIRE ANYONE TO BUY THE LAND: at Manoel Island a deed was signed between the developer and the Gżira Local Council, establishing a non-profit foundation to ensure heritage buildings, foreshore and significant green park spaces are restored and preserved for the whole community — so a local council can be a party to it, and the developer can be bound by it. AND NGOs CAN HOLD HALF THE BOARD OF A NATIONAL PARK: Il-Majjistral Nature & History Park is run by a federation of Din l-Art Ħelwa, Nature Trust (Malta) and the Gaia Foundation, with three NGO representatives, three public-sector representatives and a chairperson — a precedent to cite wherever a community is told park management must rest with government.

trackers.desc: National company / corporate registry. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.desc: National — National Audit Office of Malta. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Malta.

trackers.name: Malta Business Registry
trackers.desc: National beneficial-ownership register: official database of the natural persons who ultimately own or control companies and legal entities. Access restricted to authorities/obliged entities.

trackers.name: Daphne Caruana Galizia Foundation
trackers.desc: Foundation continuing the anti-corruption and money-laundering investigations of assassinated journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, and pressing for justice and rule of law in Malta.

trackers.name: ePPS eTenders
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Malta, and for how much.

trackers.name: National Statistics Office
trackers.desc: Malta's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Malta.

trackers.name: Malta Environment Foundation — no deadline, and first-timers are preferred
trackers.desc: A FUND THAT ACTIVELY PREFERS GROUPS THAT HAVE NEVER BEEN FUNDED. Priority is given to grassroots NGOs who have not received funding from MEF before — the same newcomer preference this map records for Seoul and Malaysia, and the opposite of the track-record gates in India and Ireland. If you have never been funded, say so; it counts in your favour. AND THERE IS NO DEADLINE RACE: the call remains open for the foreseeable future, with 3–4 steering committee meetings a year at which applications are reviewed — so submit when ready and expect a decision at the next committee. TWO CONCRETE GATES: you must be a voluntary organisation registered with the Office of the Commissioner for Voluntary Organisations (OCVO) with a strong environmental focus, and hold an active account with a local bank. WHAT THEY SELECT FOR: measurable and sustainable long-term results, capacity building, participation by the local community, and projects sufficiently visible to leverage additional support from other funders — visibility is a stated selection factor, so design for it. Training, equipment and facilitation are fundable, not only activity. OBLIGATIONS: interim and final reports, possible site visits, and participation in evaluation questionnaires and focus group discussions.

trackers.name: VO Funding Portal — including a scheme that pays your EU co-financing
trackers.desc: ONE PLACE LISTING THE SCHEMES OPEN TO MALTESE VOLUNTARY ORGANISATIONS — and it contains the answer to a barrier this map records again and again. Alongside the Sustainable Development Fund (grants to non-profit organisations for environmental, social and economic sustainability aligned to the SDGs, capped at EUR 10,000 per project and covering up to 80 percent of eligible costs — so budget the other 20 percent), the portal lists a scheme intended to support the co-financing obligations of voluntary organisations benefitting from EU institutions funding. If an EU grant requires a match you cannot raise, there is a national scheme aimed precisely at that gap — which is worth checking for in other member states too. Also listed: training and capacity-building schemes, and the Voluntary Organisations Project Scheme run by the Malta Council for the Voluntary Sector. FOR LARGER AMBITION: EU LIFE action grants are open to private non-commercial organisations including NGOs registered in the EU, and NGO Framework Partnership Agreements support operating grants co-financing NGOs' operating costs where they pursue an aim of general Union interest and are primarily active in environment or climate action.

trackers.name: Industrial Emissions Portal — what the facility actually releases
trackers.desc: IT ANSWERS ‘WHAT IS THIS FACILITY RELEASING, AND HOW MUCH’ — with named sites and quantities, not a description of a regulator. The Industrial Emissions Portal gives public access to environmental data from industrial facilities across EU Member States, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, Serbia and the UK. The Industrial Emissions Portal Regulation (IEPR) replaces the earlier E-PRTR Regulation and implements the Kyiv Protocol on Pollutant Release and Transfer Registers — binding since 8 October 2009, the only legally binding international instrument on PRTRs, and a protocol to the Aarhus Convention. THE MECHANISM IS REPUTATIONAL, AND THE UNECE SAYS SO OPENLY: though it regulates information about pollution rather than pollution directly, it is expected to exert downward pressure ‘as no company will want to be identified as among the biggest polluters’. That is the campaign use — the register produces a ranked, official, quotable list. THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT, AND IT PREVENTS A FALSE CONCLUSION: an installation not shown on a PRTR is either not an industrial activity covered by it, OR has not reached the stated pollutant-specific thresholds. Absence from the register is NOT evidence of no pollution — check the activity list and thresholds before relying on an absence. TWO DEFINITIONS THAT HELP: ‘the public’ includes natural or legal persons and their associations, organizations or groups, so an unincorporated community group qualifies; and a ‘facility’ is installations on the same site OR ON ADJOINING SITES under one operator — which matters where a plant has been split across parcels. As a scale example the UK register covers 91 pollutants back to 2007. IF YOU NEED ANOTHER COUNTRY: prtr.unece.org keeps a PRTR Global list of national registers, maintained by the OECD Working Party on PRTRs with UNECE, alongside CEC Taking Stock for North America and the NGO-built Blue Map Database in China — where a government has not built a register, that is the precedent for one built anyway.

trackers.name: Aarhus Compliance Committee — one person may bring the State itself
trackers.desc: THE ONLY ROUTE IN THIS MAP BY WHICH ONE PERSON CAN BRING A STATE ITSELF BEFORE AN INTERNATIONAL BODY over environmental decision-making. Under Decision I/7 (2002), paragraphs 18–24, communications may be brought by one or more members of the public concerning any Party's compliance — no organisation, no accreditation, no minimum number. The ACCC is a quasi-judicial body reporting to the Meeting of the Parties. THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD PART: YOU DO NOT HAVE TO EXHAUST DOMESTIC REMEDIES. Paragraph 21 says the Committee takes account of any available domestic remedy unless its application is unreasonably prolonged or obviously ineffective. What you must do is state whether steps have been taken and, if not, why not — a section of the form, not a bar to entry. WHAT MAKES IT INADMISSIBLE: anonymity, abuse of the right, being manifestly unreasonable including de minimis, incompatibility, or concerning a non-Party or a State that opted out — and no State has opted out. The only one most people risk is ‘de minimis’: frame it as a systemic failure of information, participation or access to justice, not a complaint about one permit. PRACTICALITIES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT LANDS: there is a required format, and cut-off dates tied to meetings — as a worked example, communications received by 4 May 2026 were for the 15 and 18 June 2026 meeting, provided they were complete, in format, and needed no translation. Check the current cut-off; missing it costs a cycle. Submit in English, French or Russian — the secretariat translates, but needing translation can push you past a cut-off. Send copies, not originals. AND KNOW THIS BEFORE YOU FILE: once preliminary admissibility is determined the case gets a number and BECOMES PUBLIC — there is a confidentiality section on the form. The process runs receipt → admissibility → response by the Party → draft findings → public hearing → final findings and recommendations. Address: Aarhus Convention Secretariat, UNECE, Palais des Nations, Geneva. CONFIRM YOUR STATE IS A PARTY before relying on this — this entry is recorded here on the basis that the state is bound by the Kyiv Protocol to the Convention, which implies but does not prove Party status.

trackers.name: EIA Directive — ask for the screening determination
trackers.desc: IF A PROJECT NEAR YOU IS PROCEEDING WITHOUT AN EIA, THERE IS A PUBLISHED, REASONED DOCUMENT EXPLAINING WHY — AND ALMOST NOBODY ASKS FOR IT. Annex I projects get mandatory EIA; Annex II projects — the far larger category — go through a screening procedure using the Annex III criteria. Under Directive 2014/52/EU the developer supplies specified Annex IIA information, and that determination SHALL be made available to the public and must be duly motivated. Ask for the screening determination: it is the most useful document in the procedure and the one people do not know exists. TIMING: determinations must be made within 90 days of complete information, unless the authority extends the period giving reasons in exceptional cases and informs the developer. BUT BE REALISTIC ABOUT THE LIMIT: proposals to require public participation during screening were dropped from the 2014 text as impractical — you have a right to the determination, not a right to be heard before it is made. THREE MORE THINGS THE 2014 AMENDMENT GIVES YOU: reports must be more understandable to the public, especially on the current state of the environment and alternatives; competent authorities must prove their objectivity to avoid conflicts of interest — making a conflict a ground of challenge, not a complaint; and the grounds for consent decisions must be clear and transparent. ASK ALSO WHETHER A SCOPING OPINION HAS BEEN REQUESTED — it fixes what the assessment is required to look at. Reports must carry a non-technical summary (Annex IV), and information must be provided as early as possible, electronically, by public notice or bill posting, or in local newspapers. THE DIRECTIVE IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING: Member States may lay down more stringent conditions and fix penalties — check the national transposition before assuming the EU minimum applies. The regime is Directive 2011/92/EU (applying since 17 February 2012) as amended by 2014/52/EU, codifying rules in force since 1988 and aligned to the Espoo and Aarhus Conventions. ONE PATTERN TO WATCH: the legislative history records concern that formal screening could become a ‘mini-EIA’ before the full EIA — an unusually detailed screening determination is itself an argument that full assessment was warranted.

trackers.name: Espoo points of contact — a named official, and ‘were you notified?’
trackers.desc: A NAMED OFFICIAL, A DIRECT EMAIL, AND A QUESTION WITH A DOCUMENTARY ANSWER. The UNECE publishes the points of contact regarding notification under article 3 of the Espoo Convention on EIA in a transboundary context: notifications of activities likely to cause significant adverse transboundary impact shall be transmitted to the relevant points of contact. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ORDINARY LAND CASE: if a project sits near a border, the affected country's point of contact should have been notified — so ask both points of contact whether notification was given. It is a cheap, precise question, and failure to notify is a procedural defect in the consent. The list gives each Party's named official, department, postal address, telephone and email: Czechia's sits in the Department of EIA and Integrated Prevention at the Ministry of the Environment; Denmark's is the Agency for Green Transition and Aquatic Environment using the functional address espoo@sgav.dk; Croatia's is a Director at the Ministry of Economy and Sustainable Development; Canada's is the President of the Impact Assessment Agency. PREFER A FUNCTIONAL ADDRESS WHERE ONE IS LISTED — named officials move. AND NOTE A ROUTING PATTERN: some Parties route notification through their Ministry for Foreign Affairs c/o their Permanent Mission in Geneva rather than an environment ministry — where that is so, the environment ministry may not hold the file and the foreign-ministry route is the correct one. A SECOND DIRECTORY, AND A SECOND ROUTE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT: the EEA publishes a list of Eionet national focal points covering 32 member countries and 8 cooperating countries (Albania, Bosnia, Kosovo, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine). Data are reported upwards — from stakeholder, to competent authority, to the EEA, to the Commission — so if your national authority has reported something, the EEA holds it too. Where a national body is unresponsive or its figures look wrong, the same data sits one level up in a body with no stake in the local decision. CONFIRM YOUR COUNTRY APPEARS ON THE LIST before relying on it. SCOPE: Espoo governs transboundary notification and Eionet governs data reporting — for the domestic EIA procedure itself, see the EIA Directive entry recorded separately.

trackers.name: Flimkien għal Ambjent Aħjar (FAA) — joins residents' planning objections (Malta)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Maltese non-profit working since 2006 across Malta and Gozo, whose listed methods include campaigns and planning objections alongside heritage tours and community events. Its pattern is to join residents already objecting to a specific application rather than run separate campaigns — recent examples on its channels include supporting residents of a two-metre-wide Valletta alley against a joinery workshop beneath their homes, and joining objections to a townhouse conversion inside Attard's urban conservation area. It maintains a contact route specifically for environment and planning concerns, separate from general enquiries. THE CASE IT PUBLISHES THAT EVERY MALTESE OBJECTOR SHOULD READ FIRST: application PA 03552/15, a six-storey addition on a house that had been certified unstable, was recommended for refusal by the Planning Authority's own case officer, by the Sanitary Officer and by the Cultural Heritage Officer — and was approved anyway. The refusal grounds turned on sanitary law limiting building height in narrow streets to preserve light and air. A case officer's recommendation to refuse is not the decision. A community that hears its objection has been accepted by the case officer should treat that as the halfway point, not the end. HOW IT PAYS FOR ITSELF, WHICH IS ALSO HOW YOU HELP: it runs heritage tours, gardening workshops and lectures, and states that ticket sales fund the campaigns. Turning up to an event is a concrete way for a community with no money to contribute to the body objecting on its behalf. IT COMPLEMENTS RATHER THAN REPEATS: Malta's other ally in this file holds sites under guardianship deeds. This one contests applications. Different fights, different phone calls.

trackers.name: Nature Trust – FEE Malta — manages the protected sites, and fronts the joint demands
trackers.desc: WHO THEY ARE: a non-profit environmental NGO founded in 1962, one of the oldest in the Maltese Islands, voluntary organisation VO0048, a privileged partner of WWF and the Maltese coordinator for the Foundation for Environmental Education. Its own statement of purpose is conservation, managing areas of natural and scientific interest, and lobbying for effective environmental legislation. WHAT IT ACTUALLY HOLDS, WHICH IS THE POINT FOR A COMMUNITY: it manages or is taking on a list of named sites — Wied Għollieqa Nature Reserve, Xrobb l-Għagħin Nature Park, il-Ballut Natura 2000 at Marsaxlokk, il-Magħluq Natura 2000 at Marsascala, Pembroke garigue Natura 2000, Fiddien and Chadwick Lakes, Ħirkewwa Marine Park, Simar Nature Reserve at Xemxija, Foresta 2000 near Mellieħa, and Majjistral Nature and History Park jointly with others. If a threatened Maltese site adjoins or resembles one of these, there is an organisation with management experience of that exact habitat and a track record the authorities already recognise. Simar is a degraded wetland it restored into a Ramsar site of international importance — useful precedent when a developer argues ground is too far gone to be worth protecting. AND IT ORGANISES THE OTHERS: it has fronted joint environmental demands to the political parties, endorsed by Extinction Rebellion Malta, Għawdix, Moviment Graffitti, Rota, the Grow 10 Trees Project, Wirt Għawdex and Żminijietna. That is the third confirmation in this file that small-island cases move when organisations sign together — the same pattern as the two Cypriot Akamas letters. Ask who else will sign. IT NAMES THE THREATS ITSELF: urban development and land reclamation head its own list, alongside illegal hunting, littering, water scarcity and climate impacts. WHAT IT IS NOT: not a land buyer and not a law firm. Malta's other entries here are the guardianship-deeds body and the objections body; this is the site manager and the convenor.

trackers.name: Moviment Graffitti — publishes the objection template and the deadline (Malta)
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Maltese organisation set up in 1994 at 67 Strait Street, Valletta, info@movimentgraffitti.org, active against the exploitation of people, the environment and animals. It states that it is autonomous from any economic power or political party, has no hierarchies, and welcomes new members as activists or supporting members. In a two-party island that independence is the first thing a residents' group should check, and it is stated outright. WHAT IT DOES ON A LIVE APPLICATION, WHICH IS AS PRACTICAL AS THIS FILE GETS: on a proposed lido reclaiming land from the sea it published the objection address, the deadline, and the application number to cite — and put an objection template on its own channels so any resident could send one. Nothing else in this file combines the site, the reference number, the closing date and the ready text in one place. IT ALSO PAYS FOR APPEALS: it launched a crowdfunding campaign to appeal a permit for uprooting 800 trees and heavy construction on the Comino Nature Reserve, publishing its bank account and IBAN, and asked the public to leave contact details through a dedicated form so further action could be organised. A community facing an appeal it cannot fund has a working precedent for raising the money publicly. AND IT WORKS ACROSS THE PARTY LINE: it helped set up Kamp Emergenza Ambjent, took a lead in the campaign for coastal access at Manoel Island in alliance with a Labour-led council, and teamed up with a Nationalist-led St Julian's council and a Labour-led Pembroke council to oppose a project on land granted by government to a developer. Two councils of opposing parties on the same objection is the strongest local configuration available in Malta, and it has assembled it. WHAT IT IS: direct actions, protests, coalitions and awareness work — not a law firm, not a land buyer, not a funder for others. Its own framing is that development should be judged by its effect on people's lives rather than carried out for its own sake.

trackers.desc: National public-procurement / budget-transparency portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Russia, and for how much.

trackers.name: Общественная экологическая экспертиза — a citizens' review with legal standing
trackers.desc: A STATUTORY PROCEDURE, NOT A PROTEST. Federal Law 174-ФЗ of 23 November 1995 gives an entire chapter to the rights of citizens, public associations and other non-state non-commercial organisations in environmental review, and to public environmental review as an institution: article 21 (objects), 22 (conducting), 23 (conditions), 24 (refusal to register the application) and 25 (the conclusion). It is a registered procedure running in parallel with state review and producing a formal заключение. READ ARTICLE 24 FIRST: it sets out the grounds on which registration may be refused, and that is where applications die — the refusal grounds are your drafting checklist. AND THE LEVER MOST PEOPLE MISS: the law provides for organisation of public environmental reviews по требованию населения — at the demand of the population — and for informing federal executive bodies about planned economic activity on the territory of the municipal formation. Residents can demand their municipality organise a review, and the municipality carries an information duty about planned activity on its own territory.

trackers.name: Is your site inside an ООПТ? That decides whether review is compulsory
trackers.desc: THE THRESHOLD QUESTION FOR ANY RUSSIAN SITE. State environmental review is mandatory for capital construction planned within the boundaries of federal-level protected natural territories (ООПТ) — excepting listed social infrastructure objects that are not category I or II and sit in settlements listed under article 3_1 of Federal Law 33-ФЗ. It is also mandatory for especially dangerous, technically complex and unique objects, and defence and security objects, planned within regional and local-level ООПТ where federal law permits building there at all. So establish whether your site sits inside an ООПТ, and at which level, before anything else — it determines whether review is compulsory. NOTE HOW WIDE THE BAIKAL DEFINITION IS: the Baikal natural territory covers the lake, its water protection zone, its catchment within Russia, adjoining protected territories, and the adjoining land up to 200 kilometres west and north-west. PUBLIC REGISTERS TO MINE: Rosprirodnadzor maintains a register of public discussion materials and a register of issued state environmental review conclusions — primary evidence of what was decided and what was consulted on.

trackers.name: Before you organise: designation risk under the foreign-agent laws
trackers.desc: SAID PLAINLY, BECAUSE IT AFFECTS HOW YOU USE EVERYTHING ELSE HERE. Russia's foreign-agent and undesirable-organisations legislation has been applied to environmental organisations, several of which have been designated or liquidated; designation brings labelling obligations, reporting burdens and personal legal exposure for those involved, and status can change faster than any directory is updated. THIS MAP THEREFORE RECORDS STATUTORY MECHANISMS RATHER THAN A LIST OF ORGANISATIONS TO CONTACT FOR RUSSIA — the rights in 174-ФЗ belong to citizens and municipalities and do not depend on joining any organisation. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES: check the current designation status of any organisation before affiliating with it or accepting funding from it; be aware that foreign funding is the specific trigger the legislation targets, so international grants recorded elsewhere in this map carry a risk in Russia that they do not carry elsewhere; and prefer routes that operate through your own municipality and through registered statutory procedures, which are harder to characterise as foreign-directed activity. Verify the present state of the law before acting — it has changed repeatedly and this entry may lag it.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Get into the ten-year regional scheme — it plans terminations too
trackers.desc: THE DOCUMENT THAT DECIDES WHETHER YOUR SITE IS EVEN A CANDIDATE. Under Zakon No. 150-Z of 15 November 2018 on specially protected natural territories, региональные схемы рационального размещения ООПТ местного значения are developed by oblast and Minsk city executive committees together with the National Academy of Sciences and other interested bodies, for a ten-year period, and include measures planning the declaration, transformation and termination of заказники and local памятники природы — approved by local councils in agreement with Minprirody. THREE CONSEQUENCES: get into the scheme, as with Thailand's provincial action plan recorded elsewhere here; the same scheme plans TERMINATIONS as well as declarations, so read it for what is being removed; and the Academy of Sciences is a statutory co-author, so a scientific case addressed to НАН Беларуси reaches a body with a drafting role. STATE ADMINISTRATION IS SHARED: the President, Council of Ministers, Minprirody, and local Councils of Deputies and executive bodies — with article 9 setting out the local powers expressly. Minprirody maintains the реестр, the register of specially protected natural territories, which is where to establish existing status. A BROADER CONTAINER TO KNOW: a биосферный резерват includes individual protected territories as well as other territories where rational (sustainable) use of natural resources is purposefully stimulated — a category that expressly takes in ordinary land under economic use.
