trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)
trackers.desc: THE REGIONAL CARIBBEAN CONSERVATION FUND, established September 2012, managing roughly USD 70 million through two instruments — an Endowment Fund of about USD 43 million that is a permanent funding source to National Conservation Trust Funds, and the EbA Facility. APPLY TO YOUR NATIONAL FUND, NOT TO CBF, for the endowment stream: at national level the NCTFs lead the grantmaking process, with proceeds held in country-based subaccounts. The EbA Facility is the direct route, awarding through competitive calls for proposals — medium grants USD 250,000–1 million, large grants up to USD 2 million — scoped to the marine and coastal zone, so an inland project must show its connection there. Eligible recipients expressly include community-based organisations and non-registered citizen groups, alongside NGOs, government agencies and universities. CBF has supported the establishment of conservation trust funds in 8 countries, contributed to management of over 500 protected areas, and worked with over 50 local implementing partners. IF YOU ARE TOO SMALL FOR EbA: CBF partners with GEF SGP across 12 shared countries — the community-scale sibling route, recorded separately in this map. CUBA-SPECIFIC ROUTE: CBF partners with UNDP Cuba to channel funding through GEF SGP Cuba, so the practical door here is the GEF Small Grants Programme country office rather than a national conservation trust fund.

trackers.name: Ley 150/2022 — environmental damage now carries civil and criminal liability
trackers.desc: IF YOU ARE WORKING FROM LEY 81 MATERIAL, YOU ARE WORKING FROM THE OLD LIABILITY REGIME. Ley 150/2022 ‘Del Sistema de los Recursos Naturales y el Medio Ambiente’, approved 14 May 2022 and published in Gaceta Oficial No. 87 of 13 September 2023, defines the concept of environmental damage and establishes civil and criminal responsibility for those who cause it — a precision absent from Ley 81, which is described as having lacked clear mechanisms to hold infringers effectively responsible. It regulates the actions of the State, of citizens and of society in general. ACCOMPANYING MEASURES: restructuring of CITMA as governing body of environmental policy; Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica; and monitoring and continuous reporting on compliance. Strategic assessment applies to plans and programmes, not only projects — so a sectoral plan or investment programme is assessable in its own right. CITE THE CONSTITUTION TOGETHER WITH IT: Article 75 gives all persons the right to a healthy and balanced environment, tied to the survival, wellbeing and security of present and future generations; and Article 90(j) makes it a duty of citizens to protect natural resources and velar por la conservación of a healthy environment. That is a duty, not only a right — where individual standing is narrow, making a report discharges a constitutional obligation rather than asserting an interest.

trackers.name: Ley 81 art. 16 — local bodies can propose stricter local standards
trackers.desc: THE ROUTE THROUGH THE BODY YOU CAN ACTUALLY REACH. Article 16 of Ley 81 (11 July 1997) provides that los Órganos Locales del Poder Popular may propose to the competent bodies the establishment, in their respective territories and in attention to their particular situation, of environmental norms and parameters more rigorous or specific than the general ones. A local assembly can propose stricter standards than the national baseline, framed as responsive to local circumstances. The law also allows dirimir discrepancias between organs of government and whatever other declarations relating to specific areas, ecosystems or resources are needed to fulfil its objectives — a catch-all declaratory power. ASK WHICH OF THE ELEVEN INSTRUMENTS APPLIES: Title III lists environmental planning, ordenamiento ambiental, licencia ambiental, evaluación de impacto ambiental, the environmental information system, the sistema de inspección ambiental, education, research, economic regulation, the Fondo Nacional del Medio Ambiente, and the regimes of administrative, civil and criminal responsibility. Licence and inspection are separate instruments — an inspection is not a licensing act, and both generate documents. ADDRESS WILDLIFE TO THE RIGHT MINISTRY: protection of wild flora and fauna belongs to the Ministry of Agriculture and the Ministry of Fishing Industry, not CITMA. Article 8(h) covers preservation of cultural heritage associated with the natural setting.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Ley 217 art. 20 — the money to pay owners must exist before the declaration
trackers.desc: THE STRONGEST ADVANCE-COMPENSATION PROVISION IN THIS MAP. Protected areas are declared by law, and article 20 of Ley 217 lists six things that must be taken into account before the declaratoria — including (5) the budget line to pay, in cash and in advance, the owners who would be affected, (2) a technical study covering biophysical, social and cultural conditions, and (6) the indigenous communities where the area is established on their lands. The appropriation must exist before the area is declared — so if a declaration is proposed over your land, ask which budget line covers point 5. Compare Lesotho, where late payment was a breach; here the money must be voted beforehand. ARTICLE 21: all activities in a protected area must conform to the plan de manejo approved by MARENA — and where an area has no management plan, activities run under the default regime, so the absence of a plan is itself worth checking. Article 18 objectives include protecting watersheds, hydrological cycles and aquifers and the surroundings of historical, archaeological and artistic monuments — a route where your site has heritage value. The law declares the environment patrimonio común de la nación, makes it the duty of the State and of all inhabitants to protect and restore, and requires the State to support indigenous communities of the Autonomous Regions, the Pacific or the Centre — not only the Caribbean coast.

trackers.name: Ley 445 — communal land, with or without title, and a fund to demarcate it
trackers.desc: ‘WITH OR WITHOUT REAL TITLE OF DOMAIN’ IS THE OPERATIVE PHRASE. Ley 445 defines communal land as a geographic area in possession of an indigenous or ethnic community with or without title — comprising inhabited land and the traditional scope of its social, economic and cultural activities, sacred places, forested areas for reproduction and multiplication of flora and fauna, boat construction, and subsistence hunting, fishing and agriculture. Possession founds the claim, and sacred sites and forest reproduction areas are named categories. THE CONSTITUTIONAL PROTECTION TO QUOTE: communal lands cannot be encumbered and are inembargables, inalienables e imprescriptibles — not attachable for debt, not alienable, not lost by lapse of time. THE PROCEDURE: article 41 creates CONADETI, which directs demarcation and rules on applications; you begin by filing with the corresponding CIDT. AND THERE IS A DEDICATED FUND FOR THE COST: a Fondo Nacional de Demarcación y Legalización de Tierras Comunales, administered by CONADETI under Finance Ministry supervision, for which CONADETI must render accounts. GOVERNANCE ON YOUR OWN TERMS: elections and removals of communal and territorial authorities follow the customs and traditional procedures of the communities (art. 6). AND THE COUNCILS OWE YOU A TRANSLATION: art. 67 requires the law to be translated and widely disseminated in the languages of the indigenous peoples. It covers the Atlantic Coast and the Coco, Bocay, Indio and Maíz river basins, and traces to the Harrison-Altamirano treaty of 1905.

trackers.name: The Dui Hua Foundation
trackers.desc: US-based humanitarian NGO founded in 1999 that maintains the world’s largest database of China’s political and religious prisoners — tens of thousands of cases compiled since 1980 by systematically mining Chinese court records — and uses it to prepare prisoner lists submitted directly to the Chinese government, securing clemency, sentence reductions and better treatment for hundreds of at-risk detainees including dissidents, religious practitioners, ethnic minorities, and women and juveniles in prison; it is the only group conducting sustained direct human-rights dialogue with Beijing on individual prisoners.

trackers.name: 环境民事公益诉讼 — who may sue, and on what evidence
trackers.desc: THE STANDING TEST, FROM THE SUPREME PEOPLE'S COURT'S OWN INTERPRETATION (adopted 8 December 2014, in force 7 January 2015). Under Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law a social organisation may sue over pollution or ecological destruction harming the public interest if it is registered with the civil affairs department of a government at or above the level of a city divided into districts, and has engaged specifically in environmental protection public interest activities continuously for more than 5 years with no record of violation. If those are met the court shall accept the case; the organisation must not seek economic benefit from the suit. WHAT THE TERMS MEAN: social groups, private non-enterprise units and foundations all count. YOUR CHARTER DECIDES WHAT YOU CAN SUE ABOUT — the test is met where the charter states that the purpose and main business scope is protecting the social public interest, and the public interest at stake in the suit must be related to that stated scope. ‘No violation record’ means no administrative or criminal penalty in the course of business in the 5 years before filing. HAVE THIS READY WHEN YOU FILE: registration certificate, charter, the annual work reports or annual inspection reports for the 5 consecutive years before suit, and a signed and stamped declaration of no violation record. Article 9 lets the court invite you to add claims such as ceasing the infringement and restoring the original state if what you asked for is too narrow to protect the public interest. THE LIMIT: this is the CIVIL route. Environmental administrative public interest litigation — challenging a government decision — can be brought only by the procuratorate, so a challenge to an approval must go through persuading it to act.

trackers.name: CEPF — Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund grants
trackers.desc: MONEY THAT REACHES SMALL GROUPS. CEPF funds civil society organisations of all sizes — farmers' cooperatives and community groups as much as universities and international NGOs. Small grants average about USD 15,000 and large grants about USD 150,000; in the Indo-Burma Phase IV call, which listed China among its eligible countries, small grants ran to USD 50,000 and large grants USD 50,000–250,000. ITS STATED PREFERENCES FAVOUR YOU: priority goes to projects showing a leading role for local organisations or building local civil society capacity, and to projects supporting Indigenous and local communities in community-based or co-management conservation — explicitly including actions that enhance local communities' tenure and resource use rights. Small grant applications in that call were accepted in Chinese and other regional languages, not only English. HARD CONDITIONS: your organisation needs its own bank account and must be able to receive charitable contributions under national law; the project must sit inside a biodiversity hotspot where CEPF currently works and support at least one strategic direction in that hotspot's ecosystem profile — read the profile before writing anything. Excluded: anything that could adversely affect critical habitat, introduce invasive non-indigenous species, or remove or alter tangible cultural heritage. CHECK THE CURRENT CALL: eligible countries are listed per call and windows are fixed — Indo-Burma Phase IV ran 2 February to 16 March 2026. Since 2000 CEPF has given over USD 300 million to more than 2,700 organisations across more than 112 countries.

trackers.name: 社会公益型保护地 — a 50-year management agreement instead of a purchase
trackers.desc: YOU CANNOT BUY THE LAND, SO YOU CONTRACT FOR IT. In 2011, with Sichuan provincial support, China's first civil nature reserve was created at Laohegou, Pingwu County — core giant panda habitat and a migration corridor that sat in no legally protected area system, with management limited to basic patrol and fire prevention while poaching, snaring and poison-fishing were common. THE MECHANISM: a 50-year entrusted management agreement (委托管理协议) with the county gave the Taohuayuan Foundation long-term management rights over three forest parcels within 110 km², with the foundation raising social funds and taking full responsibility for establishment, management and financing. YOU NEED A REGISTRABLE LOCAL ENTITY: a 民办非企业 private non-enterprise unit, the Pingwu Laohegou Nature Conservation Centre, was registered to run it. The model is described as more flexible than government reserves, able to work where government cannot, and able to bring collective and individual land into protection at relatively low cost — made possible by collective forest tenure reform. Recognised by the State Forestry Administration, it has been replicated at Bayuelin (Leshan, Sichuan) and Xicaohai (Heqing, Yunnan).

trackers.name: 保护地役权 and 社区协议保护 — easements and community agreements
trackers.desc: TWO CONTRACT ROUTES, WITH THEIR LIMITS STATED. Conservation easements (保护地役权): Qianjiangyuan National Park and others have piloted collective forest and moso bamboo easements, and Article 22 of the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park Regulations (Trial) expressly lets the park authority manage collectively owned natural resources through easement contracts. BUT LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP RECORDS REAL WEAKNESSES: subjects, rights, creation procedures and registration requirements differ widely between localities and lack internal consistency; practice is usually led by the protected-area authority or local government, emphasising public objectives with little attention to protecting private property rights; and some localities hold back over doubts about the legal basis under the Civil Code. Community conservation agreements (社区协议保护) follow a clear sequence: first establish who owns the resource and who can authorise — reserve authority for state reserves, the village for collective land; then mobilise, choosing communities with genuine willingness and organisational capacity; then negotiate and sign, drafting a conservation plan and a development plan together. At Longge village in Sanjiangyuan this took about 5 months of discussion and produced a cooperative joined by all 53 herding households. AND THE APPROACH THAT MADE IT WORK NEAR LAOHEGOU: the foundation did not start by policing hunters — it asked what the community's own grievance was, found it was outsiders digging medicinal herbs, and villagers amended their own 村规民约 to bar them. Only then did protection extend to wildlife, and the community accepted it.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Kuwait Regional Convention (ROPME) — and its Judicial Commission
trackers.desc: THE ONE BINDING ENVIRONMENTAL INSTRUMENT COVERING ALL EIGHT GULF STATES. The Kuwait Regional Convention for Cooperation on the Protection of the Marine Environment from Pollution was signed 24 April 1978 and entered into force 1 July 1979 — 30 articles, described as the basic legal instrument binding the eight States of the Region. ALL EIGHT ARE FULL PARTIES: ROPME records ‘no signatories without ratification, acceptance, approval or accession’, so unlike some regional instruments there is no signed-but-unratified state to argue about. ARTICLE II fixes the Sea Area by coordinates, from Ras Dharbat Ali (16°39'N, 53°3'30"E) to Ras Al Fasteh (25°04'N, 61°25'E) — a treaty boundary you can check a project location against. Use the term ‘ROPME Sea Area’: it was coined by the Plenipotentiaries to achieve unanimity, cooperating in spite of existing geopolitical boundaries, and it is the name all eight accepted. THE ORGAN MOST PEOPLE DO NOT KNOW EXISTS: alongside the Council and Secretariat, ROPME has a Judicial Commission, established March 1989, of 6 nationals of Member States highly qualified in international law. In a region with almost no environmental litigation route, a standing judicial commission under a ratified convention is the most significant legal fact available — though this entry does not assert that individuals may petition it; establish who may seise it first. AN EVIDENCE SOURCE THAT NEEDS NO SITE ACCESS: ROPME's scientific bodies include a Remote Sensing Unit, alongside RIIS and MEMAC. WHICH PROTOCOL FITS YOUR ISSUE: oil-spill emergency response; land-based sources of pollution — the limb for a coastal development, discharge or reclamation; and transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. Development is named as a stressor in ROPME's own statement of purpose. At stake: over 20 species of dolphin and whale, all five subtropical turtle species, and more than 1,000 fish species, most endemic.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a pan-African feminist rapid-response fund with reach across all 54 African countries — small grants released quickly for unanticipated, time-critical situations rather than planned programme work, covering safety and protection needs when defenders are threatened and short windows for advocacy after an unexpected event. WHO IT SUITS: women's rights organisations, feminist collectives and movements in which women or gender-diverse people are the primary decision-makers. It does NOT fund individuals, and the action must be strategic, genuinely unanticipated, and completable in under three months. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is emergency money for a moment, not a budget for a campaign — decisions are fast and grants are modest.

trackers.name: Commission d’Accès à l’Information (CAIDP)
trackers.desc: Côte d'Ivoire's CAIDP is the independent authority for access to public-interest information and public documents, enforcing the 2013 access-to-information law with powers of injunction and sanction. It handles complaints, monitors compliance and reports annually, and launched the ACCESS CAIDP portal in 2025 with full rollout targeted by December 2026. USE IT: injunction powers mean it can order release rather than only recommend it.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Côte d'Ivoire, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Côte d’Ivoire — CEPICI (Guichet Unique de l’Investissement)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Guichet Unique des Formalités d’Entreprise (GUFE) centralises company creation, modification & dissolution and RCCM registration, Côte d’Ivoire. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Marchés Publics
trackers.desc: National public-procurement portal. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Côte d’Ivoire, and for how much.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists. It found violations of articles 1 and 24 of the African Charter — article 24: ‘all peoples shall have the right to a general satisfactory environment favourable to their development’ — and of article 21, the right to natural wealth and resources. THE FAULT WAS AN OMISSION: the state ‘defaulted in its duties in terms of vigilance and diligence’, and ‘the omission to act and to prevent damage to the environment characterises the violation’. It ordered restoration within the shortest possible time and measures to prevent further damage, citing the ICJ that the environment ‘is not an abstraction but represents the living space, the quality of life and the very health of human beings, including generations unborn’. THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHO YOU SUE: the Court held it had no jurisdiction over the private oil corporations, which were struck from the suit. You sue the State for failing to regulate; you cannot sue the company here — naming one as respondent loses that part of the case. AND PLAN FOR ENFORCEMENT: commentary records the Court did not identify a means for Nigeria to implement the ruling, and the ICJ later wrote to the President pressing for enforcement — judgment is the start of an enforcement campaign, not a self-executing remedy. Proposals to require exhaustion of domestic remedies were rejected by ECOWAS experts and Heads of Government, so the direct-access rule has been tested and held.

trackers.name: ORFAO — comparative land-law tables, and a directive in draft
trackers.desc: COMPARATIVE LEGAL TABLES FOR YOUR COUNTRY AND ITS NEIGHBOURS, IN ONE DOCUMENT. The Observatoire Régional du Foncier Rural en Afrique de l'Ouest (ORFAO), hosted by UEMOA, publishes a regional study on rural land markets containing side-by-side ‘cadre légal comparé’ tables — one covering Bénin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire and Sénégal, another Guinée-Bissau, Mali, Niger and Togo — plus typologies of direct and indirect interventions in land markets and a table of regulatory issues and families of instruments. If you need to know what instrument exists in your country and whether a neighbour has a stronger one, that is the document — comparative tables let a campaign point to a neighbour's provision as an achievable ask rather than a novelty. A WINDOW IS OPENING: on 26 June 2026 in Ouagadougou the UEMOA ministers for urbanisme, habitat, domaines et cadastre approved a draft directive to harmonise rules on immatriculation foncière, accès au titre de propriété and a système d'information foncière, aiming at a common framework of land governance. BE PRECISE ABOUT STATUS: that was a DRAFT directive approved by ministers, not an adopted and transposed instrument — check adoption and transposition before relying on it. But transposition is the moment domestic land law is reopened in each state, and that is when community provisions can be argued for. FOR A GRAZING OR TRANSHUMANCE DISPUTE: a regional pastoral situation bulletin covers 11 West African countries with the support of decentralised technical services — an evidence source drawing on the same services you would otherwise approach one by one. RECORDED PLAINLY: cattle theft is documented as a driver of conflict and instability in the Sahel, so a land dispute here may sit inside a security context that changes what is safe to do. And confirm your state's current ECOWAS standing — several members are recorded as suspended.

trackers.name: SOS Forêts and the OI-REN platform — about forty Ivorian NGOs and community associations, and the ones who go to villages to explain the forest code
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: an Ivorian conservation NGO, led by the mangrove scientist Wadja Egnankou, which is also the way into the two networks that matter for a community facing eviction or a concession. It sits in the Observatoire Ivoirien pour la gestion durable des Ressources Naturelles (OI-REN), a platform of about forty NGOs and community-based associations, and in Alerte Foncier, which campaigns to consolidate the land rights of rural communities — two doors that are far harder to find directly than through a member. WHAT THE NETWORK ACTUALLY DOES ON THE GROUND: OI-REN has run information and awareness missions in village after village to explain the 2019 forest code, working with the ministry and funded by an environmental law organisation, on the stated basis that rural communities need the law made intelligible to deal both with logging operators and with the forest administration. It has also filed civil society commentary on national forest policy, and its analysis was cited alongside human rights organisations pressing for an independent observer and auditor of the classified forests written into the forest code. WHY THIS MATTERS HERE MORE THAN ELSEWHERE: Côte d'Ivoire has 231 classified forests, and residents of them have been forcibly evicted — people who had farmed there for years, moved out without adequate rehousing or replacement farmland, according to human rights investigations of the forest agency's operations. If you live in or beside a classified forest, the risk is eviction rather than purchase, and the network is what documents it. SOS Forêts itself works on mangroves and supports village women's associations in production activities such as solar salt. WHO IT SUITS: forest-edge and coastal communities in Côte d'Ivoire. CAVEATS: these are conservation and advocacy organisations, not lawyers — no litigation service, intake route or fee information was found; and OI-REN's own web presence is thin, so a member organisation such as this one is the practical point of entry.

trackers.name: AFOR — the Ivorian rural land agency that issues village land certificates, free under the World Bank-funded programme, and the certificate lets the village sue
trackers.desc: WHO TO APPROACH: the Agence Foncière Rurale, created because the 1998 rural land law had failed in practice — by the end of 2015 less than 1 per cent of the 23 million hectares of rural land had been certified — and given the autonomy and resources to run national certification. WHY THE CERTIFICATE IS WORTH THE TROUBLE: village communities holding collective rights over community land can obtain a Certificat foncier, and once it is published the certificate confers on the group the LEGAL CAPACITY TO GO TO COURT and to carry out acts of land management. That is the difference between a village that is talked about in a land dispute and one that can be a party to it. WHAT IT COSTS AND HOW LONG YOU HAVE: certificates issued under the donor-funded rural land policy programme have been delivered free of charge to beneficiaries — a pilot in one region produced 2,000 certificates, with an extension phase targeting 37,000 more across the country in sixteen months. Note the deadline that follows: the three-year period to convert a certificate into full registration was removed, and a 2023 decree set it at ten years — so check which rule applies to your certificate and diarise it, because an unconverted certificate can lapse. WHO IT SUITS: Ivorian village communities and rural landholders who want documented collective rights before a concession, plantation or classified-forest decision lands on them. CAVEATS: this is a state agency, so it is the counterparty as well as the service — certification has been controversial for over two decades and the process itself generates disputes between customary holders, migrants and long-term farmers; the roll-out depends on donor-funded programme phases reaching your area; and for support in dealing with logging operators or classified-forest eviction, the SOS Forêts / OI-REN entry is the civil society side.

trackers.name: AFJCI legal clinics — free legal advice with no bureaucracy, about ten clinics across Côte d'Ivoire plus a mobile one
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Association des Femmes Juristes de Côte d'Ivoire, which for nearly twenty years has run cliniques juridiques — listening, orientation and advice centres offering the most vulnerable and remote populations quality legal support, FREE OF CHARGE AND WITHOUT ADMINISTRATIVE FORMALITIES. The first fixed clinic opened at the Abidjan headquarters; six more followed in 2013 with European Union and UN backing, and reporting describes around ten clinics across Ivorian territory, with clinic locations including Abidjan and Bouaké and coverage extending to communes of Abidjan and departments of the Gbêké region. It also runs a MOBILE legal clinic that travels to rural localities — documented as far as Niandégué in the Bouna department — ending with free itinerant legal consultations giving advice, information and referral. WHAT IT ACTUALLY PROVIDES: legal consultations, judicial assistance, and SUPPORT WITH PROCEDURE COSTS — beneficiaries of assistance, including supplementary judgments and procedure fees, are identified during its listening sessions. It trains community relays and leaders, and broadcasts on radio. A clinic that pays some of your procedure costs is rarer in this file than one that gives advice; ask about that at the first meeting. WHO IT SUITS: Ivorians who cannot pay a lawyer and need advice, orientation or help with court costs — particularly women and rural households; useful alongside a land certificate application. CAVEATS: a women-jurists' association whose priorities are gender-based violence, civil status and family law rather than land or environmental litigation — approach it for access to justice, not as anti-development counsel. Clinic coverage depends on project funding cycles. For rural land certificates, Côte d'Ivoire's AFOR entry; for forests and logging, SOS Forêts.

trackers.name: Côte d'Ivoire's assistance judiciaire — decentralised to EVERY first-degree court since 2016, and here is the exact document list to bring
trackers.desc: WHAT IT IS: assistance judiciaire is a statutory mechanism letting people without sufficient resources assert their rights in court AS CLAIMANT OR DEFENDANT WITHOUT BEARING THE COSTS — it is effectively free, per the justice ministry, and it may be sought by any natural person OR by a private association whose object is a work of assistance. An association can apply on the strength of its purpose — which matters for a village committee or a landowners association rather than an individual. WHERE TO FILE: décret n°2016-781 of 12 October 2016 DECENTRALISED the service, creating a BUREAU LOCAL at each first-degree jurisdiction to hear applications at first instance instead of a single national bureau, expressly so people in remote areas can reach justice without financial obstacle. You may therefore address the request either to the president of the bureau central at the justice ministry's civil and criminal affairs directorate, or to the president of the bureau local at the seat of each Section de tribunal or Tribunal de première instance across the territory. THE DOCUMENT LIST, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT DECIDES WHETHER YOUR FILE IS ACCEPTED: attach (1) a certificate of taxation or NON-taxation issued by the tax collector for your domicile; (2) a copy of the decision you intend to appeal, or of the title you want enforced; and (3) any document proving insolvency — for example a CERTIFICAT D'INDIGENCE issued by the police commissioner or the head of the administrative district. The certificat d'indigence is the pivot: obtain it first, from the police commissioner or the district head, because nothing else in the file substitutes for it. Note that a title you want ENFORCED is listed — like Burkina, this covers execution, not only trial. WHO IT SUITS: Ivorian households and associations that cannot pay court and advocate costs in a land, certificate or expropriation dispute. CAVEATS: A STATE SCHEME, and reporting notes assistance judiciaire remains poorly known, particularly among women; the indigence certificate depends on an official's signature. For free advice clinics including a mobile one, Côte d'Ivoire's AFJCI entry; for rural land certificates, AFOR; for forests and logging, SOS Forêts.

trackers.name: Centre pour l'Environnement et le Développement (CED)
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: founded in 1994 in response to Cameroon's forest-management crisis and now working across land tenure, forests and the extractive industries — oil, gold and other mining — from Yaoundé. It supports communities and local associations in their dealings with the administration, forestry and extractive companies, conservation projects and industrial plantations, and campaigns for recognition of customary and Indigenous forest land rights in Cameroon's land reform. USE IT: the site carries a legal library covering national legislation, international texts, natural-resource contracts and court decisions; a map library including forest-cover and land-allocation mapping by department; and policy briefs on customary tenure, women's land rights and illegal gold mining. It also runs the Coalition Foncière Nationale and the LandCam platform. Its stated support extends to local NGOs elsewhere in the Congo Basin, but this entry is placed for Cameroon only, which is what its own site evidences.

trackers.name: Chambre des comptes de la Cour suprême du Cameroun
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Cameroon — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: Commission Nationale Anti-Corruption (CONAC)
trackers.desc: National anti-corruption body of Cameroon — investigates graft, financial crime and abuse of public office.

trackers.name: Cameroon — Ministry of Finance (MINFI)
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the General Budget Directorate prepares the State budget and MINFI publishes budget-execution & public-finance reports, Cameroon. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Cameroon.

trackers.name: Cameroon — Business Creation e-Portal (CFCE / mybusiness.cm)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the official electronic one-stop window (Centres de Formalités de Création d’Entreprises) for online company creation & registration, Cameroon. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: MUSEBA Journalism Project
trackers.desc: Cameroonian watchdog newsroom covering large-scale corruption and illicit financial flows in Central Africa.

trackers.name: COMIFAC Treaty and Plan de Convergence — and its community protocol
trackers.desc: A TREATY BODY WITH A TEMPLATE YOU CAN COPY. The Traité relatif à la conservation et à la gestion durable des écosystèmes forestiers d'Afrique Centrale, signed by heads of state at their second summit on 5 February 2005 in Brazzaville, instituted the Commission des Forêts d'Afrique Centrale — described as the unique instance d'orientation, de décision et de coordination for subregional forest action, and the cadre politique et juridique global for cooperation in the field. A transboundary forest question belongs in that forum. The Plan de Convergence is the reference framework for all such interventions — first edition 2005–2014, revised in 2014 for 2015–2025 and restructured into 10 strategic axes, executed by a Secrétariat exécutif. CIVIL SOCIETY IS A NAMED STAKEHOLDER in implementing it, alongside state administrations, CEEAC and the private sector — so participation is built into the framework, not conceded case by case. Axis 7 covers capacity and participation des acteurs, expressly contemplating micro-projets générateurs de revenus pour les populations locales; axis 9 covers innovative financing mechanisms. THE DOCUMENT LIBRARY IS THE MOST USEFUL PART: COMIFAC publishes a worked Protocole Bioculturel Communautaire for a named village, a guide to inventorying genetic resources and traditional knowledge, a paper on les droits d'usage des peuples autochtones et communautés locales et les obligations qui en découlent, a subregional APA (access and benefit-sharing) strategy, and directives on forests and the SDGs built with FAO as 5 principles and 12 directives across 31 prioritised targets. A community biocultural protocol published by a treaty body is a template, not a theory. AND ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS IS QUOTABLE: the Plan records that participatory natural resource management and mediation of use conflicts, though already mapped out, are insufficiently developed.

trackers.name: FODER and the SNOIE system — a villager's alert can become a ministry control mission, a suspension and a fine, through a certified procedure
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Forêts et Développement Rural, the Cameroonian association that developed the Système Normalisé d'Observation Indépendante Externe (SNOIE) — a standardised, ISO 9001:2015 certified set of procedures for documenting illegal exploitation of natural resources and directing the resulting complaint to the right authority. The certification is the trick: it makes a civil society report hard to dismiss as hearsay. HOW A COMMUNITY ENTERS IT: SNOIE missions are triggered by complaints from individuals or by community alerts — in one documented case a FODER field mission was launched after 38 alerts collected and sent by a single community member through a real-time forest monitoring platform. Communities are the sensor; the certified procedure is what converts what they see into something the state must answer. WHAT IT HAS PRODUCED, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: denunciation reports submitted to the forests ministry led to two logging companies being suspended with legal proceedings opened against them — the suspension explicitly lasting until the case is resolved; more than half of SNOIE reports in its first three years drew a response from the ministry; and between 2016 and 2019 the reports contributed 72.5 million FCFA in forest revenue to the state through fines and public auction of illegally cut timber seized after the resulting control missions. An enforcement route that makes money for the ministry is one the ministry keeps using. Infractions documented include unauthorised logging in the national forest estate, logging outside title boundaries, breach of forest operating standards, and logging in community forests without the annual exploitation certificate — so it works against abuses of community forests too. It runs with other Cameroonian organisations including CeDLA, ECODEV and PAPEL, and the system has been extended to the Republic of the Congo. WHO IT SUITS: forest communities in Cameroon that can see illegal cutting and need it acted on. CAVEATS: this is documentation and denunciation, not litigation or land tenure — it addresses ILLEGAL activity, and a lawfully permitted project is outside its reach; the outcome depends on the ministry acting; and for community land rights and mapping Cameroon's CED entry is the other half.

trackers.name: RELUFA, Yaoundé — works the gold-mining east where farmland is being taken, and names the reason companies never talk to you
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: RELUFA, a Cameroonian civil society organisation based in Yaoundé working on land grabbing, mining and food justice, and one of the two organisations academic research identifies as carrying the socio-environmental justice demands of communities in Bétaré-Oya in the East region, where semi-mechanised gold mining has taken agricultural land, destroyed harvests and degraded watercourses in a rural commune whose people depend on forest ecosystems for food. THE SENTENCE THAT EXPLAINS A DECADE OF FRUSTRATION, from RELUFA's president: the companies “do not communicate, they do not want to get involved… they know only one local shareholder: the GOVERNMENT. They do not deal with civil society or with local communities. That is why you see these conflicts.” If a company will not meet you, that is not an oversight — it is because its only recognised counterparty is the state that licensed it, which tells you where to aim. WHAT THE DEMANDS LOOK LIKE WHEN COMMUNITIES SET THEM: the East-region work insists that beyond material and financial compensation, what must be recognised is the collective identity of impacted communities, their attachment to the territory, their culture and their territorial rights — the same argument this file records from Lesotho and Ghana, that compensation methodology is the fight. Cameroonian community testimony gathered nationally describes the recurring pattern precisely: land dispossession, customary rights ignored, and abusive land registrations facilitated by corruption — which is why demands centre on recognition of customary rights, a single land registry, limits and surtax on unexploited concessions, and free, prior and informed consent written into Cameroonian law. WHO IT SUITS: Cameroonian communities losing farmland to mining or agro-industry, particularly in the East. CAVEATS: an advocacy, research and coalition organisation, not a law firm or a fund. For participatory mapping that has stopped a plantation, Cameroon's CED entry; for certified illegality alerts that trigger company suspensions, FODER's.

trackers.name: Cameroon's community forests — up to 5,000 ha per village under a management agreement, about 300 already granted and 200 applications waiting
trackers.desc: WHAT TO APPLY FOR: the forêt communautaire (FC), created by Cameroon's 1994 forest law and its 1995 implementing decree to let local communities participate in managing forest resources and share the benefits. THE DEFINITION SETS THE LIMITS, so read it before hoping: an FC is an area of the NON-PERMANENT forest domain — forest land that could otherwise be converted to non-forest uses — of UP TO 5,000 HECTARES, held under a MANAGEMENT AGREEMENT (convention de gestion) between a village community and the forest administration. It is the non-permanent domain that matters: this is precisely the land most exposed to being reallocated to somebody else, which is why getting an agreement over it is a defence rather than a formality. THE STATE OF PLAY IN NUMBERS: roughly 300 community forests have been attributed to communities, with more than 200 further applications pending covering around 600,000 hectares — so the queue is real and long, and an application filed now joins hundreds. An international conservation organisation reports having supported the creation and management of more than 60 community forests since 2003, mostly on the periphery of protected areas, and supports local civil society to take part in the Local Consultation Frameworks around certification. THE LIMIT TO PLAN AROUND, DOCUMENTED ACROSS THE REGION: customary territories are usually far larger than 5,000 ha — people hunt and gather well beyond it — so subdividing them arbitrarily to fit the ceiling generates conflict between neighbouring villages. Agree the boundary with your neighbours before you file. WHO IT SUITS: Cameroonian village communities in the forest zone wanting a legally recognised area they manage and benefit from, especially beside a protected area or a concession. CAVEATS: a management agreement with the administration, NOT a land title, and it applies only to the non-permanent domain — land already inside a permanent forest reserve or an allocated concession is outside it; the attribution process is slow and document-heavy. For participatory mapping that has stopped a plantation, Cameroon's CED entry; for certified illegality alerts, FODER; for mining in the East, RELUFA. WHAT YOU ACTUALLY HOLD, IN THE PLAINEST TERMS PUBLISHED: a Cameroonian farmers' paper puts it as the state GIVING RIGHTS OF USE to a village community that asks for them — it is a little as if THE STATE RENTED THE FOREST TO THE COMMUNITY: THE STATE REMAINS OWNER, the community as tenant may use the forest WITHOUT PAYING, under the administration's control. Tenant, not owner — plan on that footing, and keep the convention and your management plan where you can produce them. Under article 37 of the 1994 forest law and its 1995 implementing decree, a community forest is an area of the NON-PERMANENT forest domain, up to 5,000 ha, under a CONVENTION DE GESTION between a village community and the forest administration, generally for 25 YEARS — and for that duration ALL RESOURCES DRAWN FROM THE FOREST BELONG TO THE COMMUNITY, with use, long-term management and the use of the benefits belonging wholly to it. THE DISQUALIFYING CONDITION, CHECK IT FIRST: the area requested MUST NOT ALREADY HAVE BEEN ALLOCATED TO A FORESTRY COMPANY — which is why applying BEFORE a concession is granted is decisive. HOW IT IS WORKED IN PRACTICE: at one community forest the 5,000 ha is subdivided into ANNUAL CUTTING BLOCKS OF 200 HA on a 25-YEAR ROTATION, with NGO training for members in silviculture, directional felling, sawing and measurement. Scale: by December 2002 194 applications covering nearly 700,000 ha had been made; more than 330 community forests are validated or in progress. AND THE FAILURE MODE TO GUARD AGAINST, REPORTED BY A COMMUNITY GROUP ITSELF: individual villagers SELLING PRIVATE PARCELS OF LAND inside the community forest area. The threat to a community forest is as often internal sale as external concession — write the rule against individual alienation into your constitution before you get the convention, not after.

trackers.name: Cameroon's assistance judiciaire (loi 2009/004) — it reaches the ADMINISTRATIVE courts, covers ENFORCEMENT, and some disputes qualify automatically
trackers.desc: WHAT THE LAW COVERS: loi n°2009/004 of 14 April 2009 organising assistance judiciaire, which lets a person without sufficient resources be dispensed from paying the fees of the auxiliaries of justice whose assistance is needed to plead. THE THREE PROVISIONS THAT MATTER MOST, and the first is the most valuable sentence in this whole francophone sweep: (1) it may be granted before ALL JURISDICTIONS OF THE JUDICIAL ORDER AND EVEN THE ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER — the administrative courts are where you challenge a permit, a concession or an expropriation decision, so a state scheme that funds administrative litigation is a scheme that can be pointed at the state itself. (2) It applies WHATEVER the nature of the procedure — contentious or gracieuse — and expressly to PROCEEDINGS FOR THE EXECUTION OF JUDGMENTS OR ANY OTHER ENFORCEABLE TITLE, so a judgment you cannot afford to enforce is covered, as in Burkina and Côte d'Ivoire. (3) Article 2: assistance judiciaire is EITHER provided AS OF RIGHT by special legal provisions BECAUSE OF THE NATURE OF THE DISPUTE, or granted on application — so before assembling a means file, ask whether your category of dispute already qualifies automatically. Article 3 states the effect precisely: the beneficiary obtains either a judgment or its execution, with dispensation from advancing all or part of the costs they would normally bear. Whether you are claimant or defendant is irrelevant, and the law also fixes how applications are introduced and investigated, and the conditions under which assistance can be WITHDRAWN. WHO IT SUITS: Cameroonians without means in a land, plantation, mining or expropriation dispute — particularly anyone contesting an administrative decision. CAVEATS: A STATE SCHEME with an indigence assessment and a withdrawal power; the text dates from 2009, so confirm the current bureau and procedure locally. For participatory mapping that stopped a plantation, Cameroon's CED entry; for certified illegality alerts, FODER; for the mining east, RELUFA; for community forests, the FC entry.

trackers.name: Cour des comptes du Bénin
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Benin — audits government accounts and the use of public money.

trackers.name: Benin — Ministère de l’Économie et des Finances
trackers.desc: National budget authority; governs & manages the economy and public finances and publishes the State budget, Benin. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Benin.

trackers.name: Benin — MonEntreprise.bj (APIEx)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the APIEx electronic one-stop window for company creation, registration & management, Benin. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists. It found violations of articles 1 and 24 of the African Charter — article 24: ‘all peoples shall have the right to a general satisfactory environment favourable to their development’ — and of article 21, the right to natural wealth and resources. THE FAULT WAS AN OMISSION: the state ‘defaulted in its duties in terms of vigilance and diligence’, and ‘the omission to act and to prevent damage to the environment characterises the violation’. It ordered restoration within the shortest possible time and measures to prevent further damage, citing the ICJ that the environment ‘is not an abstraction but represents the living space, the quality of life and the very health of human beings, including generations unborn’. THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHO YOU SUE: the Court held it had no jurisdiction over the private oil corporations, which were struck from the suit. You sue the State for failing to regulate; you cannot sue the company here — naming one as respondent loses that part of the case. AND PLAN FOR ENFORCEMENT: commentary records the Court did not identify a means for Nigeria to implement the ruling, and the ICJ later wrote to the President pressing for enforcement — judgment is the start of an enforcement campaign, not a self-executing remedy. Proposals to require exhaustion of domestic remedies were rejected by ECOWAS experts and Heads of Government, so the direct-access rule has been tested and held.

trackers.name: ORFAO — comparative land-law tables, and a directive in draft
trackers.desc: COMPARATIVE LEGAL TABLES FOR YOUR COUNTRY AND ITS NEIGHBOURS, IN ONE DOCUMENT. The Observatoire Régional du Foncier Rural en Afrique de l'Ouest (ORFAO), hosted by UEMOA, publishes a regional study on rural land markets containing side-by-side ‘cadre légal comparé’ tables — one covering Bénin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire and Sénégal, another Guinée-Bissau, Mali, Niger and Togo — plus typologies of direct and indirect interventions in land markets and a table of regulatory issues and families of instruments. If you need to know what instrument exists in your country and whether a neighbour has a stronger one, that is the document — comparative tables let a campaign point to a neighbour's provision as an achievable ask rather than a novelty. A WINDOW IS OPENING: on 26 June 2026 in Ouagadougou the UEMOA ministers for urbanisme, habitat, domaines et cadastre approved a draft directive to harmonise rules on immatriculation foncière, accès au titre de propriété and a système d'information foncière, aiming at a common framework of land governance. BE PRECISE ABOUT STATUS: that was a DRAFT directive approved by ministers, not an adopted and transposed instrument — check adoption and transposition before relying on it. But transposition is the moment domestic land law is reopened in each state, and that is when community provisions can be argued for. FOR A GRAZING OR TRANSHUMANCE DISPUTE: a regional pastoral situation bulletin covers 11 West African countries with the support of decentralised technical services — an evidence source drawing on the same services you would otherwise approach one by one. RECORDED PLAINLY: cattle theft is documented as a driver of conflict and instability in the Sahel, so a land dispute here may sit inside a security context that changes what is safe to do. And confirm your state's current ECOWAS standing — several members are recorded as suspended.

trackers.name: Eco-Bénin — it sets up community conservation areas that the villages themselves manage, and it sacralised 500 hectares of mangrove
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Beninese NGO founded in 1999 that helps communities create Aires Communautaires de Conservation de la Biodiversité (ACCB) — community conservation areas — and then leaves the villages managing them. Its established areas include the Bouche du Roy and Lac Ahémé in the Mono transboundary biosphere reserve. THE PROTECTION IT USES THAT NO LAW PROVIDES, AND WHICH IS WORTH THINKING ABOUT ANYWHERE CUSTOM STILL BINDS: alongside ecological restoration, Eco-Bénin has placed 500 hectares of mangrove under the protection of the Zangbéto divinity — the “night watchman” — sacralising the forest so that local custom, not only the state, forbids cutting it. Around 500 hectares of degraded mangrove have been restored across the two community areas, 475,000 mangrove seedlings produced in a single year, and more than 1,500 community members trained in mangrove management. WHY THE MONEY SIDE IS THE POINT: the organisation runs community ecotourism as the economic pillar, projects are managed by the host communities themselves with the stated aim that they become autonomous, and between 10 and 25 per cent of takings goes to community projects — a school repair, latrines — or to the poorest households. Conservation that pays is conservation that survives a bad harvest. It also distributes improved cookstoves to cut pressure on forest, and works with allies including a dam-affected persons' committee at Adjarala and the Lac Ahémé fishers' association. WHO IT SUITS: coastal, wetland and forest-edge communities in southern and northern Benin that want an area recognised and managed locally rather than allocated away. Zogbadjè, Calavi; +229 95 28 52 20; contact@ecobenin.org. CAVEATS: this is conservation and ecotourism development, not legal defence — there is no litigation capacity here, and no purchase of land; a successor entity, ECOBENIN INTERNATIONAL, now also uses the name, so confirm which body you are dealing with.

trackers.name: Synergie Paysanne — Benin's peasant union, which funded legal support for 200 farmers dispossessed by a member of parliament
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Synergie Paysanne (Synpa), founded in 2002 by young farmers and Benin's first peasant union, with around 2,000 members, campaigning on family farming, against GMOs and agrofuels, and squarely on land grabbing. WHAT IT HAS ACTUALLY DONE FOR DISPOSSESSED FARMERS: in 2008 it funded legal support for an association of 200 farmers dispossessed of their land by a member of parliament, in a village in the Plateau department in the south-east. It also promoted a practical tool most smallholders never hear about — the formalisation of oral customary contracts for the loan, gift and leasing of farmland, which it pushed with landowners and mayors to open up land that urban elites were hoarding, and which was written into the 2007 rural land law on its proposals. If you farm land you do not own under an oral arrangement, getting that arrangement written down is the cheapest protection available to you. THE DEFEAT IT IS HONEST TO RECORD: between 2010 and 2013 the union mobilised hard against the draft land code, which it regarded as an instrument for agribusiness and land grabbing. Researchers who studied that campaign concluded it was a political failure — technical advocacy plus media denunciation won the union institutional recognition and a seat in the drafting arenas, but not the changes it sought, and the technical investment weakened its collective dynamic. Advocacy alone did not stop the code. WHO IT SUITS: Beninese smallholders and farming associations facing dispossession, large-scale land acquisitions, or insecure customary access. CAVEATS: NO CURRENT CANONICAL WEBSITE WAS VERIFIED — this entry points at the union's own blog, which is dated; approach through Beninese farmer networks. It is a union, not a law firm: it has financed legal support rather than provided it, and Benin's Eco-Bénin entry covers community conservation areas.

trackers.name: Benin's aide juridique decree of October 2024 — and the three French words that decide which help you are actually asking for
trackers.desc: WHAT THE NEW LAW GIVES YOU: Benin adopted in Council of Ministers the Décret N°2024-1275 of 23 OCTOBER 2024 regulating AIDE JURIDIQUE in the Republic of Benin — the newest legal-aid instrument recorded in this file. Its stated purpose is to secure equal access to law and justice and to prevent discrimination in access to justice whose origin might be ILLITERACY, IGNORANCE OF ONE’S RIGHTS, ethnicity, gender, religion, social or economic status, disability or any other cause. Illiteracy and not knowing your rights are named in the decree itself as forms of discrimination to be remedied — that is unusually direct, and it is worth quoting when someone tells you the problem is that you do not understand the procedure. THE VOCABULARY THAT DECIDES YOUR REQUEST, and it applies across every francophone country in this file: AIDE JURIDIQUE is the whole set of free assistance mechanisms — awareness-raising, advice, analysis AND representation before a court or any conciliation or arbitration body; AIDE JUDICIAIRE is assistance to a litigant before the court itself; AIDE JURIDICTIONNELLE is the FINANCIAL aid the state grants to litigants whose income is insufficient. Ask for the wrong one and you will be sent away: if you need money for costs say aide juridictionnelle, if you need someone beside you in court say aide judiciaire, if you do not yet know what you need say aide juridique. A published national brochure explains the Benin scheme in question-and-answer form. WHO IT SUITS: Beninese households — including farmers facing dispossession — who cannot pay for legal help, and anyone in francophone Africa who needs to name the right service. CAVEATS: A DECREE ADOPTED IN OCTOBER 2024 IS A NEW MACHINE — confirm locally which office receives applications and whether it is operating in your commune before relying on it; seven countries in this file have statutes whose implementing machinery never arrived. For the peasant union that funded legal support for 200 dispossessed farmers, Benin's Synergie Paysanne entry; for community conservation areas, Eco-Bénin.

trackers.name: Benin's sacred forests and arrêté 021/MEHU — a national framework for COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT of sacred forests, with recognition through the mairie and the forest inspectorate
trackers.desc: THE FOREST NOBODY DARED CUT: Benin lost roughly 44,000 HECTARES of forest between 2001 and 2022 — 26% of its cover — yet certain spaces resisted, NOT through a law or a public policy but through CENTURIES OF COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT AND CULTURAL PROTECTION. THE INSTRUMENT THAT PUT LAW BEHIND THAT: the INTERMINISTERIAL ARRÊTÉ N°021/MEHU/MDGLAT/DC/SGM/DGFRN/SA OF 16 NOVEMBER 2012, ESTABLISHING A FRAMEWORK FOR THE COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT OF SACRED FORESTS IN BENIN, which ALLOWS LOCAL FOREST MANAGEMENT BY THE LOCAL POPULATIONS THEMSELVES and confers RECOGNITION THROUGH STRUCTURES INCLUDING THE MAIRIE AND THE FOREST INSPECTORATE, WHICH THEN ACCOMPANY the enrichment and conservation actions undertaken. Your commune hall and the forest inspectorate become partners rather than obstacles — that is the whole point of the 2012 arrêté, and it is the cheapest recognition route recorded in West Africa. HOW IT REACHED THE VILLAGES: the PROJET D'INTÉGRATION DES FORÊTS SACRÉES DANS LE SYSTÈME D'AIRES PROTÉGÉES (PIFSAP) integrated sacred forests into the formal protected-area system, strengthened the legal and institutional framework and promoted COMMUNITY CO-MANAGEMENT; named forests recognised through it include WIANSO, SINATABÉ and WÊWÊRÉ at Bembèrèkè (Borgou), each managed by a named community — Gandé and Sinadouwirou among them — and each proposed as a protected area before 2000 but only made effective locally by the 2012 arrêté. If your forest was proposed for protection decades ago and nothing happened, the 2012 framework is the instrument that finished the job for three named forests. Cite them. WHAT COUNTS AS ONE: Beninese sacred forests fall in four categories — fetish forests (nearly 60%), secret-society forests (21%), COMMUNITY FORESTS PROTECTED COLLECTIVELY BY VILLAGERS (10%), and CEMETERY FORESTS where graves are integrated into the woodland (8%) — supplying medicinal plants, fruits and animal products, and protecting soils against erosion. A burial ground is a recognised category here, which matters everywhere in this file where a community's strongest claim is its ancestors rather than a title. A forestry engineer's stated priority is equipping these forests with FUNCTIONING MANAGEMENT ORGANS AND TOOLS, arguing communes can mobilise resources through them; a Beninese NGO won a UNESCO-Japan prize in 2025 for restoring the OOKPO sacred forest at Pobè, in existence since the 17th century. WHO IT SUITS: Beninese villages holding a sacred grove, burial forest or collectively protected woodland. CAVEATS: RECOGNITION UNDER AN ARRÊTÉ, NOT TITLE — the registry records continuing pressure for a full legal declaration. For Benin's three-word aide juridique vocabulary and the 2024 décret, the legal aid entry.

trackers.desc: Official Supreme People's Court portal publishing effective court judgments and decisions, mandated since 2017. · Find here: Vietnam's official portal for the publication of court judgments (Supreme People's Court).

trackers.desc: Vietnam's national enterprise registration portal. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: National Business Registration Portal (Vietnam)
trackers.desc: Vietnam's official national business registration portal. Here you can trace companies, their directors and filings registered in Vietnam.

trackers.name: National e-GP (muasamcong)
trackers.desc: Vietnam's national e-procurement system. Here you can trace which firms win government contracts and tenders in Vietnam, and for how much.

trackers.name: General Statistics Office
trackers.desc: Vietnam's national statistical office, publishing official national accounts and government-finance statistics — government revenue, expenditure, deficit and public debt. HOW THIS DIFFERS: this gives AGGREGATE national totals, not project-level detail — use it for the big picture, not to see who won a specific contract (use the procurement portal) or what one project cost. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Vietnam.

trackers.name: Cộng đồng dân cư is a forest owner — and the district decides
trackers.desc: A COMMUNITY IS A FOREST OWNER IN ITS OWN RIGHT. Under the Forestry Law 16/2017/QH14, chủ rừng means an organisation, household, individual or cộng đồng dân cư to whom the State allocates or leases forest, or who receives it by transfer, gift or inheritance — so a community sits in the same category as an organisation, and forest can be inherited and gifted, which most community-forest regimes in this map leave unaddressed. THE DEFINITION IS BROAD AND NAMES THE WORDS DIFFERENT PEOPLES USE: Vietnamese people living in the same thôn, làng, ấp, bản, buôn, bon, phum, sóc or similar residential point and having the same customs and practices — shared customs are part of the test, so document them. GO TO THE DISTRICT, NOT THE PROVINCE: under article 23 the district People's Committee allocates, converts and revokes forest for residential communities, while the province handles organisations and leases to foreign-invested enterprises. Note the asymmetry — for communities the district may allocate, convert and revoke, but the leasing power listed for households is not listed for communities. Where a revocation area contains both organisations and communities, the province decides or delegates down.

trackers.name: The state pays for your forest inventory — use it
trackers.desc: AN OBLIGATION THAT IS ALSO FUNDING. Forest owners must carry out kiểm kê rừng (forest inventory) and submit to inspection — by the district forestry agency for households, individuals and communities — declaring data on prescribed forms. BUT THE SPECIALIST FORESTRY AGENCY MUST GUIDE AND SUPPORT TECHNICALLY AND MUST PROVIDE FUNDING FOR THE INVENTORY to owners who are households, individuals or communities. The state pays to document what you hold — elsewhere in this map communities must fund that themselves, and it is usually the step that stops them. WHAT OWNERSHIP GIVES YOU: quyền sử dụng rừng, the right to exploit the forest's uses and enjoy its fruits and income; and for planted production forest, possession, use and disposal of trees, livestock and other assets you invested — planted assets are owned outright even where the land is not. Note also giá trị rừng, defined as the total value of the ecosystem's components and its forest environmental values — a statutory basis for valuing environmental services, not just timber. TWO POLICY COMMITMENTS TO QUOTE BACK (article 4): the State ensures resources for special-use and protection forest, and protects the lawful rights and interests of communities engaged in forestry. And where an international treaty Vietnam has joined differs from this Law, or Vietnamese law is silent, the treaty applies.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: Royal Audit Authority
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Bhutan, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Bhutan — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; prepares & publishes the national budget and budget reports, Royal Government of Bhutan. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Bhutan.

trackers.name: Anti-Corruption Commission of Bhutan (ACC)
trackers.desc: Bhutan’s lead anti-corruption body — investigates and prosecutes graft, runs asset declaration and corruption prevention.

trackers.name: Bhutan — Corporate Regulatory Authority (CRA)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the CRA (formerly Office of the Registrar of Companies, upgraded 2024) incorporates companies and runs the online single-window company registry & compliance system, Bhutan. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Every Bhutanese is a trustee — the clause an individual can cite
trackers.desc: THE STRONGEST CONSTITUTIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL PROVISION IN THIS MAP. Article 5 of the 2008 Constitution requires that a minimum of 60 percent of Bhutan's total land be maintained under forest cover for all time — a permanent safeguard, not a policy target. AND IT VESTS A DUTY PERSONALLY: Article 5 states that every Bhutanese is a trustee of the Kingdom's natural resources and environment. That trusteeship clause is what an individual cites — stronger than the diffuse-interest provisions this map records for Paraguay and the Dominican Republic, because it is framed as a duty held personally rather than an interest shared collectively. HEADROOM: actual forest cover is around 71–72 percent and more than 51 percent of the country is protected across 10 national parks and sanctuaries — the largest protected share of any Asian country — so the 60 percent floor is not currently the binding constraint. BUT DO NOT MISUSE THE MANDATE: the World Bank's Bhutan Forest Note records that public debate is ‘prone to the misconception that sustainably managed forests do not count toward forest cover’. Arguing that management per se breaches the 60 percent mandate will fail — argue degradation, conversion or biodiversity impact instead. Only about 3.5 percent of land is managed for commercial production.

trackers.name: Community forests run on a certificate — and rule 63 can cancel it
trackers.desc: TWO THINGS TO READ BEFORE YOU NEED THEM. The Forest and Nature Conservation Rules and Regulations 2017 govern Community Forests with named provisions on sale of surplus forest produce (r.61), royalty (r.62), cancellation of the Community Forest Certificate (r.63), formation of CF network and association (r.64) and monitoring and evaluation (r.65). Your community forest exists by certificate, and rule 63 provides for cancelling it — read the grounds now, not later. And rule 64 gives community forest groups a statutory basis for forming a network and association, so groups can organise together rather than each negotiating alone. The 2017 Rules supersede all earlier government notifications, circulars, orders and rules. THE TENURE RULE: under rule 12, private registered land acquired by the Government for national interest becomes State Reserved Forest Land from the date of acquisition — conversion is automatic on that date. CHECK WHICH ACT YOU ARE READING: the Forest and Nature Conservation Act 2023 replaces the 1995 Act and both circulate; its 11 chapters cover State Reserved Forest Land, nature conservation, soil, water and waste, forest-based industry and offence and penalty, with powers in the Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources and the Department of Forests and Park Services. Your local contact is the Divisional Forest Office in the dzongkhag.

trackers.name: Bhutan Trust Fund — individuals and unregistered groups can apply
trackers.desc: NO LEGAL PERSONALITY REQUIRED — which removes the commonest barrier in this map. The Bhutan Trust Fund for Environmental Conservation, established 1991 as the world's first environmental trust fund by the Royal Government with UNDP and WWF and a US$20 million endowment, incorporated under Royal Charter in 1996 and renewed in 2021, is autonomous of government, with a Management Board fully Bhutanised in May 2001. ANY AGENCY, INSTITUTION, COMMUNITY OR INDIVIDUAL THAT IS BHUTANESE IS ELIGIBLE — recorded applicant types include communities and non-registered citizen groups, individuals, NGOs, subnational government and towns and municipalities. THE PAPERWORK IS WHERE GOOD PROPOSALS FAIL: small grant proposals may be submitted at any time of year in the prescribed template (with a separate annual call for larger grants); proposals from an agency must be approved by their head and carry an official forwarding letter; and an individual working in any agency, public or private, needs a No Objection Letter from it. Get the forwarding letter or NOL before drafting, not after. Fundable sectors include land management, sustainable rural livelihoods, community development and eco-tourism; thematic windows have included managing development impacts — expressly reducing environmental harm caused by development activities. It is also accredited to the Adaptation Fund (since 2018, valid to 6 February 2029) and the Green Climate Fund (2020), so it is a route to international climate finance too. Contact: Post Box 520, Genyen Lam, Thimphu; 975-2-33981.
