trackers.name: Associação Projecto Vitó
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Cape Verdean environmental association that began on Fogo as a volunteer effort after a sea-turtle rescue and now works on Fogo, Brava, Santo Antão, São Nicolau and Santiago, and in the Reserva Natural Integral dos Ilhéus do Rombo. It supports management of the Parque Natural do Fogo and the operationalisation of the Fogo Biosphere Reserve, working through citizen science and transferring technical knowledge to civil society. The first environmental NGO awarded Cape Verde's Medal of Merit, First Class. USE IT: as the organisation with standing and field presence inside Cape Verde's protected-area network — the route to getting a site monitored, documented and argued for. It is a conservation and education body, not a campaigning or legal one.

trackers.name: Biosfera
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: a Cape Verdean NGO working on coastal and marine species and their habitats from São Vicente, with long-running field operations on the uninhabited island of Santa Luzia. It states a dual mission — conservation, and mobilising Cape Verdean civil society for the protection of the environment — and its strategic objectives include protecting coastal and marine habitats, promoting responsible artisanal fishing and reducing pollution that disturbs species and habitats. USE IT: as the coastal counterpart to the protected-area bodies. It is the organisation to approach about a shoreline, a fishery or a marine habitat under pressure, and the one in Cape Verde that most explicitly treats mobilising the public as part of its job.

trackers.name: Cabo Verde. Supremo Tribunal de Justiça
trackers.desc: Cabo Verde. Supremo Tribunal de Justiça — supreme court (Cabo Verde).

trackers.name: Tribunal de Contas
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Cabo Verde, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Cabo Verde — Ministério das Finanças
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the DGPOG prepares & publishes the State Budget (Orçamento do Estado) and provisional accounts, Cabo Verde. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Cabo Verde.

trackers.name: Cabo Verde — Casa do Cidadão (Porton di nos Ilha / Empresa no Dia)
trackers.desc: National company registry; the Casa do Cidadão portal handles company name reservation (Certificado de Admissibilidade de Firma) & the “Empresa no Dia” incorporation regime (IRN), with beneficial-ownership disclosure via CENTIF, Cabo Verde. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Urgent Action Fund–Africa (rapid response grants)
trackers.desc: RAPID MONEY WHEN SOMETHING SUDDEN HAPPENS — and it is open all year. UAF-Africa is a pan-African feminist rapid response fund, founded 2001 in Nairobi, with geographical presence in Africa's 54 countries and over 6,000 grants resourced. BE CLEAR ON SCOPE: it supports women, girls and gender-diverse people and women's rights organisations — it is not a general environmental fund. It belongs in this map because it fits a specific and recurring situation: women land and environmental defenders facing threats, harassment or security risks. NO FUNDING CYCLE — apply as soon as an urgent situation requires it, to proposals@uaf-africa.org. THREE GRANT TYPES: rapid response, protection grants up to USD 15,000, and advocacy and alliance building up to USD 30,000. FOUR CRITERIA, ALL REQUIRED: strategic (tied to a plan for structural change), unanticipated (could not have been foreseen), time urgent (must happen within 3 months or the opportunity is lost), and sustainable. The ‘unanticipated’ test is what disqualifies most applications — planned programme work does not qualify, by design. Applications may be written in French, English, Swahili or Arabic. Both registered and informal groups may apply; individuals are not funded.

trackers.name: Conselho Assessor — a statutory council per island, or per protected area
trackers.desc: A NAMED BODY WHOSE STATED PURPOSE IS POPULATION PARTICIPATION. Article 22(1) of Decreto-Lei n.º 3/2003 of 24 February provides that the government department responsible for the environment may create a Conselho Assessor for each island or, exceptionally, for a single protected area, with the object of facilitating management through the participation of the population and cooperation. TWO QUESTIONS FOLLOW: does a Conselho Assessor exist for your island or your area — and if not, can one be requested? The composition is set out in the Boletim Oficial, I Série n.º 44 of 23 July 2014, with certain representatives designated by the respective members of Government, so the balance between state and community seats is checkable in the gazette rather than a matter of practice. This is the route into management decisions short of litigation, and in a small-island jurisdiction it is likely to be the more productive one.

trackers.name: Six categories — and two of them have never been used
trackers.desc: PICK YOUR CATEGORY KNOWING WHICH ARE EMPTY. Decreto-Lei n.º 3/2003 creates the typology of protected areas and gives them juridical content, configures the Rede Nacional das Áreas Protegidas as an open system into which declared areas are progressively integrated, and articulates the public participation guaranteed in the Lei de Bases da Política do Ambiente. ‘An open system’ is the phrase to use — the network is designed to keep admitting areas, so a proposal works with the statute's logic; and the participation guarantee lives in the Lei de Bases, so cite both. THE SIX: Reserva Natural (15 sites, in integral, parcial and temporal subcategories — a ‘temporal’ reserve is protection for a defined period); Parque Nacional — no sites have been decreed; Parque Natural; Monumento Natural; Paisagem Protegida — zones where the integrated action of man and nature has created aesthetic or cultural value, protection centred on maintenance and restoration, so this is the category for a worked, inhabited landscape; and Sítio de Interesse Científico — places generally of reduced dimension holding populations threatened with extinction, of which none have yet been designated. For a small site with a threatened population that category is unused rather than unavailable — being first is harder, but it exists and is designed for small sites. Coverage exceeds 10 percent of the country, about 632.09 km²; Parques and Reservas Naturais are at least 75 percent of the network. Responsible body: Direção Nacional do Ambiente.

trackers.name: ICCA Registry and Protected Planet — and registration is not a precondition
trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. Land that is worked rather than preserved is not excluded. But note the exclusivity: a site can be a protected area or an OECM — it is not possible to meet both, so ask which is being proposed. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.

trackers.name: ADAD, Praia — Cape Verde's oldest environmental association, and the 2020 decree that gives you an EIA to comment on
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Associação para a Defesa do Ambiente e Desenvolvimento (ADAD), a legally constituted NGO created in 1991 in Praia, Santiago, and published in the official gazette — the country's long-standing national environmental association, working on sustainable practice, biodiversity protection and environmental justice, alongside education and engagement with decision-makers. It is a member of the international conservation union and of regional marine and coastal networks, so a small island community has a route through it to outside technical and legal attention. Address: Avenida Cidade Lisboa, Fazenda, Praia, Santiago. THE LEGAL HOOK TO NAME, and it is recent enough that many people do not know it exists: Decreto-Lei n.º 27/2020 approves the legal regime for environmental impact assessment of PUBLIC AND PRIVATE projects likely to produce significant effects on the environment, published in the official bulletin of 19 March 2020, with requirements for impact studies and assessment processes aligned to established good practice. If a hotel, quarry, marina or road is proposed near you in Cape Verde, ask which EIA was done under the 2020 regime, and ask to see it — that document is the only formal opening most residents will get. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdean residents and community associations facing coastal development, quarrying or infrastructure, and island groups needing a national body with international network reach. CAVEATS: NO VERIFIED LIVE SITE OF ITS OWN WAS FOUND — this entry points at the conservation union's member record, and the association's public presence is largely through social media; it is an environmental association, not a law firm or a fund. For Sao Vicente and marine reporting, Cape Verde's Biosfera entry.

trackers.name: Cape Verde — free legal assistance is a state-assured right delivered by STATE-APPOINTED ADVOCATES, with an access-to-law institute alongside
trackers.desc: WHAT YOU ARE ENTITLED TO: in Cape Verde access to free legal assistance is a right ASSURED BY THE STATE, so that every citizen regardless of economic condition can have adequate legal representation — and the service is delivered by ADVOCATES APPOINTED BY THE STATE who act in judicial proceedings AT NO COST to the beneficiary. The mechanism is appointment, not application to a fund: what you are asking for is the nomination of an advocate, and the phrase to use is apoio jurídico / assistência jurídica gratuita. THE INSTITUTION NAMED ALONGSIDE IT: the Instituto de Acesso ao Direito e à Justiça (IADJ), described as a principal instrument of legal support, offering ORIENTATION and LEGAL REPRESENTATION to citizens; the Ordem dos Advogados de Cabo Verde sits beside it, running continuing training for advocates. The barriers the same account names are the familiar pair — lack of financial resources and the COMPLEXITY OF LEGAL PROCEDURES — with government and NGOs running free or reduced-cost assistance programmes to mitigate them. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR AN ISLAND LAND DISPUTE: Cape Verde's development pressure is coastal and touristic, and the country's environmental impact regime — recorded separately in this file — gives a resident a document to contest; a state-appointed advocate is how an ordinary household actually contests it, because the EIA route is worthless if nobody can file. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdeans without means facing an expropriation, coastal development, inheritance or property dispute on any island. CAVEATS: THIS ENTRY IS SOURCED FROM A CAPE VERDEAN LEGAL-SECTOR PUBLICATION RATHER THAN A GOVERNMENT PORTAL — confirm the current procedure and the IADJ's contact details with the Ordem dos Advogados de Cabo Verde before relying on specifics; appointment depends on advocate availability across a nine-island archipelago. For the EIA regime and the national environmental association, Cape Verde's ADAD entry; for Sao Vicente marine reporting, Biosfera.

trackers.name: Fundo do Ambiente, Cape Verde — a public institute that finances environmental preservation projects, and it funds MUNICIPALITIES directly
trackers.desc: WHERE TO APPLY FOR MONEY: the FUNDO DO AMBIENTE, a Cape Verdean PUBLIC INSTITUTE whose current statute was approved by Decreto-lei nº59/2020 of 5 August, developing the regulatory norms foreseen in the Lei de Bases da Política do Ambiente and establishing the fundamental principles for managing and protecting the environment against all forms of degradation. The financing regime for projects relating to environmental preservation activity sits in Decreto-Lei nº40/2013. A dedicated financing decree plus a public institute means the money is not discretionary charity — cite the decree number when you ask what the current window is. WHO IT ACTUALLY PAYS, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART: documented disbursements go to MUNICIPAL COUNCILS — the Câmara Municipal de São Miguel received a rotating excavator to give effect to its projects, and a new urban solid waste collection truck, and a memorandum of understanding was signed between the Fund, that municipal council and the island water utility. Equipment and works through your own câmara municipal is how island environmental money actually lands — so the lever, as in Mali, is the municipal council rather than a direct community application. Ask your câmara what it has requested from the Fundo do Ambiente and what it received; both sides of that are public. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdean municipalities, associations and communities with an environmental preservation, waste or water project on any island. CAVEATS: A STATE FINANCING INSTITUTE — it funds environmental preservation, NOT litigation, land purchase or opposition to a licensed development, and the documented flow is to municipal councils rather than to villages directly; confirm the current window and eligibility before relying on it. For the 2020 EIA regime and the national environmental association, Cape Verde's ADAD entry; for a state-appointed advocate, the legal assistance entry; for Sao Vicente marine reporting, Biosfera.

trackers.name: Cape Verde's protected areas and their Conselho Assessor — article 22 lets a council be created FOR A SINGLE PROTECTED AREA, to secure local community participation
trackers.desc: THE SEAT AT THE TABLE AND HOW TO GET IT: Cape Verde's protected areas sit in the REDE NACIONAL DE ÁREAS PROTEGIDAS under DECRETO-LEI Nº3/2003 of 24 February, with categories including Parque Natural, Reserva Natural and Reserva Natural Integral, each delimited by its own decreto-regulamentar. ARTICLE 22 IS THE PROVISION TO QUOTE: the government department responsible for the environment MAY CREATE A CONSELHO ASSESSOR FOR EACH ISLAND OR, EXCEPTIONALLY, FOR A SINGLE PROTECTED AREA, to facilitate management THROUGH THE PARTICIPATION OF THE POPULATION and cooperation between administrative bodies — and where such a council has been created its stated objects are TO SUPPORT AND ENSURE THE PARTICIPATION OF LOCAL COMMUNITIES AND PARTNER ENTITIES, and TO PROPOSE DIRECTIVES AND ACTIONS. A council can be created for ONE protected area, and its job is your participation — that is the cheapest formal standing available in Cape Verde: ask the environment department to constitute a Conselho Assessor for the area you live beside. WHAT THE DECLARATIONS ARE BUILT ON, which tells you what argument works: the Boa Vista Parque Natural do Norte was declared to conserve natural values AND THEIR INTERACTION WITH THE SOCIOECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT OF LOCAL POPULATIONS, THROUGH THE STRENGTHENING OF TRADITIONAL ACTIVITIES. Traditional activity is written into the ground of declaration — so a fishing or salt-working practice is an argument FOR protection, not an obstacle to it. WHAT THESE AREAS FACE, DOCUMENTED ON SAL: the Ponta do Sinó reserve is ALMOST ENTIRELY SURROUNDED BY RESORTS, its size reduced not only by government decrees but by the loss of sand migration, with dunes that have disappeared; threats listed are vehicle traffic across the dunes, coastal development, light and noise pollution, and disturbance of nesting and feeding sites. The Baía da Murdeira reserve, created 2003, is the ONLY officially designated MARINE reserve in Cape Verde — about 2,067 hectares; Costa da Fragata covers 2,693 hectares, 346 on land and 2,347 marine. Local conservation work is run as COOPERATIVE MANAGEMENT of the protected areas — training, trail delimitation, codes of conduct, dune restoration, and community outreach including GUIDE TRAINING AND SUSTAINABLE LIVELIHOODS FOR FISHERS AND RESIDENTS. WHO IT SUITS: Cape Verdean island communities beside a protected area or facing resort expansion. CAVEATS: STATE-DECLARED AREAS WITH ADVISORY COMMUNITY BODIES, NOT COMMUNITY TENURE — the council is assessor, and decrees have themselves reduced reserve areas. For the EIA regime, Cape Verde's ADAD entry; for money, the Fundo do Ambiente entry; for a state-appointed advocate, the legal assistance entry.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists. It found violations of articles 1 and 24 of the African Charter — article 24: ‘all peoples shall have the right to a general satisfactory environment favourable to their development’ — and of article 21, the right to natural wealth and resources. THE FAULT WAS AN OMISSION: the state ‘defaulted in its duties in terms of vigilance and diligence’, and ‘the omission to act and to prevent damage to the environment characterises the violation’. It ordered restoration within the shortest possible time and measures to prevent further damage, citing the ICJ that the environment ‘is not an abstraction but represents the living space, the quality of life and the very health of human beings, including generations unborn’. THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHO YOU SUE: the Court held it had no jurisdiction over the private oil corporations, which were struck from the suit. You sue the State for failing to regulate; you cannot sue the company here — naming one as respondent loses that part of the case. AND PLAN FOR ENFORCEMENT: commentary records the Court did not identify a means for Nigeria to implement the ruling, and the ICJ later wrote to the President pressing for enforcement — judgment is the start of an enforcement campaign, not a self-executing remedy. Proposals to require exhaustion of domestic remedies were rejected by ECOWAS experts and Heads of Government, so the direct-access rule has been tested and held.

trackers.name: Department of Forestry — and 66 parks demarcated since the 1950s
trackers.desc: A DOCUMENTARY STARTING POINT MOST COUNTRIES IN THIS MAP CANNOT OFFER. Between 1950 and 1954 a forestry adviser identified and demarcated 66 forest parks for conservation and production — timber, bamboo and rhun palms — so if your site is one of them, the demarcation record exists. The colonial administration's own conclusion that total protection for all the parks was impractical is the origin of the participatory turn that followed. The Department's operational mandate rests on the Forest Regulation of 1978, with the Forest Act 1998 and Regulations legally requiring communities to participate in fire prevention and participative forest management — note that participation is a legal requirement on communities, not only an entitlement, which cuts both ways before an approach. The Department works to the Gambian Forest Management Concept, developed with the Gambian-German Forest Project since 1980. Current policy: the National Forest Policy 2023–2032. The parent ministry is the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resources.

trackers.name: Community Forest Committee — the state transfers ownership, after probation
trackers.desc: THE GAMBIA TRANSFERS OWNERSHIP, NOT A CONCESSION — and that is rare enough to cite across borders. The community forestry concept foresees an ownership transfer of forest land from the State to an interested community: not a management agreement, not a use right. COMPARE WHAT THIS MAP RECORDS ELSEWHERE: Cambodia's community protected areas give management rights but not exclusion rights; Burkina Faso's GGF is a concession; Guinea classifies forest ‘to the benefit of’ a collectivity. Where a neighbouring community is negotiating a concession, The Gambia is the comparator. The Gambia is recorded as one of the first countries in Africa to introduce community forestry nationwide, the concept being the flagship of the 1995 Forest Policy and the 1998 Forest Bill. THE ROUTE RUNS THROUGH A COMMITTEE YOU FORM AND ELECT: communities establish Community Forest Committees or Village Development Committees whose members are elected by the local population, trained by implementing partners and then responsible for planning, coordinating and managing delivery — including natural resource-based income-generating activities. THE STEP MOST APPLICANTS UNDERESTIMATE: the community must go through a training and probation period, which is then evaluated, with the final aim being reservation of the forestland as a gazetted Community Forest. Plan for probation and assessment, not an application — the gazettal comes at the end, not the beginning. The programme also provides literacy and basic skills, civic and health education, so the route carries adult education with it rather than assuming it.

trackers.name: NEA Inspectorate — 26 inspectors for the whole country, and every enforcement notice on record fell inside Greater Banjul
trackers.desc: WHERE A POLLUTION REPORT GOES, AND HOW FAR THE AGENCY CAN ACTUALLY REACH. The Inspectorate of the National Environment Agency enforces ten instruments, including the National Environmental Management Act 1994, the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations 2014, the Environmental Discharge (Permitting) Regulations 1999 and the Environmental Quality Standards Regulations 1999. Its first response is administrative, not judicial: an Improvement Notice or a Demand for Compliance, with litigation held back as a last resort. As at 4 January 2022 it had served 121 such notices, all of them within the Greater Banjul Area, against a national inspectorate of 26 people — one acting principal inspector, nine senior inspectors and sixteen inspectors. Up-country, the absence of a notice against a site is not evidence that the site is clean; it is more likely evidence that no inspector has been there. The page names the unit and its statutory basis but gives no complaint form, no email address and no service standard for responding to a report, so a written complaint to the Agency's head office in Kanifing, copied to the relevant regional office, is the route that exists rather than the route that is advertised.

trackers.name: NEA environmental assessment programme — the Class A / B / C screening decision is the one worth contesting early
trackers.desc: THE SCREENING CLASS DECIDES HOW MUCH SCRUTINY A PROJECT EVER RECEIVES, AND IT IS SET BEFORE ANY STUDY BEGINS. The Agency's own explainer describes three classes: Class A requires a mandatory assessment, Class B a limited one, and Class C none at all on the basis that the impacts are treated as negligible. A project placed in Class C generates no assessment document to comment on, which makes the classification, not the report, the thing to challenge. The explainer also names the lead-institution arrangement — for oil and gas the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority leads, with lands and survey, parks and wildlife, physical planning, water resources and the affected community brought in as stakeholders — so the body holding the file may not be the environment agency at all. Terminology note for searching the register: the Agency now writes ESIA rather than EIA, and older documents use the earlier term. This is a published programme description hosted on the Agency's own domain; it is not a procedure manual and it states no comment deadline, and no public register of screening decisions was located on the site.

trackers.name: NALA will advise you on a land case and will not represent you in one — and the same page carries the two bodies that can act
trackers.desc: CHECK THE CIVIL GATE BEFORE BUILDING A PLAN AROUND FREE COUNSEL. The Ministry of Justice's own description of the National Agency for Legal Aid states that it provides legal advice as well as legal representation in criminal matters in court, at police stations and in prisons. Advice is general; representation is criminal. A community facing an acquisition or a nuisance can therefore get an opinion from NALA but should not expect an advocate from it. Headquarters in Banjul with centres at Basse and Farafenni; the West Coast Region and Central River Region centres are described as still being established. Three telephone numbers are published and no email address, no means test and no application form. The same page lists the two bodies that can actually act on a land dispute without counsel: the Alternative Dispute Resolution Secretariat, headquartered at Fajara with pilot centres at Farafenni and Basse, which runs arbitration, conciliation and mediation as an alternative to the courts; and the National Human Rights Commission at Kotu, which holds the powers of the High Court at trial — to hear complaints, summon and examine witnesses on oath, and enforce its decisions, including measures to protect the life and safety of an individual. NALA maintains no website of its own; this is the State's canonical page for it, not a third party's description.

trackers.name: IHRDA, Banjul — pro bono counsel that takes community cases to the African regional courts, and publishes a case intake form
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: the Institute for Human Rights and Development in Africa, founded in Banjul in 1998 by two lawyers who had worked inside the Secretariat of the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights and concluded the regional system was profoundly underused. It provides pro bono legal counsel to victims of human rights violations, before national courts and before the African regional bodies — the African Commission, the African Court, the ECOWAS Community Court of Justice, the East African Court of Justice and the SADC Tribunal — and filed the first case ever brought before the African Commission. WHY IT BELONGS IN A MAP ABOUT LAND: the regional system is where African communities have won the landmark land rulings. The Endorois decision held that an indigenous community's rights to property, culture, religion, disposal of natural resources and development had been violated by their removal — a precedent any dispossessed community's lawyer should know exists. IHRDA maintains Africa's most comprehensive human rights case law database, free to search, which is where you find what has already been won. AND — UNUSUALLY IN THIS FILE — IT PUBLISHES A CASE INTAKE FORM: it says plainly that it is a small organisation with substantial work, that it prioritises cases with the potential to benefit wider communities and achieve systemic change, and that it provides legal expertise only and NOT financial or material assistance. It also runs country-specific litigation workshops to get civil society actors filing cases themselves, and mentions a legal defence fund supporting litigants. 949 Brusubi Layout, AU Summit Highway, P.O. Box 1896, Banjul. WHO IT SUITS: communities anywhere in Africa whose domestic remedies are exhausted or blocked, especially indigenous and minority communities facing dispossession. CAVEATS: entered under The Gambia because that is where it is based and registered — its work is continental. Regional cases take years and produce decisions that states must then be pressed to implement; it does not fund your costs; and its stated focus areas are refugees, minority rights, children and economic and social rights rather than environmental law as such.

trackers.name: Les Amis de la Terre-Togo (ADT-Togo)
trackers.desc: Togo's first NGO wholly dedicated to environmental protection, founded on 20 June 1990 and formally recognised as an association the following year, and the Togolese member of Friends of the Earth International. Its work spans biodiversity, climate, desertification, water and sanitation, chemicals, mining and scrutiny of public decision-making, delivered largely through community dialogues, agro-ecology training and youth education from its Lome office. WHO TO ENLIST: a first port of call for a Togolese community rather than a litigator — ADT-Togo is a focal point for the national civil-society networks on climate and energy, so it is the quickest route to finding who else already works on a site. Note the canonical domain is amiterre.org; several older wordpress and .tg addresses for this organisation still circulate.

trackers.name: ECOWAS Court of Justice — file directly, but sue the State
trackers.desc: A COURT YOU CAN REACH WITHOUT EXHAUSTING DOMESTIC REMEDIES. The ECOWAS Community Court of Justice has held human rights jurisdiction since 2005 and has broad access and standing rules permitting individuals and NGOs to bypass national courts and file directly. THE PRECEDENT: in SERAP v Federal Republic of Nigeria (ECW/CCJ/APP/08/09) the Court dismissed all three preliminary objections — no locus standi, no jurisdiction, statute-barred — and rejected the government's attempt to exclude an Amnesty International report from the evidence. NGO research was admitted as evidence, which matters when no state data exists. It found violations of articles 1 and 24 of the African Charter — article 24: ‘all peoples shall have the right to a general satisfactory environment favourable to their development’ — and of article 21, the right to natural wealth and resources. THE FAULT WAS AN OMISSION: the state ‘defaulted in its duties in terms of vigilance and diligence’, and ‘the omission to act and to prevent damage to the environment characterises the violation’. It ordered restoration within the shortest possible time and measures to prevent further damage, citing the ICJ that the environment ‘is not an abstraction but represents the living space, the quality of life and the very health of human beings, including generations unborn’. THE LIMIT THAT DECIDES WHO YOU SUE: the Court held it had no jurisdiction over the private oil corporations, which were struck from the suit. You sue the State for failing to regulate; you cannot sue the company here — naming one as respondent loses that part of the case. AND PLAN FOR ENFORCEMENT: commentary records the Court did not identify a means for Nigeria to implement the ruling, and the ICJ later wrote to the President pressing for enforcement — judgment is the start of an enforcement campaign, not a self-executing remedy. Proposals to require exhaustion of domestic remedies were rejected by ECOWAS experts and Heads of Government, so the direct-access rule has been tested and held.

trackers.name: ORFAO — comparative land-law tables, and a directive in draft
trackers.desc: COMPARATIVE LEGAL TABLES FOR YOUR COUNTRY AND ITS NEIGHBOURS, IN ONE DOCUMENT. The Observatoire Régional du Foncier Rural en Afrique de l'Ouest (ORFAO), hosted by UEMOA, publishes a regional study on rural land markets containing side-by-side ‘cadre légal comparé’ tables — one covering Bénin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire and Sénégal, another Guinée-Bissau, Mali, Niger and Togo — plus typologies of direct and indirect interventions in land markets and a table of regulatory issues and families of instruments. If you need to know what instrument exists in your country and whether a neighbour has a stronger one, that is the document — comparative tables let a campaign point to a neighbour's provision as an achievable ask rather than a novelty. A WINDOW IS OPENING: on 26 June 2026 in Ouagadougou the UEMOA ministers for urbanisme, habitat, domaines et cadastre approved a draft directive to harmonise rules on immatriculation foncière, accès au titre de propriété and a système d'information foncière, aiming at a common framework of land governance. BE PRECISE ABOUT STATUS: that was a DRAFT directive approved by ministers, not an adopted and transposed instrument — check adoption and transposition before relying on it. But transposition is the moment domestic land law is reopened in each state, and that is when community provisions can be argued for. FOR A GRAZING OR TRANSHUMANCE DISPUTE: a regional pastoral situation bulletin covers 11 West African countries with the support of decentralised technical services — an evidence source drawing on the same services you would otherwise approach one by one. RECORDED PLAINLY: cattle theft is documented as a driver of conflict and instability in the Sahel, so a land dispute here may sit inside a security context that changes what is safe to do. And confirm your state's current ECOWAS standing — several members are recorded as suspended.

trackers.name: JVE — an environmental organisation with branches in dozens of Togolese localities, and a standing programme on dams and mining
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: Jeunes Volontaires pour l'Environnement, founded on 23 November 2001 by Togolese students who had watched their country's land degrade, now an IUCN member with its international secretariat in Lomé. THE REACH IS THE POINT, because in Togo almost everything else is capital-bound: JVE reports around 32 to 40 local branches inside Togo, with regional antennas relaying activity at community level from Vogan (60 km from Lomé), Tsiko (140 km) and Kara (450 km) — so the north of the country is actually covered — plus national representations across roughly 25 African countries, each with relative autonomy. WHAT TO ASK FOR SPECIFICALLY: among its five published programmes is one on social justice covering dams, mining, and economic, social and cultural rights, alongside work on environmental impact assessment, access to water and river protection, sustainable agriculture and campaigning on genetically modified organisms. That programme, not the youth-and-volunteering framing, is the part that matches a community fighting a project. It runs weekly radio and television output and a monthly paper, which is a distribution channel a village campaign does not otherwise have. 131 rue Ofè, Tokoin Casablanca, BP 8823, Lomé; founder and executive director Sena Alouka. WHO IT SUITS: Togolese communities facing dams, mining, water loss or land degradation, and community groups elsewhere in West Africa able to reach a national representation. CAVEATS: an environmental education, volunteering and advocacy organisation, not a law firm — no litigation capacity, no intake route, no fee information; branch counts differ between its own listings (20 towns, 32 branches, 40 localities) and several published pages are old, so confirm which branch is active near you.

trackers.name: Centre pour la Justice Environnementale — works the Togolese phosphate belt, where the compensation is 5 CFA francs per square metre a year
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a Togolese environmental justice centre working with the communities around the phosphate operations — Kpémé, Goumoukopé and Hahotoé-Kpogamé — where the processing plant sits on land the villagers had to give up. Its stated work is upholding the rights of those neighbouring communities against social and environmental injustice, pressing for effluent treatment before discharge, reduction of gas and dust emissions, and direct accompaniment of affected communities, including income-generating activities. THE NUMBER THAT TELLS YOU WHAT A BAD LAND DEAL LOOKS LIKE, and which any community should compare their own offer against: when the phosphate company was established the villagers ceded land, and the company now pays the former owners 5 CFA francs per square metre — roughly three-quarters of a euro cent — per year or per quarter depending on the plot. Residents also report that the jobs went to casual and contract workers, so the plant brought neither land rent nor employment. A perpetual rent set decades ago and never indexed is worth nothing; check whether your agreement has a revision clause before you sign it. WHAT TOGOLESE CIVIL SOCIETY IS DEMANDING ON RESETTLEMENT, published jointly by a human rights committee, two development associations and the phosphate-affected persons' association ASIPTO, is a usable checklist: count new dwellings separately from those already counted; raise the rent per square metre; raise the housing construction payment to at least 2 million CFA francs per dwelling to match current costs; publish clear directives on responsible land tenure governance; and seek the CONSENT and full participation of the people facing relocation as rights holders. Togo's expropriation regime rests on a 1945 decree and a 1974 ordinance, and campaigners note that expropriation must be for a legally established public purpose with just, prior and fair compensation. WHO IT SUITS: Togolese communities facing mining pollution, land cession to an industrial operator, or relocation. CAVEATS: an advocacy and accompaniment organisation, not a law firm; ASIPTO, the affected people's own association, may merit its own entry; and Togo's Amis de la Terre and JVE entries cover the wider environmental and social-justice work.

trackers.name: Togo's aide juridictionnelle law of 24 May 2013 — the state can pay for your case, in full or in part, and it covers settlements as well as trials
trackers.desc: WHAT THE LAW PAYS FOR: Togo's loi portant AIDE JURIDICTIONNELLE, adopted 24 MAY 2013, under which the state may grant FINANCIAL AID in the context of a procedure before a court AND/OR IN A TRANSACTION — and the aid may be TOTAL OR PARTIAL. Two things there are easy to miss: partial aid exists, so being told you do not qualify for full support is not the end; and the aid covers a NEGOTIATED SETTLEMENT (transaction), not only a trial — which matters enormously in a land dispute where the realistic outcome is a deal rather than a judgment. WHO CAN CLAIM IT: it is granted on request to Togolese nationals; nationals of a state bound to Togo by a bilateral agreement recognising the benefit; refugees recognised by Togo; and ASYLUM SEEKERS whose claim is pending before the national eligibility commission. Displaced and non-citizen residents are inside this scheme by name — rare enough in this file to be worth checking for in your own country's text. WHERE IT SITS: the law completed a national policy on access to law and legal dissemination targeting the population's priority legal-information needs, within a judicial reform and modernisation programme running since 2006 with UN development programme support. Read it alongside the francophone vocabulary recorded in Benin's entry — this is the FINANCIAL limb, so the words to use at the counter are aide juridictionnelle. WHO IT SUITS: Togolese households and communities — including those around the phosphate belt — who need the state to fund a case or a settlement, and refugees or asylum seekers in Togo. CAVEATS: THIS IS A FUNDING SCHEME, NOT AN OFFICE THAT ARGUES YOUR CASE — confirm which bureau receives the request and what proof of means it wants; the law dates from 2013 and implementation should be verified locally. For the phosphate communities and the resettlement checklist, Togo's Centre pour la Justice Environnementale entry; for wider environmental and social justice work, Les Amis de la Terre-Togo and JVE.

trackers.name: Togo's forêts communautaires — the Village Development Committee becomes the forest's LEGAL ENTITY and files for registration; 43 are registered, most others have no legal status
trackers.desc: HOW A TOGOLESE VILLAGE GETS ITS FOREST REGISTERED: community forests in Togo are governed by the LOI PORTANT CODE FORESTIER OF 2008. The route is shown by ALIBI-1, whose community moved BEFORE the state did — working with a national association it put in place and SECURED 5,496 HECTARES of forest adjoining the classified forest of Abdoulaye. THE VEHICLE, AND THIS IS THE STEP TO COPY: the COMITÉ VILLAGEOIS DE DÉVELOPPEMENT IS TODAY THE LEGAL ENTITY MANAGING THE FOREST, and it is that committee which launched the process of IMMATRICULATION — REGISTRATION OF THE FOREST BY THE ENVIRONMENT MINISTRY. Your existing village development committee can become the forest's legal person; you do not need to create a new body, you need to give the one you have the forest and then register it. The management committees are constituted to represent every part of the community — traditional chieftaincy, farmers' groups, folkloric groups, women's associations — and the paperwork presented publicly is the CHARTE DE GESTION and the CONTRAT DE MISE À DISPOSITION. Ask for those two documents by name. RESULTS AND SCALE: at Alibi bush fires, anarchic wood-cutting and poaching fell considerably through the local management committee, and the case became a national school example; elsewhere ECO-GARDES are trained and equipped from each canton to patrol, and beekeeping with distributed hives gives the committee an income. A village that began with a 14-metre firebreak and a 10-metre tree belt grew a community forest 350 to 850 metres deep around the town, zoned into 25 ha conservation, 44 ha forest and 33 ha agroforestry. THE HONEST PROBLEM, STATED BY TOGOLESE RESEARCH: community forests exist in many forms — sacred forests, village reforestation — but FEW OF THEM HAVE LEGAL STATUS; only 43 have been registered with the environment ministry across all regions. An unregistered community forest is the commonest situation in Togo and the most fragile — registration is the whole difference. WHO IT SUITS: Togolese villages holding a sacred forest, a reforested belt or any communal woodland without papers. CAVEATS: REGISTRATION IS MINISTERIAL AND MANAGEMENT-PLAN BASED, not a title deed; research finds management committees need organisational support and diversified income to hold. For the phosphate belt and the resettlement checklist, Togo's Centre pour la Justice Environnementale entry; for state funding of a case or settlement, the aide juridictionnelle entry.

trackers.name: ADN — Associació per a la Defensa de la Natura (Andorra)
trackers.desc: Andorra's nature-defence association, founded in 1986, working on conservation, research and public information across the whole country. WHO TO ENLIST when a development touches a valley, a river or a protected area — its record is the reason to: it made the first proposal to protect the Madriu valley in 1997, a valley now inscribed as World Heritage, and it still publishes the documents from that campaign. You CAN: use its Denúncies channel to report an environmental breach, and draw on its practice of naming areas that ought to be protected and pressing for their designation, which is the lever in a country with little formal land-protection machinery. It also runs river monitoring through Projecte Rius, so it can supply baseline water data. For activists: this is a volunteer scientific association, not a law firm — expect evidence, designation proposals and a public voice rather than representation.

trackers.name: Andorra business registry (company register)
trackers.desc: Accountability source (official company register); Andorra business registry (company register) — the official register of companies and legal entities in Andorra — the primary public record of corporate existence, ownership, directors and filings. HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM A BENEFICIAL-OWNERSHIP REGISTER: this shows the registered entity, its directors and filings; where a separate beneficial-ownership register exists, use that to reach the real humans behind a shell company.

trackers.name: Andorra — Ministeri de Finances
trackers.desc: National budget authority; the Department of Budget & Patrimony prepares the State budget and manages budget execution, Andorra. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Andorra.

trackers.name: Andorra — Registre de Societats
trackers.desc: National company registry; the official corporate register recording all legal entities (name, legal form, registration number, directors, share capital & status) in the Principality of Andorra. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: Tribunal de Comptes
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Andorra, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Biodiversity subsidy — individuals may apply, and it is undersubscribed
trackers.desc: A GRANT WITH ALMOST NO COMPETITION — the opposite of the position almost everywhere else in this map. The Subvenció a favor de la biodiversitat i del paisatge is an annual call run by Medi Ambient, and the Government extended the 2026 deadline to 31 July 2026 after finding that as at 16 June only one application had been formalised in each of the two calls, despite several expressions of interest — the extension's stated purpose being to favour greater participation. WHO MAY APPLY: any natural person with capacity to act and an administrative identification number (NIA), and any entity with its own legal personality and a NIA acting through a representative holding the electronic certificate for representatives of legal persons. Recorded beneficiaries include public and private entities, particulars, non-profit associations and holders of agricultural, livestock and beekeeping operations. ASSEMBLE THE PAPERWORK BEFORE DRAFTING: the bases de la convocatòria duly signed; a declaration (annex 1) that you are not a debtor of the Administration; a responsible declaration (annex 2) on capacity to contract with the public sector; and a bank domiciliation authorisation (form H1T003). A SECOND CALL RUNS IN PARALLEL: subsidies to prevent damage caused by protected fauna in agricultural, livestock and beekeeping operations — where protected species are the source of local opposition, that is the fund which answers it. What has been funded shows the range accepted: educational fishing courses, and the Federació Andorrana de Caça i Pesca's perdiu xerra breeding centre using radiotelemetry to track survival of released birds — so a hunting and fishing federation and a commercial guide are both among the funded; this is not restricted to conservation NGOs. Apply via the seu electrònica at e-tramits.ad.

trackers.name: Recurs administratiu — but planning is expressly excluded, and nothing stops
trackers.desc: READ THE EXCLUSION FIRST, BECAUSE IT COVERS MOST LAND DISPUTES. Any person who considers themselves harmed by an act of the Administració General may lodge a recurs administratiu before the Govern — against definitive acts and against procedural acts that make continuation impossible or produce indefensió — but ‘queden exceptuats els recursos en matèria de construcció i urbanisme’. Construction and urban planning are expressly outside the ordinary administrative appeal, along with fiscal matters and anything with a special statutory procedure. So do not file a general recurs against a planning decision assuming it is the right route — establish which special procedure applies, and note that planning powers in Andorra sit substantially with the comuns rather than the Govern. WHERE IT DOES LIE: one month from notification, under article 129 of Llei 14/2023 of 3 July, the consolidated Codi de l'Administració. Eligible to file: any natural person with capacity to act and a NIA, and any entity with legal personality and a NIA. The resolution ends the administrative route. THE TRAP TO PLAN AROUND: under articles 52 and 135, ‘la interposició de recurs no suspèn l'execució de l'acte impugnat’ — lodging an appeal does not suspend execution. Works may proceed while you appeal; any suspension must be sought separately, and nothing stops by itself.

trackers.name: Batllia and the Raonador — name the co-defendants; the Ombudsman is free
trackers.desc: TWO ROUTES ABOVE THE ADMINISTRATION, AND ONE COSTS NOTHING. THE SECCIÓ ADMINISTRATIVA DE LA BATLLIA: the recurs contenciós administratiu is governed by Llei 9/2022 of 7 April, replacing the 1989 law that had originally created an administrative jurisdiction which did not previously exist in Andorra. Proceedings start with a demanda addressed to that Section (article 16), which must identify the party and justify its legitimacy; identify the act, actuació or reglamentary norm challenged and which administration authored it; and identify the parties to be treated as co-defendants. TWO CONSEQUENCES: a reglamentary norm is directly challengeable, not only an individual act — the regulation itself can be the target; and you must name the co-defendants yourself, which in a development dispute means identifying the promoter, not only the administration. Administrations are defended by lletrats of their own legal cabinets. THE RAONADOR DEL CIUTADÀ IS THE FREE ROUTE, taking complaints against Andorran institutions on rights and freedoms set out in the Constitution as they touch the Administration, and reporting annually to the Consell General. Its own reports record why it matters: people entitled to go to the Batllia ‘desisteixen d'acudir-hi per manca de recursos’ — give up going for lack of means. It keeps a dedicated urbanisme sector, so planning complaints are a recognised category even though excluded from the ordinary recurs. LIMIT: in the justice sector it is limited to transmitting the complaint to the Consell Superior de la Justícia. LEVERAGE: its reports record files closed without reply from the administration despite reminders of the obligation to answer — a documented non-response, published to Parliament, is itself a usable outcome.

trackers.name: Eurosite / ELCN — who already holds land near you, and the easement route
trackers.desc: A DIRECTORY OF THE PEOPLE WHO ALREADY HOLD AND MANAGE LAND IN YOUR COUNTRY — which is who you need when the answer to a development is getting the land into protective hands. Eurosite, established 1989, is one of the largest pan-European organisations bringing together NGOs, governmental organisations and private bodies, with members from the Atlantic islands to the Black Sea and from Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. ITS ELCN STRAND IS ABOUT PRIVATE LAND SPECIFICALLY: the European Land Conservation Network was built to support private landowners — non-public bodies or individuals — willing to engage in conservation ON AT LEAST PART OF THEIR LAND. That last phrase is the opening: a landowner who will not sell may still protect a portion, and there is a European network built to make that happen. The three tools it promotes are conservation easements, privately protected areas, and land stewardship agreements. AND A FUNDING ROUTE IS ATTACHED: ELCN and the ILCN have run sessions on using EU LIFE funding for private land conservation, aimed at landowners and conservationists preparing a LIFE project proposal; in November 2025 Eurosite-ELCN launched a working group on nature finance and land stewardship focused on finance mechanisms that mobilise private investment, co-chaired by the former head of the EU LIFE Programme. IF YOUR FIGHT IS A QUARRY, ASK FOR THIS BY NAME: Eurosite and partners published work on project selection criteria for conservation easements to protect nature in European quarries — a published European method for putting an easement over one. The network also co-hosts meetings of the Commission's Expert Group on the Nature Directives (NADEG) on tools and incentives for private land conservation — the most important working-level platform between the Commission, member states and interest groups. IF EUROSITE DOES NOT REACH YOUR COUNTRY, the International Land Conservation Network (founded 2014, the first global network of private land conservation practitioners) is the wider net, active from Canada to Australia to Latin America. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THESE ARE: networks of practitioners — they connect you to the organisation that can act; they do not buy land themselves. Ask the network who operates in your country; membership is not asserted here.

trackers.name: The comuns — seven parish authorities holding the communal land (Andorra)
trackers.desc: THE FACT THAT CHANGES WHO YOU WRITE TO: under the Constitution of the Principality of Andorra the seven comuns — the local public bodies of the parishes — manage and administer the goods of parish property, among them the communal public domain, which accounts for a high percentage of Andorran forest area. Each parish has its own Comú and manages directly the cadastre, public services, the communal patrimony and urban development, with its own legal personality and wide competences including planning, territorial planning and regulation of land. SO IN ANDORRA THE LANDOWNER AND THE PLANNING AUTHORITY ARE OFTEN THE SAME BODY. A community with a threatened site on communal ground is not looking for someone to buy it — it is asking its own parish authority, which already owns it and also decides what may be built on it. Write to the Comú, and ask which of the two hats it is wearing. THE PRECEDENT THAT SHOWS THIS WORKING: the Madriu-Perafita-Claror valley — 4,247 hectares, about 9% of the country, inscribed as World Heritage in 2004, with a periphery of roughly 4,000 further hectares — was protected through a Carta signed in January 2003 by government ministers and by the cònsols of Encamp, Andorra la Vella, Sant Julià de Lòria and Escaldes-Engordany on behalf of the comuns of the four parishes. Four parish authorities acting together protected a tenth of Andorra. THE TENSION TO EXPECT, and it is public: the Associació de Propietaris de Terres Andorranes — the association of Andorran landowners — publicly blames the comuns for urban planning disorder and legal insecurity, complaining that after the pandemic they went too far one way and now too far the other, and citing a boundary where building is permitted in one parish and not at all across the line in the next. Planning powers really do differ sharply between parishes, and landowners are organised and vocal about it. WHAT THIS IS NOT: not an NGO and not a funder. It is the level of government that holds the land, and in a country of seven parishes it is reachable.

trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a regional environmental endowment established in 2012, managing an endowment plus a sinking fund for Ecosystem-based Adaptation, which it disburses mainly through partner National Conservation Trust Funds rather than directly — it helped establish several of them, including the Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia and St Vincent funds. Its EbA window runs open calls for proposals. WHO IT SUITS: organisations doing on-the-ground ecosystem work that reduces climate vulnerability. Check whether your country has a national trust fund first — that is usually the door, and the CBF itself is the wholesaler behind it. HOW IT DIFFERS: endowment income committed for the long term, so it funds sustained protected-area management rather than a campaign. APPLY TO YOUR NATIONAL FUND, NOT TO CBF — for most of the money. CBF is a regional umbrella: at national level the partner National Conservation Trust Funds (NCTFs) lead the grantmaking process, with endowment proceeds held in country-based subaccounts and channelled through them. So for the Conservation Finance stream, the regional body is the wrong door — find your NCTF. THE EXCEPTION IS THE EbA FACILITY, which awards through competitive calls for proposals and is a direct route. THE NUMBERS: EbA medium grants USD 250,000–1 million, large grants up to USD 2 million — large by the standards of most funds here, and not aimed at a small unincorporated group acting alone. Eligible recipients expressly include NCTFs, NGOs, community-based organisations, government agencies, universities and the private sector. SCOPE CHECK: the EbA Facility covers the marine and coastal zone of the insular Caribbean, so an inland project must show its connection to marine and coastal ecosystems. IF YOU ARE TOO SMALL FOR EbA: CBF partners with GEF SGP across 12 shared countries — that is the sibling route for community-scale grants, and it is recorded separately in this map. Endowment disbursements go to NCTFs that have signed agreements with CBF, the first in 2016 with Fondo MARENA in the Dominican Republic.

trackers.name: CANARI — Caribbean Natural Resources Institute
trackers.desc: WHO TO ENLIST: a regional technical non-profit founded in 1989 and headquartered in Trinidad, working with grassroots and community-based organisations across the Caribbean on participatory natural resource governance. It supplies capacity rather than representation: coaching, mentoring, training of trainers, facilitated dialogues for planning and policymaking, and practical evidence tools including participatory GIS mapping, three-dimensional modelling and participatory video. WHO IT SUITS: community organisations that need to be equipped for a planning or policy fight. COVERAGE NOTE: CANARI is not registered as a non-profit in this country, but has delivered sub-grants to communities here under its Caribbean ecosystem-restoration work, so it does operate here — ask what is currently running. It is not a litigator and its re-granting is tied to donor projects. IS YOUR SITE A KBA? CHECK BEFORE YOU WRITE ANYTHING. CANARI publishes the CEPF Caribbean Islands Biodiversity Hotspot Ecosystem Profile, which identifies 45 Key Biodiversity Areas and 6 conservation corridors covering 28 KBAs as priorities for funding support, with maps — formulated through a process engaging over 200 stakeholders from more than 160 organisations. A campaign whose site is a KBA, or sits in one of the six corridors, has a materially stronger funding case and should say so explicitly. CORRECTED — AND THIS STREAM IS CLOSING. CEPF returned for a Phase II running August 2021 to July 2027, and CANARI is once again the Regional Implementation Team, managing US$11.8 million. THE ELEVENTH AND FINAL SMALL-GRANT CALL offers USD 5,000–50,000 for projects of up to 12 months between April 2026 and March 2027, and the tenth call was the final open call for large grants in the region — so treat the current call as the last scheduled opportunity, not one of many, though targeted solicitations may still fill portfolio gaps. ELIGIBILITY NARROWED IN PHASE II: the Phase I list of 11 countries no longer applies; Phase II calls name Antigua and Barbuda, The Bahamas, the Dominican Republic, Jamaica, Saint Lucia, and St Vincent and the Grenadines, with CEPF stating 7 countries initially eligible. BUT THE SITE TEST CAN OUTRANK THE COUNTRY TEST: applicants based outside the eligible countries may submit provided activities focus on a conservation need within a priority corridor or site. THREE RULES: applicants must not be a government agency (government-owned bodies qualify only with independent legal personality and authority to receive private funds); joint projects are eligible with one lead organisation; and NGOs, community groups, universities and private enterprises may all apply. ASK BEFORE YOU DRAFT: RIT Manager Nicole Brown, caribbeanrit@canari.org — applicants uncertain about eligibility are expressly encouraged to make contact first. A Grievance Redress Mechanism exists for concerns about a funded project. WHAT CANARI ITSELF IS: a non-profit technical institute of thirty years' standing that acts as a conduit, channelling funding, information and technical support to CSOs — not a standing grant fund. Its project pattern is small grants plus technical coaching for partner CSOs to run participatory community vulnerability assessments and then design a project from the results.

trackers.name: Antigua & Barbuda — Ministry of Finance
trackers.desc: National budget authority; responsible for public finances, economic planning, revenue & budgeting, Antigua and Barbuda. Here you can trace how the public budget is allocated and spent in Antigua and Barbuda.

trackers.name: Antigua & Barbuda — Intellectual Property & Commerce Office (ABIPCO)
trackers.desc: National company registry; ABIPCO handles company & business-name registration alongside intellectual-property administration, Antigua & Barbuda. — Holds to account: state firms & government-linked companies — find their registration, directors and filings.

trackers.name: National Audit Office
trackers.desc: Supreme audit institution of Antigua and Barbuda, auditing government accounts and the use of public money. HOW THIS DIFFERS: an audit body reports AFTER money is spent — use it to find documented waste, irregularity and misspending already uncovered, not live tenders; for who is winning contracts now use the procurement portal, and for aggregate budget totals the statistical office.

trackers.name: Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court (ECSC)
trackers.desc: A SUPERIOR COURT OF RECORD SERVING NINE EASTERN CARIBBEAN JURISDICTIONS, and the practical point is that you file at home. Established 27 February 1967 under the West Indies Associated States Supreme Court Order, the ECSC serves 6 independent states — Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, St Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, St Vincent and the Grenadines — and 3 British Overseas Territories — Anguilla, the Virgin Islands and Montserrat. It has unlimited jurisdiction in each member state and territory, and High Court operations are decentralised through registries in each participating territory, headed by trained registrars, allowing local filing, case management and initial hearings by resident or assigned judges. It exists so that very small jurisdictions can reach specialised judicial expertise without funding a standalone supreme court. THE BENCH HAS BEEN BRIEFED ON ESCAZÚ: ECLAC and the Government of Saint Lucia ran a consultation with ECSC judicial officers on the Regional Agreement on access to information, public participation and justice in environmental matters — so an environmental access-to-justice argument goes to judges who have had that agreement formally explained. Headquarters: Heraldine Rock Building, Castries, Saint Lucia; tel 758-457-3600; an e-Litigation Portal is available. CHECK YOUR FINAL COURT BEFORE PLANNING AN APPEAL — appeals from the ECSC go to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council or the Caribbean Court of Justice depending on the territory, and this is not uniform across the nine. For St Kitts and Nevis the final court is recorded as the Privy Council.

trackers.name: Bahamas National Trust
trackers.desc: WHAT IT DOES: an independent statutory body created by the Bahamas National Trust Act 1959, modelled on the British National Trust and given the job of ACQUIRING LAND and managing protected areas nationwide; it now holds and runs 32 national parks covering over two million acres, and its governing council seats government, private-sector and scientific representatives. Park rules are made under section 24 of the Act, so its bylaws carry legal force on trust property. USE IT: to propose a threatened Bahamian site for national-park status or trust acquisition, and to check whether land a developer wants already sits inside a park boundary.

trackers.name: Caribbean Biodiversity Fund (CBF)
trackers.desc: WHERE TO RAISE MONEY: a regional environmental endowment established in 2012, managing an endowment plus a sinking fund for Ecosystem-based Adaptation, which it disburses mainly through partner National Conservation Trust Funds rather than directly — it helped establish several of them, including the Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia and St Vincent funds. Its EbA window runs open calls for proposals. WHO IT SUITS: organisations doing on-the-ground ecosystem work that reduces climate vulnerability. trackers.name: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund (CEPF)
trackers.desc: A FUND WHOSE SMALL-GRANT APPLICATION IS A SINGLE LETTER. CEPF (founded 2000; a joint initiative of the French Development Agency, Conservation International, the EU, the GEF, the Government of Japan, the MacArthur Foundation and the World Bank) has funded more than 2,500 grantees. THE METHOD IS COPYABLE: a marine gap analysis engaging about 40 scientists and practitioners from more than 26 organisations across three consultations, identifying priority areas of interest for further vetting — evidence assembled collectively, then a specific written ask. CONTEXT: the first Bahamian protected area dates from 1892 and the Exuma Cays Land & Sea Park (1958) was the first of its kind — a managed no-take zone. Bahamas National Trust: P.O. trackers.name: Caribbean Court of Justice (CCJ)
trackers.desc: YOUR FINAL COURT OF APPEAL — this is one of only 5 states that have acceded to the CCJ's Appellate Jurisdiction, replacing the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council for civil and criminal appeals: Barbados, Belize, Dominica, Guyana and Saint Lucia. Everywhere else in the Eastern Caribbean the final court remains the Privy Council, so do not assume the CCJ is your appeal route from a neighbouring jurisdiction's practice. BE CLEAR WHAT THE OTHER JURISDICTION DOES NOT COVER: in its Original Jurisdiction the CCJ interprets the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas on freedom of movement of people, goods, services, capital and the right of establishment — it does not extend to human rights generally, and it is not an environmental forum. A land-defence claim does not fit there unless it has a cross-border economic dimension, such as a project licensed to a company from another CARICOM state. WHERE IT DOES FIT, INDIVIDUALS CAN GET IN: under Article 222 a natural or juridical person may seek special leave, granted where the Treaty intended the right to enure to the benefit of individuals, the applicant has been prejudiced, and the member state entitled to espouse the claim omitted or declined to. 35 such cases have been brought, so the route is used rather than theoretical — Trinidad Cement Ltd v Republic of Guyana [2009] CCJ 1 (OJ) established that individuals and companies can use the Treaty to make their own state comply. The Court sits as a court of first instance there, its rulings immediately binding in international law, and hearings are broadcast live.

trackers.name: Maya Leaders Alliance [2015] CCJ 15 — the abstention undertaking to quote
trackers.desc: THE JUDGMENT, AND THE SENTENCE THAT DOES THE WORK. The Caribbean Court of Justice — Belize's highest appellate court — affirmed that Maya customary land tenure in the Toledo District gives rise to collective and individual rights under sections 3(d) and 17 of the Constitution, constituting property equal in legitimacy to any other form of property. THE UNDERTAKING TO QUOTE: the Court accepted the Government's undertaking that until the recognition measures are achieved it shall cease and abstain from any acts — whether by government agents or by third parties acting with its leave, acquiescence or tolerance — that might adversely affect the value, use or enjoyment of lands used and occupied by Maya villages, unless preceded by consultation to obtain their informed consent. Note the breadth: it reaches acts merely acquiesced in or tolerated, not only permitted — a concession granted or an incursion ignored falls inside it. In the immediate term the Solicitor General directed heads of departments to immediately cease all activities and operations on the affected lands. WHAT PROMPTED IT: authorisations for oil drilling, logging, grazing and surveying, including the Golden Stream incursion where the Lands Department issued an agricultural lease over Maya village lands.

trackers.name: A judgment is not implementation — watch the policy that implements it
trackers.desc: TWO LESSONS FROM WHAT HAPPENED AFTER THE WIN. 1. PERSISTENCE THROUGH APPEALS WAS THE STRATEGY. Favourable judgments in the Belize Supreme Court in 2007 and 2010, upheld by the Court of Appeal in 2013, then the CCJ in 2015 — roughly two decades, with the government appealing at every stage and the courts ruling for the Maya at every level. Note also the tactical value of the Consent Order of 22 April 2015: both parties conceded that customary tenure exists, which the CCJ said rendered moot the contest over whether the rights existed at all — removing the foundational question and leaving only remedy. 2. THE ORDER HAS YET TO BE FULFILLED. The CCJ heard arguments on 29 November 2022 specifically on Belize's compliance with its own 2015 decision, and compensation for the constitutional breaches remained outstanding. AND WATCH THE IMPLEMENTING INSTRUMENT AS CLOSELY AS THE JUDGMENT: a draft Maya Customary Land Policy dated 8 December 2023 was reported to contain last-minute inserted language under which companies would no longer need free, prior and informed consent for industrial activity outside determined circular areas. A policy written to implement a ruling can narrow it. Context: in 2010 Belize granted oil concessions in the Sarstoon-Temash National Park. The CCJ treated IACHR findings as persuasive though not binding, alongside Saramaka People v Suriname.

trackers.desc: CHECK WHETHER YOUR SITE IS ALREADY IN A REGISTRY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — it may carry a designation nobody locally mentioned. The World Database on Protected and Conserved Areas at protectedplanet.net is a joint UNEP and IUCN product managed by UNEP-WCMC, drawing on almost 500 data providers in 245 countries, updated monthly and downloadable; it underpins the UN List of Protected Areas. THE OECM ROUTE IS THE ONE MOST COMMUNITIES MISS: a site qualifies as an other effective area-based conservation measure if it delivers sustained, positive conservation outcomes EVEN THOUGH IT MAY BE MANAGED PRIMARILY FOR OTHER REASONS — so a grazing commons, a sacred site or a watershed managed for water supply can qualify without being managed primarily for conservation. THE ICCA REGISTRY IS THE ONE COMMUNITIES FILL IN THEMSELVES: at iccaregistry.org, communities themselves provide data, case studies, maps, photos and stories, and its operators state it is meant to be used to enhance advocacy and recognition — not merely as an inventory. Documenting a territory there creates a citable, third-party-hosted record. THE SENTENCE THAT MATTERS MOST: UNEP-WCMC states these territories must be recognised and respected ‘whether or not they have been reported to the ICCA Registry’ — registration is NOT a precondition of rights, and anyone arguing a claim is weaker for being unregistered is arguing against the registry operator's own position. AND USE THE SCALE FIGURE CAREFULLY: over 1,500 sites are reported under indigenous and community governance — just 1 percent of all recorded sites, with UNEP-WCMC adding that no one knows how many ICCAs exist globally. That 1 percent measures how little has been recorded, not how little communities conserve. Filter Protected Planet by governance type to find such sites; UNEP-WCMC's manual Global Databases to Support ICCAs gives guidance on contributing data.
